start: The cold of that year's winter cut deep into my bones, but it wasn't the icy wind that stopped my breath.
He walked with her through the snow-covered park. The bare branches of the cherry trees looked like claws of ash against the leaden sky.
There was a letter in my pocket. A neat envelope folded with care. My hands shook, not from the frost, but from the confession I was about to utter.
Then, the air suddenly became solid. As if he had inhaled splinters of glass.
A sharp, suffocating pain pierced the center of my chest. My heart... stumbled. Then he galloped in a wild, chaotic rhythm.
My knees buckled against the icy snow. I heard his muffled scream in the distance, a sound muffled by the storm that was beginning to cover my vision.
The darkness did not fall suddenly. It was a slow fade, a free fall into a pit where the beats became fainter and fainter...
prologue_hospital: I woke up to the monotonous beeping of a heart monitor. The smell of antiseptic and sterilized sheets filled the air.
The doctors called it 'severe cardiac arrhythmia with congenital defect'. Clinical and cold words to say that my heart was a time bomb.
I spent months in that bed. The seasons changed on the other side of the glass without me being able to touch them.
My old friends gradually stopped coming. Their visits became shorter, more uncomfortable, until silence was total.
Finally, the head doctor handed me a brochure: 'Yamaku Academy'. An institution specializing in education for young people with disabilities and chronic medical conditions.
'A place where you can live at your own pace, Hisao,' they told me. I didn't know if it was a second chance... or a merciful exile.
act1_yamaku_gate: The hill leading up to the academy is steep. I stopped twice to catch my breath and press my palm to my chest.
The cherry trees were in full bloom. A soft shower of pink petals descended in spirals on the asphalt under the soft spring breeze.
The deafening song of the summer cicadas echoed throughout the valley, a vibrant and constant symphony that filled everything.
So this is my new world... A school built on a hill away from everything.
Towering reddish brick buildings and tree-lined courtyards rose through the wrought-iron gates. Students in uniform walked in small groups chatting and laughing.
At first glance they looked like completely normal students. But I knew that each of them carried a silent battle in their own body.
act1_hallway_meeting: I entered the main building looking for the principal's office to hand in my transfer paperwork.
The aroma of waxed wood and old paper was familiar and calming.
Wahaha~! Be careful out there, new recruit!
A girl with pink hair in ringlets stood in front of me with a radiant smile overflowing with energy.
Beside him, a girl with dark blue hair and thin-framed glasses regarded me with an analytical severity that chilled the blood.
(He moves his hands in a precise flurry of quick signs without taking his dark eyes off mine.)
Shizune says you're ten minutes late according to the preliminary school schedule! I'm Shiina Mikado, but everyone calls me Misha! And this is Shizune Hakamichi, the president of the Student Council!
Oh... hello. I'm Hisao Nakai. It took me a while to get up the hill... heart problems.
(He frowns slightly and makes a couple of cutting gestures with his fingers.)
Shizune says that excuses don't work in Yamaku, but she'll make sure you don't get lost in the hallways!
act1_dorm_kenji: In the afternoon I was assigned room 205 in the male dormitory ward.
As I tried to open the lock with my new key, the next door swung open with a loud screech.
STOP THERE! Identify yourself before I take defensive measures!
A boy with bottle-bottom glasses and a thick scarf in the middle of summer pointed a slide rule at me accusingly.
Hey, calm down... I'm your new neighbor, Hisao Nakai.
New neighbor? Hmm...that's exactly what an undercover agent of the radical feminist conspiracy would say.
I'm Kenji Setou. And let me give you the first survival tip on this hill: don't trust the girls here.
Yamaku is not what he seems, brother. There are files that the administration hides... things that happened at past festivals.
Past festivals? What are you talking about?
Shhh. The walls have ears. Take this before they see us.
Kenji slid me a crumpled envelope with newspaper clippings before slamming his triple-locked door.
tues_seq_1: I wake up in a strange room.
Solid morning light shines on the light gray ceiling. I forgot to close the curtains last night.
I?
This is my room, isn't it?
My room…
This is the third room this year that I'm supposed to call “mine.”
Several things around me remind me that, indeed, I am the one who is supposed to be living here.
My bags on the floor, my new school books on the desk.
My numerous medications on the nightstand.
I stare at the bottles for a moment, pondering, until I open one of them, shake out a pill, and remove a pill from a sheet of aluminum foil.
I pass them with a drink of water without thinking about the chemistry.
My uniforms are in the closet.
I sneak out of the covers and stretch my back before getting dressed.
Putting on a new school uniform feels like wearing someone else's clothes.
The artificial smell of generic detergent invades my nose, but the feeling of fresh fabric against my back is pleasant, natural.
It feels like a school uniform, as it should. It's not much different from what I used to wear before.
That goes for other things too. So far, this place seems to be more or less like a normal school.
Except for the people.
I remember my talk with Kenji yesterday, Shiina's constant laughter, and Shizune's broad sign language gestures.
Well, I've only met three students so far. Maybe they aren't so normal, but I'm sure others are.
Or, maybe people like them are what passes for normal around here?
Yeah, what passes for normal around here? What do people do?
I didn't see many kids hanging out after school yesterday, so maybe there are clubs. If so, I wonder if I should join one.
Throughout class, the question lingers in my mind, so I decide to ask Shizune about it when we split into groups.
After all, she was the one who said that if there was anything I wanted to know, I should ask her.
She crosses her arms and shifts her gaze slowly to Shiina, who seems more concerned with trying to wear down the eraser on her pencil so that the top is perfectly flat and even.
Ahaha~! Sorry, sorry, Shicchan~! Is there anything you would like from me?
Oh~…I see! Hm… That's a good question, Hicchan.
My first thought is that that means he doesn't know, which is worrying. Maybe I'm being too negative. Well, anyway, Shiina, please don't prove me right.
Oh, that's right! Everyone is encouraged to join a club. Many people do it because there really isn't much else to do.
There are also school events, like the festival that will take place in a few days. Almost all the students at school tend to help out with it, doing whatever they can.
So! To tell you the truth you were transferred at a very hectic time… maybe you could help too!
Sure.
What is the festival about?
Shiina freezes.
…Guahahaha~! I don't know, Hicchan, the truth is that it's a local event, and I'm not from this area, so...
She begins to ask Shizune in sign language to get her out of trouble. Shizune adjusts her glasses at the end in a curiously smug gesture, and begins gesturing in sign language forcefully and harshly.
Hey? Oh.
Who cares?
Shiina puffs out her chest as she shouts Shizune's words at me with a disproportionate amount of pride.
Too high. I can see heads turning to look in our direction.
Not so high...
Human beings evolve with each generation! The ideals and beliefs behind a festival will inevitably change over time!
Now it's about delicious fried food and fun little games that you play to win prizes~! Hahahaha~!
The teacher clears his throat loudly, hitting his palm with the elongated wooden pointer as if it were a baton. He gives us an incisive look.
tues_seq_2: Finally realizing where we are, Shiina suppresses a squeal and quickly falls silent. Shizune, however, doesn't look embarrassed at all, ignoring him without concern.
We're halfway through class, and we should get to work.
That's right, Shicchan~!
That? It's true~! Hicchan, are you asking because you're interested in joining a club?
It could have been my eyes playing a trick on me, but I think I saw a suspicious look exchanged between them. Shiina's tone has also changed, although she does that in every other word, anyway.
Yes, I was thinking about that.
Shiina and Shizune look at each other again.
I'm about to ask what they have in mind when something dark flits in my peripheral vision, catching my attention.
From the corner of my eye, I see the girl with long, dark hair get up from her bench and slip silently toward the door.
It doesn't look like she was working in any group, and no one seems to notice her besides me.
I glance at the teacher, who is also watching the dark-haired girl leave.
Why don't you say anything?
Hicchan? Is something bad happening?
Do I look as uneasy as I feel?
Or was Shiina just looking at me while I looked at the girl who left?
No, nothing.
Very good~! Well, since we were asking, you don't have any plans for lunch today, do you?
“I had thought about going to the library and checking out some books.”
…Not really.
So do you want to have lunch together?
Sure.
Hurray~! Wahahaha~! Very good, Hicchan~! Perfect!
The rest of the class passes without incident. The long-haired girl never returned.
Before we have time to think a little more about where it might have gone, the teacher informs us that it is time for us to stop working.
Shizune seems more than a little upset that we barely managed to finish all of our work on time. I'm just glad I finished it, it's not a contest or anything like that.
Yes it is, Hicchan!
Impossible.
Oh really?
Oh really.
I'd noticed this before, but it's kind of funny how Shiina always moves her hands, translating into sign language not only what she says, but what everyone else is saying at any given moment.
Of course, it must be so Shizune can understand. His eyes jump from side to side between Shiina and I's hands.

I don't know who I'm supposed to be seeing. I'm talking to Shiina, but I could be wrong; Maybe I should turn to see Shizune. I'm used to looking in the direction of the person whose voice I'm hearing, but seriously...
Shizune can't hear me, but it would be disrespectful to speak to her only through Shiina. Then again, isn't that what she's doing?
No, at least he's looking at me. This is all very confusing and will take some getting used to.
It is not a contest, because contests are competitions for a prize. If there is no prize at stake, then it is not really a contest.
Shizune's eyes flash dangerously with a competitive gleam. She stares at me, as if surprised that I'm challenging her. I think maybe this is a contest for her.
I've never noticed before how blue and dark his eyes are; It is truly a captivating look.
Are you sure, Hicchan?
Very safe.

Ha ha ha! You're wrong, Hicchan, because~!, I don't want to be the slowest one in the class. Therefore, what is at stake is my confidence in my abilities, and the prize is the satisfaction of putting them to the test.
Wahahahaha~!
Shizune pushes her glasses up in a very self-assured manner.
I would argue further, but the bell rings, and she quickly stands up and picks up her backpack, looking at me expectantly.
I had almost forgotten that I was supposed to have lunch with them.
Where do you want to eat?
tues_seq_3: The cafeteria?
Hahaha~! That's so simple... It's okay~! Come on!
Simple? Well I think so...
At my old school, I liked to eat outside, near the back of the building. It was a good place, but I didn't find it until the end of my freshman year.
I wonder if there is a similar place to eat here. Shiina seems to suggest it.
Shizune and Shiina pull me towards the cafeteria, which is surprisingly not crowded. Some students may prefer to eat indoors or outdoors. I saw that some of my classmates brought their lunches.
After finishing eating, Shiina continues where we left off recently.
So, Hicchan, you wanted to know about clubs and stuff, right? Right~?
Right, Shicchan! Well, I think it makes sense to ask first.
Exchanging small gestures of confirmation, they turn to face me again, and Shiina straightens her posture as if she were going to give a speech.
Hicchan, is there something you're really interested in?
I used to play soccer, but I'm not really interested in it. I don't follow teams and players or anything like that.
Lately, I usually just read a lot.
Hm… There's a book club, right, Shicchan? TRUE! But~! It looks like they already have all the members they can have at the moment. Sorry, Hicchan… It's a very popular club.
Oh, okay! But back on topic, Hicchan, does this mean you don't already have something in mind?
Not really.
Good! Great~! That's great, Hicchan! Really great! Hahaha~! Wahahahaha~!
Why is it so cool?
For no reason.
Well, Hicchan, besides clubs and the upcoming festival, there's one more thing...
The student council!
I see. I didn't know this school had a student council. Although, just to tell me that, that was a most melodramatic setup.
I'm pretty sure they both know it, because Shizune seems a little embarrassed about it, and Shiina is laughing.
Shizune quickly regains control of the discussion, so to speak. After all, it's still Shiina who has to give voice to everything she says.
Hahaha~! Hmm? True, true... Hicchan, maybe you should join the student council! They could use more people~. Yeah! Definitely! You should definitely join!
Because?
Well, for starters, we could hang out every day, Hicchan~! Shicchan and I are on the student council.
In fact, Shicchan is the president.
I'm starting to get the suspicion that Shizune and Shiina may not exactly be the most impartial people to talk to about this.
As if reading my mind, Shizune quickly adjusts her glasses and signs something to Shiina.
Hahaha~! Of course, we're not trying to get you to join just because we would benefit from your joining the student council, and therefore we would have an incentive to try and urge you to—
So, they are admitting that—
Ahaha~! No! We don't admit anything~! I mean, Hicchan, of course it would be nice if you joined, and we'd be grateful.
But even without all that, joining the student council shows a healthy interest in the running of one's school.
Yep~! It's true, Hicchan. Also, don't you want to spend time with us after school, Hicchan?
I don't know if she's being honest or if this is just really good acting. They both seem to be trying hard to look as pretty as possible, even though they're already really pretty to begin with.
Well…
Then it's decided. Welcome to the student council, Hicchan~!
That? No no!
Aahhh… See, Shicchan? Of course it wouldn't be that easy.
Yup! It's true, but it would be very boring if it had been that simple. Well good~! Now Shicchan owes me a candy!
Were they betting on this? Hey, my life is not a game!
Shizune seems very intrigued by this as Shiina finishes translating it for her. The aggressive glint returns to his eyes.
Wow~! That sounds interesting, Hicchan. Let's play a game!
That's not what I said.
tues_seq_4: How about Daifugō, Hicchan? If you lose, you'll have to join the student council~!
No, absolutely not.
Ahh~, why not?
Well, because you two have the same incentive, and therefore the same goal, which is to get me to join the student council, right?
Yup!
Yeah, that's not my goal. But what this means is that the two can ally themselves and I would be at a clear disadvantage. So, I'll have to refuse.
Hicchan! I am very offended! Are you perhaps saying that you don't trust us, and that we would be capable of doing something so i-in-without-zero...? That makes me so sad...
Excuse me?
It's difficult to differentiate where Shizune's influence ends and Shiina's thoughts begin.
In order to redeem yourself for hurting a young girl's feelings, you should definitely join the student council!
No!
How about a game of table football, instead of Daifugō?
Table soccer?
Yes~! It's something they play in America~! You take a coin, and try to shoot it between the goal posts that the other player makes with his fingers!
Isn't that great~? It's the ultimate form of competition between two people, Hicchan~!
…And that primary and secondary school children also play it, Shicchan? Wow! That means it's a game that actually separates the boys from the men!
More like the children of the slightly older children. Anyway, I'm not going to play that either. The very fact that you know about it means you're probably surprisingly good at it.
Hahaha~! Yes yes~, that's true! How did you know, Hicchan?
Shizune scowls at Shiina, letting me know that she possibly shouldn't have admitted it so easily.
I wouldn't say I'm happy with his attempts to get me on the student council, but I'm a little curious about what he's doing here.
I've never been to one before, or even met anyone who was in one, so I'm interested. I also think I like Shizune and Shiina, so maybe it wouldn't be so bad.
Okay, Hicchan, how's Risk? The game of world domination!
I don't know what that is.
It's very funny, Hicchan. Fights for control of the world, armies and all.
It seems like Shizune would be good at this.
If you want to play, we can do it after school.
Oh really, Shicchan? We can play just for fun, Hicchan. Shicchan hasn't played in a while, so if you want, no strings attached~!
Well, okay...
Good! Good, very good~! Perfect~! Then we'll meet after class in the student council room, Hicchan!
Wait, why there?
Because~! That's where we save the game.
Wahahahaha~!
I grimace to tell them how little I like this, but it's more for show than anything else.
So I finally agree, but only after I get Shizune to acknowledge that it doesn't mean anything concrete just to go take a look and play a game with her.
Lunch ends, and we go back to class.
During the afternoon classes, the long-haired girl comes back and sits in her place without saying a word.
Again, no one seems to notice, or if they do, no one says anything. I want to ask Shiina about it, but I don't want to be nosy.
After class, Shizune and Shiina quickly find me on the first floor of the lobby and latch onto me, covering every flank in case I try to escape.
I feel a little offended, but I had been considering it. However, I'm a little worried that enough people have run before for them to be on their guard.
What about the escort? This doesn't make me feel very comfortable.
In fact, it makes me feel like a dangerous prisoner being transported to his cell.
Wahahaha! Is something wrong, Hicchan?
That's right, we're just going to play a game of Risk, remember?

I don't know, Shiina, this all seems kind of sinister to me. I'm starting to think that the moment we sit down to play, they will tie my hands and feet and torture me until I agree to join the student council.
Well, that's pretty unlikely, but still... For some reason, it just seems like a very plausible thing...
tues_seq_5: Getting to the student council room is as simple as turning two corners from where we left.
That? That's all? This makes them being so all over me seem a little silly.
That's not true, Hicchan, Shicchan says that there are people who, when their life is threatened, have shown the ability to have superhuman bursts of speed.
“Your life is threatened”?
Her expression unchanged, smiling, Shiina says something to Shizune, who makes a disconcerting face and puts her hands behind her back, looking pleased with herself.
Mm~ hm hm hm~…
Shiina feigns deafness and hums happily. Stop, I know you heard me; you have no excuse, unlike Shizune.
Shizune opens the door to the student council room. It is an extremely simple and sparsely decorated room, although it is quite spacious, perhaps even a little larger than a classroom.

There's a large table surrounded by chairs in the center, and a smaller desk prominently placed in the back, which I assume is Shizune's. There are also some benches and chairs stacked to the side. Spare parts, perhaps?

Besides the tables and chairs, the room doesn't have much else to offer. Just a couple of filing cabinets and bookcases filled with old school records and documents. There's not much more. In fact, there is nothing else.
This is… quite a gloomy room. They could have put at least one plant in here, or something. But the most notable thing this room doesn't have is other people.
Are we early?
No~.
What do you mean by “no”? Does that mean no one else will come today?
Yes, that's right~.
Before he can ask why that is the case, Shizune claps her hands together with a very vigorous clap.
Hicchan, let's play Risk! Come on, you promised, didn't you? You have to do it~!
Hahaha~! Good good good~! Do you want to know the rules? We can explain them to you while we set everything up!
As Shiina speaks, Shizune pulls out what appears to be a board game from behind one of the file cabinets and throws it on the table.
This actually looks kind of interesting.

After Shiina spends a little more time than she would prefer going through the bases in a somewhat vague and confusing step-by-step guide, Shizune declares that the game has begun with a decisive move, cutting the air with her arm.
Shizune has been infecting me with her aggression. I'm starting to feel more competitive than I intended going into this.

Halfway through the game, while I'm trying to figure out how to defend myself against Shizune's two-pronged attack, she breaks my concentration by tapping her fingers on the table to get my attention.
Hicchan, Shicchan wants you to know that you're taking a long time to make a move.
Shicchan also says he'll let you stay with Australia if you agree to join the student council~!
I thought this was a no-compromise game.
The very fact that she hangs that over my head as an offer means that she knows that I care about the outcome of this game.
And anyway: No!
Shicchan admires your fighting spirit and would be a benevolent dictator who will forgive your people if you agree to join the student council~!
Hahahaha~!
You're so competitive, Shizune.
She seems to take it as a compliment.
I would expect the student council president to be a little more magnanimous.
Mag—ná—ni—ma…?
She doesn't seem to know what the word means or how to say it in sign language, so she takes out a piece of paper and writes it for Shizune, who in response says it in sign language to Shiina.
Shiina presses her index fingers against her temples, as if trying to physically imprint the word into her memory.
Suddenly, Shizune bursts into a flurry of gestures. Shiina looks intimidated by the rhythm of his heated gesticulation.
Ah, wait, slow down please, Shicchan… Hey, Hicchan~! Shicchan says you are going to lose!
Tell him I will crush his world empire with my rebellion.
Ah… Okay…
Those eyes of his shine with childish mischief.
She says you don't have a chance if you keep playing like this! No, you won't~!
Either she is truly making fun of me, or trying to trick me.
However, I have nothing more to lose, so I might as well try something different.
Maybe if I deploy my forces and try to control more territories, I could regain the advantage.
tues_seq_6: Shizune seems to focus on conquering entire nations, so maybe I can sacrifice my dominance in continents to gain smaller countries.
It's worth the try.
A few turns later, I end up losing the game anyway.
Shizune adjusts her glasses victoriously and allows herself to gingerly shake a fist in the air in celebration.
I won, I won~! Hurray~!
No need to translate that, it was pretty clear.
Wow~! Don't be so sad, Hicchan~! You were really doing your best, that's what I think!
However, sometimes your best attempt isn't good enough~. If anyone knows about that, it's me~! You did very well for someone who just learned today!
Hicchan, you attacked Iceland and North America at the same time, that is a very bold move. Shicchan is impressed~!
The mark of great ones is that they are bold, and can follow through to the end~! You're already halfway there; Isn't that cool, Hicchan?

However, that is not enough; Potential alone is not enough! Potential is meaningless if you don't take the first step, and the first step is meaningless if you don't keep moving forward. I want to see more.
You're right, Shicchan~, but that's so demanding...
Shizune leans forward, suddenly looking a lot less playful and more like the serious person I expected her to be all along.
Hicchan, would you like to join the student council?
She really doesn't waste any time, does she? But...
It's only my second day of school, so I'm hesitant to commit to anything so soon.
I haven't even looked at other clubs yet.
But spending time with Shizune and Shiina doesn't seem like it's something I'd hate.
I still need more time to think about it before deciding for sure.
Maybe. I'll talk to you later about that.
It's okay, Hicchan~! But, I hope you're not saying that just to not make us feel bad.
No, seriously.
Seriously~?
Hicchan, if you're going to say that, you're saying that that's definitely the truth, and there can be ~no mistake~!
I know, I know. I guess I should have my revenge for losing, at the very least.
Shizune smiles in a mischievous way that feels like twisting the knife into the wound of my defeat.
He's probably just trying to throw me off.
Looking at the board again, I have a pretty good defense set up, and I'm not going to mess it up by doing something reckless.
A few turns later, I lose the game anyway.
Shizune adjusts her glasses victoriously and allows herself to gingerly shake a fist in the air in celebration.
Wahahaha~! Hicchan, you lost when you let me take North America.
I mean, Shicchan, not me.
Taking control of North America is ambitious, because it provides a bonus of five troops, but you can attack it on three fronts, so you must defend them all~!
I thought you'd have more guts. What a disappointment.
Ambition, Hicchan, your game needs to be more daring! Ambition, ambition~!
I was really excited when you took South America, but then you switched to playing defensively just because you gained a little bit of an advantage. That's not right, Hicchan.
You didn't take enough risks, and when you did, you didn't succeed. That's terrible, Hicchan.
Damn, how much do you care if I played too carefully? There's no need to rub it in my face.
I wonder if you could even be of any use to the student council...
What is this, reverse psychology?
I guess I don't have to worry about joining or not in that case.
Giving up just like that? I expected more from you.
Seriously, is Shizune trying to taunt me into joining the student council?
Besides, I don't even want to join. It's only my second day, I can't make that kind of commitment.
I haven't even taken a look at any other clubs yet. And these two, they are a little strange.
tues_seq_7: Well, I'll consider joining the board, but I want to take a look at the clubs before I decide.
Seriously, Hicchan? Aren't you just saying it to make us feel better?
Yeah yeah, I'm just not sure I want to.
Ahh…
It's okay, Hicchan, but we won't give up so easily. You said “maybe”; There's still a chance you'll change your mind~!
Come on, it could really be fun! We could play more Risk and maybe one day you'll beat me, unless we graduate before then.
That doesn't make me any less reluctant to join, you know?
Wow~! I'm sure you're not that bad at board games! Maybe we can play a game you know then, to give you a head start.
Maybe he just said it to make them feel better, after all.
Oooh, that's so cruel, Hicchan...
I glance at the clock mounted on the wall and realize that I've spent a lot more time than expected playing Risk.
Excuse me, I think I have to go. I wanted to go to the library. It's not closed now, is it?
Shizune scratches her head and gestures at Shiina.
How difficult can it be to determine if the library is open? There's a clock right there on the wall.
It shouldn't be, unless the librarian is absent.
I think you're right, Shicchan.
Um... we think the library is open. It is on the second floor; there is no loss. Do you want us to show you where it is?
No thanks, it's fine. See you tomorrow.
Goodbye~!
Up a flight of stairs and I run into a problem.
The hallway on the second floor is an exact copy of the third floor.
Spacious, of course; and simple, as only hallways can be.
The problem is that the library's whereabouts are not as easy to determine as one would think.
Classrooms are marked with signs indicating which group they belong to, but then there are a plethora of unmarked classrooms.
Is the library one of them? Or is it just somewhere down the hall?
I bet on the latter and choose my address at random.
After turning the corner, an unmarked door catches my attention because it is not closed.
It's not open though, just barely ajar so I can tell it's open and nothing more.
It would make sense for the library door to be open invitingly, and while this one isn't exactly open, it's good enough.
At least this means someone is inside and I can ask for directions no matter how embarrassing it is.
I push cautiously on the center of the door with the tips of my fingers, every muscle in my arm ready to retreat at any instant.
The feeling of being a stranger in this school cannot leave my mind, so I instinctively fear doing something wrong upon entering.
The door creaks slowly as if complaining from a deep sleep, yet it is much easier to open than I had anticipated.
Leaning forward and poking my head further and further in to see the place as quickly as possible, the meek “Hello…?” on my lips it is quickly taken from me.
This... is not what I expected.
Without thinking I let the door open fully, taking in the lone figure taking center stage in an otherwise abandoned room.
The situation steals my voice, leaving me standing in the doorway staring at the beautiful girl.
Evidently having taken the time to assess the situation, the girl gently lowers the teacup and opens her eyes, but doesn't turn to look at me.
How are you. Can I help you?
Looking directly in front of herself, the movements of her lips seem to break the silence more than words.
Still, it is the soft, measured voice that reminds me that she is a being separate from the room itself.
Not only is she probably the tallest girl I've ever seen, but among the foreigners I've met she's surprisingly different.
Oh, hello. Sorry for the intrusion, I was just… kind of lost.
He takes a moment to formulate a response before speaking. Every action you take feels like it was carefully choreographed beforehand.
Would you like to take a seat?
tues_seq_8: …Unexpected, considering I'm intruding.
Ehhh… thanks.
I slowly walk to another seat across from her as the girl rests the teacup and saucer on the wooden table between us.
The way she doesn't follow my movements with her head shows it... That, and the slight haze in her eyes, means she must be at least partially blind, like Kenji.
Come to think of it, his voice doesn't have any detectable accent either. I guess she must be half Japanese.
As I take my seat, his composure catches me a little off guard. His air of relaxed confidence makes silence entirely comfortable.
The calming atmosphere is so different from the student council office.
I take it that you are a new student at Yamaku?
Oh yes. I just got transferred yesterday.
I have the distinct feeling that my speech patterns do not match his formality, accentuated by his moderate reverence.
Which I rush to match, before realizing the futility of the action.
I'm Elena Satou. Nice to meet you…
Hisao. Hisao Nakai.
He nods before gesturing in the approximate direction of his teacup.
Would you like a cup?
Sure.
As much as it pains me, I can't keep up with his formality at events.
She nods politely, taking the order calmly.
Without another word, he rises from his chair and prepares a second cup of tea from a collection of supplies placed along a shelf.
A brush here, a brush there, his left hand often lightly touching the side of whatever container he's pouring into… it seems to be a process he's followed dozens of times before.
As I lean in slightly to look down the side of her back, she appears to use her long, delicate finger to measure the correct amount of water into the cup.
It's one thing to see the different disabilities that the students in my class have, but it's quite another to see how they all seem to adapt.
Shizune and Shiina have no problem working together to communicate with me, and Elena herself seems to have alternative solutions to problems I've never thought of.
Although I feel a little guilty that she does all the work, she seems happy to follow the “correct” procedure of the offerer preparing the tea.
And well,
His soft voice brings me out of my silent observation.
What room were you looking for? It is not common for this to be visited after school.
The library. Shizune and Mi—I mean, some classmates, told me I was on this floor.
He finishes pouring water into the teacup and nods, a metallic tap coming from the cup indicating that it is being stirred.
I am aware of Miss Hakamichi, as are most of the students. That you are with them means that you are in group 3-3, right?
That's how it is. In the science classroom with Mutou.
She giggles before placing the spoon on the shelf and walking slowly towards the table, cup and saucer in hand.
He is quite a character. I imagine you will come to like it; like the majority.
After he puts the teacup on the table, I gently hold it and take a sip. I'm more of a coffee drinker, but this seems like a particularly bad time to mention it.
However, the aroma is quite pleasant. I don't think it will be difficult to ingest.
Thank you, Satou. It tastes pretty good.
She smiles and quickly waves in front of his face.
Elena, please. There is no need to be so formal.
He says this despite his extremely polite way of speaking. Oh well.
I guess I should try asking him about her, since he really seems like he's taking care of me.
So, which group are you from? I imagine it's one of the third years.
That's right, I'm in group 3-2; which is on the third floor, just like yours. It is taught by Miyagi, and is specifically for both blind and partially blind students.
I see.  Ah, I mean, uh, ex-excuse me...
I feel like slapping myself. However, seeing her face, she doesn't seem bothered in the slightest.
Wow, there's no need to change your way of speaking because of me.
tues_seq_9: Oh, sure. Sorry, I think I'm really showing how new I am around here.
An environment like this would be a big change, so I can't blame you for that. Although the same cannot be said for everyone, many have come to assimilate their condition.
A category that would include her, it seems. Feeling quite willing to move on from this particular topic, I move on to another.
Do you come here often for tea? It is a very nice place.
Thinking about it, this room could be their version of the place behind my school where I liked to eat lunch.
I come here frequently during lunch time. My duties as a group representative don't leave enough time for an “official” club, so a friend and I use this room for tea.
Group representative, huh?
Compared to Shizune, her usual mannerisms and gestures seem to be almost completely opposite. While Shizune is outspoken and has a fierce tenacity, Elena seems relaxed and calm, almost distant.
Come to think of it, she could be helpful in having a less biased view of school clubs.
What kind of clubs are there to join?
Hmm… the most popular are the track club, which uses the field near the school during lunchtime, the baseball club, and the book club in a room near the library.
Although there are also several small ones, such as the art club and the music club.
At a time when I find myself just wanting to recover, rushing to join a club right away seems unappealing.
I wonder if this school has the same rule as my old school...
Is it mandatory to belong to a club?
It is not, although it is recommended.
Oh, how good. That's a relief.
I have truly let my guard down around this girl, to have let such a thing out. The fact seems to make him a little amused.
Not wanting my tea to get cold, I finally start drinking it while Elena does the same.
Looking over his shoulder at the window, I notice that the light entering the room has a distinct orange tint.
Even here, time does not stand still.
Oh, time has gone quickly.
Sorry?
TRUE. She is blind. Of course, you can't see the sunset.
It's just that it seems like the sun is starting to set.
That seems to be a surprise to her. I guess he must have lost track of time.
I'm sorry, Hisao. I didn't mean to keep you on your way to the library for so long.
I react quickly to allay their concern.
Oh no, it's okay. The library is still open, isn't it?
She pauses and takes a moment to think about it.
It's probably something I should have asked Shizune when I had the chance, but I think it's likely that Elena would know, in any case.
It's true. It is open until half past six on weekdays.
A quick glance at my watch confirms that I have enough time to arrive.
Hmm, I think I'll retire in that case. It's been a pleasure chatting with you, Elena.
She smiles and nods firmly, her hands folded elegantly on the table in front of her.
It was a pleasure.
Oh, now that I think about it... would you like me to show you where the library is?
I wouldn't be able to ask for more help. You should be able to find it without problems.
Well, unless my navigation skills fail me.  Which they seem to have a habit of doing.
No problem, I was going to go chat with the librarian anyway. I could introduce them.
This is getting better and better. It is very difficult to deny your offer.
If you're sure, then that would be great. Thank you.
As he rises to follow me, he takes in his hand a straight, retractable cane that he had slipped into the handle of his bag on the ground.
Compared to the cane the boy in my group had, Elena's looks thinner and longer. His must be for support, while Elena's is for navigation.
Together we left the peaceful hall and entered the empty hallway on the way to the library.
tues_seq_10: Side by side, slowing my steps carefully to match hers, we slowly walked through the hallway.
It doesn't take us long to reach the door of the warm-looking room, apparently situated in the center of the floor rather than in one of the wings.
Ladies first.
She gives a smile of appreciation for the gesture, and walks ahead as we enter.
To the left is the wooden library counter, and the library itself to the right.
It easily overshadows my old school library, with the distinct aroma of old books giving the place an almost old-world feel.
There don't seem to be many students here. Considering the time, it is not surprising; They are probably in the schoolyard or in the dormitories.
Yuuko, are you here?
He says it on air since the librarian seems not to be present and of course Elena can't see him.
The unexpected thing is that it seems to have results.
Something hits the counter from below, followed by a quiet moan.
Oooh.
The source, apparently the librarian, quickly crawls out and bounces up into extremely rigid attention.
Hello, Elena. How can I help you?
His voice is strained in a failed attempt to sound casual as he rubs the back of his head.
Good afternoon. What just happened? I heard a strange sound.
It's nothing, I just hit my head.
You see, I dropped an eraser under the desk and while I was looking for it I dropped a pencil, and while I was looking for both things you came and surprised me...
Are you okay? I'm sorry, I couldn't know—
It's okay! Okay, sorry for worrying you.
This is nothing, worse things have happened to me.
She's quick to reverse Elena's apology, trying almost frantically to push aside the possibility that there might be something wrong with her hitting her head on the counter.
Yes… worse things have happened, hehehe…
The girl nervously fiddles with her fingers while Elena doesn't seem to get rid of her worried expression, and then moves some papers on the counter for no reason.
A little shorter than Elena, full of glasses and freckles and a very worried look, she seems to fit perfectly in a library.
Ah, Elena! Did you get my message?
Message… hmm…
Oh, the two imported books that arrived?
That's how it is! That's how it is! They finally arrived! I can't believe it took so long, but—
Halfway through their celebrations, partially because they managed to change the topic, I'm sure; He notices me out of the corner of his eye and freezes completely when he does.
Oh no, excuse me for not noticing you sooner!
Do you need to check out a book? Or return it? I'm sorry! I'm sorry!
The way he can change his mood so quickly is a little disturbing.
Come with me. Yuuko, this is Hisao, a new student. Hisao, this is Yuuko, the school librarian.
Pleased to meet you.
Hisao. Good. Hisao. Nice to meet you too. Hisao.
For a second she visibly tries to engrave the name in her mind so as not to forget it.
Yuuko often arranges to import foreign braille books for me.
Would you like to tell Hisao a little about the library?
Elena's innocent suggestion is met with an expression of abject terror.
I... Please Elena, I can't. I don't know what he might be interested in. This is too much responsibility.

How this is any kind of responsibility is beyond me, but her objection is so sincere that I don't doubt for a second that she would rather eviscerate herself right here than tell me where the light novels are.
But...
So are there many braille books here?
I try to save the day by asking the first thing that comes to mind. It seems to work at least partially, as Yuuko seems... not exactly relaxed, but at least a little less tense.
wed_seq_1: I feel tired this morning, probably because just yesterday was a very tiring day. On top of that, I woke up earlier than necessary.
After greeting Shizune and Shiina, I begin to do the work as indicated on the blackboard. It seems this day is going to be heavy.

I don't have a problem with that now though. Shizune and Shiina might be on top of me trying to get an answer out of me as to whether or not I've decided to join the student council, even if it's only been one day.
I wouldn't be surprised if they tried, and I don't have an answer for them if they did. So, this situation is convenient for me.
About ten minutes after class started, Yumi walks in and takes a seat, but no one looks at her. The teacher doesn't even comment on his tardiness.
He, however, stops us to say that we will form groups again.
I turn my head and see that Shizune and Shiina are looking at me. Shizune gives me a smile that is as cute as it is threatening. This is a smile that says, "We've got you. There's no escape."
Hicchan~, looks like we're together again! Long live, long live~!
Shiina leans to the side as Shizune pushes her bench closer to mine. There really is no escape, unless he jumps out the window.
Jumping out the window is not the best option, unfortunately.
What's up, Hicchan?
Oh… Hicchan, have you been thinking about what you said yesterday? You said you'd think about joining the student council, didn't you?
It's okay, Hicchan. We were talking about it after you left, and it would be rude to expect you to have an answer so soon, right? True~!
Hahahahahaha~!
I'm so happy that you two are able to laugh at my expense, and even happier to know that you know how crazy you both can be.
Now that that's over, Shizune quickly returns to her serious mode and taps today's homework with the back of her hand in a very dramatic and important manner.
When I finally see the pages, almost everything is just reading. There are really only two problems.

I almost want to say something about how your rush to get started seems to be too much, considering the small amount of work. In fact, Shizune probably knows how little it is, and she just doesn't care.

Yes, it seems that the volume of work does not interest you as much as the fact that there is work at all; the actual amount is not important. She approaches everything with the same level of ambition.
As I read, I let my gaze wander around the room and find Yumi trying her hand at solving the problems. It seems like she's working alone.
I don't remember seeing her work with other people before.
Remembering how shy she is, it's to be expected.
Hey, that girl over there...
Huh? Who, Hicchan?
She. Yumi. Over there. Does she always work alone?
I think so, Hicchan. Do you feel bad for her because she is alone?
I was just thinking maybe you could work with us or something.
Hmmmm… No, I don't think that's a good idea, Hicchan.
Why not?
Shicchan wouldn't get along with her.
Because?
Shiina turns the question around, letting out a laugh that sounds quite strange; She's nervous, but she still has that sing-song tone present in everything she says.
Well why not, Hicchan.
Shizune has already noticed our conversation, and it makes me realize again how Shiina has been translating everything she's been saying this whole time.
What, Shicchan? Is the friend of my enemy my enemy? That sounds very harsh, I'm not going to say that.
You said it anyway.
I know, Hicchan, it's okay if you listen to us~!
I wonder if this is Shiina's way of keeping things even, since without her, I wouldn't be able to understand anything Shizune says, and vice versa.
Is that also why she's translating all the time, so that there's never a conversation where Shizune is left out?
Anyway, we should start with the problems now, Hicchan.
We finish with time to spare, and I decide to ask if there is any other alternative to the cafeteria, since frankly, the food so far has been mediocre.
This causes Shizune and Shiina to start arguing with each other about their favorite restaurants. Everyone is downtown, so I don't think there's time to go there. And what with the account?
Are they arguing just for fun?
Maybe. They seem so distracted by it that they don't even notice the start of lunchtime.
I look over my shoulder toward the back of the room.
wed_seq_2: It seems like she is studying her notes from last class.
It is a curious sight; everyone else in the class seems to be busy with lunchtime.
Socializing, gossiping, rearranging their benches, those with lunch boxes mingling and chatting like everyone else, only interrupted by brief periods of eating.
But, when I see Yumi, it feels like I'm the only one who can see her. Almost as if she were invisible, like hiding in plain sight.
Are they harassing her? Are you isolating yourself from the rest of the class by your own decision?
I see her look over her shoulder toward the back entrance of the room.
Come to think of it, she hasn't turned a page since I started watching her.
I guess he's waiting for someone.
I do what I always do when I don't know what to do.
Like now.
I've already started reading one of the books I checked out yesterday, and I brought it with me to school to fill the empty times between classes.
I find the page I turned the corner to to mark the place where I stayed last night, and I start from there.
Shiina and Shizune are still arguing heatedly, probably still about restaurants.
If I joined them, I would just be caught in the middle of it, or worse, I would be pressured to join the student council.
Shiina is not speaking out loud since there is no one who needs to hear what they are talking about.
But why does he tend to translate things even when Shizune doesn't need to understand what's being said, or even weirder, when Shizune isn't even present? What a strange conflict of habits.
I find it difficult to concentrate on the book, and also, lunchtime invites me to leave the monotony of the living room. I do so, walking down to the cafeteria.
Shiina and Shizune, having come to a conclusion of some kind or another, follow in my wake although still talking animatedly.
I still feel bad for making her run away yesterday, so I better say something.
Oh, how are you, Yumi?
Hi…Hisao?
Well, at least remember my name.
Hey... I just wanted to apologize for yesterday.
I didn't mean to scare you or anything.
It's just that I'm new here and I thought I should get to know my classmates.
When Yumi looks up to see me, I notice her scars once again.
It's a little disconcerting that you can barely see them from across the room, but they're so noticeable up close.
E… it's okay.
It...it was my fault.
Nah, it wasn't anyone's “fault,” it kind of just happened.
So are you waiting for someone? I saw you turning towards the door before...
Y-yes… Elena.
Oh, you mean Elena, the blind girl?
Yumi just nods in response, and I can't help but wonder if defining people by their disabilities is a faux pas of the worst kind or is just normal here.
I guess that explains why Elena ran after her yesterday.
She seems to be a nice girl. Are you two friends?
Y-yes.
As if willing Elena to appear, she checks over her shoulder again.
I think I'm making her nervous again.
I hope I'm not worrying you right now...
N-no, that's not it.
Only it's easier if Elena doesn't come...
Oh, why is it hard to move around the room?
Not…really.
Yumi's gaze passes over my shoulder and towards Shizune.
wed_seq_3: Shizune?
Yumi nods once more.
What's with her? Don't they get along?
Yumi shakes her head. Clearly this is something he doesn't want to talk about.
It makes sense in a strange way that Shizune and Elena don't get along so well.
Communication between the two would be nothing short of impossible. It's hard enough to talk to Shizune through Shiina, even when you can see the hands of whoever is "talking."
Yumi is so focused on Shizune that I'm the first to notice Elena at the door.
Oh, it's here.
Yumi turns around to confirm it. Seeing Elena, he quickly goes to the door.
Elena…
Ah, Yumi. Good morning. Is the president here?
Y-yes.
Again Yumi glances over her shoulder at Shizune, as if to confirm that she can't hear them even though that's impossible.
I guess we'd better get going, then.
Elena's sigh and tone of what seems like frustration make me raise an eyebrow. I guess there is some kind of enmity between the two.
It's intriguing, but that's not really something I would ask about. I'm sure if it was something they wanted me to know about, they would tell me.
It's only my third day here; I should be making friends, not figuring out why people are enemies.
Still, it's kind of funny to find that this school has little fights, just like my old high school.
Even if people are more tolerant of each other, they are still going to annoy each other.
Hello Elena. How is everything going? I'm sorry for making you run yesterday...
Oh wow, is that Hisao? I didn't realize you were here...
It seems like Elena is a little embarrassed for being so frank in front of me.
E-excuse me Elena. I thought you had realized...
No, it's okay, Yumi.
Hisao, please don't worry about yesterday. It was just a misunderstanding.
If you say so. I'm still understanding this place.
Well, I think you'll find most people here much more tolerant than in other places.
If you feel a little confused, please don't hesitate to ask questions.
Sure, I'll remember it.
Ah…Elena…
Elena makes a small gesture of recognition.
I'm sorry Hisao, but we have to go.
Right now Yumi really doesn't look at all comfortable here, and Elena still looks a little embarrassed.
I wonder if my apology really had any impact.
Do you mind if I accompany you both?
I know I'm pushing it a bit, but... Elena pauses, still smiling.
I'm sure we could accommodate you, couldn't we, Yumi?
She turns to look at Elena, then at me, and then she becomes tense and with her eyes wide open.
C… sure.
Alright, shall we go?
I'm sure Elena wouldn't do this so easily if she saw how scared Yumi looks, but she can't help herself anymore.
Declining after the deal has been closed would only cause confusion and problems.
Shiina and Shizune are still discussing their choice of a lunch spot, incomprehensible for a pair of high school students who have to take a taxi at least to get downtown and back on time.
What haven't they finished yet?
Oh, sorry Hicchan! Were you waiting for us?
wed_seq_4: Don't you have plans?
Plans?
For lunch?
Well, no, so I thought I'd hang out with you guys.
Shiina smiles victoriously at my lack of plans, and excitedly translates my response to Shizune.
If you don't have anything specific planned, do you want to go to lunch with me and Shicchan? Oh, we're going to go to town for lunch though… Don't worry, Hicchan, it's not that far.
Sure, I'll go with you.
And with that, we left the room.
Just around the corner of the hallway something hits me in the chest with the force of a runaway train.
Opening my eyes, I see a pair of saucer-like green eyes staring at me.
They belong to the perpetrator, a short girl who bumped into me and has now fallen on the hallway floor.
He wears a PE uniform and a very worried frown. The first thing seems like a pretty strange thing to wear during lunch time.
…The most surprising thing, however, is that it has no legs.
Or you have them, but they are not made of flesh and blood. Their pale, visibly flesh-and-blood thighs end in shins and feet made of some black metallic or plastic-like material.
They look disturbingly artificial and unnatural. They almost make me forget that my chest is hurting.
The girl winces slightly in pain, rubs her nose and jumps up.
Oh damn... Hey, are you okay? I'm really sorry!
I wasn't looking where I was going, and you came out of nowhere. Excuse me… Excuse me!
She looks really distraught, the way an injured puppy looks distraught.
I quickly forget about my anger or anything similar, as hurt puppies are my weak point.
Alright. Don't worry about that... oh...
I say that, but there is a stabbing pain growing in my chest, and I know that this may be the biggest danger to my condition.
Don't overexert yourself, don't forget your medications and, above all, don't get hit in the chest.
I try to rub my solar plexus to chase away the pain, holding my breath in an attempt to hear my heartbeat.
It seems normal...
Hey, should I go get a nurse?
The girl's high-pitched, worried voice wakes me up.
I stare at her dumbfounded for a few seconds, until I realize that I probably looked worse than I actually did, doubled over and looking completely tense.
Damn, I'm worrying too much about my heart.
Ehh… no need, I'm fine.
Managing to say something in response, I straighten up, feeling my sore ribs one last time, and take a deep breath.
The girl took my breath away. For a long time. But it was nothing more than that.
Are you sure you're okay? I hit you pretty hard.
Alright. I said it was fine, and nothing is broken. Nothing happened.
Excellent! I was for—
I feel a hand on my shoulder at the same time the girl's eyes widen in horror, and whatever she was saying is interrupted by a very eerie—
Ouch!
I don't have time to look behind me because Shizune is already pushing me to the side and advancing towards the girl with large steps while signaling her furiously.
Miss Ibarazaki, I saw that. Running in the hallways is strictly prohibited.
Shiina translates, right behind Shizune, but her voice is feminine and playful, not filled with the divine fury that the movement of Shizune's arms seems to require.
Hey, I'm sorry, I was going to get some stuff, and I was in a bit of a rush.
It has been told a thousand times before. His reckless attitude endangers other students, and even worse, he is explicitly against school regulations.
The girl blushes and begins to act restless and nervous like a little girl caught misbehaving.
It's so cute that I start to smile.
I already know! I—I, ah, I was just…
wed_seq_5: Make sure this doesn't happen again... although I'm sure telling you this is pointless and only gives me more of a headache when you choose to ignore the regulations.
Do you understand, Sora?
The little girl sticks out her tongue in response.
Aaah!
I have to go!
The teacher will cut off my head! I promised him I would help him with the printing, but instead I went for a run! I'm sorry, but I have to change and everything!
Before Shiina, Shizune or I can say anything, she has already bolted from where she was a second ago, almost halfway to the stairs.
Shizune looks like she's about to explode at any second, so I smile at her in a vain attempt to calm her down.
Are you okay, Hicchan? That Ibarazaki girl is always like that, causing trouble for others.
You know, I'm pretty sure Shizune wouldn't call me “Hicchan.”
It doesn't matter, it doesn't matter!
Yeah, anyway, I'm fine. It just took the wind out of me.
That's great, Hicchan!
I wouldn't call it great, but I'll let it slide this time.
So, let's hurry up, Hicchan~! Let's have lunch!
We promise it will be great!
I will trust you. What kind of place is it?
A restaurant, or something?
It's a tea house, Hicchan~!
A tea house… that sounds kind of fancy.
Why are you looking at your wallet, Hicchan? It's okay, if you don't have money we'll pay for you~!
That's very kind of you. Thank you.
It's okay, Hicchan! We're friends after all, right, Hicchan?
It's only been three days. Are we really friends so quickly?
Heh. Although, hearing that makes me happy.
Oh, but it's only for today, and only if you accept right now! Do you want to go, Hicchan?

I'm starting to wonder if this is some kind of trap. Is this a suggestion from Shiina or Shizune? This is important. I'm still a little apprehensive about the possible motives of a girl whose favorite pastime is the game of world domination.
No, I'm just being paranoid. In fact I already like them, and I have to go to town at some point. So why not now, with them?
In fact I had never been to a tea house before. All my expectations are from what I have seen of them on television.
But those were period novels, and these are modern times. It could very well be an ordinary cafe, and they simply call it a tea house.
Anyway, that makes me curious too, so that's another reason to tag along.
Sure.
That's great, Hicchan~! That's great, that's great! Hurray~!
Shiina jumps up and down briefly to show how happy she is, making some faces turn towards us.
Shizune opts for a polite, tiny pat that lasts a full two seconds before returning to her usual stoic appearance.
Would it kill you to be a little more cheerful, Shizune?
Oh? I didn't realize that Hicchan was a king. Hahahaha~!
Shizune adjusts her glasses as Shiina passes on her message completely without sarcasm.
I assume it would hurt more if I could say it with Shizune's intention, so for once I'm happy to have Shiina as a barrier between us.
I'm not telling you to jump for joy just because I'm having lunch with you. I'm not that arrogant.
She seems to accept this, and we head into the village with Shizune in the lead.
We have to run now, there is an important student council meeting about the festival. And we've finally decided where to eat~!
Too bad you can't join us, but this lunch meeting is for council members only.
We can take you there some other time! Oh, but that would be like a date, wouldn't it?
Wow~!
wed_seq_6: The girls leave downstairs.
I didn't make it far from the third floor hallway before this commotion shook me, literally. I should go too.
Lunch and afternoon classes pass without incident.
I read most of the book I had started yesterday, and eat a little of the almost inedible things the cafeteria offers.
The class is tedious.
So we left, the three of us together.
Elena walks next to the wall, letting her cane gently tap against it every now and then. Yumi is right next to her, so close that she's practically half-hugging her as they walk.
Even though this must make it very difficult for her to walk, Elena doesn't even flinch.
The moment we turn the corner of the hallway, something hits me in the chest with the force of a steam train. Yumi lets out a small squeal and my vision briefly darkens.
Hisao, what's going on?
She isn't aware of what happened for obvious reasons, but she sounds very worried. More than the situation warrants, really.
Someone crashed into me, nothing serious. I just gasped.
Hey, sorry, it's my fault. I was going to get some things, and I was in a bit of a rush.
That “someone” here is Sora, isn't it?
The small girl coughs softly and moves her plastic or metal feet, looking up at them before saying anything.
Hello, Elena. Yumi.
I guess the girls know each other.
Please try to be more careful. You may be tough enough to withstand these types of accidents, but there are people who aren't.
The girl blushes and begins to act restless and nervous like a little girl caught misbehaving.
It's so cute that I start to smile.
I already know! I—I, ah, I was just…
Aaah! I have to go!
The teacher will cut off my head! I promised him I would help him with the printing, but instead I went for a run! I'm sorry, but I have to change and everything!
Before any of us can say anything, Sora has already bolted, leaving the hallway eerily silent.
Does this kind of thing happen often here?
There are more rules than usual in Yamaku for running in the hallways.
…But that rarely stops Sora, it seems.
Elena shakes her head slightly and offers a light, serene smile.
I'm afraid there may be nothing we can do to stop it. Shall we leave then?
Elena sets off down the hallway, and Yumi quickens her pace behind her.
The path to the room that the two use to have tea is quite easy to remember, still fresh in my mind from yesterday.
Watching her walk in front of me, I notice that she walks very quickly, taking long, heavy strides with determination.
Maybe if we were walking through a snowstorm it would make sense to walk like this, but it's a perfectly sunny day. Anyway, it makes me feel exhausted just looking at it.
We arrive at the teahouse in what Shiina claims to be “record time,” probably due to Shizune's fast pace.
I'm a little disappointed to see that it's not a huge feudal-era building with mats on the floor and women in kimono serving tea.
It's actually more like a cafe, as I thought. It's not like it's a bad thing. It looks very good.
As soon as I walk through the doors, someone immediately appears in front of us, as if they've been lurking this whole time.
Welcome! Thank you for frequenting this establishment!
The upper half of his body is thrown forward in a bow that appears like an ax chopping wood.
I'm surprised to see that it's none other than Yuuko, the librarian.
Hey, I didn't know you worked here.
Oh… Yes, I work here. I'm a waitress... I've been working here for a year, six months and two weeks... Thank you for choosing to come here, is there anything I can do for you?
Hello, Yuu-chan~!
Hello.
Shiina, do you two know her too?
wed_seq_7: Of course, Hicchan~! After all, Yuu-chan works at the library~! I don't go very often, but Shicchan knows her! And~, we both come here a lot, so it's kind of like we see her all the time!
Ah... Yes... Shall I bring you the usual? And… if there is anything you want, please don't hesitate to tell me at any time.
You don't have to be so formal, we all know each other.
It's also pretty empty today, so you can afford to take it easy.
I hoped she would stop looking so nervous, but my words have the opposite effect.
No... I'm a waitress, this is my job, I have to... do it properly.
Good, good~! That's good for Shicchan! Yuu-chan, please bring Shicchan what he usually asks for, and I'll order some green tea with milk and honey.
No pressure.
Oh yeah... but... this is my job, and... there's always pressure. Sorry, I'm arguing with a client... Sorry! I'm sorry, I'm sorry!
Yuuko bows again at sixty miles per hour. I decide to give up and join Shizune and Shiina at a table.
As soon as I sit down, Yuuko returns looking even more worried than before.

I'm sorry! I'm really, really sorry, I forgot to take your order... I... I'm not paying attention to the customers, that's not right... I'm sorry... If there's anything I can do to make up for it, please tell me...
It's okay, Yuu-chan, Hicchan didn't order anything, so it's not your fault, don't be upset.
It's true. I think I should order now, but I really don't know what this place offers, and there doesn't seem to be a menu.
Yes, she is right. I'll order some coffee, and... a sandwich, if you have one. Whatever sandwich you think is the tastiest, because Shizune will pay for my lunch.
Shizune frowns and gives me alternating looks of surprise, indignation, and bewilderment, unable to decide between the three.
Hicchan, well how much money do you have in your wallet? It can't be that little, right? Right? We should divide the cost by three, to make it fair~! Yes, I won't accept anything else~!
Shiina turns to Yuuko.
Yuu-chan, Shicchan says he wants three of whatever is most expensive on the menu~.
No!
Hahaha~! It's just a joke, Hicchan...
Oh… okay, I think the turkey sandwich is the tastiest sandwich… And it comes with free soup… Although a good employee would recommend the dish with the most… or the most expensive dish…
Am I bad at my job?
No! That sounds good, I'll order that. And some coffee.
Alright.

He returns a few minutes later with our drinks and my sandwich. Shizune seems fine with just her tea, while Shiina also ordered a parfait. I don't know why, as I can't imagine many other things that could go worse with tea.
Oh well. I take a bite of my sandwich. It's very good.
Hicchan, have you thought about joining the student council?
Hey?
Don't talk with your mouth full, Hicchan...
I wash down my meal with a sip of coffee, which is also surprisingly good. But now is not the time to comment that this place has good food.
You said you understood that it was too early to expect him to make a decision so quickly! That was like three hours ago!
A man must be determined, Hicchan!
You should really join the student council, Hicchan. Come on, it will be fun!
People always say “come on, it'll be fun” about things that are never, ever fun.
Don't you believe me, Hicchan?
Is Shizune or Shiina saying it? What an adorable expression; but the effect is a bit discordant, as if he had multiple personalities.
Hicchan, that's depressing. We just want to spend time with you...
It's true, Shicchan! Yes, that's a good point too!
Yes, this is beneficial, it solves all our problems~.
Yeah, I thought Hicchan would appreciate it too... That makes me sad.
Suddenly I feel pushed aside.
It is impolite to talk about someone without letting them participate in the conversation.
Shizune adjusts her glasses, laughing to herself.
Aw, but it's true, Hicchan~! And you would be helping us, membership has been really low this year.
wed_seq_8: How low?
Ah, that's a secret, Hicchan.
No, I want to know how low it was. How low is “low”?
Ahaha…
Five?
Less?
Well…
Zero?

Wow~! Hicchan, that's not important. What matters is that the number is low, and that's why we'd appreciate you giving us a hand, especially with the festival coming up so soon, and what looks like it's going to be a busy year in general.
So you're not going to answer my question?
No~.
I sigh and sit up straight in my chair, trying to look as defiant as possible, because this seems like an important matter and I don't want to let it go so easily. I feel stupid, like a puffer fish.
Well, at least tell me this: How many people are in the student council? Total?
Um, well, Hicchan, we're definitely short-staffed, but we have more than enough members to get the job done. Yup, yup~!
It's not just you two, is it?
Hahaha~! Hicchan, that's funny~!
But~! It's definitely not just us.
Are you sure? Are you absolutely sure?
Yep~!
I stare at the two, trying to see if they make a misstep and confirm my worst fears.
Shiina frowns, looking uncomfortable, but that's probably because I'm looking at her.
Shizune, on the other hand, returns my gaze with one of her own.
Maybe he's challenging me, looking at me over the frames of his glasses. So mocking; and so surprisingly immature, like a little girl beckoning to someone to invite them to play with her.

Hicchan, your two pretty student council representatives have been trying to make you feel welcome and are even buying you lunch. You should show your gratitude by joining the council so you can at least help them.
Yes, it would be great if you could just file some papers for us, and… the festival is coming soon, and we have to build the stalls for the games and food, just a few.
So, if you were there, it would be much easier for us…
Please, Hicchan?
What an interesting good cop-bad cop routine.
I'm going to try it. Why not?
Only once.
Okay, I'll do a test. It doesn't mean I'll join in, or anything definitive, it just means I'll help out a little, and then I'll see. And this leaves us at lunch, I'm not doing this because I want to.

I finish the last of my sandwich, and this makes Shiina realize for the first time that she has a parfait. He begins to devour it much to Shizune's chagrin, as I can see from the way he plays with his fingers that he had a lot to say.

Every time I look at Shizune, she looks at me with tremendous concentration and intensity. This time is no exception, his face has no expression; maybe you are thinking. Eventually, it gives rise to a smile.

He says something in signs and, obviously, I don't understand it at all. She has to know that. Then he does it again with a childish playfulness that shows through the speed and energy of his gestures.
Shiina, what did he say?
Shiina looks up from her parfait, torn between wanting to help and continuing to eat.
What does this mean?
I try my best to repeat with my hands the same movements that Shizune did. I quickly realize that this is not very easy. Imagine doing this all day, as your only form of communication.
Hmm~…Sorry, Hicchan, I can't tell you.
Why not? Is it an insult?
No, Hicchan, I can't tell you why~! It means something nice.
Something nice, huh? Well, they're back to their tea and food, so I guess this conversation is over for now.
I don't really understand it, but this makes me wish I could. Maybe you could even try learning sign language. This school might have courses for that.
Would I really do that? I think about it as I finish the rest of my coffee. I wonder why he would even be motivated to think about it.
I'm having such a good time that I don't even realize that we should have gone back to class ten minutes ago.
wed_seq_9: Even if I went back to school right now, it would take at least… thirty minutes? Maybe. I can't risk running fast with my illness, so it would take at least that long to get there.
Well, already 10 minutes late, it wouldn't matter even if I could teleport.
Is something wrong, Hicchan?
I just realized that lunchtime ended ten minutes ago. It's only my third day and I'm already missing a class.
Yep~! It's already late for you.
Hey, that's not funny, for you too! And aren't they both on the student council? They are setting a bad example.
Hicchan is a sanctimonious man...
But~! Hicchan's right, he's already late for class, and~ it seems like you're getting off the mark too, Hicchan, because you're not making an effort to go.
As your student council representatives, we're going to have to do something about this and make sure you're punished for this~!
But you two dragged me here, this is all your fault. Take responsibility!
Hicchan, we were just inviting a potential student council member to try to recruit him. It's business, business~! But~! You're not a council member, so there's no excuse!
Yes, there is. That potential student council member is clearly me.
Yeah! Are you going to join the student council, Hicchan?
Shizune haughtily raises her teacup and wiggles her extended pinky up and down.
Hicchan, if only you were a member of the student council…
But~! You can still join, Hicchan! If you join now, you won't be in any trouble, and we can have many more enjoyable excursions like this all the time! It'll be fun~!

I'm starting to think that maybe this was all an elaborate trap to get to this moment. Maybe Shizune lured me here, betting on the possibility that I would lose track of time and be forced into this situation.
Diabolical... Well, considering what I know about her, I should have been more on guard. But to admit that I got into this, even a little, would be unforgivable.
I try to read Shizune's intentions in her eyes, but she just returns a blank, innocent look. He takes a sip of his tea, like he's mocking me.
By the way, Hicchan, I didn't plan this at all, it just happened to turn out this way~!
I was about to dismiss my theory as paranoid, but this puts a new spin on things. I almost fell from astonishment.
So this whole thing really was an elaborate trap, from the very beginning, all just to put me in a bad situation and force me to join the student council.
Ahahahaha~! You look so nervous, Hicchan~! Did you really think we were fooling you all this time?
Aren't they?
Hicchan, did you really think…?
Shiina frowns, looking heartbroken. Soon Shizune frowns as well, following his example. How much synchronization. Like two drops of water. They must be twins.

Shicchan says she's flattered, Hicchan, but doing that kind of thing would be a grossly inappropriate abuse of power, and an imposition on your free will~! And also~! It would be blackmail, too! Shicchan would never do something like that, ever!
I think about asking Shiina “are you sure?” but I resist the urge.
Anyway, Hicchan, what Shicchan says is true. Since you're with us, and we're doing student council work, it's okay if we miss a class or two.
Not that this is a good excuse to do it...
…Or one that should be used more than three times a month…
Or something that can or should be abused...
So~! Definitely, but we definitely need to go back to school! At some point~!
Wow~!

Shizune waves to get Yuuko's attention and points to her empty teacup, indicating that she wants another one, while Shiina hurries to finish her parfait so she can order something else. Maybe I should too.
I'm still hungry, and the portions here are rather small. The most important thing is that Shizune will pay for everything, and with that in mind, I ask Yuuko for another sandwich.
By the time we leave the teahouse I have not only missed one class, but two.
Shizune and Shiina seem content to let the whole day pass, lingering even longer by suggesting a tour of the city that turns out to cover a two-block radius from where we started.
We eventually return to school, and the rest of the day passes as if nothing had happened. When classes end, Shizune and Shiina pack their backpacks and leave the classroom before me.
Now that I think about it, this is the first time I've been left alone.
It's weird, I almost miss them. The room empties quickly, and I am the last one out the door.
However, when I try to leave the lobby, an arm comes down in front of me like a toll gate, stopping me immediately.
Oh, hello Shizune.
A pair of hands behind me cover my eyes, followed by a sudden burst of laughter.
Hello, Hicchan~! Guess who I am!
wed_seq_10: Shiina asks with a complete lack of sarcasm, which means she doesn't think I instantly knew it was her for many obvious reasons.
I wonder, who could it be? Well, it's definitely not Shiina...
Hahaha~! It is!
Shiina turns around to stand in front of me and next to Shizune.
Hicchan, are you busy right now?
Busy going to my room, yeah. See you tomorrow!

I try to escape, but Shizune is too agile to get past her. As someone who used to play soccer, this is embarrassing. Not to mention, this attitude is attracting some strange looks. You should give up while you can.
Hicchan, could you please go upstairs and get a couple things from the art room?
Why me?
Hahaha~! Shicchan thinks that if the art teacher sees us, he will say hello, and she doesn't like him!
Ignore it.
He tried, but even with Shizune being deaf, he will try to say “hello~!” anyway!
Does he run away?
I never run away!
A definitive tone so strong that I can perceive it even through Shiina. I can see that there is no point in pursuing this topic with Shizune.
Shiina, why can't you go?
Stairs make me dizzy, Hicchan!
Shizune nods her head, as if confirming it.
Please, Hicchan? We need these things to build the stalls for the festival, and you said you'd help out a little, right? Right?
I really shouldn't, but I guess just this once would be okay.
Alright.
That's great, Hicchan! Thank you~!
This is what we need!
He hands me a piece of paper to take.
I'm sure this list was written by Shizune. It is handwritten, but each letter is uniform and perfectly formed, as if it had been typewritten.
Not only that, the list is also exhaustively detailed, complete with numbering, bullets, and even little boxes.
In short, what she wants is paint, brushes, cardboard and an easel. Only certain types and specific amounts of each of them. I wonder how I'll get all this down the stairs without breaking my neck.
Elena and Yumi quickly get down to the business of preparing lunch.
Before I can even open my small bag of food, Elena is already busying herself with her thermos and tea bags while Yumi prepares both of our lunch boxes.
So, is this what they meant by coming here almost every day?
Yes, Yumi and I usually have lunch here. It's comfortable for both of us, so we end up using this room regularly.
After seeing Yumi's reactions to me over the past few days, I can understand why that is a big help. That, and Elena can also get some peace of mind outside of her group.
I take a seat at the end, after Elena has poured tea for us and sat down.
The more time I spend with these two girls, the more I think they are the perfect antithesis to Shiina and Shizune.

Even without a voice, Shizune is direct and sassy, ​​and Shiina seems to get along well with everyone. On the other hand, Elena is soft-spoken and relaxed while Yumi seems to be the shyest girl I've ever met.
So how are you doing in Yamaku, Hisao? You looked a little nervous earlier.
Besides getting lost from time to time, and getting knocked out of my classroom? Well, I think...
You…you looked pretty hurt. Are you really… okay?
For a brief moment I consider telling Yumi and Elena about my condition, but I refrain.
I'm not sure why, but for some reason I feel uncomfortable talking about it to these relatively unknown people, even though they've been pretty friendly.
Yes, it was nothing. I was just a little surprised.
Judging by the girls' expressions, I don't think they're believing it. But, in what I assume is their way of respecting my privacy, they don't press the issue.
I guess that's one of the unwritten rules around here; “don't ask.” Even if some people's condition is obvious, like with Yumi, there's still hopefully a story involved.
Everyone has something they're not comfortable talking about, and I think everyone here recognizes that.
So, uh... how long have you been at this school? They both seem to know the place pretty well.
thur_seq_1: The sound of an alarm pulls me out of fitful sleep into the unpleasant state of wakefulness.
I stay under the blanket for a few minutes, gathering the energy to get up while thinking of excuses as to why I haven't done so yet.
Honestly, I wouldn't mind staying here all day. School is surprisingly exhausting after a long break, and the culture shock hasn't gone away yet, I think.
However, despite being under the impression that skipping classes is easy here, I don't think they'll let me get away with it that easily.
And the nurse will surely get annoying with the exercise lecture, too.
So eventually I get up, swallow my morning medications, and put on my old soccer clothes.
Thanks to my illness, I was exempt from participating in Yamaku gymnastics classes, so I was not given a sports uniform.
I would order one to cover such a contingency, but wearing my old soccer clothes is a bit nostalgic.
