I can't use it for that anymore, so maybe I can have a new life this way. A little like me.
After all, if I'm going to start taking care of myself, I can't afford to be lazy. I'll start from the bases.
Foundations that include keeping the rest of my body in shape along with the little I can do to strengthen my heart.
Maybe then I can return to something close to a normal life; or at least something in which you are less likely to drop dead at any moment.
It seems a bit stupid to me, really.
But I guess this way I can at least honestly tell the nurse that I'm doing something about my health.
It's not like he was a great runner to begin with.
It doesn't cost anything to try, I think.
I am surprised to discover that I am not the only one present on the track.
Not only that, it's also a face I've seen before.
The girl with prosthetic legs who knocked me down yesterday in the hallway is running on the track agilely, like a half-mechanical gazelle.
What was his name? It was a short one, but I can't remember.
He appears to be circling at a somewhat relaxed trot, his prosthetic legs tapping rhythmically against the hard surface of the track.
I wonder what reason he has for running so early in the morning. Maybe it's because of something similar to my case, and the nurse is forcing the poor girl to jog just like he does with me.
I definitely wouldn't be here if it weren't for my health, and for your insistence that I do it.
And even with things the way they are, it's just to get it off my back soon.
The fact that I was less likely to find anyone to witness my pitiful attempts to get in shape was merely a happy accident.
I would leave, but it seems that my former attacker noticed me on her last trip.
He waves happily and trots towards me.
Good morning! Your name is Hisao, right?
She smiles, apparently pleased to have remembered my name.
Maybe you don't remember me.
Sora? I knocked you to the ground in the hallway yesterday.
“Miss Ibarazaki?”
She imitates Shiina “imitating” Shizune, failing to get that faint happy tone with her high-pitched voice.
How could I forget such a, er, powerful presentation?
Sora has the decency to look slightly regretful for a moment before laughing.
Yes, excuse me for that. Again.
Hmm, well, as long as you don't make a habit of it, I guess I'll be fine.
Brilliant!
I'm not sure if he realized I was joking.
So the “spy-advisor” the nurse was talking about… is it really you?
That's how it is!
I was expecting someone from the nursing staff, to be honest.
What, are you saying I don't look like I could be a spy?
No, it's more like a relief. I was afraid I had someone watching my every move.
Unless you're here to do exactly that.
thur_seq_2: No, I'm here for my own reasons, the nurse just asked me if I had seen “an exchange student with messy hair and a face like he was lost” on the track.
So why are you here?
Sora makes a dramatic pose.
Training!
So that?
Athletics!
Ah, I see. So you're on the track team?
Sora nods enthusiastically.
Yup! I'm one of the best runners, too!
And modest about it, too.
Hey, you should join!
It's good exercise, you know.
I think that much activity is probably impossible for me.
Nah, I'm not even sure if I really like running that much.
Besides, I'm not interested in organized sports, you know?
It's true. I hadn't even been very interested in football.
I mean, I would run around and play with my friends and stuff, but that was the only reason I played.
It wasn't for the glory that can be found on the playing field, that's for sure.
Sora seems to understand what I'm trying to say.
I see, I see. Not very involved in all that organization.
But now that you're here, that means we're going to be running together, huh?
That? Eh, sure, I think.
Sora looks happy.
Are you going to warm up?
Real men don't get hot.
Oh no, you should always warm up! Hisao bad!
He scolds me enthusiastically, but then smiles and walks over.
I hate warming up too.
He laughs suddenly.
Heck, and I don't even have to stretch my legs!
As if to confirm her statement, she bounces up and down a few times, giving the passing impression of standing on springs. Their prosthetics appear to be quite elastic.
Come on!
And so we start running around the track, and I can immediately see that she wasn't lying about being good at running.
Sora moves fluidly, launching into a kind of wild abandon.
I find myself focusing on running properly.
Hands outstretched, right?
And something about landing on the ball of your foot, instead of your heels...
I try to match my pace to Sora's, but it's quite difficult.
Apparently I'm not very good at it.
Maybe Sora could help me with that one day.
Frankly, I don't remember if there is any particular way to run, but I can't help but feel like I'm doing it wrong, somehow.
I feel weird compared to Sora, who never seems to miss his stride.
I don't think I want to do this anymore.
I don't really feel up to doing more than a few laps today, and I quickly transition from jogging to walking.
Sora continues running, and doesn't seem to notice that I stopped until he passes me a second time.
thur_seq_3: He brakes quickly, breathing evenly in contrast to my own gasps.
Are you done yet?
I let my head hang painfully.
Heh, yes.
I'm not in very good shape right now.
Sora nods, then smiles at me once again.
He seems to smile a lot.
Well, the important thing is that you started, right?
Next time, you just have to try to hold on longer, and then longer, and longer, and eventually you'll be great!
I'll keep that in mind.
But I think I'll go get ready for class now.
Shouldn't you go too?
Sora shrugs nonchalantly.
Nah, I have plenty of time.
I notice he's not wearing a watch.
Are you sure?
Another disinterested shrug.
Not really… But I have to finish my routine!
See you later, Hisao!
Uh, yeah. See you.
I'm not sure if this morning's experiment was a success or a failure, but I have to admit that I feel a little good about getting out this morning.
And like Sora said, I just have to keep trying to get better, right?
Practice makes perfect, or something like that.
It's nice to at least feel like I've taken some control over my own health.
I'll have to try to keep this up.
Other than feeling more tired than before, I don't think I accomplished anything this day.
I'm so out of shape it's embarrassing.
All of this may have been a waste of time. I'll find some other way.
I head back to the dorms to clean up and put on my uniform, trying to resist the urge to take a really long, hot bath.
I'm tired from all that running, so I just want to relax, but I don't want to break my slowly manufactured routine of getting to school before the morning rush.
After taking a long bath anyway, I dry myself off and leave the cabin to put on my clothes.
Out of nowhere, a shadow appears within the mist, threatening and radiating malicious intentions. Violently breaks through the fog.
What's up?
What are you doing here? What the hell, you scared me! What's your problem?!
I should be asking you that. I've been looking all over the place for you, man.
What do you mean “all over the place”?
I want to ask if he's been looking for me while like this, completely naked, but I stay silent.
I finally realize that I'm still naked too and quickly hold my shirt in front of me, but Kenji doesn't seem to notice anything.
His glasses are foggy. But then why don't you clean them? Is your vision so bad that it's like you're perpetually seeing through a fog?
You know, your room, and… Yeah, that's it. Hey, I mean, in the end I still had to get up. Whatever. It's not important. Can you lend me some money?
He makes an innocent face and looks away, trying very hard to look very casual. Not working; he is as transparent as his window-sized glasses.
Speaking neutrally like this, wearing nothing, feels awkward.
In fact, in some ways it's even more uncomfortable to be naked in front of someone when they can't see me being naked. Not to mention the fact that he's naked too.
I try to shake the feeling off, with little success.
Money? Sure.
thur_seq_4: Fabulous.
Wait, why do you need it?
Ehhhh…
Can't you just give it to me because I had the good will not to take a look in your pockets while you were bathing?
I could have done it, but I exercised self-control. And in the end, isn't it the intention that counts? Come on, be a comrade.

This doesn't make sense. If it is the intention that counts, I must deny the loan, since his thoughts were so clearly impure and his intentions are probably more sinister since he cannot tell me what they are. I say this to him.
I'm offended man, but if that's your game, then fine, I guess I have no choice. I want to order a pizza, and I already have most of the cost of the pizza. I need your help for the rest.
I get some of that pizza too, right?
Are you serious?
Sure. I'd give you some, but you have class, you don't have time to eat pizza.
What about you?!

I'm not going to class, I have to wait for the pizza and pay the guy. And then eat it. It's not easy. You have to sneakily get the pizza. If you don't, everyone will see you. And to the pizza. And they will ask for a slice.
It's a tough world out there. Everyone wants a piece. Then you're left stranded in an unforgiving world. It's happened before, that's why I know.
Every day, I plan my revenge, so that when the people who offended me order a pizza, I'll be there. Always vigilant!
Kenji breaks into a dramatic pose, completely without irony.
But yeah, I only need like 400 yen. Please! You are my only hope! I can't go outside and buy my own pizza, it's too far away!
I try not to go out unless absolutely necessary. Let me tell you what happened the last time I went out without carefully planning ahead.
I was outside. I can't remember what I was doing. Something. Stand still? Maybe wondering how I got there.
And then, out of nowhere, it happened.
Like a bolt of lightning, splitting the sky, just as you split a sandwich into two equal pieces to make it more manageable to eat, a bird shit on my head.
It was the second most shocking moment of my life.
Which was the first?
He ignores me and continues talking. I want to grab it and shake it. Are you just trying to keep talking? I'll go with that option, even if it's more likely that he just didn't listen to me.
It was like the openings of some types of anime series.
You know how there's always a part where the main guy is fighting his rival, and they fly at each other and clash swords and there's like big, dramatic auras of color and zoom?
It was like that, but with poop.
I understand.
So yes, I need money. Please? Don't leave me flying, man. I only need like 1000 yen.
I thought there were 400.
Alright.
What?
I'll pay you, I swear.
You better do it, that's what it means to borrow things.
I don't know when I'll be able to pay you.
You have a week.
Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhggggggggggghhhhhhhh……
Kenji grimaces in pain and makes sounds like a dying cow, a particularly disturbing fact given the fact that his baton is directed freely.
You're not supposed to be so rigid about money between brothers in arms, man. Men have it bad enough with everything as it is.
Did you know that male porn stars only earn half of what female porn stars earn?
That doesn't mean anything unless you're a porn star.
So maybe I'm a porn star, alternatively, fighting to survive while fighting feminist agendas, and you can't even share your crumbs with me, you bastard. Nobody understands. Nobody.
Wouldn't feminists be against pornography in the first place?
This feminist plans thing again?

This thing is important. I can see that you don't give a damn, but this is serious, here. Feminists... are a dangerous enemy, don't make mistakes. Take them lightly, and you'll wake up in the morning with a knife in your back, bam! Out of nowhere!
How do you wake up in the morning if someone stabbed you while you were sleeping?
thur_seq_5: Women are terrible at stabbing things.
I thought you just said not to take them lightly.

Well, don't take the big things lightly. Individually they are not a threat, but if there was some kind of war, like a big war, with men on one side, and feminist forces on the other, it would be very ugly.
And that day will come, when feminists come out of their top-secret global feminist headquarters around the world, and say “Now is the time, motherfuckers!”
You're being ridiculous, there's no such big “world feminist headquarters” building, where were they even going to hide that?
I mean, it would have to be massive, you couldn't hide that on Earth, someone would notice a huge fortress with only women in it.
Who said he was on Earth?
I turn my back on Kenji and start practicing threatening faces in a mirror so I can figure out what kind of gesture will best express my emotions. He can't see me from this distance anyway.
Which, unfortunately, means he just continues to rant without any regard for sanity or sensitivity.
Without a doubt, there is a war going on. A war that not many know about, but it is a huge one that one day will overflow, and encompass the entire known world.
So, we'll have to choose sides. We will have to take a stand. In fact, it's happening right now.
Imagine it, the bloody battlefield. A brutal conflict without end.

I almost gave up, when I thought this cause was silly... When I got tired of the rawness of our fight... When I mistook the time the power went out for a feminist assault, and I thought the end was near...
But then I realized that if I gave up, everything would be over, I was like, “hey” and I knew I had to get serious. Because I'm the last sane man in a crazy world. It's about duty.
It must be a crappy move if everything revolves around one naked guy ranting in a bathroom to another naked guy.
So can you give me the money?
He's blocking the way out, it's starting to get cold because I'm still naked, and I want to go to class, so I agree to hand him the money.
Formidable. Thanks, boy. We should go bowling some other time.
Bowling?
Without a doubt, it is the ultimate sport. There are almost no female bowlers either, making it also the most manly sport.
Should I wear my pink bowling shirt with her shoe game or the pastel green one with highlighted flowers?
Are there bowling clothes?
Maybe.
Anyway, you better pay me what I lent you.
I can pay you back with things, right?
I don't have the time to ask you to explain what that means.
Don't know. I have to go to class, you're like getting through it.
Oh. Sorry. Sure, I don't want to delay you, and I have some things to do too. The time has come.
The time for what?
I just like to say that.
Okay, now the time has truly come.
So that?
I have to use the bathroom. Get out of there.
I was about to do it! And what does that mean? It's a big bathroom.
AND? I have to be alone or I can't go. The pressure…
It's okay. What if someone else comes in?
I'll think of something.

I give him my practiced gesture and he looks a little silly reflected in his glasses. He either doesn't notice it or doesn't see it, anyway, so I get dressed and run back to my room, feeling like it's been an eternity since I woke up.
That's time I'll never get back. I'll make him pay for this somehow.
But right now, I have to go to class.
I'm the first person in the room, although I think I arrived too early. On the other hand, sitting here alone for 20 minutes sure beats having to suffer that time with Kenji.
The combination of fatigue, frustration and boredom is starting to make me feel very tired.
I black out for a second, waking up when my head hits the surface of my desk.
Rubbing my forehead, I realize that this is as good a reason as any to stay up and then stop coming to class so early.
Eventually I hear a knock outside in the hallway, and Elena's tall figure appears in the doorway. She is not in this group, so she must have some other matter. Maybe he's looking for Yumi.
thur_seq_6: Elena stops at the door, acting hesitantly as if she were a vampire who can't enter unless invited. I consider doing so since she looks pretty lonely standing there.
However, she enters the room on her own, after smoothing her skirt and the collar of her blouse as if it were important to look prim when entering our classroom.
With permission.
He calls into the quiet room with a delicate, probing voice. I realize that the silence may make her nervous because of her blindness, so I break it.
Good morning, Elena.
Hisao? Good morning. I didn't hear you come in.
I wonder if she thinks it's suspicious that I didn't tell her before. It's likely. If I tell too big a lie, I would sink.
Well, he was already here, just asleep until recently.
Oh. Have you seen Yumi today, by any chance?
No, she seems to come just before the bell rings... or after it. Do you want me to tell him something for you?
No, it's okay. It's strange, but I think we're the only two people at school at the moment. I didn't hear anyone else on my way here.
I guess I shouldn't have gotten up so early today.
Are you punishing yourself for doing something other people should? Punctuality is a good thing. I think so, anyway.
Today is a very busy morning. The festival is almost here, and today is the deadline for event registration, budget reports, and any other official paperwork.
It could be that everyone is trying to fill out the forms at the last minute. Maybe that's why he's so quiet today.
Hello~ hello~!
Shiina appears inside the room just as Shizune enters, screaming with an intensity that makes Elena visibly flinch.
Hey, Hicchan~!
How are you.
Look, she's the representative of the group! Hello~!
Elena smiles, probably amused by Shiina's—or Shizune's—use of the word “look.”
Good morning.
Of course, you're not the representative of this group, right, right~?
I'm not.
Elena seems more defensive in her responses to Shizune than she did to me the other day. I think they really don't get along at all.
Then I realize that Elena may not know that Shizune is present and may be trying to detect whether she is there or not, so she knows who she is talking to.
Well, all she knows is that she's talking to Shiina, but knowing that she and Shizune are practically inseparable, she might hope that it's Shizune who's really "talking."
Damn, how complicated. I decide to help Elena, for my own peace of mind more than anything else.
You're early, Shizune.
You were here earlier than us!
Shiina puffs her cheeks angrily. Why are you getting angry? Does he feel emotions from Shizune, too?
It's not that strange, however, that Shizune didn't like my little comment. It's true, I was here earlier than them, so saying something like that could have definitely been misinterpreted.
Especially for Shizune, who doesn't have the benefit of being able to hear tone of voice to gauge intentions.
Before he can begin to weigh whether or not he should apologize, Shizune has already left him behind.
Representative~! It's good that you're here~! We have to talk.
The festival comes in three days, right? All other groups have already submitted their projected budget reports for their events! Even the first years! Except you~!
Wow~!
There's still time to deliver it, isn't there?

Today! The deadline is today! You're really taking your time, aren't you? If I could do things my way, I would have had all the paperwork done days ago, but someone~! had to say “please extend the deadline~!”
Yes, that was me. Planning something on this scale is not an easy task, and a week is too short a time frame to expect an entire group to completely resolve an issue as complex as this.
Do you want to know what's more difficult than distributing funds for a group's events? Handle the same for all groups in the school and even more~! I'm the one who does that!
Shiina places her hands on her hips and stands up straight. Impressive, he's really stepping into his role. However, Elena doesn't seem to find it funny.
Hey, Shizune, aren't you being a little hard on her? There is still a whole day left.
Please, Hisao. Alright.
Elena seems happy that I'm taking her side, but also a little conflicted that maybe I think she can't take care of herself.
thur_seq_7: If this is about the budget, then I'm disappointed that you think I've forgotten about it. I understand how important it is.
So~! Can you give it to me please?
Shizune, maybe she doesn't have it right now.
He is not here at the moment. I asked two students to take care of it for me. Students in my group.
He emphasizes the last sentence to my surprise. Do you know about Shizune and Shiina's attempts to drag me into the student council?
I think word must have gotten out, so now he's using me as ammunition against Shizune. This is getting better and better...
It was your responsibility~! A budget report is not something you should just be delegating; As a group representative, it's your job to always be on top of everything!
This kind of indifference to proper procedure is really terrible~!
They completed it, being able to do so, but the students have been sick recently, so they couldn't come to school and give it back to me. If you wish, I can apologize on your behalf for falling ill.
Okay~!
Although Shiina doesn't pick up on Elena's little hint, Shizune does, and she seems torn between being offended by Elena's forwardness and jumping for joy at the possibility of a challenge.
Elena, don't they live here at school? It's a five minute walk, you know~.
What could they have that prevents them from taking 5 minutes out of their busy lives… to leave something that will affect the enjoyment of the entire group?
Elena opens her mouth to say something, but Shizune closes the distance between them and begins gesturing furiously, waving her hands like an orchestra conductor.
Shiina tries her best to convey the same passion, but doesn't seem to lose her cheerful tone. The result is interesting and somewhat surreal.
And what's up with that attitude~? I said it's not something you should be delegating; You are the representative of the group, aren't you?
Tell me the names of those two students, they should have your job if you can't even be in charge of something so simple yourself.
A form is not the entirety of what I am supposed to take care of.
Elena's tone is becoming slightly impatient, but she's doing a good job of not letting Shizune see how upset she's getting. He is playing with his cards close to his chest.
Shizune, on the other hand, wraps her fingers around the edge of her glasses happily, knowing that Elena can't hear or see how excited she is.
Of course, you do so much, representative~! It must be so complicated being you~!
Elena purses her lips at Shiina's words, clearly understanding the intention behind them even though Shiina utters them without even a hint of the sarcasm they are supposed to have.
Shizune and Elena don't get along, that's clear, but this seems a little extreme. It seems Elena has had enough and is ready to fight back.

In fact I was discussing the budget report before you arrived. You must be very talented to have finished all your student council duties so quickly that you can track me down to make sure I don't forget mine.
Are you accusing me of being lazy? It seems like you're confusing me with yourself~!
I don't believe it. That would be a very difficult thing for me to do; compare me with you
You're right, the difference between us is like heaven and hell.
And it is not difficult to guess which of the two you would represent.

The air between them ripples with the heat of their enmity. Well, not really. However, they can no longer hide it. Even Shiina seems to be beginning to understand the true nature of this conversation.
Hicchan~! Don't be lazy either~!
What are you talking about?
Aren't you going to be part of the festival, Hicchan? You will, right? So~! I hope you do a lot more than this person to make sure there are no setbacks~!
Why am I being dragged into this? I think I've done more than enough.
If you're mad at Elena, that has nothing to do with me.
Now, wait just a second… are you implying that the president is more right to scold me than she is to scold you?
Oh damn, I think I could have said it better.
No, I don't know anything about it but... what I want to say...
What are you saying, Hicchan?
I just hardly think it's fair for you to say that, seeing as I've helped them.
The environment has changed. This is like a duel between two gunmen now. Well, it was like that before too, but now Shizune's attention is on me.
And Elena's too, although she remains silent. I'm afraid I made her very angry without realizing it.
Are you saying I'm wrong?
What a dangerous situation.
It's too early to argue with you... Yes, I think it's unfair of you to jump on me.
Hicchan, you want too much~! But~! You have a point in favor. Okay, okay~! You're not lazy, Hicchan.
thur_seq_8: Hahaha~!
Shizune pushes her glasses up with her thumb, almost in a gesture of approval.
That's ok! If you're not useless, you shouldn't let anyone say you are~!
But the next time I say it, it really will be because you'll be letting me down as the lady group representative here, so don't let it go to your head!
Elena takes the hint, a venomous expression frozen on her face.
Representative~! Shicchan says, “Don't forget that report, please~!”
I won't do it.
Would that be all?
Yep~!
So, good day everyone.
His voice would have cut the air in the room in half, if it were more tangible.
Elena leaves the room, understandably in a bad mood but still managing to look poised and calm as usual.
Shizune, you really went a little overboard today.
It's true, Shicchan, just a little~.
If I had been waiting for Shizune to grudgingly admit that I was right about that too, I think I would have waited too long. She doesn't respond.
Hahaha~! Shicchan thinks you should mind your own business.
Hicchan, we have some last minute things to do before school~! We might be late, so~! Can you please cover us?
Sure.
Perfect~! Hurray~! Very good~! Thanks, Hicchan!
They walk outside even though there are only ten minutes left before the bell rings, signaling the start of classes.
Hey, I'm the new kid, remember?
It's not like I could have done much, even if I wanted to.
That's true, you shouldn't expect an exchange student to throw themselves into their first week.
Elena being on my side feels strangely comfortable so I decide to support her too.
Yes, you are being irrational with both of us.
Excuses, excuses. The group representative lady has had plenty of time to present her report.
And we repeatedly offered you a position to help with the work of the student council, but you refused to commit to making the festival a success.
Yes, but like I said before, I'm not sure if...
I don't have time for this now; No matter what he does, it will mean getting into a confrontation with Shizune, and that's what she wants.
One way or the other. Forget it.
I turn my back on them.
Elena, classes will start soon, so we can continue talking later. I'll tell Yumi that you were looking for her.
I can feel Shizune freeze. Perhaps this is the first time she has been ignored in such a way.
Thanks, Hisao, I'm leaving then.
Elena gives me the sweetest smile I've seen all week, and turns to leave.
As soon as Elena walks out the door, I suddenly feel hesitant to turn around to face Shizune.

I can feel her eyes burning into my back, and I can't muster the courage to look at her. She must be furious. I keep waiting for Shiina to say something to ease the tension, but it's really asking too much.
In the end, I return to my seat and listen to the sound of Shizune's footsteps as she marches out of the classroom. He doesn't return until a few minutes before class.
I turn my back on them.
I return to my seat and turn off my ears so as not to hear the grand finale of the argument between Elena and Shizune.
Eventually, Elena leaves our classroom and both Shizune and Shiina sit down, not speaking to me.
I can feel Shizune's eyes burning my back. She's probably mad at me, but I'm just as mad at her.
I don't understand why she had to drag me into the argument.
Yumi doesn't come to morning classes at all, leaving a lonely empty seat in the back of the classroom.
I should tell her that Elena was looking for her if I see her later.
thur_seq_9: After the events of this morning, class is pretty boring in comparison. I lazily turn the pages of my textbook.
We've been covering the same number of pages each day, so reading ahead is more or less giving me a preview of what tomorrow's lesson will be about.

The clock at the front of the room rings unbearably loud. The teacher hasn't said anything in over seven minutes, choosing instead to cover the board with rows and rows of equations straight from the book.
The rhythmic crash of the chalk against the blackboard seems to synchronize perfectly with the ticking of the clock.
I start copying the equations just to pass the time, not noticing Shiina's head peeking over my shoulder until she's almost completely above me.
What are you doing?
I try to balance between saying it quietly enough not to draw the class's attention, but loud enough to attract hers.
What are you doing, Hicchan~?

Panic spikes inside me when Shiina starts speaking at her normal volume, and I blurt out a hurried response while keeping my voice low, even though she's just destroyed any hope I might have had of being discreet.
I'm copying those things, what are you doing? Why so strong?
Ooh~, really? But it's all in the book... That's why no one else is copying it~!
I know, why are you talking so loud?
Why are you speaking so softly, Hicchan? It's hard to listen to you.
I look around to see if anyone noticed our conversation and it's pretty obvious that everyone has, even the teacher.
Shizune smiles shyly, and I start to wonder if Shiina is doing this because she told her.
Is this because of what happened between her and Elena earlier?

Is this what I get for trying to be reasonable? For trying to take the middle path? Shizune is excessively proud of herself, although at this point I should know to expect that kind of attitude from her.
Why are you doing this?
Hey?
Shiina is completely oblivious to the awkward look the teacher gives us both, as he tries to balance the textbook on one finger.
For a brief second it looks like things could get ugly, but the teacher simply looks away, as if it's not worth it.
I guess this is a good thing, and I sink back into my seat with relief.
The rest of the day passes without a hitch, and this time I am able to appreciate that it was.
When the bell rings, I'm not in a hurry, so I stay a while, reviewing what we saw in class today. I prefer to go out last anyway, so I don't have to deal with all those people in the hallways.
I notice that Shizune and Shiina also stayed behind, talking to someone from another group.
Shizune is signing so fast that her hands are making noises that remind me of swords cutting through the air.
Shiina is desperately trying to match her, but it's obvious that she can barely even understand her.
I lower my head. Whatever they're discussing seems like a serious matter. Probably something beyond me.
Not only that, but Shizune also seems angry, although it may simply be her natural sternness making her appear that way.
Shizune signs to the point where her wrists make noise, and Shiina struggles to spit out her vocal equivalent.
Sometimes he stumbles over sentences as if he were dealing with tongue twisters. And on top of that, she has to translate everything the other girl is telling her into sign language.
It seems like hard work.
Shiina looks tired, almost like she's about to faint.
Fortunately for her, their affair soon ends and the girls return to their seats once again.
Uwaaah! How tired I am!
Shiina hangs her head on her bench, looking exhausted.
The preparations for the festival must be hard for you.
Indeed, it seems that the people at this school take the festival very seriously. Every time I see people hanging out before and after school they are always talking about their plans for it.
It's a great thing to see that everyone is so enthusiastic about it.
I'm probably the only one who doesn't have something to do.
Shizune begins to speak in sign language and Shiina perks up, looking at her hands with slightly unfocused eyes.
She signs with strong, heavy, dramatic movements.
Shiina translates her signs into speech for me.
She does it so well that it's almost as if Shizune is actually speaking, transmitting her thoughts directly through Shiina.
Well, we're on the student council, you know, so we're pretty busy.
thur_seq_10: Sarcasm?
Hey?
The tone of Shizune's actions makes me think she's “speaking” dismissively, but Shiina plays it off normally, replacing any intention she might have had with her own light-hearted spin on things.
It's still disorienting, I don't think I'll ever get used to it.
It doesn't matter.
How could I forget, with you two trying to get me to join in at least twice a day?
Hahaha~! But, Hicchan, some might say the work is too much.
It would be nice if the students showed a little more support for his leadership, a little appreciation for those who are working so hard to make it all possible.
Maybe, for example, a little help. That's not asking too much, is it? Yep~! Help would be appreciated~! From students like you~!
If the students showed their dedication and school spirit, and offered their help, well, I don't exactly need it...
But I wouldn't necessarily reject it either... So~! It would be nice if someone did it...
Oh? Hello~!
I look over my shoulder and see Yumi timidly looking into the classroom, most of her body hidden behind the door.
Hey! Playing criminal again?
Yumi blushes brightly at Shiina's direct question, even if it was only joking.
Shizune looks at her sharply, causing Yumi to look down and begin to walk away to the point where only her fingers can be seen nervously gripping the edge of the door.
Maybe he is showing his dislike towards Yumi by association of his dislike for Elena.
It seems that way, and Yumi probably knows it too.
It seems they have momentarily forgotten to make me stay for the rest of the day.
What's wrong, Yumi?
Has Elena... passed by... here?
I'm sorry, I haven't seen Satou. Although she, uh, came in the morning.
Yumi continues to look uneasily at Shizune, who in turn gives her her usual analytical look. What are you trying to do?
Of course Shizune isn't going to look away, and she's intimidating enough on her own; so I can only imagine how terrified Yumi must be.
It's a little funny though, seeing Yumi's reaction to Shizune's normal attitude. It seems that this is what happens when two completely opposite poles come together.
Do you... do you know w-where it is?
If he has any brain left, he's in his classroom, working on his festival project. But who knows where that woman is lounging.
He must be wasting his time somewhere, just like Hicchan~! Wow~!
Damn, what's up with Shizune and her need to point out things like this?
He must be wasting his time somewhere~! What a useless woman~!
Yumi nods quickly and hastily leaves, obviously to avoid any further contact with Shizune. Unfortunately, this turns his attention entirely back to me.
But Hicchan isn't useless, right? TRUE? He said it himself~! Wow~!
I can see where this is going, and I want no part of it, not after that experience yesterday.
Well, good luck with your preparations…
I start packing things into my backpack, ready to run for the exit.
Unfortunately, I'm at the other end of the classroom.
The short distance to the door seems like a vast No Man's Land to me now.
Both Shizune and Shiina begin to slowly maneuver in front of me, cutting off my escape route in an eerily cautious manner that makes me think of ship-to-ship combat.
I think Shicchan is saying that you should help us, Hicchan~!
Geez, I wouldn't know, she's so subtle.
But~! That's the intention, so please? I can't keep up, we actually have to build stalls for the festival, almost all of them on our own, can you believe that?
Hammering boards over each other, over and over again, it's very hard!
I'm so used to it that I was pretending to have a hammer in my hands during class, and I didn't even realize it!
He hits his bench a few times, imitating hammer blows.
It's so repetitive, I can't stand it! And yesterday, I hammered all the boards one on top of the other...
fri_seq_1: My alarm goes off, and I shake myself uselessly for a moment until I remember that I had decided to give running another try in the morning.
I don't know if this was my best idea, but I'm determined to move forward.
This is about my health, after all.
Sure, things haven't been great for me lately, but that hasn't made my existence so intolerable that I don't try everything I can to stay healthy.
Besides, it's about exerting some kind of control over this matter, right?
If I can get that, well, I can get anything.
At least that's what I keep telling myself.
Once again, it seems I am not alone in my career.
Apparently Sora has already been here for some time.
And apparently he's been working out for a while now.
With all this, when the hell is he coming to the track?
Oh, it's you!
I'm surprised to see you again!
Why is that?
Well, not many people make it back for a second try.
She frowns, seemingly bothered by a passing thought.
Like the rest of the athletics team, for example.
Still, it was supposed to be voluntary, so it's not a big surprise.
And I guess it's too early in the morning...
He shrugs, and suddenly seems to have forgotten what he was talking about.
The expression of displeasure disappears completely, and he seems to suddenly return to his previous line of thought.
Good! Come on then!
What?
You're here to run again, right?
Well, yes.
Then let's go!
I find myself suddenly grabbed and pulled towards the track.
Things seem to be arranged in a way that reflects yesterday's race.
That is to say, I seem to be fighting, while Sora moves with a ease that I find enviable.
It's incredibly annoying, getting exhausted so easily.
I know I should be patient, work and move forward little by little, but…
It's hard to stay positive in the face of this.
We circled the track and began our second lap.
Sora seems to have grown impatient keeping up with me, and begins to walk away.
This is where I gave up yesterday.
I let Sora go at her own pace, and she shows no mercy, moving forward half a turn in an instant.
I don't blame her.
I mean, it's not like I'm putting up any kind of real fight here, right?
Instead, I'm just running at a steady pace, which is what I should be doing, right?
There's no need to push my limits at this stage of the game.
God, is this even worth it?
When we finish the second lap, I stop again.
Sora continues, and it almost seems to me that she is disappointed.
Well, that's stupid.
I have nothing to prove to him…now that I think about it, I have nothing to prove to myself, either.
fri_seq_2: I'm fine the way I am.
And what I am not is a runner.
This was probably a bad idea.
Maybe there is something else I can do instead of this.
Getting up this early sucks, anyway. There must be another way to stay healthy.
Walk, maybe. Nice walks in the afternoon.
Yes, that sounds good. Running is not for me.
I wave goodbye to Sora and return to my room.
I'll think about something else another time.
What am I doing here?
Am I really just going to give in and allow Sora to get ahead?
I quicken my pace.
The second round is over quickly, and without a second thought I continue.
Sora turns and looks at me over his shoulder and smiles.
Are you still going?
I wouldn't want *phew* for you to think *phew* that I'm out of shape *phew*.
Sora laughs—without breaking his stride, not even a bit—and speeds up even more.
Well, if this is how we are going to play...
I also increase my own pace.
I can feel my lungs burning, and my legs are starting to wonder what the hell I think I'm doing.
The lactic acid screams in my muscles, but I close my ears.
I can't allow myself to be left behind, because that would be a defeat.
The rational voice inside my head slightly wonders when we started playing a game.
I would respond, but I'm having a lot of trouble thinking right now.
It's too fast.
How the hell does he manage to keep—
It's like a rope is pulling on my chest, a suffocating sensation of tightness and pain.
Before I can think anything other than “Oh shit,” the track disappears from beneath my feet.
I stumble, one hand shooting up to clutch my chest, the other hitting the floor trying to keep it from landing on my face.
Sora turns around and opens his eyes wide.
Hisao!
She yells at me, running full speed from the other side of the track.
What's happening?
Nngh—Nothing, just…
Keep your breathing constant.
Calm down. Don't panic.
Don't panic.
Do you need me to bring the nurse?
I close my eyes, isolating myself from the outside world.
My heart struggles to regain its rhythm.
Slowly, the pain in my chest begins to subside.
Soon he leaves as if nothing had happened.
It wasn't… nothing? No, something happened there.
I open my eyes and see a very worried Sora.
I think I'm fine.
fri_seq_3: My voice sounds strange even to myself, strange and phlegmatic. That makes Sora frown.
I don't think you are.
She seems to have made up her mind, and nods to herself.
Yes. You come with me.
You have to see the nurse.
Sora grabs my arm and drags me. I feel a little shaky, but I refuse to accept Sora's offered shoulder for support.
To tell the truth, I am a little ashamed of my own weakness.
I'd really rather not have made Sora worry about me, but it seems to be too late.
As hell, I'd really rather not have made anyone worry about my condition, but at this point, it seems to be too late for that too.
I'd like to be able to deal with all of this on my own, without being a bother to anyone else.
And since I'm craving things, I'd rather not have this condition in the first place.
Nurse!
Sora bursts into his office without knocking, but this doesn't seem to alarm the nurse in any way.
Good morning, my ray of sunshine. What's happening?
Ray of sunshine? Anyway, he calmly drinks from his coffee cup, but puts it on the table after following Sora's gaze towards me, standing at the door.
Hisao? What brings you here?
We were running and you tripped and grabbed your chest and I thought about coming for you and making you wait there but you said it was okay but then I thought you should see him anyway and—
Calm down, Sora. Calm down.
Hisao, what happened?
Don't know. We were running, and then my chest started hurting like that time, but it went away after a few seconds.
It was just some palpitations or something.
The nurse frowns, as if to say that “just a few palpitations” is some kind of oxymoron.
I didn't mean something like this when I suggested exercising. You have to be more careful, Hisao.
I was being careful, it's just...
Now that I think about it, “I just got into a race with one of the track team members” doesn't seem as reasonable as I had thought.
It's just what?
Um... I mean...
He was competing with Sora.
Sora, is this true?
Sora fidgets, looking adorably regretful.
Ah well...
Finally he can't seem to force himself to say it out loud, and simply nods.
The nurse sighs and rubs his forehead with one hand tiredly.
Sora, you have to be more sensitive to other people's limits!
I don't know if he told you, but Hisao has a bad heart, and having him compete with you was incredibly irresponsible.
Hey, actually I started it.
The nurse is stunned by my statement.
What your WHAT?
We were just running, and Sora started to walk away, and so I uh, sped up to catch up with her.
The nurse looks up at the ceiling, murmurs a prayer for patience to some god or another, and turns his gaze back to the two of us.
So they're both stupid.
That's comforting, I think.
Oh come on, Hisao. I have to make sure your heart isn't going to explode or something.
I dutifully obey and follow him into an adjacent room where we make sure that I am not, in fact, going to writhe and die.
So, what do you feel?
fri_seq_4: I don't know. Not much. Tiredness, but it could just be from exercise.
You should stay here for a few hours and rest, and we'll see how you feel after that.
I'm not going to object, so I lie down on the infirmary bed.
An extremely miserable Sora walks in after getting a good scolding from the nurse in the other room.
I couldn't hear what he was saying through the closed door, but I'm sure they weren't compliments.
Look, I'm sorry, I'm so sorry.
I should have been more careful.
Hey, you didn't know. It's not your fault.
She looks terribly discouraged and regretful, and my words don't do much to encourage her.
I want to make it up to you.
Again with that decisive nod.
So you have to come have lunch with me.
I'll carry it for you, okay? Something very, very good!
I start to say “You don't have to…” but then I shut up and only nod when I see his face.
Good!
We meet on the roof.
Us?
Yup! The weather is nice, so the rooftop is a great place for lunch, you know.
I see.
You're coming, right?
You wouldn't deny me the opportunity to make it up to you, would you?
Of course not.
Brilliant! See you there!
I tread water somewhere between dream and reality, feeling completely exhausted.
Not only my body, but my entire being is without strength and paralyzed, apart from my senses.
I swallow hard and then try to stay as still as possible, which in this state is not a very difficult thing for me to achieve.
The nurse is on the other side of the curtains that he drew to give me privacy. I can see his shadow move from side to side in the sunlight.
He has opened his office window. It's windy outside.
The white curtains flutter in the breeze in a heavy, lazy movement, like waves. The light filters through them slowly, partly absorbed by the fabric.
I close my eyes. The breeze on my face feels like the soft fabric of the curtains.
I listen to my heartbeat for a moment, trying to drown out the sound of the nurse typing on his computer, and my own heavy breathing.
It is stable.
Damn, not even a week and I've already ended up in a place like this. I really messed up this time. He should have known better than to act like the half-baked star athlete in front of a real one.
And why did I try to act brave, as if those palpitations were no big deal, even when it was obvious that they were?
It was just a reflex, pushing him out, keeping him in.
I didn't want it to happen.
He didn't want Sora to see it.
Aaah…
Stupidstupidstupid.
I have to be more cautious, or I'll end up in the hospital again, or worse.
That's my last thought before I give in to exhaustion.
I fell asleep. For how long? What time is it?
I feel a little dizzy and I keep blinking compulsively.
Pushing the curtain aside, I squint against the unfiltered light pouring in through the window. The texture of the canvas doesn't feel at all like the wind it used to.
The nurse looks up from his work, sitting exactly where he was before.
fri_seq_5: How do you feel?
I really can't say it, that's why I don't answer anything. I feel a little groggy for falling asleep at such a weird hour, hopefully I don't look too weird.
What time is it?
Me speaking with a hoarse voice trying to get some guidance. The nurse looking at his watch before answering.
Things seem to happen in slow motion.
Ten and a quarter.
I try to think what it means for a moment but I'm not really sure.
You didn't answer my question, Hisao.
Oh. Good.
So get off that bed, and let's see how you do. No…
I try to do just that, only to falter when I move too fast. The nurse moves to hold me by one arm and sighs.
… get up very quickly, is what I was going to tell you. Just sit down, I'll check your blood pressure to make sure.

Wow, my good intentions lasted a long time. I remain silent, ashamed of myself, while the nurse busies himself with an old-fashioned device and my arm. After a couple of minutes, he puts it away, neither looking satisfied nor dissatisfied.
Are you OK. Has your head stopped spinning?
Good. And how's the rest of you doing?
You didn't show good judgment out there, Hisao.
I swallow the reply I was going to make. That's what I had thought, but hearing it from someone else makes me want to protest.
It's not nice to hear what he says. Doesn't make him any less right.
No, sir.
He nods, still looking as neutral as before.
It would be easy to get mad at him if he said “I told you so” or something like that, but he doesn't.
I can try to help you stay healthy, but in the end the decision is yours. I hope this little episode is something that reminds you of that.
Here, a note for your teacher. To avoid an interrogation.
I take the piece of paper he offers me and walk away as I can't think of anything else to say, it's not like I really want to either.
Stay out of trouble, you hear me? I don't think it was more than a scare, but next time it might be different.
I hear it.
There is some way to go to the school building directly from the auxiliary building, but I have no interest in searching for it and possibly getting lost, so I take the exit I know works.
I stop on the stairs of the auxiliary building, deliberating for a moment between going to the dorms to get my things and my books or going straight to class.
The sun makes my eyes burn, so I head to the bedrooms.
I wake up and take a hot shower.
Back in my room, the first thing I see is the familiar row of medicine bottles lined up on my wardrobe, and it depresses me, as usual.
It's annoying. I thought it was fine. I thought I had made peace with this, that I was over it.
But what I really did... was allow myself to forget that I have a problem. Being here certainly reminds me of reality, and trying to fight it only hurts.
Reflecting on it won't do much. I've done this before, for months. Looks like it's time to get over it.
If I allow myself to forget that my life will definitely not be as long as everyone else's, I won't get anywhere.
My life may be different from others. But it's a life in progress.
Here's how I'll rationalize it.
I gulp down the usual handful of pills, trying to push the sudden gloomy feeling out of my head. Then I prepare to leave early for class, as usual.

Walking out into the hallway, he notices Kenji coming from the corner of the hallway, stealthily heading towards his room with a large bag. As he sneaks past me noiselessly like a ninja hiding in plain sight, I decide to call him.
Hey.
Jump at the sound of my voice.
Oh, what's up, man. I didn't realize you were there. I'm very tired.
I think he didn't see me, but that's not the problem.
Where were you so early? Shopping?
Nah, I wasn't shopping. Sometimes I have to visit... the math teacher. Yes, I thought it would be a good idea to find out when the next exam would be, as it tells you in advance if you want to know.
fri_seq_6: And so what's in the bag?
It occurred to me to go shopping while I was away. I need supplies to continue the fight against the vast feminist conspiracy.
Oh, very good.
I thought you weren't going out.
Now I wear a hat.
I decide not to point out the fact that he's not wearing a hat.

An awkward silence settles between us and then Kenji breaks it by pushing his door slowly, releasing a squeak into the air that only increases the awkwardness of the moment. He leaves the bag inside his room and closes the door.
I'm surprised you went out of your way to find out the date of an exam. Trying to take advantage of an opportunity to study is quite diligent.
I never study.

I just wanted to know what day the next exam was. I still have to take it, duh. I need to know in advance to know which day I cannot miss classes. He usually sends updates on that crap over the phone, so I had to go out and find out.
And why do you have to go out, when you can find out with your phone?
I don't bring a phone.
What do you mean you don't bring a phone? Do you mean you leave it at home?
Nah, I don't use phones. I don't have a phone. Telephones. I don't have a phone.
Why don't you have a phone? How can you not have a phone? No phone? Nothing?
I just don't like phones. In fact, they scare me a little. I don't know why. I think it's some kind of repressed trauma.
But basically, when I hear a phone, I get nervous. It's my darkest secret.

I have two theories about that: either I have some fear of receiving some deadly, vague, ominous call that could alter my life, or I was hit with a phone in the past. Hit so badly I can't remember it.
Hit in the head.
Well, where else could I be hit with a phone to make me unable to remember it? The ass?
Unexpectedly logical. Now I feel very depressed. Sensing that this conversation is more or less over, Kenji opens his door again and prepares to enter.
Well, I'm going to sleep, my friend. May you enjoy.
Classes are going to start in 20 minutes.
I already did something for today. Too tired to go to school.
Hey, do you need some lip balm? I bought two by accident because I thought the store had started selling individual double A batteries.
Thanks but no thanks.
The door at the end of the hallway opens, crashing against the wall after being pushed too hard. The sound is followed by thunderous bubbling laughter, and I instantly know who it is.
With the noise, Kenji disappears into his room like a ninja, slamming the door just as Shizune and Shiina walk here.
The first walks with short, efficient steps, while the second more or less bounces off the walls.
I try to do the same as Kenji, but it's too late. Shiina puts her foot on the doorstep to prevent me from closing it, so I have no choice but to let them in.
Hey, Hicchan~! Hello~ hello~!
How are you.
What are they doing here?
I wonder if the pause between those two sentences was long enough to be polite.
Hicchan, how rude~! We are coming to pick you up!
Did it occur to you that we thought you were going to run away and we came to make sure that wasn't the case? Surely not, Hicchan~!
Hey, I didn't say that's why you were here.
But now I know that's exactly why they're here.
It's time for student council work, yes it is~!
Aren't you happy, Hicchan, that you have the opportunity to help the entire~ school~! You're like a hero~! Future generations will tell stories about this day!
Interesting. I didn't think joining the student council was a feat worthy of Hercules.
Well... I guess I did promise...
I had forgotten about Shizune and it is only now that I notice her out of the corner of my eye, peeking into my room over my shoulder, her analytical gaze jumping from one object to another.
This is somewhat intrusive, the feeling of being exposed creeps up my balls. Luckily I don't have dirty clothes on the floor or anything like that.
Hm~? What's up, Shicchan?
fri_seq_7: Yes, this is Hicchan's room~! We hadn't seen her before, I hadn't realized!
It's a bit simple, but Hicchan hasn't had time to decorate it yet, isn't that the case~?
What are those things?
She points to my collection of medications on the nightstand.
It's no big deal.
I quickly stood in front of them, trying to hide the things behind me. Shizune takes a step back, with a suspicious look, but it's not an expression without concern.
I hope that if I avoid it, she understands that I don't want her harping on about it.
It's true? What are you hiding, Hicchan~?
Nothing.
Seriously~?
I realize I can't really get away from this one. They are nosy by nature and hiding it will only arouse their curiosity more.
Yeah okay, it's something, but I don't really want to talk about it, okay? Not yet.
Can't we put this aside for now?
As Shiina translates, Shizune fixes her gaze sharply on me, as focused and analytical as ever, peering at me over the frames of her glasses.
He presses his fingers against each other thoughtfully, as if weighing the value of going on longer than necessary against the insult of disrespecting my wishes.
His expression finally melts into a slight smile and he signs something to Shiina.
Okay~! So, let's wait, and become better and better friends, and one day when you feel like it, you can tell us~!
They both give me a wide smile, and I feel perplexed and a little stupid at my behavior.
They're not stupid, and they can probably guess, at least halfway, what's happening to me. And…
Such simple and kind words. I feel relieved that they don't think badly of me even though I am like that. Despite not being like the rest. Even though I can't be calm about it.
It seems that behind the hateful antics, these two girls are actually kind and good people. That's what I think.
Thank you.
So, you want me to help you for this day, right? Since I'm one of you?
Yep~!
After school?
No no no~! Now!
Now? But what about classes? Are they going to be missing again?
Hahaha~! It's for the greater good, so we sacrifice our math lessons, and maybe social studies too~!
Well, I think that's fine with me.
Amazing, Hicchan~! You said it, okay? Remember: “It's okay for me to help~”, that's what you said, right~?
Sure.
That tone… I suddenly regret saying it.
Very good~! So are you ready to go? We can go to the office together~!
No. They'll probably make me carry all their stuff or something.
Don't be stupid, Hicchan.
We've never walked to school together, Hicchan~.
I almost want to ask why we would do it, but then it hits me. They both consider me their friend, like Shiina said before. And they want us to be best friends, even.
It's strange, I've never thought of them that way. Or anyone I've met this week. Is it really that simple?
It's that simple...
Okay, let's go, then.
Shizune smiles slyly and puts her hands behind her.
Hahaha~! Great, Hicchan~! Good, very good, but first~! You had a great idea, Shicchan really liked it... So~! It's time for a game!
Oh no.
Shicchan has a 1000 yen bill in one of his hands, Hicchan~! If you guess which one, you can keep it! If you don't make it...
You will carry all our books to school~! Right, Shicchan~? True~!
fri_seq_8: She and Shizune nod at each other.
Very good, Hicchan~! Get ready~!
Carrying three backpacks instead of one, I wonder about the day ahead. What awaits us?
I can see students coming and going around the courtyard, probably preparing their own projects.
The festival is practically here. That means there are only two possible reasons why my help is required.
Or there's only a small amount of work left to do, and they just want a hand finishing the mundane final checks they're forced to do.
Or there's a ton of work pending, and Shizune is putting on a calm face as a torrent of piled-up, postponed work threatens to kill us all.
Still, they've already gone too far this time. Annoying busybodies.
It's no big deal.
Really~, Hicchan? It doesn't look like anything, to me.
What a long line of jars, right~? True~! What are those all about, Hicchan?
Just a few things.
That seems like much more than “a few things”…

I can't blame any of them for being this way. Shiina is only speaking for Shizune, and Shizune is curious by nature. Still, I wish they would stop digging and take the hint. But Shiina doesn't, and Shizune can't.
That's why they keep pushing.
It's really none of your business.
Shouldn't they leave? A man's room is private, you know.
Shizune seems to take that as a challenge.
What does that mean, Hicchan? When someone sees something interesting, their first instinct is to ask what it is, that's obvious. What's wrong with that?
Because, like I said, there's nothing to see.
Hicchan, I think Shicchan is just worried.
What I have in my room is none of your business, that's all.
But...
Damn! Sometimes I wish you two would stop playing so much. It's not fun all the time. You know that, right?
I say that with more force than I intended, almost shouting it in Shiina's face. She shudders and freezes in mid-translation, and even Shizune reacts even though she hasn't heard me.
I think my angry face said everything that needs to be said.
After Shiina finishes translating, the girls look at each other with guilty faces.
Okay, Hicchan, we'll leave you alone.
It's the first time I've heard Shiina speak without the characteristic ups and downs of her voice. It feels so strange to hear, and I want to apologize, but they have already turned to leave.
As the silence settles, I regret what I said more and more.
The girls quietly leave, and after a while of standing in my room I get dressed and follow them.
Dude, whatever.
He quickly enters his lair, finally allowing me to go to class.
The hallways are as quiet as the courtyard was, naturally since everyone is in class. I lightly knock on the door of 3-3 and open it when Mutou knocks on the other side.
Sorry for being late.
Fifteen pairs of eyes turn to me.
Good morning, Nakai.
Mutou seems a little confused by my late arrival, like I've interrupted his flow or something.
Judging by the boring lectures that his classes tend to be, that may be the case.
I pass you the note that the nurse gave me. Mutou takes it with a nod and reads it quickly.
He raises his eyebrows and gives me a slightly stern look but doesn't say anything, just nods solemnly once more.
I shrug and he gestures for me to move so naturally I do.
Only two pairs of eyes keep following me as I walk to my seat.
I'm not the least bit surprised when I feel Shiina's nail poke through my shirt about fifteen seconds after I sit down.
Psst! Where were you?
fri_seq_9: It's not your business.
I know this is possibly the worst answer I can give you since it will only serve to get your attention, but I don't have the energy to come up with a more elaborate excuse right now.
However, Shiina gives up. She is unexpectedly quick to give up this day.
In a minute he's back to peck me with his finger.
Come on, tell us! Shicchan is very interested too!
I was just getting my hopes up. He only went to talk to Shizune, probably to come up with ways to make me loose my tongue.
Back up to negotiate again.
As a member of the student council, it is your duty to tell us why you are missing class! Especially if it's something very, very, very fun~!
With a demon. She doesn't know when to stop.
Well, sure. Whatever. I'll tell you. I was having a great time.
I had a heart attack first thing in the morning and then spent a few hours with the head nurse for fun.
The best morning of my life, I have to tell you.
I try to imitate his ridiculous humming while keeping my voice down so no one else can hear me. The words spit out of my mouth.
Hicchan, you had a what? Oh really?
Just forget it. You heard me.
But Hicchan, this is important!
No, seriously. Leave me alone. We're in the middle of class, too.
But Hicchan!
Shiina sounds shocked, or perhaps panicked. I wonder if she realizes herself that it wasn't the brightest of ideas to be so nosy.
I let it stew in its own juices for a few moments before responding. This won't translate to Shizune but I'm not interested.
Don't be messing around, Shiina.
And tell that to Shizune too.
As the words leave my mouth, I immediately regret saying them, but it's not like I can take them back.
To my partial surprise, Shiina actually shuts up although I don't bother to check if she passes the message on to Shizune. It doesn't matter either way.
Mutou ends his class in a generic talk about the festival in two days.
Give up. I'm not going to talk.
Is that so~?
She thinks about it for a moment.
But how greedy, Hicchan~!
I can hear the pout in her voice, disappointed and downcast.
He steps back again for the moment to negotiate with the cerebral half of the dynamic duo, before returning.
I think we should have lunch together and discuss this more… says Shicchan.
We invite.
Plus, you have to make it up to us for not being there in the morning and we need help with work~!
The other students around us start to look at us, possibly because Shiina is leaning over the desk too much, so much so that we are almost touching heads. Her curly hair brushes my neck.
It smells like shampoo and probably whatever is put in there to make it look that way.
I think the girl in front of me is trying to listen. I hope no one is getting the wrong idea about this, although I'm not quite sure how it would be possible to get any other kind of idea.
Luckily Mutou remains unconscious, or deliberately ignores Shiina. Until now.
I can't really win this one, can I?
I'm sorry, I can't. I already promised to have lunch with someone else.
Eeh? Who? Is it a girl~?
Her giggle forces me to quickly come up with something else so she doesn't get the wrong idea.
It's nothing like that! It's... a little complicated.
Complicated… yes, that is my life, despite having settled into a daily school routine.
Everything must be put into a new perspective within this second life, reconsidered from the point of view of this new self.
fri_seq_10: The me with a broken heart.
Besides, I don't know if I'll be able to come to the council after all.
Or at least for now. I have another matter to focus on first.
That's true. I must rethink my priorities. This is something that has been on my mind since the nurse gave me that lecture. I really can't afford to pretend I don't have this condition.
I'm surprised you can think so analytically, but I'll go with the flow for now.
I promise to give a proper explanation later, but not now, okay? Please tell Shizune I'm sorry to disappoint her.
If you say so, Hicchan.
She sounds surprised, and serious, I don't think I've heard Shiina like that before.
Luckily Shiina understands that I'm serious, a stroke of luck that I was able to say what I wanted so clearly that even she understood it. She steps back to translate our discussion to Shizune.
Neither of them talks to me after that.
Okay, I'll go with you, but stop bothering me for the rest of class, okay?
