You know, how she just talks talks talks about nothing for hours. It's like your head is made of bubblegum-scented bath foam jelly.
You are more or less the same, but not really. It's very helpful if you stay here.
I'm not sure if that's a compliment or not. It's probably neither; with Aiko being the largely neutral person she is.
So is there anything specific you'd like me to do to make you not think?
Just know.
So not knowing what I should do, I just sit in an empty box watching her continue painting, idly turning the pages of the book about drinking beer.
Aiko has a serene expression on her face, her dark green eyes hiding whatever she might be thinking behind them. No, wait, he's supposedly not thinking about anything, right?
He silently hums a tune, interrupting it from time to time with polite requests for more paint or another type of brush.
Her concentration is admirable, even though she seems sleep-deprived and under pressure to finish the job.
Centimeter by centimeter the painting gains more shape, details being added upon details, colors intertwining with each other, filling the empty spaces, growing one on top of the other.
I find myself thinking about inspiration and motivation to create art, again.
Where does one get ideas? They don't come out of nowhere, and I don't think there are muses that magically inject a little inspiration into your head.
Ideas have an origin and a purpose.
The more I think about it, the more convinced I am that Aiko is lying about her mural, or at least twisting the truth. Maybe she doesn't realize it herself.
You can't do anything creative without having an idea of ​​what you are going to create. That would go against the definition.
Each stroke must be decided to be drawn. Even if it is done randomly, then that, too, is a conscious decision.
So your paintings, even this one, must be based on having some deliberate goal or idea of ​​what to paint.
If Aiko's idea is to have no idea, like she said, does that count as having an idea?
A logical paradox? That seems to be Aiko's modus operandi for most of her interactions, so I wouldn't be surprised if she hasn't even noticed this herself.
I wonder if I should say it, but I'm not sure I want to engage in a logic argument with this girl.
One of us would probably end up shorting out pretty quickly, so I throw out the idea.
Aiko is squirming and shuffling, restless.
Even his usual blank countenance occasionally breaks down into rather difficult-to-interpret expressions, the kind that one simply doesn't reveal by accident.
sat_seq_9: All good?
Yes. No.
My back started to hurt again.
This painting is too big, after all, and it is difficult to paint in this position.
Do you want to take a break?
After this part is over.
She certainly doesn't take a break, and I don't bring up the topic again because that would be completely and utterly pointless.
Aiko continues her work and I stay with her: I like watching her paint, and now I'm going to be a member of the same club she is in.
When he declares the mural finished, it is already so dark that I have no idea how he can notice it.
There is no celebration, no general sense of a job well done, just a tired, laconic “I'm done” and then we both go to sleep.
I keep asking myself that same thing. The lack of something better to do, probably.
He lets out a laugh, then checks his watch.
I really must go now. Tezuka, I'm pleased to see this little project is going so well.
I just stopped by to remind you not to run away tomorrow. I've invited certain people to the festival because of you, and I'm sure they would like to meet you too.
Also, Monday's club meeting is cancelled, since I'll be out of town. I guess you can do something between yourselves, if you want.
He leaves, turning extravagantly, then walking away as dramatically as walking is possible.
What a strange teacher.
I'm leaving too. See you later, Aiko.
Raising my hand, I turn to head up the stairs to the bedrooms.
Maybe, if I can finish reading these books today, the entire day tomorrow will be free for the festival.
We need to go for more, then.
I open my mouth to say that in fact, the two of us aren't necessary for such a simple task as finding another canister of Prussian blue, but Sora has already grabbed my arm and started dragging me.
I wave my hand at Aiko, who doesn't seem to have noticed the two of us leaving.
Well, you'll notice when you go for the Prussian blue and find that it's not there yet.
Maybe.
Probably not, in fact.
While I'm busy thinking about how strange Aiko is, Sora has been dragging me back to the art room.
I feel like I'm starting to run out of breath.
What's the rush?
Hey?
Sora is giving me a questioning look, like he's trying to figure something out.
It's just that you seem to be in a hurry.
I don't think I can keep up.
Understanding dawns on his face.
You're not out of breath, are you?
There is almost a playful accusation in his tone.
I'm tempted to deny it, but then I realize that I've been breathing heavily since we stopped.
I guess it's kind of obvious.
A bit. Not everyone can be fit, you know?
There must be everything, right?
Sora frowns. It's not a particularly good pucker.
Hey, that's...
Should I… get in shape?
It's not that I haven't decided to try that yet.
After that turmoil on the track I realize that there is a real need to get some kind of running habit.
sat_seq_10: I was, after all, feeling pretty good until I had my false alarm.
Well, actually I wasn't. But it was… fun?
Meanwhile, my comment seems to help Sora come to some kind of decision.
Well, that's all then.
She gives me a serious look.
You will join me.
Excuse me, what did you say?
In the mornings.
You and I are now running buddies.
I already have a well-planned routine. In fact…
She shows a crumpled sheet of paper.
I have it right here with me.
I take the sheet of paper and give it a quick wipe.
Times, dates and returns, everything arranged.
A slow increase from just a few laps a day to…
Jeez, do you expect to have me running marathons?
And where did you find the time to put all this together?
And how long have you been planning this, anyway?
Have you been planning this?
A bit.
But it's actually the nurse's idea!
He told me to keep an eye on you to make sure you worked out just like he told you to!
A vast conspiracy?
Maybe Kenji is connected to something here...
This seems like a lot to just “keep an eye on.”
Well, to be honest I've been trying to find a morning running buddy for a while now.
Oh my God, Kenji! If only you could see the scheme revealing itself!
Why do you need a partner, anyway?
It's easier to maintain a training plan if you're not the only one doing it.
Isn't it obvious?
You're less likely to quit if someone else is counting on you to be there, right?
I see. And this will not only keep you running, but it will also ensure that I keep running too.
Which means that I will be obeying the nurse...
...and I'll be watching over you just like he asked!
You catch on quickly, Hisao.
What if I refuse?
I have no intention of refusing, of course.
But I have to put up at least symbolic resistance to that masterfully executed plan.
Well, if you refuse I'd have to pout.
And you'd have to live with being the guy who made Sora Ibarazaki pout.
You don't want that on your conscience, do you?
As if to prove it, Sora starts pouting.
It's the most adorable, heartbreaking thing I've ever seen.
Very good! I will do that!
Just…don't do that!
sun_seq_1: The next day, I wake up feeling a little dizzy. It's almost noon.
Sleeping in is fine, since it's Sunday and there are no classes.
But it is not just any Sunday, but the day of the festival as well.
From my window I can already see some people at the soba booth throwing noodles into plates for people craving low-quality food.
I swallow a handful of my morning medicine and consider how to get through the day.
There will be a few exams next week, but I don't consider them as ominous as the others, so I'm not as worried about them as I probably should be.
With no pressing obligations regarding education, you should be free to spend the day at the festival as you wish.
Finishing my morning routine, I go out to the hallway, with the intention of walking around and finding something to eat.
Passing by his door, I decide to see what Kenji has planned for today on impulse.
I'm curious if you have plans, since everyone is doing something.
On the other hand, I can imagine him building a soundproof shelter in his room.
Or possibly something like a fort, complete with a “No Girls Allowed” sign.
…and with “The Girls” crossed out and “Nobody” scrawled crudely under that.
Knocking on his door which is luckily free of any type of signal, I hear once again the disturbing click of at least ten locks being removed. The door opens just a crack.
Who is it?
You're supposed to ask that before you open the door.
Oh, it's you. Damn, it's early.
It's not really that early.
What's going on, man?
Nothing, I was going to ask you what you're doing today.
Half the school is already outside.
Outside? Because?
What?
What of what? Is today a special day? Why are they there? Who are they?
I can hear them. It's strong... don't tell me... Has the invasion started?
He suddenly looks more alarmed.
What day is it, man?
Sure, I guess you can't see the big wooden booths outside, and the people selling things...
What the hell are you talking about? I keep my curtains closed all the time to thwart snipers.
Ehh, it's the festival. You know that… Right?
Oh shit, is that today? Ah, damn. Ah… Damn. Damn.
I can't believe I forgot, I don't have my fort finished yet. This is bad.
This is going to be a really bad day… It's good that you told me this, man. This is going to be a bad day.
Because?
Oh man, they will be everywhere. The people. Outside my window. Socializing!
Kenji rubs his temples nervously, suddenly looking very sick.
It'll be loud as hell. Damn, and I was going to go outside today, but now it's ruined, everything is ruined.
This is horrible. This sucks. This sucks!
What the hell, this really sucks. Now I can't go anywhere. There is nowhere to run.
Kenji looks nervous. You could even say that he is absolutely losing control.
I can't believe this. So that's what today was.
Damn, and I couldn't even prepare for that.

I couldn't even fortify myself and now it's here and I can't do anything. You should have told me this before, boy. I mean, at least, I know, but… I could have known sooner! Imagine what he could have achieved...
I'm sorry. I thought you knew.
So I take it you're not doing anything today?
sun_seq_2: Even the weather is good. Yesterday was very windy, so I thought today would be cold. However it's not, so there's no reason to just stay inside. You should definitely check out the festival.
Kenji growls and covers his face with his hands.
Ugh, no, no! I can't do it. They'll eat me alive out there, I know it.
That has to be a joke, but he said it with such a serious expression. Relatively serious.
What are you going to do? We should hang out here, you can help me build my fort. We could still make it in time if we work together.
I'm going to have to hang out with the student council, since I lost a bet.
I realize that we don't agree on when and where. I'll just wait for them rather than risk not meeting each other in the chaos outside. They must be busy running around and organizing things, anyway.

It's funny. He would have assumed that the price of losing to Shizune in her stupid game would be much more severe. This is just an excuse to spend time with her. In that case, I guess she just wants me to have fun.
Even if she can't reach out and make her intentions clear, they might be good intentions after all, and I think I'm starting to like her more.
I could skip going, but it would be a waste. And I also want to go. I mean, you know, today looks very exciting. More than anything, it will be interesting.
The student council? That? Does that still exist?
Isn't that like, two guys?
They are both girls.
Oh really? Are they cute? Damn no, wait… are they cute?
No! It doesn't matter! I heard that the student council president is insane... that whoever she is never speaks and only gives orders through lackeys.
Shit, they're the same in every school... She sounds like a heartless bitch. Bitches everywhere.
If there are two girls, they outnumber you two to one. That's a dangerous situation, kid. Who knows what could happen.
Damn, the student council is only two women, but they have too much power.
They must be stopped.
I can see them, plotting ways to force their feminist plans. I can't trust an administration like that.
This is not good. Not good!
Curse. Shit! Curse!
Don't know. I'm pretty hungry so I thought I'd go get some food first and then wander around the attractions.
Your class project looked really good, and I had a hand with it so I want to at least see that one and talk to Elena I guess.
Speaking of which, don't you have any obligation to the project?
Are you sick in the head?
That blind girl is up to no good; I can feel it in my spleen, man. His presence is like a dark shadow that stands in the way of my great vision.
As expected of blind people.
That.
Besides, I thought you were too...
He raises his hand to interrupt me.
Only legally.
Metaphorically, I can see further than any man before me has seen.

Kenji stares stoically into the metaphorical distance to emphasize his statement, jutting his chin confidently to appear more masculine. In fact it's just the corridor wall two meters away but it doesn't matter.
I can see the future of the human race, and it is a dark one unless the threat of women is quelled.
They are everywhere.
Well, I joined the art club so I guess I'll go with them.
You did what?
I joined the art club.
Man, that was a bad move. Really bad. You don't know what kind of girls are in the art club. Disturbed and anguished beauties that rip out your heart and eat it raw.
Well, I know a member of the art club, and I really don't see Aiko suddenly turning into a psychopathic killer.
That seems unlikely.
Don't say that. Don't fool yourself. You have no idea what you're dealing with here, man. They are the worst type.
They drag you in with this pseudo-intellectual shit and when you least expect it, BAM!
Bam what?
sun_seq_3: Kenji seems slightly taken aback by my skepticism, but no less shaken.
It doesn't matter.
Be careful man, be careful.
I wonder... I'm a little hungry, but I made this deal that I would try to take better care of myself. Be healthier, you know.
I don't know if I should avoid takoyaki completely, or head straight for it.
Deal? It sounds ominous. So what will you be getting in return?
Nothing, I guess? It's not that kind of deal.
Do you know Sora, from our generation? We agreed to something like watching each other's backs and...
Aeeeeeeee!
The shrill scream and the expression of abject terror on Kenji's face chill my blood. It's like I told a Catholic priest that I sold my soul to the devil.
She! You sold your soul to the devil, and you got nothing in return?
What the hell is wrong with you, man?
Do you know who you're dealing with?
She is a danger to public health. Do you know how many people he sends to the hospital monthly with his carefully placed flying tackles?
It's one of them! A key player in the vast conspiracy that aims for the complete submission of all things manly.
I can't believe what I'm hearing. I trusted your judgment, man. I thought we were brothers.
You have to cancel before it's too late.
This festival too; It's just one of their ploys.
He fumbles with his scarf nervously, faster and faster as if he were trying to start a fire, then slowly begins to calm down once the panic attack runs its course.
I'm going to have to find somewhere to hide, a safe haven. And then knock myself out so I wouldn't have to experience this horrible day.
I have the perfect thing for that. Now I must prepare.
Don't go to the festival.
Alright.
See you later, friend.
The door slowly closes with a soft squeak and I don't know how to feel about what Kenji just said.
I consider what I want to do with Shizune and Shiina. Deciding it's best to be extra prepared, I sneak to my room to stock my wallet with money.
I wonder if they have that game where you try to catch goldfish in a paper net?
It seems to be much easier than they make it seem. On the other hand, if I were to catch a goldfish, I'd have no real reason to keep it.
What am I going to do with a fish in my tiny room? Cook it?
I could give it to Shizune or Shiina, but that might be crossing the line.

It's a real problem. They're both cute, but I don't think I'll have a chance with either of them. Despite everything, I consider the idea of ​​doing it. I imagine how they might react if I gave them a gift tonight, like a fish or a doll.
Shiina would probably laugh like she always does. Shizune could knock him away from my hand.
Maybe it's not such a good idea after all.
Okay, I think I'm ready.
A long while later, I decide that this might be another nerve-racking test devised by Shizune. Even if it isn't, it's starting to get a little late.
I decide to go outside and look for them, even though I don't know where I could check. They might be really hard to find today.
As soon as I take a step outside, I almost collide with Shizune.
Hello, Shizune. Where is Shiina?
I try to sign it as best I can, but really I'm just making it up. I have to ask Shiina to teach me some of this.
Here!
Shiina appears from behind Shizune, smiling widely.
We're just here to make sure you'll come with us to the festival.
Don't give up on your promise~!
Promise? I don't think I promised anything.
Stop trying to get out of this!
sun_seq_4: Come on, Hicchan, it'll be fun! You need this, anyway, or you'll become good for nothing!
You don't want to become one of those people who just stays in their room all day, being paranoid, do you?
I find myself casting a glance over his shoulders at the door to Kenji's room across from mine.
I hope she hasn't heard that, but I think Shiina wants the opposite.
No, of course not. I was just joking a little, and I was about to leave anyway. You two had no business coming here.
Actually? Ahahaha! Shicchan was worried that you would try to get out of this somehow!
We need you, Hicchan~!
Hey?
I think my heart just stopped for a moment.
I don't have the skills to throw the dolls of their bases in that game... and Shicchan refuses to throw things.
Shizune looks at me, immediately noticing my disappointment. She uncrosses her arms and adjusts her glasses.
What did you think we were referring to? I refuse to throw anything.
Why, Shicchan? That's weird...
Well, anyway, Hicchan, you've thrown a ball before, right~, right~? So! You have to come with us!
I am surprised by your logic. I don't know if they're joking or not.
Heh, I'd be offended if I didn't know they were joking.
They're joking, right?
It is what it is, Hicchan~! It is what it is what it is what it is what it is!
Well, that's comforting.
Come on, let's go! The deaf band is getting ready outside your window.
Shiina grabs my hand and tries to pull me out of the door, but it's clear she's not trying at all.
Shizune looks at us both, blushing slightly and fiddling with her glasses impatiently.
I'm not used to this kind of casual contact, but I have nothing against him. How could I refuse?
It's still light outside, but the Sun is getting ready to set behind the trees.
It seems like half the school is out there, and I can even see some faculty members standing off to the side, pouring themselves some punch.
They are about to empty the entire container, much to the dismay of the girl working the stall.
There are some fortune tellers casually talking to their friends, while others have already started throwing horoscopes at anyone who walks within reach.
I think that kind of tactic is a little too aggressive, but it shows that they're into it. It refreshes you to see that, but I don't know if I'll be able to get used to it.
Well, we should get something to eat. Hungry, Hicchan?
Now that I think about it, I haven't eaten all day.
I don't really want to eat fried noodles.
Don't worry, there are other fried foods!
Is there any food that is not fried?
Sweets. Junk food is the essence of celebrations!
Wahahahaha!
Come on, I—I mean, Shicchan—will treat you to something~!
A?
Just one~! Just so you can build up energy for your throwing arm!
Oh, but it looks like not all the booths have finished being set up, so you might not be able to get what you want.
I look around, surprised by the number of stalls. It's incredible, this festival seems bigger than the ones you could actually see in the towns.
Despite what Shiina said, it seems like half the school is already celebrating.
The animated chatter of at least half of the student body resonates in the air.
I can smell food cooking, and that's only making me hungrier by the second.
Come on, Hicchan, the food is already disappearing fast! If you want takoyaki, we need to move now!
I would like some takoyaki~! Come on, let's eat that!
sun_seq_5: It's okay, I haven't had takoyaki in a long time. I join.
Shizune leaves before Shiina can translate that to her, walking briskly towards the takoyaki stand as Shiina and I try to catch up with her.
Shiina laughs as she skips over to Shizune, who orders three orders of takoyaki by holding up three fingers.
I never noticed it before, but for someone who's obsessed with high-end tea, it's a little strange that Shizune is also so into fast food.
I take the plate of takoyaki from him and wonder if I should start eating. It looks extremely hot.
I can see the smoke coming out of there and the oil bubbling on the surface.
Shizune and Shiina look at me, as if waiting for me to eat before they can start.
I can't back down, so I stick one on the tiny fork protruding nonchalantly from the corner of the plate.
However, before I can even put it in my mouth, Shizune and Shiina eagerly begin eating, Shizune taking quick but delicate bites of her takoyaki while Shiina eats with delight like a small child.
I think at the end of the day, they're both just girls like every other student here.
This is nice. I don't think I've had an opportunity like this in a long time to just hang out with other people and enjoy their company.
Even before coming here, I've been going through a very busy year. So busy that I didn't even realize what I was missing until now.
Here, I feel at peace.
This is a relaxing atmosphere. I didn't know these types of festivals still existed.
Hey? Hicchan, aren't you going to eat your food?
No, yes I will eat it.
I hope you're not chickening out just because it's too hot.
It's not that.
Even his teasing is starting to become charming.
I eat quickly before my food can cool, thinking that the dimly lit paper lanterns glowing warmly against the sunset make this a beautiful sight.
Before I can finish my last bite of takoyaki, Shizune stands in front of me, standing perfectly upright with her arms rigidly behind her back.
I can see that she is trying her best to look as serious as possible, but even she can't hide her good mood, as there is a slight smile on her face.
Ahahaha~! Come on, Hicchan, let's play some games!
Have you finished putting them together?
No, but it doesn't matter, it doesn't matter~! Come on, Hicchan, before it gets crowded!
Shiina puts her hand on my shoulder and laughs very loudly.
Come on! Come on! The awards really look great this year, really, really~! Wouldn't you like to win some prizes for two cute girls like us?
Shiina gives her best “cute” look, which is certainly pretty cute. I look at Shizune, expecting her to do the same, but she just looks at me like I'm crazy.
Shiina, stop doing that!
Wait... I'm Shiina...
Hicchan, hurry up, you've been holding that piece of takoyaki for like a thousand years!
Ha ha ha!
I like to taste everything I eat. Even this.
Without warning, Shizune steals the takoyaki from my hand and quickly pours it into her mouth with a smile.
It happens so fast that there is no way I could have stopped it.
Before I can even fully understand what just happened, Shiina bursts into laughter, and Shizune smiles at me, probably the closest I've ever seen her come to laughing.
Well, this solves that~! Wow! Hahaha!
Shizune takes my right hand, and Shiina takes my left.
You will come with us! There's a lot to do tonight, you should try harder to enjoy it!
Hahahaha~!
Running through an already sizable crowd, we played game after game, ring toss, whack-a-mole, and games I've never heard of.
We rarely win, but it's fun nonetheless.
Hey, do they have that goldfish catching game here?
Of course! I didn't know you liked that game, Hicchan!
Well, I've always wanted to try it. It doesn't seem very difficult.
sun_seq_6: Are you sure about that, Hicchan~?
Wahahaha~! Okay, okay! We'll see! It must be around here somewhere!
But where are you going to keep your fish? Do you have a container for it?
Well, no...
Maybe he'll eat it!
Hahahahahaha! Ahahahahaha!!
It's okay, Hicchan, if we win any fish, we'll give them to you!
Oh really? Another game? Well then.
Shizune cheerfully pushes me towards the booth, trying to hide her excitement in her eyes.
Fortunately, neither of them manages to catch a single fish, although I don't do any better.
I can't help but laugh as they immediately begin to pull me towards a particularly long and colorful stall I helped build.
I remember this one; It had been a real martyrdom to do it.
The booth attendant, a plain-looking guy with dyed brown hair, breaks his lethargy when he sees us walking toward him. I notice two things:
First, it's one of those games where you throw a ball into a pyramid of opaque pots and try to throw as many as possible.
Four balls for 50 yen, that's very good.
Second, there are instructions on how to play in braille. I almost want to say something, and see if Shizune and Shiina see it too.
Either they don't see it, or they don't find it strange at all.
Hey! It's good to see you, Hakamichi! Thank you very much for your help with this booth. Having fun?
Shizune glances over at Shiina, who translates everything for her in a flash, and then smiles at the operator.
Haha~! It was nothing, nothing at all, really~! Without a doubt, this is great, I think the best festival we have put together so far!
Shiraki, we would like to play this, okay, right?
Of course~, it would be really great if you would just give your pretty, hard-working student council representatives an award, for all the hours we put in to make all this possible!
Hahaha, haha… No.
If Shiraki has anything, it's eggs.
Hey, I built this stand, and it was backbreaking work, too. I wasted two hours of my life, I think I deserve at least one free round.
Me too!
Me too!
After some hesitation, he eventually relents, handing us four balls each with a shrug.
Barely a second later, Shizune and Shiina release their balls in front of me.
And now what?
Don't tell me that after making such a fuss about this, you guys aren't even going to play?
Not after the way we teamed up against Shiraki.
You stay out of this please~!
Shizune turns to me and starts shaking her hand dismissively. Shiina seems torn between translating for herself and comforting the booth operator.
Ahahaha! Hicchan, where is your sense of chivalry? Also, I... Shicchan, has a policy against throwing balls!
Ah, sorry, Hicchan. I don't know if my aim is that good, either. However, you must be very good at these things, right, right? It shouldn't be a problem for you!
This looks simple enough. The boats aren't even that far away, the only challenge is that these are ultralight balls.
I throw one hard at the boats, and it bounces unceremoniously.
What the devil?
Oh yeah, it's not as easy as it seems. There is water inside the boats. Trade secret.
That's not very fair!
This must be why it's four balls for 50 yen. How clever.
Come on, Hicchan, you can throw them away! You have eleven more chances! Go!
Maybe you guys should do it.
Shizune? Do you want to try?
sun_seq_7: Shizune shakes her head emphatically from side to side.
I laugh, this is actually very funny.
Positioning myself, I throw another ball at the pyramid of boats and manage to make them move just a little.
Both Shizune and Shiina are casting longing glances at a cat-shaped doll.
After all, they are not so different.
Sometimes I wonder if Shizune would sound like Shiina if she could talk.
No, they are not that similar.
I throw another ball, realizing that it's actually quite simple. If I can hit two pots in the bottom column at the same time, it's an easy win.
A small crowd is already starting to form, so there's really pressure on me. Nine more shots.
Preparing like a baseball pitcher, I throw as hard as I can and the bounces come crashing down.
Triumphantly, I ask for my girly cat doll prize and Shiina laughs out loud as if she were the one who won it.
Shizune looks at me with her usual blank expression. It's clear that she wants the doll too.
Hicchan, congratulations~! What are you going to do with that doll?
There is no correct answer. I have to negotiate carefully.
I... I don't know.
Ok~ I'll take it, if you don't want it...
Unless you want to keep it to yourself, Hicchan. I didn't know you liked dolls. How delicate.
I don't like them. I have no use for this.
Can I have it then?
His eyes are piercing into my soul.
This is a decision I don't want to make. I turn again toward the booth.
Hey, do you have another one of these dolls?
Actually, yes, just one more.
Okay, prepare everything again, I want to try to get that one out too.
I still have eight attempts.
As soon as the game is set up again, I throw as hard as I can once again, but miss.
Ha ha ha! Trying to win another one? Taking the easy way out, Hicchan?
If it's that easy, you could try.
No thanks~!
Tell me, Hicchan, can you at least let go of the doll while you throw the balls?
There's only one more left, you better make it! If you fail, I will kill you~!
But what a clever way to get away from giving me the doll! And by me, I mean me~!
Ahahahaha~! Just kidding!
I can see that Shiina wasn't planning any harm with that, and Shizune seems to enjoy her joke, smiling at her, but a moment later she looks a little depressed.
I decide to give him the doll, at least while I'm trying to win the other one. It's kind of hard to aim while holding a giant cat.
Thanks, Hicchan. Shicchan looks happy, Hicchan~! But, you're going to win one for me too, right?
That's what I'm trying to do, isn't it?
I shoot again, but my aim is too bad this time.
My arm feels a little heavy too, like the blood isn't flowing properly to it.
I mentally scold myself, thinking that it's pathetic that I could have gotten tired of something like that.
Then I realize that maybe it's because of my heart. If it is, then I don't know what to think.
It's depressing that even something as small as this is enough to make me realize my own mortality.
I guess there will never be a time when I can forget about it.
Even today, when I thought I could just enjoy myself, on this beautiful night and in this beautiful place, I can't escape the reason why I am here.
I have never felt so at peace in my life, in this place that is unlike any I have ever been to.
sun_seq_8: It's hard now to avoid thinking the unthinkable:
That maybe he was sent here to die.
These past few days have been some of the best of my life. The first time in a long time that I have felt truly alive.
But in the end, I am someone who finds myself reminded at every moment that if I climb too many stairs or throw a ball too hard I could die at any second.
I will always be limited by this.
I feel depressed about it, and also angry. In the end, I care about my life, and I enjoy it, and it's more fleeting now than it's ever been.
I wonder what will finally finish me off. It could be anything, if I'm this weak and pathetic: a bad fall, a blow to the chest, a stray baseball.
Now I have lost my will to keep playing this game, but I keep playing anyway.
Suddenly, I feel a fleeting sensation of pain in my chest. It comes and goes instantly, but it's enough to trip me up just a little.
Shizune jumps back, startled. He approaches, looking at me with concern. Shiina puts her hand on my shoulder.
Hey, Hicchan, are you okay?
Yes, nothing happens. I'm really not feeling very well right now. I think I'm sick. I don't think I can continue.
Shiina frowns.
Don't put pressure on yourself. If you are that sick, you will only get sicker.
Look, the festival is just starting, and we've been playing games for a while. We can take a short break if you're tired.
Good idea Shicchan, I'm feeling a little tired too! I think we're all a little worn out, running around the school, Hicchan!
I nod. They don't seem to notice anything unusual. That's good.
We walk through the sea of ​​people, with Shiina gamely pointing at the faces of everyone she meets. Shizune holds the stuffed cat in her arms, cradling it unconsciously. They seem to be having fun.
Suddenly, I feel a hit of guilt.
Due to my poor health, we all had to stop.
Hicchan, we're both a little hungry. What about you?
I'm not as hungry as I could be, but I do want something to eat.
That's more than enough, Hicchan~! So what should we get to eat?
I don't really care.
Ah! How about sandwiches, then? And we'll need something to drink too! Shiina will get everything!
What?
Shizune looks at me and smiles, and I realize that she might be trying to cheer me up with a joke. I laugh.
Hicchan, it's getting a little crowded, so maybe we won't be able to eat here. It's also getting a bit rowdy.
Maybe we should go eat up on the roof.
It's fine with me. It might be a good view, and there might be a bit of a breeze.
Then it's okay! I guess I should go get the food and drinks now… So I'll see you guys later~!
Shiina awkwardly waves her hand and then runs away.
Before, I didn't notice how the paper lanterns look like illuminating the dark night, but now that I can see it, it is really an amazing sight.
Fireflies float overhead, their soft glow making it appear as if they are snowing lights in the night sky.
This kind of thing would be impossible to see in the city.
Shizune tugs on my sleeve impatiently and crosses her arms, frowning as if to show displeasure at me for distracting her.
You know, I don't know how to read sign language.
Now that I think about it, isn't it kind of stupid of me to have said that to a deaf person? I couldn't have listened.
I shrug, hoping to show him that I don't understand. Shizune shakes her head and dismisses him with a wave of her hand.
Maybe I should make the time to ask Shiina for some sign language lessons.
Climbing up to the roof, I find myself again amazed at the enormous size of this school. The grounds are so vast I can't believe I didn't realize it before.
As I make my way across the rooftop, walking behind Shizune, I can't help but be awed by the stars shining in the sky.
Shizune and I sat on a bench. She seems to be in a good mood as she smiles softly as a breeze blows through her hair.
We look down at the festival, which looks like a sea of ​​glowing amber lanterns and waving paper fans packed with people, some of them festively dressed in yukatas.
In fact, most of the girls seem to be wearing yukatas. I wonder why Shizune and Shiina didn't dress up like this today.
sun_seq_9: They would both look good in yukata. I briefly think about the guys they would wear.
Shizune would probably go with something traditional. However, Shiina's thing is a little harder to guess.
Shiina arrives, out of breath from running towards us, trying to keep the food in her arms from falling.
Arranging everything on the floor, she falls back.
Ahahahahahahahaha~! That took a while! Come on, you two didn't tell me what you wanted, so I brought some rice punch, some sandwiches, and some candy too! A little bit of everything!
That's great. Well, let's eat.
Shiina takes a bite of a small triangular sandwich.
So Hicchan, what do you think of the festival? It's nice, isn't it?
Sure.
The stars look good today. This couldn't have been a more perfect day.
The sound of people talking below us is like soft music along with the chirping of crickets in the distance.
I take a sip from the punch can and look at Shiina, who looks like she's sleeping comfortably with her back extended and a half-full can of apple juice balanced on her stomach.
Shizune sits with her legs drawn close to her, rocking back and forth slowly like an impatient child as she looks up at the sky.
They are both quite cute. I look around and I can see many students holding hands with their girlfriends or boyfriends.
Not far from us on this roof, there are couples looking up at the stars or down at the festival lights, holding hands.
Part of me wants that.
Looking at Shizune and Shiina, I wonder if I should ask one of them out one day. I wonder if it would be worth the risk.
The golden hands moving across the face of the delicate watch on Shizune's wrist catch my attention, and I see that it's getting a little late. But the festivities are still in all their splendor.
Shizune is still holding the stuffed cat I won by the paw. She notices me looking at him.
Indifferently, he offers it to me. I smile, wanting to ask her what I would do with him, but she couldn't understand me.
I shake my head and try my best to tell him to keep it, hoping he understands.
As I look towards the school, I can see many people before me, all of whom are happy and cheerful.
Looking at them makes me feel happy.
This really was something special. Today it was worth it.
But I still can't shake off the feelings of guilt and melancholy from before, they keep clinging to me, and I can't let them go.
Shizune makes some signs to me, and I can't understand her. No matter what I say, you won't be able to hear me.
I can't understand you, Shizune.
Well, whatever. I wonder if we both consider ourselves guilty for this. Anyway, I apologize for not being able to understand you.
You know, I'm almost, almost happy that you tried to make me come here. However, if I try to date you, I may have to think more about that side of you.
No, actually… I'm happy. Today was nice.
You would be prettier if you smiled more, you have a nice smile.
Frustrated, she stands up, arms behind her back, looking authoritative and confident against the backdrop of stars.
Suddenly, Shizune throws her arms towards the open sky, appearing to grab it in her hands.
It's like he's telling me to look at everything in front of me:
The school, bathed in the glow of the festival and illuminated with the colorful yukatas, the roof illuminated by fireflies, the sky so vast that it imposes that feeling of admiration on you.
What do you want? I slowly realize it over time. This beautiful scene before me is proof that there are things wonderful enough that ruining them with a bad mood is unforgivable.
And I can feel the weight of Shizune's personality accentuating the idea.
Thanks, I guess.
I look away, but then Shizune grabs me by the shoulder, her watch brushing against my cheek.
With her left hand, she points to the sky.
With faint pops, fireworks begin to explode in the sky, each spreading a bath of brilliant colors that slowly dissolve into the darkness.
I can't even fully remember the last time I saw fireworks, much less such a grand display. Not to mention that they are apparently being launched from the school; It's almost impossible to believe.
The lights in the sky blend with a second salvo from the town below, and seem timed to complement each other like two parts in a duet.
They continue for maybe fifteen more minutes, and then they stop.
Shizune notices that her hand is still on my shoulder and carefully removes it, looking a little uncomfortable.
sun_seq_10: Regaining his composure, he smiles, hands on his hips and chest puffed out.
It is in these moments that she looks more like a normal teenage girl. Full of energy, happy, and carefree.
I remain thoughtful as I eat with Shizune, both of us silently watching the crowds below gradually disperse.
She sits leaning forward slightly, her chin resting gently in her hands and a satisfied look on her face with just a hint of melancholy.
At all times still gently holding the stuffed cat.
I start to feel tired and tell her that I'll see her and Shiina tomorrow, not even realizing that she can't hear me, and then I start walking back to the dorms.
I feel warm and alive, even in this cold night air.
The image of Shizune standing energetically before the stars, denying me my self-pity, does not escape my mind easily.
If…if it only takes a moment for love to exist, I think I might be falling in love with her.
Just a little bit.
It's a little unsettling, and now I'm starting to feel insecure.
Should I bother going?
I have a book that I have wanted to read.
Something about a clandestine postal service that may or may not exist.
It's short, too. I could have it finished in a day.
But would that be a good way to spend my time?
Well, yes. It definitely would be.
But I guess it would probably be a better idea to go outside.
See the festival.
Trying to fit in with all the other side attractions.
Honestly, I should at least make an attempt to maintain the somewhat affable personality I've had this past week.
Maybe go eat something, my stomach suggests.
It's almost lunch time... I could at least get something from one of the stalls outside.
Soon I'm outside, surrounded by several students and people who may or may not be their parents.
Every so often I catch a glimpse of someone who clearly came from town simply for the promise of a festival.
They are easy to identify.
Those who can't stop looking, and behind their eyes you can see that they are thinking "Well, what's wrong with this one here?"
It almost makes me want to yell at them.
But at the same time, can I deny that I've been doing the same thing all week?
A wave of something like disgust covers me completely; a sense of guilt for my own intolerance.
I push those thoughts aside, focusing on the pangs of hunger that burn my gut like a wildfire.
The aroma of something fried takes me to the promised land, where I can get something for lunch.
I'm barely asking for my order when a loud voice interrupts me.
Hey, what the hell are you doing?
Buying breakfast—uh, ah, lunch.
Breakfast?
Do you mean you just got up?
Suddenly sleeping through the morning feels like a crime.
No, I meant lunch…seriously.
You're not believing it.
Lunch?
That's not a healthy breakfast at all!
He rips the food out of my hands and gives me a fierce look.
What the hell is this girl doing?
Hey, that's my breakfast!
mystery_prelude: The sunset turned the clouds over Yamaku a bloody purple.
I was alone in the middle of the deserted courtyard. The bustle of preparations for the school festival had completely ceased.
And then... something happened that made my blood run cold.
The deafening chorus of thousands of cicadas died away in a split second. Zero sound. Zero vibration.
Why...why did they suddenly become silent? They never turn off all at once...
A rustle of dry leaves sounded behind me. I turned around with my heart pounding.
There was no one... Only a long shadow that dissolved between the trees on the hill towards the lighthouse.
Kenji's file... 'The year the cicadas fell silent, Keiko disappeared on the hill.'
act2_branching_crossroad: Night fell quickly on the hill. The sea breeze carried a thick smell of storm and saltpeter.
I had Kenji's file burning in my hands and the certainty that something sinister was threatening the girls' safety during the festival.
Where should I go before the storm reaches the academy?
sora_seq_1: The beeping of my alarm shatters the silence of the early morning, and I wonder where I get the motivation to get up.
There's still a while before school, but I agreed to run with Sora in the mornings.
The truth is, running doesn't interest me much as a hobby, or even as an exercise that could possibly lengthen my life.
However, I feel obligated to fulfill what I promised Sora yesterday, and that is why I am putting on shorts and a light t-shirt.
The cold morning air caresses my face as the sun's rays cause the dew on the grass to sparkle, almost blinding me at first.
As I head toward the track, an unpleasant thought strikes me.
What if this is all some kind of prank by Sora?
Would I really be surprised?
Hell, I'd probably do it to the new guy too.
At the very least, I'm sure Sora and Aiko took bets on whether I would actually show up or not.
I feel some trepidation as the track comes into view.
You're late!
It seems that Sora is already here. What a relief.
Not according to my watch. We both arrived early, in fact.
Curse. You caught me.
Sora is sitting in the stands, dressed in her running clothes, waiting for me with some patience.
I'm glad you're really here. I was afraid this was a joke or something.
Nah, I would never make someone get up early for anything.
Besides, Aiko now owes me 500 yen. She didn't think you'd really come.
I knew it!
It's good to know that Sora was on my side, at least.
Sora jumps off the stands and starts stretching.
She is remarkably agile, almost like a dancer.
I also prepare to stretch, but then I realize that I don't remember exactly how to do it properly.
It's been years since I've had to stretch for something, if you don't count my lame attempt at running last week.
And actually I think I didn't stretch beforehand that time either.
The specter of my long hospital stay looms large again.
Although I can't say I was very active before the hospital stay, so maybe I'm just feeling melancholy.
Sora giggles as he watches me stretch.
No no no Hisao, you must hold on longer!
I try! It hurts a little bit.
Ha! That's because you're not in shape. You should gain some flexibility, like this.
To demonstrate, Sora crouches down and places his head between her legs.
God bless you, Sora.
I see. Should I strive for those kinds of things?
Of course! Flexibility is important for any athlete. The more you stretch, the faster you can run.
That doesn't make any sense to me, but Sora seems to think it's true.
With Sora's help, I manage to stretch properly.
I can't help but notice that when she thinks about how to explain things to me, her mouth purses in concentration.
It's adorable.
Not bad, Hisao. Come on, we better start running.
We'll start with just a mile, okay?
That's four laps around the track, got it?
Sounds good.
It shouldn't be too difficult, right?
sora_seq_2: A vague memory of having run the same thing in gym class emerges in my head.
Yeah, it wasn't that bad.
Sora sets a good pace, and I position myself behind her.
Try to follow me, okay, Hisao?
Copied.
We completed the first turn without incident, although I can already feel my heart rate rise slightly.
As I passed the second bend, I started breathing through my mouth.
Sora doesn't seem to have a single drop of sweat.
As if to punctuate his superiority, he turns around and begins to run backwards.
Are you okay, Hisao?
Never…better.
Oh really? In that case maybe I should increase the speed, huh?
Oh…no,…you shouldn't…
… demand… too much… of you.
The heaviness of my gasps and exhales makes the sentence sound less convincing than I expected. Sora just smiles and turns around again.
You rule, Hisao. We will maintain this pace.
I have the feeling that they are making fun of me.
If I weren't in such terrible shape, I'd probably be offended.
By the third lap, my breathing is based on irregular gasps.
I'm also covered in my own sweat. Disgusting.
We close the turn to start the fourth lap, and Sora looks back, smiling at me.
Here we go!
She zooms off at blinding speed while I stubbornly stick to my pace.
By the time I reach the first turn, she is already finishing the second.
As I struggle on the other side of the track, Sora continues running and catches up to me.
Come on, Hisao! You can do it!
I would answer him, but I'm too focused on getting air into my lungs and ignoring the burning in the muscles in my legs.
Part of me wants to say something like, “Maybe you can, but I'm about to die.”
On the other hand, I doubt I can form any words right now.
Sora keeps up with me as I make my way around the second corner and cross the finish line.
That sprint seems to have made her sweat.
It has actually caused his shirt to become slightly transparent. She is apparently wearing a black sports bra.
I feel a slight twinge of guilt for being the kind of guy who looks at a girl's chest, but my chest and legs burn so much that I can't care less about it.
Not bad for a first try, Hisao.
So— …very kind… of you… to say that.
Sora doesn't seem exhausted, but at least she's breathing heavier than before we started running.
It must be the sprint's fault.
Hey, I gotta run a little more. You should walk around the track to relax.
Then we can stretch, and we'll be done, okay?
Sounds great.
My legs are on fire, and I'm still breathing hard, but amazingly my heart seems to be taking the strain well.
Another triumph of medical sciences, I suppose.
You should put your arms behind your head. Makes it easier to catch your breath.
Surprisingly, he is right. I begin to stroll along the track, happy to feel myself catch my breath.
I see something blurry as Sora runs past me.
sora_seq_3: Watching her run is absolutely fascinating.
It's not just because he wears prosthetics, although that's interesting.
The most interesting thing is the way his face changes.
I can't help but glimpse it as she runs, but her eyes seem to come to life with a kind of ferocious joy.
It's like there's nothing else in the world except her and the track.
By the time I've reached the final stretch, Sora seems to have finished his sprints.
He's breathing heavily now, but he has a satisfied smile on his face. She beckons to me happily as I approach her.
You feel better, right?
In fact, yes.
Do you want to take another ride with me? I also have to cool down a little, you know.
Part of me would rather sit down and not move, but something tells me that would be a bad idea.
Plus, if I sit down, I might never get up again.
Sure, why not?
Now Sora also has her hands behind her head, which makes her look quite relaxed.
And the positioning of his arms lifts his shirt enough so that I can see a small sliver of his belly.
I try hard to act like a gentleman and not stare, but the contrast of his skin against the red shorts is quite striking.
So how do you feel, Hisao?
Surprisingly well, actually. I'm sore and tired, but...surprisingly fine.
As soon as I say it, I realize it's true.
Sure, part of me wants to drop to the ground and die, but I feel like I've accomplished something.
It's almost like a glow throughout my body that persists despite the pain.
Yes, it's runner's high.
Runner's high?
Yes, it has something to do with… adrenaline?
Sora thinks for a moment as we walk, trying to remember.
Then he shrugs and smiles at me.
I actually don't remember it. It's a nice feeling though, right?
Better than sex, right?
I open my mouth to respond just before I process what he just said.
Sora looks at my face for a few moments before letting out a laugh.
Sorry, sorry! I couldn't resist it! You're too easy!
Why did I agree to run with you again?
Sora only laughs harder. She grabs my forearm and tilts it, allowing her a better look at my watch. His face changes the moment he sees the time.
Oh no! We better hurry, Hisao!
Classes start in an hour, and I need to shower!
Maybe I should do it too...
I also have to see the nurse... Maybe he'll write me a note for being late!
Why do you need to see the nurse?
Sora points to his prosthetics, as if that explains everything.
It is important to check for irritation.
You know, from sweat or friction, or whatever.
Normally I only go after practice, but if we're going to be doing these races in the mornings I guess I'll see him twice a day.
Wait, so Sora started these races when I showed up?
If it is more convenient for you to run with me later…
Don't be stupid! I've wanted to start running in the mornings for a while now.
sora_seq_4: But if I didn't have a partner to do it with, it would be harder to maintain a routine.
It's always harder to walk away from a commitment if you're letting someone else down, you know?
So you will be my companion during the mornings!
We both need exercise, so it all fits together, don't you think?
Yes, perfect.
Although, did it have to be me?
Well, I guess I can't complain too much. Sora is quite fun to be with.
And he is right. Yes I need exercise. Doctor's orders, even.
Sora quickly says goodbye.
Okay, I'm leaving! Come have lunch with us, okay?
What?
Lunch! You know, the food? In the middle of the day? Come with us!
Where?
On the roof Aiko likes it up there.
When?
At lunchtime, when else? That was a stupid question.
Yes, but in some ways I felt like I needed to ask all three questions so as not to leave any loose ends.
Sora lets out a laugh, and then smiles. I don't think I've ever seen a girl smile so much before.
Not bad, Hisao. See you soon!
And with that, he takes off running like a bullet towards the school building.
I guess you'll visit the nurse first.
I rush back to my room and jump into the shower, only to find that the water takes a moment to warm up.
The shock of the freezing water almost killed me.
I manage to warm up the water a little and have a good time feeling my muscles relax.
My heart, amazingly, is the least affected by the race.
I guess that's a good thing, even if it makes me feel a little wimpy.
I mean, at least I'd have an excuse besides “I'm not in shape” if my heart was bothering me.
I guess I'll just have to get on with this racing thing, otherwise I'm sure Sora wouldn't forgive me.
It's not until I get out and dry off that I realize I only have ten minutes left to put on my clothes and go to class.
Shit.
The hands of the clock finally free me from the tedium of another class more full of fun.
Getting up from my seat turns out to be more of a problem than I anticipated.
My legs are killing me from the morning run.
Maybe doing the races with Sora isn't such an encouraging idea after all.
However, the race has given me a hell of an appetite.
I'm halfway to the cafeteria when I remember that I have my lunch with me.
My parents saw fit to provide me with some pre-packaged things when I moved, and it was a good thing.
The hallway is full of students heading to the cafeteria.
Walking back is like swimming against the current, but I have an appointment to keep on the roof.
It takes me a while to find the stairs that lead to the roof, although I'd bet that Sora and Aiko aren't up there yet.
In fact, I think I saw Sora in the hallway, among the people walking towards the cafeteria.
I go out the door that leads to the roof and take a deep breath.
The cool air blowing against my face almost makes my legs hurt less.
Maybe if I get on my head...
Part of me wants to be surprised that Aiko is already here.
sora_seq_5: What will you achieve with that?
Things in the clouds.
Can't you just... see them normally?
Aiko rolls her eyes in something approaching exasperation.
Then I wouldn't have a new perspective.
And does being upside down really give you a new perspective?
Aha! That took her by surprise. Aiko looks thoughtful.
Maybe you're right. Maybe from the side.
As Aiko lies down on the bench to look up at the sky, I give up.
Fortunately Sora chooses that moment to burst through the door carrying two bags.
He almost ripped the door off its hinges.
I'm sorry it took so long! There were a lot of people in line.
She places the first bag in front of Aiko and takes a seat on the bench next to her.
Do you buy Aiko lunch?
Sometimes, yes. I'd make Aiko return the favor by buying mine, but I'm not sure how I'd carry it.
Plus I would never buy him lunch.
If Aiko was offended by Sora's comment, she doesn't show it. Sora wheezes.
How ungrateful.
I'm not sure if they're joking with each other or if I'm witnessing the start of a girl fight.
They look at each other for a few tense seconds before starting to smile.
Hey, Sora, do you think being upside down gives you a new perspective on things?
Didn't we already have this conversation?
Sora looks thoughtful, apparently giving the question some thought.
After a long, deep pause, he speaks.
I have no idea.
Well, at least she's as lost as I am.
Hey, Hisao, you're coming to the track meet, right?
The question comes out of nowhere and catches me off guard.
Eh… I still don't know?
Honestly, Hisao, after all the trouble I went through to let you run with me in the mornings, you won't even go to my track meet?
Wasn't she the one who asked me to accompany her to the races?
In fact, he didn't even give me a choice.
Wait, no, I didn't say that...
She looks radiant, as if I had agreed to give her a million dollars.
So you will come after all! That's great!
I didn't say that either!
I'll go too, so I'll make sure he comes, Sora.
Good idea, Aiko! Maybe we can go eat or something after the competition is over?
I feel like I just got ripped off, but not by these two.
More like by an external force, pushing me irrevocably towards my destiny.
…Or maybe I shouldn't read books that show so many conspiracy theories. Or I could end up sounding like Kenji.
However, I think I'll have to go now.
I don't think I can stand to see them disappointed.
They would never forgive me.
And when is it?
sora_seq_6: Next week, fool! I told you a few days ago.
No, you didn't.
Did I forget? Well, you still won't forget to come, right?
Of course not! I'll even put a note on the calendar or something!
Aiko nods solemnly.
It's probably a good idea, you know. Unless time changes its course.
Can you do it?
Aiko shrugs reluctantly.
He hasn't done it yet, but you never know...
This time it's Sora who shrugs.
I guess nothing can be done if that happens.
Unless you're a time traveler or something.
You don't really think that can happen, do you?
I don't think we believe it... or do we?
Aiko shrugs again. That seems to be their default response to everything.
I guess not. But I reserve the right to change my mind at any time.
Coming from Aiko, this statement makes a disturbing amount of sense.
The fact that I notice it now scares me a little.
I wonder if Sora feels like this all the time.
Although if he does he doesn't show it. Sora simply nods.
As expected.
What is that supposed to mean?
This time, it's Sora who shrugs.
It's like he's using Aiko's own weapons against her.
Your response is the kind of thing I would expect from you, that's all.
Am I really that predictable?
Sora's smile seems to border on gloating.
Nah, it's just that your unpredictability is pretty predictable.
Well, okay then.
I don't get a chance to see if Aiko meant it or not, as the bell rings.
I didn't notice at all how lunch time was passing.
Hanging out with these two was too interesting.
Sora jumps, a panicked look on his face.
Oh no! I needed to stop by my room to pick up my notebook for the next class!
Don't you wish you had a time machine now?
Aiko looks a little smug as she says this sentence; as if he had just won an argument.
Sora ignores Aiko's comment.
Sorry, Hisao, but could you make sure to throw away our trash?
I usually clean up myself, but I have to run!
Sure, no problem.
Sora darts out with an urgency I'm starting to expect from her.
I don't bother asking Aiko why she can't help. She already seems to be absorbed in something else as she walks away.
She's probably used to Sora doing the cleaning, and for some reason I doubt Sora has ever complained to her about it.
Cleaning up after lunch doesn't take long, so I have plenty of time to take out the trash and go to class.
Shiina greets me with a wave and a wicked smile as I walk through the door.
sora_seq_7: I didn't see you in the cafeteria, Hicchan.
Yes, I decided it was too crowded there.
Shiina's smile widens even more.

An almost sinister smile crosses his lips.
It's like a smile of resignation.
And I don't think you can help me, anyway.
That hurts.
I don't want to tell him that it hurts, but it does.
Doesn't she realize that I want to be there for her when things are bad?
Well, I won't pressure you on that.
But I'm here for you if you later decide you'd like to talk about it.
It might help.
I can see the furious debate behind Sora's eyes.
It seems like she wants to tell me, but she's not sure if she can or not.
Hey, forget about it for now, okay?
We have to run.
With the mention of running, something he can control, Sora returns to his usual self.
TRUE!
Hurry up and stretch, Hisao!
We have to start moving!
She takes off, much faster than I'm used to.
Still, I try to keep up with him, stubbornly testing my limits.
That leaves me with a feeling of freedom, like my heart doesn't matter anymore.
sora_a3_seq_10: It makes me want to laugh, filled with the sensation of moving outside of what I once called my limits.
The nurse's warnings not to cross the line echo in my head, and I ignore them.
This feeling I have, this willingness to risk a heart attack for something as trivial as a morning run, feels atypical of me.
But is it?
Or rather, should it be?
I have a weak heart, of course.
One that will never be able to have the speed or stamina that Sora's has.
But I probably wouldn't be able to become that good even if I had a healthy heart.
As we round the final bend, I feel my legs screaming in protest, but for the first time, I ignore them.
He accelerated to finish with a sprint, almost catching up with Sora.
That was never going to happen, of course.
Still, I feel surprisingly good.
Oh, right, my legs feel like they're about to catch on fire, and I'm having trouble staying upright.
But there has been something of a change today.
And it's all thanks to the girl smiling at the finish line, waiting for me.
That felt a little faster than usual.
My comment is met with a smile and a shrug.
I can't let you think I'm going to be soft on you, can I?
But you managed to get through it without a problem.
Well, I couldn't have done it without you.
Still feeling the ecstasy of the race and motivated by a surge of gratitude, I catch Sora in a hug.
Thank you.
Seriously, I'm not just saying that.
I am indebted to you.
Sora seems agitated by my words, squirming uncomfortably.
Don't be stupid, Hisao.
Someone had to drag you out here, right?
And it's not like you're not doing anything for me, right?
I needed a running partner, remember?
I shake my head, still having no intention of letting go of Sora, who stops squirming and just looks down at me with a rapidly intensifying blush that almost seems out of character for her.
No, that's not true.
You wanted a running partner, but you didn't need one.
If I hadn't shown up the day after the festival, you'd still be running, right?
But it doesn't work the other way around.
I only managed to do it a few times before the festival.
And without you, I probably wouldn't have gotten anything done after that.
Sora smiles at me and pokes a finger in my chest.
You're quite lazy, Hisao.
Hey, I was flattering you!
Well… you're welcome, I guess.
I will repay you somehow.
Oh, uh, well...
You know, that's not necessary.
I mean, I kind of like you, Hisao.
And being able to run with you in the mornings isn't exactly a bad deal for me, so...
yumi_seq_1: While we are arranging the pieces, a noise is heard at the door.
Good afternoon.
Elena…
Oh, how about Elena. Are you done?
Are you both here? Marvelous. Somehow, our teacher managed to gather some extra help, so I was able to leave. Have they been here since you left?
Practically. We've been playing a little chess.
W-would you like a cup of tea?
In fact, I think it might be a good idea to go outside for a while…
The instant change of mood on Yumi's face shows her opposition to this plan, even if she doesn't say anything.
I feel strangely compelled to say what is plainly visible on his face, but that Elena cannot see.
I think… I think maybe we should stay here…
Really? It's so busy here that I was thinking we should leave school and go to the local tea house.
Do you mean the Sh-Shanghai?
Of course; with everyone at the festival it must be practically empty.
Tea house?
Oh, that's right, you probably don't know about him.
There is a tea house not far from here, which we go to from time to time.
Sounds good. Yumi, what do you think?
Yumi jumps a little at being forced into the conversation, but at least she looks less shocked than before.
If… if it's Shanghai, I think it will be nice.
Well then, it's agreed. Let's get going.
Yumi and I got up from the table and our chess game.
Before I can do anything, Yumi has thrown the pieces into a small container and placed the board to the side.
Looks like we're ready now. Please, you first.
Yumi moves to Elena's side and we venture into the school hallways.
The pair lead me through a series of unfamiliar doors, and we exit through the side of the building opposite the festival grounds.
Isolated by the heavy stone of the building, the noise of the crowd has faded to a murmur.
Strange; I thought most people would be starting to leave by now…
They're probably here to see the fireworks.
Fireworks?
Yes, apparently the school is putting on quite a show. Many people come from town just to see them.
Elena's decision to leave the school grounds seems to make sense now. Yumi would probably have a hard time with the entire village descending on the school. Or ascending, as the case may be.
For the second time since I arrived in Yamaku, I find myself walking down this road with Elena.
Only now that I can barely hear the incessant noise of the festival do I realize how loud it was. I can hear my ears ringing lightly in the quiet afternoon air as they recover from the day's assault.
Yumi clings to Elena, but still manages to guide her across the road. That, and avoiding the occasional glances of curious pedestrians, seems to completely weaken his constitution.
She rarely raises her attention from the floor in front of her, and rarely utters a word.

Elena, on the other hand, maintains her own formal personality just as she does at school. It's obvious that she intentionally puts effort into her appearance, rather than hiding it the way Yumi does.
It's surprising how different they are in the way they carry themselves outside of Yamaku's grounds. That said, it is obvious that in both cases they visibly change.
Within Yamaku, everyone is “special,” which negates the “specialness” of it.
But once we venture outside the school gates, we are returned to the status of “outsiders” and generic labels.
Especially when we are still in school uniform. It's like hanging a sign around your neck challenging people to find out what's wrong with you.
I'm surprised so many students leave it on. On the other hand, with canes and wheelchairs being common among students, I guess it's not really much of a liberation.
Or maybe I'm the only one who sees this as a stigma? Maybe you get used to it after a while, like any other school uniform.
The teahouse looks pretty standard from the outside; just an ordinary building with typical signs decorating the entrance.
It looks like the kind of place you'd walk past without thinking, just another generic cafe in a sea of ​​thousands.
yumi_seq_2: If Yumi hadn't led Elena towards the entrance I would have continued down the road without even knowing it existed.

Inside the tea house you get a more traditional feel. Everything seems to have been made from the same piece of wood, from the counter and benches to the tables with high-backed armchairs on the walls.
But the most striking quality of the room is its lack of life. I think I can vaguely hear something bubbling in the distance in the background, but other than that the room is silent.
Without any direction, we simply waited near the entrance, politely obeying the “Please wait for a table” sign.
Hey, is this place closed or something?
The sound of a chair falling echoes throughout the empty room, and a head snaps up from under a table.
I wasn't asleep and welcome to Shanghai!
Yuuko, dressed in a pastel apron and holding a menu, rushes to greet us. His misaligned glasses and disheveled hair cast suspicion on his previous statement.
But whether she was asleep or not is not the first question that comes to mind.
Do you work here now? What happened to the library?
That? Elena? Hisao?
Welcome to Shanghai!
Yuuko, still waking up, gives a violent bow, knocking her glasses off in the process.
Ghieh!? My glasses…
As I pick up her glasses from the floor, Elena offers an explanation.
Yuuko works here part time as well as at the library. It's one of the reasons we like to come here.
Yuuko takes her glasses from my hands, shakily putting them on again.
Yes… that's true… thank you…
Would you like me to show you your table?
There's no one else here, so you can pick your table and order whatever you want, but it'll take a while because I'll have to do it myself...
It's okay, Yuuko. You'll be fine with just a pot of black tea and a plate of sandwiches.
Good! I'll get right to it!
Yuuko quickly walks back out of the cafe, leaving us still standing at the entrance.
She partially pushes the swinging doors open before realizing she hasn't assigned us a table.
I'm sorry! I'm sorry! Please sit wherever you want! I'll be back right away!
Following her advice, I lead Elena to the nearest table while Yumi follows us.
As I sit next to Elena, I realize how appropriate this place is for Yumi.
The tables with high-backed chairs completely separate you from the rest of the room, and they don't seem to get many customers.
All the furniture, from the cushions on the tables to the condiment jars, looks antique but not too worn.
I wonder if Elena deliberately selects places like this to take Yumi. She looks like the kind of person who would go to great lengths to attend to Yumi's unique predicament.
So, Hisao, I didn't know you played chess…
Well, not very well, but I know how to play.
I guess now the obvious question would be… who won?
Elena's innocent smile makes me doubt. I really don't want to seem like I'm bragging about my victory over Yumi.
Hi-Hisao won.
Yes... but, eh, not by much...
Damn. Saying that out loud makes me feel like I've done something terrible.
Well done, Hisao. You have achieved something that I have only failed at.
Hey, thanks. I haven't played in years, so it felt good to play again.
Y... yes... that's how it was.
Yumi plays with her hair a little and looks away as she answers, but a small smile emerges.
It's a little more extreme reaction than I expected, but still kind of cute in that Yumi way.
It catches me a little off guard, and only Yuuko's cataclysmic re-entry jolts me back into the conversation.
Is everything okay over there, Yuuko? Do you need a hand?
I'm fine I'm fine I'm fine. I have to do this properly, it's my job.
yumi_seq_3: Concentration appears on his face as he looks at the tray in his hands, as if simply looking at its contents will keep him in position.
Sadly, this is not shown to be entirely effective; the cups and saucers dance slowly over it, occasionally clanking as they collide with each other.
With great care, Yuuko places the tray on the table with only the subtlest of clashes.
There it is, see!
Hey, well done?
Thank you, Yuuko.
Yuuko's head shoots down in her distinctive bow before answering.
It hasn't been anything.
Would you like to join us? There is something else I would like to discuss about that recent order, if I can...
Oh, that's true. Elena and Yuuko were arguing over a stack of books when I spoke to Yumi for the first time.
Something about Elena helping with braille…
Oh… yes. We didn't get a chance to go through them all, did we?
Yuuko hurriedly sits next to Yumi.
Apparently his dedication to this job only goes as far as his concentration goes; once it breaks, you suddenly lose it.
I'll be at the library tomorrow afternoon if you'd like to try again...
That sounds perfect, I'll see you there after class.
Ah… L-Elena…
Oh dear, it's true. Tomorrow is Monday, how could I have forgotten?
I'm starting to feel a little left out of the conversation. Although it is something to expect; I've been here for just a week, so it's impossible to know everyone's schedules.
Well, maybe we can come to some other arrangement.
Yuuko, will you be at the library later in the week?
Hmm, maybe, but this is already late...
And there are some-some... things that I n-need...
This could be a problem…
Elena ponders for a second before discovering the answer.
I wonder if we could get help from someone else, if needed...?
Um, to do what? I got lost a while ago...
Being made to volunteer for something without even having the slightest idea of what is happening is really not my thing.
And here I thought I had finally escaped the shackles of the student council and its repeated attempts to recruit me.
Oh, of course. The other day I was helping Yuuko sort through the new braille books in the library.
But Yumi and I usually go shopping on Monday afternoons; It is quieter that day than on weekends.
Last week we couldn't go because I was busy with the festival. I managed to escape later in the week, but Yumi couldn't do it.
Well, since I can't read braille, I assume you'd like me to go shopping with Yumi?
Correct. You were a big help to me the other day.
I think I can do it. Yumi, what do you think?
I-if you don't mind...
Of course not. I'm not familiar with all the stores in the area yet, so it sounds like a good idea.
E-it's okay.
Now that we've agreed on that, should we have our tea?
It's now that I realize our tea has been waiting all this time, never getting any hotter.
It's my fault! Let me serve it for you…
Yuuko reaches out with trembling hands, but I intercept her; It doesn't seem to be in good condition to handle hot liquids.
Okay, I'll do it. Since you already made the tea and sandwiches, you've already done your job as a waitress, right?
I... I guess.
Yuuko relaxes a little, but still watches anxiously as I spread the mixture.
yumi_seq_4: As I am about to bite into the sandwich, a low, loud bang can be heard, along with a flash of light from outside.
Ah, I take it the show has begun.
Only now that I look outside do I realize that dusk has come and gone, leaving us at the peak of twilight.
Sparkling trails arch as they rise, ready to explode into the floral silhouettes of the fireworks.
Let's see!
Oh… sorry Elena…
Please don't miss the show out of consideration for me. From what I've heard, this isn't a bad place to see it.
With the exception of Elena, we hurried to the window of the small tea house to watch the show.
The colorful strobe lights play over Yumi and Yuuko's smiling faces, and for a second I forget to look out the window.
In this brand new world, there are a few things that don't change.
I think that's why the school makes such a fuss about this festival thing. It's an opportunity to show the similarities between everyone.
The show ends very quickly; Fireworks are expensive, even for well-sponsored schools.
Before returning to our tea and sandwiches, Yumi turns to me.
Ah, t-thank you for today.
…And tomorrow.
Alright; I don't think I could have faced that crowd either.
On days like this it's more relaxing to spend time away from everyone, don't you think?
Y-yes.
Anyway, we've been putting off this tea for too long already, let's get back to it.
S-sure.
We returned to the table and our light meal.
That sounded impressive. Bigger than last year.
Yes, it was great! I had never seen them prepare such a show.
It gets better every year!
I'm afraid, however, that during that time, the tea has gone cold.
Oh no! Let me do a little more! This is my fault!
Calm down, Yuuko, it's no one's fault.
I take a sip from my cup, just to prove my point.
Anyway, this tea is not so bad cold. It's like iced tea.
Oh really?
Yes, seriously. If you add a little sugar it's good.
You're sure?
I'm serious. Now why don't you sit down and we'll finish this together?
E-it's okay.
Yuuko doesn't seem convinced, but sits down anyway.
He carefully measures out about five teaspoons of sugar and adds it to his tea.
Hey, I said a little sugar...
I know, but I like my tea sweet anyway.
Curious I take a look inside his cup. As I expected, almost none of the sugar dissolves in the cold liquid.
She stirs it twice before picking it up and drinking its contents, sugar and all, in one gulp.
You're right! It doesn't taste bad at all!
Hey, well...
I turn to look at Elena and Yumi, who have finished their food while I watched Yuuko's personality in action.
Not wanting to delay anyone, I use his tactic and finish the rest of my tea in a single gulp.
Well then, it looks like we're all done.
yumi_seq_5: Should we go back now or will we serve ourselves more?
Yuuko's expression clearly shows that this is not a good idea.
I think it would be better if we go back now.
We have to get back before curfew, after all.
Oh, that's a good point.
I'll see you tomorrow, Yuuko.
I'll be waiting for it, Elena. See you later, everyone.
We make our way out of the small teahouse and into the darkness of the night.
Elena and Yumi once again take up positions, but under the cover of darkness Yumi looks slightly less stressed than when she made her way here.
We move against the occasional group of people clearing the school grounds, but Yumi seems to guide us along some small paths, avoiding most of the crowd.
Outside the dorms, the school seems strangely quiet compared to the noise of the day.
Well, thanks to both of you for today. I think I learned a lot.
It was nothing, but I'm afraid I really must go. Today has been a long day.
That's true; Elena spent the entire day today on her feet, and I can imagine that walking outside of school would be very tiring for her.
I feel a pang of guilt remembering that I was probably the only one in school who got up around ten today.
Of course.
Well, I'll see you both tomorrow. Good night.
Good night, Hisao.
N-nights.
The girls return to their bedroom, and I return to mine.
In fact, now that I think about it, today has tired me out too.
My alarm rings in my ears, only to be quickly silenced by my fist.
My body switches into automatic mode, leading my unconscious self out of bed and into the uniform.
As always, my bottles of pills sit patiently on my desk, waiting for me to take them and choose my daily dose of medicine; seventeen pills a day.
Before I know it, I'm opening the door to group 3-3, happy to see that I'm not the only one who seems to be a little hungover from festival week.
Every face in the room looks haggard. With the festival now over, it's as if everyone's life's dream has been realized.
With nothing else to live for, students have relied only on their instincts to guide them to class.
Or maybe I'm just overthinking it.
I slowly make my way to my seat and only then do I realize why the room is so quiet.
The seats next to me are happily empty; The most scandalous deaf interpreter in the world is yet to arrive.
Just as I'm about to sit down, the door bursts open, revealing a glowing Shiina; her curls swaying across the dramatic entrance and her arms stretched skyward.
Woo-hoo~! It's all over!
It seems that not everyone is affected by post-festival depression.
The rest of the class watches her, obviously thinking the same thing as me.
Shiina, still motionless at the entrance with her arms still in the air, looks around nervously.
He's obviously feeling the terrible mood, but he can't figure out exactly what to do.
Suddenly, she is thrown roughly forward.
Hey!
As he stumbles into the room, he reveals Shizune, who still has her arm outstretched from having pushed Shiina.
Thanks for the entertainment, but shouldn't you two take your seats?
Still slightly embarrassed, it takes a few seconds for Shiina to realize that she has to translate.
Oh! TRUE! Shicchan says she's not very happy with you for abandoning us last week.
