We were really busy!
Oh yeah? What about the things I had already done for you?
She says that only counts for council members. Since you declined, she doesn't owe you anything.
yumi_seq_6: Shiina leans closer and whispers conspiratorially in my ear.
In fact, I think she's just a little hurt that you didn't spend the day with her.
But she's really grateful for your work last week.
Sensing that we are talking about her, Shizune taps her fingers on the bench until Shiina turns around to look at her.
I can't make out anything about the rapid signs they're making, but from Shizune's slightly embarrassed expression, and Shiina's poorly contained laughter, I can guess.
As this exchange happens, the door opens once again, but this time at a much more reasonable pace.
Yumi silently enters the living room, and closes the door behind her.
Peeking out from under his hair, he quickly surveys the classroom.
Our eyes meet, and suddenly he freezes. He closes his eyes, takes a deep breath, and walks towards my bench.
Bu… good morning Hisao.
Good morning Yumi. You're a little late, aren't you?
I... I was talking to Elena.
S-about today.
Oh, so you have his list? We can leave right after class in that case.
C-sure.
I'm looking forward to it.
Yumi briefly shows me her sorrowful smile and then hurries to her seat.
During class, it becomes apparent that it's not just the students who are a little down after the festival.
Mutou simply gives us a list of exercises from the textbook and then sits behind his desk.
For a moment I completely forget about the short lunch period, such is the banality of the day.
It stuns the senses, and everyone seems surprised when the bell signals the end of lessons.
While I'm putting my things away, Shizune and Shiina flank me and catch me.
And well, Hicchan, it's not too late to join. We have quite a bit of post-festival paperwork to complete…
Eh, sorry Shiina, I... I have plans...
As if taking the hint, Yumi appears behind me, holding a small bag, and trying to avoid eye contact with the outside world.
Shiina widens her eyes, then bursts into laughter.
WOW! You move fast, don't you, Hicchan~? We won't disturb your appointment any longer! Wahahaha!
After the vociferous Shiina, I see Shizune taking very little interest in the scene. I could be misunderstanding him, but I think he is deliberately ignoring me.
I feel a gentle tug on my shirt, and I turn to see Yumi's eyes fixed firmly on the floor.
Come on…come on…
I understand. Shizune, Shiina, I'll see you later.
And I'm still not interested in the advice.
Spoilsport.
Shiina and Shizune retreat to the hallway, gesturing happily to each other.
Do you have all your things? Let's go.
Streams of students pour out of the school gates and onto the road to town.
It's a little strange. It's almost a scene from any other school, but the illusion is shattered by the occasional wheelchair or missing limb.
One thing I notice is that no one is alone.
And, as Yumi and I pass through the gate, I notice that she closes the distance between us.
Not enough to be considered “close”, but it is clearly not in its usual “just a little far” position.
I guess we're not close enough for her to get as close as she does with Elena.
However, even though he has moved a little closer to me physically, mentally he seems to have traveled a mile.
His hands tightly gripped the leather straps of his backpack to the point of whitening his knuckles, his head bowed and his mouth contracted tightly.
It almost looks like he's being taken to the principal's office for the first time.
I try to stifle a laugh at the thought, but to no avail.
yumi_seq_7: W-what's happening...?
I guess there's no point in hiding it...
Sorry. For a second it looked like you were in trouble.
W-w-what do you mean?
I think you need to relax a little. We're not going far, and there are only students around here, right?
Ci-true.
It bothers me a little to see Yumi so upset.
And you do this every week, don't you?
Y-yes. With Elena.
Of course. “With Elena.” I wonder if he's ever left school without it.
It doesn't seem like much at first glance, but Yumi's dependence on Elena is absurdly great.
If he can't even handle leaving school without her, how would he have managed to survive if they hadn't met?
Had he found someone else to cling to? And what brought her to Elena?
Was it because of his blindness, or was Elena just kind enough to give him a hand?
I wonder if anyone would have met the requirements.
Well, I'm here. Besides, we're not going that far. It will be over before you know it.
Yumi's knuckles slowly regain their color as she tries to hide a small smile, but that effort seems to prevent continuing the conversation.
We traveled, side by side, down the winding road down towards the town. The crowd of students disperses as we continue across the sidewalk.
The faster students move forward, and the less mobile ones stay behind, the crowd spreading out to nothing.
By the time we get to the convenience store we are practically alone.
Using me as a shield between her and the attendant, Yumi moves between the narrow aisles, adding a variety of items to her basket.
Bread, milk, tea… thyme?
What kind of convenience store sells herbs?
On the other hand, nothing about this town seems normal, which might not be such a bad thing in retrospect.
Everything is so different and uncomfortable; Stopping to think about such things is not really an option.
When I think about it, it reminds me of Yumi.
No matter how hard you try, you can't avoid its scars; They still interrupt my train of thought when I see them.
As much as I try not to admit it to myself, I think I'm forcing myself to ignore them.
Not that I myself am scar-free. The jagged line on my breastbone will never completely fade.
I just have the luxury of being able to hide it easily.
But in a way, our scars remind me that we are all in this place for a reason.
Yumi throws one last item into her basket and then timidly extends it towards me, along with a few bills.
C-c-could you p-please…
It takes me a second to understand what he's trying to say.
Oh, you want me to pay for this?
She nods, but doesn't look up.
I guess this task falls to Elena in normal situations.
Sure. Just let me grab a couple of things…
I hurriedly grab a few essential items for myself and then head to the counter with Yumi following close behind.
The attendant nods nonchalantly as he scans the items.
I guess just ignoring us is one way to deal with Yamaku's anomalies; They must receive a lot of students here, being the closest store to the school.
Each staff member must have their own way of dealing with us. Or maybe not; Maybe I'm the only one who thinks twice about my exceptional classmates at school.
Our transaction completed, Yumi and I set off back to the street.
The road is practically abandoned at this time. The students who were leaving have already left, and none have begun their return yet.
And, with only the school ahead on the road, there doesn't seem to be anyone else around.
yumi_seq_8: Certainly the emptiness is reflected in Yumi; his arms at his sides each carrying a bag, his head no longer bowed, and back to an upright position…
It's almost like I'm enjoying this walk.
So why all this strange stuff? Mixed spices? Why would you need that in school?
Some…times…m-I like to make co-food.
Well, of course, me too, but... spices?
That's a little more advanced, don't you think?
N-not really.
Well, I think it's okay. You'll have to teach me someday.
S-sure.
She doesn't seem very sure about that, but pointing it out doesn't seem very smart.
At least he seems much happier than he was on the way up this road.
That simple fact makes me a little happy.
Outside the girls' dormitories, Yumi and I organize the grocery bags with our respective purchases.
In comparison, my things certainly look flat.
I'm serious, you're making a fool of me here...
N-no I don't... I just...
I'm just kidding.
I have a pile of homework that I let go last week, so I have to go now.
Will you be okay taking all that to your room?
Y-yes.
Sure? Well then. I'll see you tomorrow.
A-bye.
We separate, and I return to my room.
Piles of papers sit on my desk, begging to be finished. With all the commotion last week, I've barely had time to catch up.
I tried to continue with my studies while I was in the hospital, but some of these things I haven't seen before, even back at my previous school.
Without being in any way prepared, I remove the lid from a can of drink, and get to work.
The days are starting to get really hot.
This morning, I woke up covered in sweat.
By the time the student body begins to leave their dormitories for breakfast and morning chores, the sun has taken full effect; Strangely, that lifts my spirits.
It's not even eight o'clock, and yet I feel that this day is going to be one of those pleasant, calm, and warm days.
If I weren't at a school that considers every absence from class a sign of a life-threatening situation, I would consider skipping the entire day and just relaxing on the school grounds.
Yes, today will be a genuinely relaxed day.
For a second, I stop mid-stretch, and consider the nurse's warning about exercising. Maybe I should have continued those morning runs.
Running with someone like Sora might have been a bit demanding, but if I had gone at my own pace…
Oh, who am I kidding? I couldn't stick to something like that without some kind of motivation.
It's not like I'm sitting around all day. The walk to and from the convenience store counts as exercise, right? Especially the uphill hill walk…
Of course, it's not a big deal. Compared to months lying in a hospital bed I'm getting quite a bit of exercise.
It seems I am not alone in my appreciation of the day.
Almost everyone in the class is looking out the window and up at the inviting sky.
Even the immutable Shizune seems to lack her usual stamina for schoolwork.
Shiina, as shameless as ever, has unbuttoned the top buttons of her shirt and is fanning herself with her notebook.
I must have been staring, because now he's sticking his tongue out at me.
Still, he shows no signs of stopping his efforts, nor is he trying to hide the fact.
The lunch bell seems to take everyone by surprise, and the class empties at a much slower pace than usual.
The heat seems to be absorbing everyone's need to hurry.
yumi_seq_9: Well, almost all of them.
Hi… Hisao?
How about Yumi, what can I do for you today?
Yumi already has a lunch bag in her hands.
I don't have to be a detective to know where this is going.
Um… would you like to have lunch with us again?
I… brought enough for everyone…
Wonderful. But you don't have to be so ceremonious about this.
Ah… okay.
I guess we go to the tea room?
P…please.
Elena said she would meet us there, so we must… we must…
Should we?
…We must go together…
Sounds like a good idea. This heat has made me very hungry.
Yumi breathes a sigh of relief, and I gather my things.
As always, the aura of the tea room is refreshing, feeling isolated from the rest of the world.
On the other hand, the school's usual hubbub seems a little muted; mostly due to laziness caused by heat exhaustion.
Yumi slowly spreads her food on the table, focusing intently on every small movement, as if trying to keep her mind away from other thoughts.
It's not much, but I can tell from his demeanor that he has prepared everything with great care.
I guess Elena isn't here yet. Should we start without her?
I-it will be here soon...
Yumi struggles with the lid of the rice container.
Let's see, let me help you with that...
I take the container from Yumi's hands, and try to force the lid open.
Despite my efforts, it seems stuck.
Let me guess, you put it in while the rice was still hot?
Y-yes. I was in a hurry...
I place the container on the table between us.
That's what I thought. It looks like this is stuck. We'll need some hot water to open it.
But that could be a problem here. We would end up with water everywhere.
Well, in that case, how about I contribute to today's meal?
At the door, Elena smiles as she holds a bag stocked with various buns and bread rolls. I can't help but do the same.
Since they both had to change plans because of me, I thought I'd bring up a little detail.
Thank you, Elena. Let me hold that for you…
With a little guidance, Elena's assortment of breads joins Yumi's riceless plate. I quickly make some tea to complete the image.
Well, I want to start now.
As I take a bite, I notice Yumi trying her best to look like she's not looking my way.
It's nothing special, although to be honest I can't complain. I am very lazy when it comes to cooking for myself.
Not bad, I guess this is made from the stuff you bought yesterday?
Y-yes.
Yumi's eyes scream at me, begging for some kind of feedback.
Well, it was clearly worth it. Thank you, Yumi.
I... wanted to show you this... after yesterday...
It's okay. I was just a little surprised at the things you were buying.
yumi_seq_10: Yumi has always liked to experiment when it comes to food. I think it's good... most... of the time.
While on the one hand Elena's smile doesn't waver, the slight change in her tone tells me that things haven't gone very well in the past.
And it's not like Yumi has many people to try her cooking...
Wait…was Elena waiting for me to go first? She didn't start eating until after I said everything was fine...
His cheeky smile tells me that this was a deliberate action. I'll have to try to figure out how to return it to him in the future, to pay for this.
Well, it's delicious, and that's all that counts, right?
Ci-true.
Elena, satisfied that she is not the first to serve as a test for Yumi's creation, begins to consume the food in front of her.
I find myself lost in thought as I watch his chopsticks gently touch the plate, their tips poking and tracing to quickly determine the position of the food as he deftly picks it up.

One would think she was a child playing with her food if it weren't for the situation, but she does it with such care and lightness that it is obvious that this is simply the way she eats this type of food.
Not wanting to miss it, I start eating too.
Yumi takes a different attitude, waiting until Elena and I have a free hand before quickly taking her part.
In a short time the containers are clean, except for the still closed rice container.
Thank you Yumi, I am satisfied.
N-no… thanks to you for the bread…
Yes, it would have been a disaster if it weren't for that.
It hasn't been anything.
But now, I have to go back. It's quite easy to arrive late after eating here.
Yes, I see what you mean. I think we'll clean up here and then leave.
Well then, good day.
Elena leaves, her cane tapping the floor across the quiet hallway.
Yumi and I quickly packed our things and remained seated, waiting for the bell.
Together, we stared out the window and into the endless blue sky.
If it weren't for the ringing of the bells, I would have sworn time had stopped.
The urge to skip class rises in my gut.
I cast a glance at Yumi who shows no signs of moving either.
No… not yet…
The interval between the warning bells and the end of lunch passes in the blink of an eye.
We really have to go... people will freak out and start a rescue search if we skip...
Yumi sighs.
You're right.
Slowly, she stands up, and I follow suit.
Silently, we made our way up the stairs to the third floor and then to our living room.
At the entrance, I take the initiative and open the door ahead of Yumi, bowing my head in apology in advance.
I'm sorry, we're late master.
I am greeted not by stern words, nor by an angry instruction to take my seat, but simply by the silence created by the fifteen or so students trying not to laugh.
Mutou, always slow, still has to come. Anyway, the fact that Yumi and I have arrived together is visibly obvious.
Pff… pffua…
That makes it about fourteen students trying, and one student failing.
Pft-wahahaha! The lovers return~!
WOWHAHAHA~!
Yes, thanks. Now you can calm down.
I pass through the door, and notice that Yumi is pressed firmly against my back, hiding her person from the rest of the class.
As my footsteps approach my bench, she eventually turns away from me and walks stiffly to hers. The effort to mentally block out everyone's presence is clearly written on his face.
Quickly checking the door for any sign of the teacher's arrival, I make a trip to Yumi's bench and whisper in her ear.
yumi_a3_seq_1: The color of the room slowly changes from the glow of afternoon to the orange of twilight. A clock slowly passes the seconds, counting in the background, at the limit of hearing.
But no matter how long you wait, the result cannot be changed.
The tiny chess piece in play makes a slight sound against the board.
Like a compressed spring, Yumi makes her move just moments after mine.
It's embarrassing. Compared to my five-minute moves, she seems to know exactly what she wants to do.
Mate.
Again… How much is it with this one? 3-2?
E-ties do not count.
Curse. You're getting better at this every day.
That, or he had been holding back. I never would have imagined something like that when I first spoke to him, but he really has a knack for this game.
Chess seems to have become a popular pastime for both; hiding in the tea room, playing a game or two after school.

From here, the students outside can barely be heard crowding around. The everyday noises below remind me a little of my life before Yamaku, although I am now quite aware that it is a life to which I will never return.
Do you like to play again?
You... I have to finish my homework...
Oh. Well, I'll see you tomorrow then.
But... what about this...
Yumi points to the tea set near the almost empty chess board.
Don't worry about it, I'll take care of it.
Oh… okay…
S-see you.
See you later.
Yumi leaves as I begin to clean the area.
The occasional whistles and cheers from the sports club outside become less frequent, eventually reaching silence.
Part of me still wants to be on some kind of team. Since I played soccer and other sports before my accident, I guess it's just normal to feel nostalgic about what I can no longer do.

But I have other reasons for coming here so often, and I don't feel too bad about losing that part of me thanks to them. Elena is already a good friend, but it's the little exchanges I have with Yumi that feel especially good.
The small victories I feel every day as I see more of what's under their self-imposed shell. That's why I come here more than anything.
As I'm putting away cups and sauce boats, I hear voices outside the door. Stopping for a moment to listen, I can tell that it is Yumi and Elena, and I decide to go outside to investigate.
Are you sure?
I'm... sure...
Ah, Hisao.
Yumi turns to look at me with a surprised look when she notices that I am approaching. Elena must have found her just as she was about to leave.
Oh wow, is Hisao here too?
Good afternoon, Elena. What's happening?

I was hoping, now that I'm done with my class rep duties for the day, that I could count on both of you to join me for tea in Shanghai. It would be nice to enjoy some time together outside of school for a change.
I would be delighted. But didn't Yumi have work to do...?
No... it's not that much...
Wonderful. It seems to be decided then.
I cross my eyes across the cafe as the three of us walk inside. As usual, there are only a handful of people at most, and the noise level is a quiet background murmur.

The support that Elena has on Yumi's arm remains as it has been throughout the slow walk down to the town, although it is difficult to say for what reason, whether for Elena's guidance, or to provide confidence for Yumi.
For a moment, Elena removes her arm from Yumi's to retract her staff as Yuuko quickly flies to where we are standing, but soon after she places it back where it was.
Welcome to Shanghai! Can I take your order?
She bows deeply, her well-conducted and professional introduction putting her in good spirits. It's a nice change from the norm for Yuuko.
Just tea, please. Yumi, Hisao?
Me a slice of cake and a coffee.
Just…t-tea…please.
yumi_a3_seq_2: It's coming right away. Please take a seat wherever you like, and I will be back soon.
Yuuko gives a small smile and nods before shuffling to the counter, and we head to some empty seats near the window at a brisk pace.
We slide to our seats, the girls at one end, with Elena's cane resting on one side, and me on the other. I notice that Yumi is not doing something she commonly does.

Instead of keeping her eyes fixed on the floor and hiding behind her blind escort, busy trying to convince herself that the world around her doesn't exist, she's just keeping her eyes down and helping Elena move.
Are you okay, Elena? You look tired.
She lowers her head a little, looking a little sorry for letting him see it.
Class representative duties can be very tiring, considering that it often means dealing with the student council.
Very exhausting indeed.
How… are the other representatives doing?
Better than me, but not much. Shizune is a demanding person no matter who she is dealing with.
It doesn't sound like you particularly enjoy the work. Why do you do it in the first place, if it's so bad?
Being a class representative is nice, and I can handle the responsibility well enough. It's just that the people involved are sometimes...
She lowers her voice, cutting her words at the right place. It's hard to imagine Elena swearing, but I imagine if anyone can make her do it, it would be Shizune.
Yumi seems to languish a little in the heat of such conflict, but before I can deflect the topic slightly, she stands up.
Yumi?
I…I'll be back in a moment.
With that, she goes to the bathroom. I guess that's one way to deal with the situation, if that was indeed his motivation.
Elena, anyway, seems a little hurt.
Don't worry about that. I don't think it was you.
But...
I think it's gotten stronger lately. You've seen it yourself... right...?
That came out a little wrong. Fortunately Elena doesn't seem offended, and by now he shouldn't really be so scared of stepping on that landmine around him.
Likely. But sometimes… I find it hard to know.
Silence reigns for a moment before two cups of tea, a cake, and a steaming cup of coffee appear in front of us.
I notice that Yuuko takes special care to place the teacup against Elena's fingertips, letting her know where it is.
Here you go.
Thank you, Yuuko.
Thank you so much.
With a quick, silent bow, the bespectacled waitress departs.
Oh, that's true. I wanted to ask you something, and now would be the appropriate time to do so.
I'm all ears.
Yumi's birthday is coming up, and I was hoping you'd join me for gift shopping in the city this weekend.
Is Yumi's birthday coming soon? I guess it would be a good opportunity to cheer her up a little.
Like Yuuko, she seems to always be teetering on the line between panic and depression, and I've never seen her enjoy herself much outside of our chess games.
And leaving that aside, learning more about the layout of the city with a friend keeping me company sounds like a good way to spend the weekend.
Sure, I'd be happy to do it. Have you made any plans about what will be done for his birthday? A party or something?
With Yumi being Yumi, maybe a small meeting would be—
Elena suddenly cuts herself off, leaving me wondering why as she brings her cup of tea to her lips and begins to sip.
After a few seconds, I notice Yumi over his shoulder walking towards us. Elena's hearing must be very good if it was the sound of the toilet door opening that alerted her.
Yumi takes her seat once more, and immediately drinks her tea. Soon the three of us are quietly eating and drinking as the sun sets.

It's a nice way to spend the rest of the daylight, and makes me appreciate the calm and serene surroundings of Yamaku. I think I'm starting to really like it here, with everything and as isolated as it could be.

I finish the last of my coffee and leave the cup on the table while the girls talk among themselves. The coffee here is a little bitter for my taste, but it's still pretty good. Better than what I can do, in any case.
The girls' discussion is mainly focused on their respective reading preferences, which makes me a little curious about a related topic.
Hey Yumi, I was wondering... besides chess and reading, do you have any other hobbies or things you like to do?
She stops dead, looking quite surprised that someone would be interested in such a question about her. It takes him a little time to formulate a response.
yumi_a3_seq_3: Um... I guess... I like to sing a little. A little c-computers too, but no… I don't really use them much.
Singing is not something I expected to hear. It's hard to imagine his singing voice, considering how softly he always speaks.
Elena, on the other hand, simply nods. She must already know all this, since she's already been friends with Yumi for a year or so.
W-what's... d-of...?
Of me?
She hesitates a bit before quickly shaking her head up and down. It's just logical that she would want to know about my hobbies after telling me hers.
There is chess, obviously, but also… hmm…
There was football too, although I can't really do that anymore. Reading, a hobby I picked up in the hospital… um…
This is surprisingly difficult. Elena and Yumi seem a little uncomfortable about the direction this is going, and the more I think about it, the more I am too.
It seems that you have acquired several things since your accident.
Elena's sincerity is covered with probably the most positive spin anyone could put on what I said. Yumi, however, is silent.
If a situation becomes difficult, your reaction always seems to be to retreat into silence to prevent things from getting worse. That, or physically withdraw.
A light ring gives us pause. As Elena reaches for her pocket, it becomes obvious that the sound is coming from her phone.
I'm sorry...
E-it's okay...
Elena nods quickly once before shuffling out of her seat and taking the call a short distance away, to avoid disturbing both of us.
It must feel good to be popular.
Yumi smiles, but doesn't take the bait to continue the conversation.
I end up leaning back and closing my eyes, relaxing as best I can.
It's nice and quiet here. I wonder what it would be like to have grown up somewhere like this, instead of in the city.
Do you live-come from the city?
Looks like I found something you want to talk about.
Yes. You could say I was a city kid through and through.
S-it sounds like they changed m-a lot of things...
That's right. However, I'm still not sure what to get out of all this. It's a bit of a culture shock, in more ways than one.
You must have gone through something like this when you first arrived in Yamaku, right? I imagine most new students do.
N-not really…
Yumi looks slightly to the side, looking unwilling to continue. I tilt my head questioningly, but a couple of seconds pass without a response.
But can't we deal with that on Monday? The consequences of the last...
I understand. I'll try to talk to her. You know what it's like when you've closed yourself off to an idea.
Yes, thanks. Then I'll call you later. See you later.
Elena's conversation ends with the click of her phone closing. She returns to our table, but doesn't take her seat.
Should you go?
Unfortunately. The class representative job calls again.
I-I can go with you.
It's okay, Yumi. I'll just go straight to the student council. There's no need to spoil a good afternoon out of consideration for me.
Also, if you accompanied me on my way back to school, who would keep our poor Hisao company?
It's okay...
I can join you again for tea later tonight, if you like. I might well need it.
We agree to the plan, and Elena says goodbye to both of us, taking her staff after Yumi passes it to her.
Despite my offer to pay Elena's share, she insists on giving us her portion of the bill, and thanks Yuuko as she leaves.
And then... we are alone. It might be nice and all to leave Yumi and I alone to have some time together, but that almost always means the two of us sitting close to each other in silence for a while.
I wonder how I must seem to Yumi.
I never thought of myself as a scary person, but having someone my own age acting that way around me makes me extremely self-conscious, like it's my fault she's uncomfortable.
She could get more used to people if she stopped being so cloistered in Yamaku.
yumi_a3_seq_4: But on the other hand… when even people much older than her react so strongly after just one look at her face, she might as well feel the same way I do now.
It's a real dead end. If he stays in Yamaku, he won't get used to socializing, but if he leaves, any attempts he might make might be thrown back at him by people who can't deal with his scars.
Want to order something else so you don't miss a beat? We haven't had what you could call a dinner yet, after all.
Yumi perks up and nods vigorously, happy that I brought up the topic for her. I catch Yuuko's attention, and she diligently comes to take our order.
Do you like something else?
I just want a special sandwich and a hot chocolate. It's a little late for coffee already. Yumi?
I-I... I want the same...

With a nod and a bow, Yuuko turns on the tip of her foot and walks back behind the counter, where she busies herself with picking out the bread and condiments and working the machine to make our drinks.
Not a word is said between us until Yuuko returns. She smiles and hands us our food and drinks, before moving towards a customer who has caught her attention.
I give up the possibility of having something like a conversation with my companion and decide to just enjoy my meal, as small as it may be.
It tastes good, like most of the food here. After a few bites, I notice something is missing. Specifically, the sound of Yumi eating.
Looking over at her again, I see Yumi looking a little uneasy behind her untouched sandwich.
Aren't you hungry?
She shakes her head from side to side. Even as she does so, the scarf of hair she keeps on the right side of her face still does its job of hiding it almost entirely.
N-it's not that.
Oh. I was ready to eat your share too.
Lucías… w-worried. I-Is...something wrong... happening?

I'm caught off guard by his idea that I'm the one who looks in trouble, but on second thought, he's probably right. My face must have conveyed my emotions without me noticing, and she's not stupid at all; rather the opposite.
We are friends, right?
Friends…
From the tone of his voice and constricted posture, it seems like I have stepped on yet another mine.
This is another reason why interacting with her is difficult; the self-imposed psychological barriers she puts between herself and others, including me and, most likely, Elena. It's a shame that—
I-I think we are...
I'm a little caught off guard by Yumi's very direct response, and more so because I was about to give up the possibility of getting any answer.
I see...
Am-am I wrong? S-sorry, I-I…
No, it's just... hearing confirmation from you about that is comforting.
To go back to what you said before: since I came to Yamaku, I've been having some problems with how I should relate to others.
I find myself laughing a little. It's surprising what a relief this has been. I can feel my face smiling as I take my cup of hot chocolate and bring it to my lips.
Ouch! It's hot...
T-that's…
That's the reason I haven't eaten yet. I-I was waiting… for my drink to cool down first.
I guess I'll wait then.
We both shared a small laugh. The situation isn't really that funny, but for some reason… it feels like laughing is the most natural thing to do right now.
I guess we were both a little nervous about each other. I was so busy thinking that Yumi was the one who had something wrong, it took her turn to remind me that I was uncomfortable too.
But whatever… it still feels a little good. Kind of nice to have someone thinking of me that way, in their own way.
Continuing a long, leisurely walk up the hill and onto the school grounds, the two of us found ourselves between both bedrooms.
Regular nightly patrols pass between the men's and women's dormitory buildings, both for safety and to quickly raise the alarm should any medical problems arise.
The guard currently on duty nods quickly at us as he continues on his way.
A loud yawn escapes Yumi's mouth before she has a chance to cover it. I have little doubt that she is already quite tired.
I better go to my room, then. See you tomorrow, Yumi.
B-good night…
We parted ways and began our separate ways, before I stopped and looked back.
Yumi is standing, waving her hand while smiling. I smile and say goodbye anyway, and after a few seconds, he turns around and walks up the stairs of his dorm building, disappearing through the door.
These little moments that we share with each other are like a little treasure. One thing is certain; I want to protect that small, delicate smile that she so fleetingly sees around so few people.
yumi_a3_seq_5: I wonder about these feelings I have when Yumi is around, and when I manage to do things for her… I don't know if they are the seed of something beyond what we share now.
The summer sun is something to be savored, but when combined with the clean country air, it is even better.

Members of the athletics club are running everywhere on the field in front of me; some are playing with a soccer ball, others are talking, and a few are laughing while two of them are playing wrestling.
None of them pay any attention to me as I sit alone in the grass, under the shade of a particularly tall tree. It's a nice, peaceful moment after a hard day of school work.
I played soccer quite often before my heart attack, so I thought it would be quite nostalgic to see them. However, what I am feeling now is very different from that emotion.

I hear footsteps approaching behind me, and I turn to the side to see one of my classmates take a seat next to me. It catches me off guard, because the two of us haven't spoken much before, and I didn't think anyone would notice me here.
What's up.
Hello. Miura, isn't it?
Just call me Miki. First names are very prissy.
I'll do it that way, then.

We both look back at the field where the boys are playing. It looks like they are preparing for a second game, with people dispersing to their positions and the ball being brought to the center of the field.
Once prepared, the whistle is blown to start the game and with that they return to their game.
Won't you play?
Nah, I'll just rest for a while.
What about you? You looked like you wanted to play when you were looking at us earlier.
So someone noticed me after all.
It's a bit of a long story.
His face tells me that I have caught his interest.
I'm in Yamaku because I have a heart problem. I actually can't play soccer anymore.
You wanted to be a soccer player, didn't you?
No, actually I was just doing it for fun. My friends played it, so I played too.
Any of those kids could have been me before my accident. But I don't feel like I have any real interest in going back either. It's a little difficult to explain.
I'm still in decent physical shape from my playing days, even if my strength has largely left me, and I get along well with the other members of the club.

When I think about it, I should feel pretty bad watching people play when I can't play anymore. But it is not like that. Maybe it's a good thing; a sign that I've gotten over it and am ready to become a new person.
Sorry, I kind of rambled.
Alright. I'm actually happy to hear that.
It sounds like you really have things under control. Some of the people who just come to Yamaku are a mess at first.
So you're a member of the track club, then?
Yep. I've been at it since I got here.
I don't suppose you're going to be friends with Sora? Short, fast runner, without legs? I don't think there are many female members of that club.
Haha, Sora. Everyone knows her, right?
But nah, I tend to get along better with men, so Sora and I don't really talk much. Anyway, what about you?
Oh well, I'm not really in any clubs. Real clubs, anyway.
But you've been hanging out with Yumi and that blonde Amazon, right?
Blonde Amazon... I suppose Elena is tall enough to fit that description, if not taller. I nod in response, not emphasizing anything about things.
So don't worry about it. As long as you have some friends, you don't need to join a club.
A loud whistle from the field attracts our attention. One of the players is on the ground, clutching his leg, and the others stop the game to advance towards him, leaving Miki grimacing.
Ouch, that looks painful. That boy really has bad luck.
As he continues to look out over the field, I can't help but be reminded of his own wounds.
His left arm, ending in a stump instead of a hand, has been bandaged the entire time I've been in Yamaku, and his wound doesn't look all that new.
She turns to talk to me again and catches me looking. We both sit in an awkward silence as she takes his bandaged arm and holds it in her lap with her remaining hand.
S-sorry. I guess I'm still a little...
It's okay. Actually.
His tone is cheerful, but neither of them say anything after that.
Every disabled student here has their own way of dealing with their problems, and that some find their conditions uncomfortable is natural. I am included in them, after all.
yumi_a3_seq_6: The injured boy from the soccer game manages to stand up with some help, and ends up limping off the field with an arm over someone else's shoulder for support.
He probably just jerked it if he can still manage to walk.
The whistle blows again, and the game continues once again with one less man on the field.
Hanging out with Yumi and that blonde girl… you have strange company.
How is that?
It's just that Yumi is like... I don't know.
Shy?
No, it's not really that. It's just... it has problems, I think. I can't really put it in any good way.
But it's not that I think he's not a good person. It's perfectly good.
Just… hard to deal with.
It sounds like Miki, or at least other people in the room, have tried to get close to Yumi in the past. And it didn't turn out very well.
I think your judgment is rather harsh, considering that everyone, not just those in Yamaku, has their own problems.
On the other hand, I haven't known Yumi for that long, so I wouldn't be surprised if there were some things I didn't know about.
I just take it as it is. He's a good person, and I think that should be all that matters.
Miki's eyes narrow a little, and her smile spreads.
You really like it, don't you?
To be completely honest…yeah, I like it. I'd appreciate it if you didn't tell anyone.
Hey, babes, you can trust me. There is no problem on that side.
To be honest, I think it's kind of cute. If you want to go for it, don't let me stop you.
Thank you.

He may say that, but he was just talking about Yumi having “dilemmas”. Still, I want to stick to the words I said. Yumi's problems don't matter; I will deal with anything that comes up, because I want to help her.
If there is even the slightest chance that I can bring Yumi out of her depression and seclusion, then I must work towards her, no matter what. If you need a prince, then I will be that prince.
As I think about the possibility of a relationship, I can see Miki smiling at me as she watches my face. I'm definitely blushing, and looking away only makes her laugh.
I don't believe it. We're just friends.
Oh. I thought I had discovered something good for a moment. I understand; Boys and girls don't need to be boyfriends and girlfriends, after all.
What he says is true, even if I really have feelings for Yumi. We're good friends right now, and I don't want to ruin that, but I also want to be more than that for her. It's difficult.

Miki gives off a different vibe than the other girls. Talking to him feels more like talking to a guy instead of a woman. The fact that she says she prefers male company doesn't help dispel that idea either.
A glance at my watch shows me that lunch break will be over in just a few minutes. Time to start back to school.
Lunch is almost over. Do you want us to go back?
Yes, we better go.

I get up from the grass and brush myself off, offering a hand to Miki to help her up as well. She takes it and easily stands up, showing off the muscles jiggling on her toned bare arms in the process.
Come to think of it, why aren't you wearing the normal girls' blouse?
Eh, it's too hot and restrictive. The men's uniform is better, anyway.
She waves her arms a little to emphasize her point, which has the side effect of showing off a particular part of her body that would be especially restricted by the blouse.
We both begin walking back to the main building through the gardens, talking as we do so.
It sounds like you're adjusting well. That's a relief. It was quite a surprise to receive a transfer student at this point in the year, considering that exams are approaching.
Don't remind me...
Haha, don't worry about them. Just study everything a day before and you'll be fine.
That doesn't sound like good advice.
She taps my shoulder a few times while smiling. I don't think she takes school very seriously.
You look like a smart guy, and Mutou has already had his eye on you. You fit like a glove.
Now to decide if that is a good or bad thing.
I still don't know what to think of this school. I've been here a few weeks now, but I still feel confused sometimes.
You'll get used to it, just give it a little time. It's just a high school, like any other.

She makes it sound so simple, but I've never thought about it that way. For me, Yamaku symbolized a marked change in my life. It was no longer normal; He was “different,” and he was going to be educated with other “different” people.
yumi_a3_seq_7: And yet, I'm walking back to class and casually talking to a classmate during lunch, after watching others play a game of soccer. Everything perfectly normal. Maybe he's right.
Maybe I should just see Yumi the same way. Everyone has their own problems; this is hardly something unique to Yamaku. After all, it's just a high school, like any other.
As we continue talking, I find myself smiling. Miki and I are different people in almost everything, but it feels good to have been able to get to know another classmate a little better.
A light breeze blows the scent of early summer through my head as I wait for Elena.
Small white clouds spread across the sky, breaking the monotony of the blue.
Hisao? Are you here?
Elena's voice dances in the breeze as if they were both one and the same.
I stop watching the sky to examine Elena.
Wearing a peach off-the-shoulder sweater and tan ankle-length skirt, along with two tan sandals, she's a delight to see.
Yes, I'm here, Elena. Near the gate.
Did you manage to escape from Yumi?
Yes. It's not unusual for me to go out on the weekends, so I don't think I've noticed anything strange.
That, and… she has someone she sees.
Elena purses her lips, as if perhaps she shouldn't have continued. I find it a little hard to believe.
Is Yumi seeing someone? Actually?
No, it's just...she sees a therapist occasionally on the weekends.
Oh. Well. That makes a lot of sense.
Elena rubs her arm in discomfort, and after a glance at her worried expression, I quickly move to change the topic away from Yumi.
Eeh…
Yes?
I was just wondering…can you handle yourself in the city?
Elena sighs at my dismay on the subject of her blindness. I am my own worst enemy, sometimes.
I can, yes. Although it's easier when I go out with a friend or my sister.
I wonder how Elena gets along with her sister. Being an only child, it's hard to imagine what it would be like to have a brother, so that makes me a little envious of her.
Very good. Well then, the bus is coming in a few minutes, so we should probably go.
TRUE; It's a long wait if we lose this one.
With that, we set off towards the bus stop on the hill. It's just a short distance from the school gate, so it's very convenient.
It's a good view from here. Coming from the city, I never really got to see a landscape like this, let alone do it on a daily basis.
This area is nice to me too. It is quiet, and away from the noises and smells of the city.
Elena's head lifts animatedly with one of her characteristic personal gestures, signifying that she has picked up a sound.
Oh, here comes the bus…
I look down the road to see the bus rolling up the hill. Your ear is a pretty useful tool.
It only takes the bus a little while to reach the stop, forcing its way up the road, and in less than a minute we are on our way to the city.
Walking through the city I feel a distinct nostalgia. The smells, the traffic, the tall buildings everywhere… it's pretty much like my native city, except for the elevated walkways.
It feels a little strange; walking through the city as casually as I would through the park, but with speeding cars passing beneath me.
While I am absorbed in reflecting on the engineering marvel that is the elevated walker, I receive a surprise.
It takes me a moment to realize that Elena has embraced my arm with hers, extending her staff in front of her with her other hand.

It startles me for a moment, but I manage to keep it hidden enough so that Elena doesn't notice. Although it was not the first time that Elena has trusted me as a guide, before she had only clung to the cuff of my sleeve.
It stands to reason that it would be easier for her to navigate a crowded, complex area like the city while securely attached, but I'm far from as accustomed to this type of contact as Elena is.
Finally realizing the growing silence between us as Elena waits for me to move forward, I quickly put my brain into gear.
You know, it was quite a surprise that Yumi likes to sing. Have you ever heard her do it?
In fact yes. We have been to karaoke sessions several times, together with my sister. I can't say that I'm very enthusiastic about the activity, but the other two like it.
Maybe Yumi doing karaoke is more appropriate than I initially thought. Just her and those she knows, all alone in a small room.
It would provide her with a rare opportunity to let her guard down, with no one else there to judge her.
Maybe it would be nice to bring her into town for a birthday karaoke party, if she's into that.
yumi_a3_seq_8: Hmm. I'm not sure I could handle the emotion very well.
I prepare to protest, but his face shows that he is still mulling over the proposition some more. It takes him a little time to come to a conclusion.
On the other hand, the best thing we can do for Yumi at this point is try to create some pleasant birthday memories. Continually treating her as if she is abnormal will not help.
I think you are right; If she has something to remember other than losses, maybe she will change.
If we bought her something nice that she could see every day then maybe she would be able to get her mind off the past and remember that she has friends.
And in any case, I think Yumi can handle something like this. In the time I've spent with him, I've learned that he's not as terribly fragile as I initially thought he was.
So, shall we leave? I'm not really sure about the layout of this area.
Very good. I would like to suggest first going for something to eat.
I haven't eaten either, so that sounds like a good plan.
Make sure you choose a good place, Hisao.
She gives me a playful smile, one that makes me smile reflexively in response even if she can't see that.
I will absolutely make sure that is the case, don't worry about that.
Once inside, I order two slices of cake and cups of tea to go with it and take them to our table.
I had labeled this coffee as the type Elena would like; small and quiet, but well maintained and somewhat elegant. Judging by the delicate smile she has, I think... I don't know if I chose well.
It's very, very strange not to see her smiling, after all.
However, I take a seat near her at one of the corner tables and place our food.
Elena delicately brings her head over the slice of cake placed in front of her, delicately taking in the aroma.
Lemon pie, right? Thank you, Hisao.
No problem. The tea is right next to her, so be careful not to spill it.
She nods appreciatively, but judging by the slightly weak smile she has, the warning wasn't really necessary. I guess the sound must have given him a clue to his position.
We both begin to eat without further ado, remaining fairly silent as we do so. Elena isn't the type to appreciate arguing while eating, and I can't say I like that either.
Eventually we both finish our meals, and the last of our cups of tea follow shortly after. Elena is the first to break the silence.
That was very good. I must say that you have chosen quite well, Hisao.
This is the first time I've been able to take a look at the city, so all I could really do was pick a place that looked good.
Uh…damn. I'm sorry.

I feel really bad for inadvertently bringing up the topic of the view in Elena's presence, but she doesn't seem to care much. On the contrary; She seems almost amused by my clumsy attempt at apologizing.
You are thoughtful, Hisao, but sometimes I fear that it gets the best of you. There is no need to change your way of speaking for the sake of me.
Elena is actually very carefree when discussing her condition. Still, I hasten to change the subject, since I can't really say that I share your familiarity with that issue.
Have you lived here long? It seems like you know this place very well.
He quickly waves his hand in front of his face to dismiss that notion.
Nothing like that. I have attended Yamaku since the beginning of high school, but I didn't walk around town much because Akira, my sister, would pick me up and drop me off.
Oh, right. You mentioned not living in the dorms until recently.
It's quite a surprise. I assumed he had been living here at least since entering Yamaku, which would make for a few years here.
I have lived with my family most of my life, then I was only with my sister. With my family moving to Inverness a while ago, and Akira working longer hours, I ended up having to move.
Inverness? Isn't that somewhere in Scotland?
Oh, didn't I tell you? My family currently lives in Scotland, my mother's birthplace. But my father's side is mainly Japanese.
Hey. The question of why Elena looks like that crossed my mind several times, but I never thought to ask. So that answers that.
To be honest, I would never have guessed. Considering you don't have an accent, I'm assuming you were born here?
You got it right. Although I am grateful for my heritage, since without it I would not have been taught English at such a young age.
And what about you, Hisao?
What about me?
He thinks about it for a moment. He probably should have thought about what to ask before changing the subject.
I'm going to go with... what are your plans for the future?
To be honest, I haven't thought about it much recently.
After my accident and the subsequent months in the hospital, enjoying my life here with you and Yumi has been enough for me.
yumi_a3_seq_9: In fact, I don't think I've thought about a “future” at all for some time now. It almost seems futile.
This is your last year of school. After this, you'll have to fend for yourself one way or another.
It's not like I don't know, I just haven't thought about it enough...
She opens her mouth to continue, but instead gives a small sigh. He seems to realize that he doesn't really know enough about my situation to delve deeper into this.
Well, we all have our own rhythm. I just hope you'll take any opportunity you see.
… I understand. I'll think about it.
As we walk out into the city, Elena takes me by the arm once again.
So, have you come up with some good gift ideas?
To be honest, no. I've never been very good at picking them out.
As absurd as it sounds, maybe we should just… look around?
Hearing Elena say those words throws me off balance for a moment.
Uh… good. How do we do that?
That's exactly the reaction I was expecting. It's simple; You can go looking at showcases and just tell me what's there.
If something interesting comes up, then we could start there.
Well… I'm not really sure about this yet, but I'll take your word for it.
I think we'll manage. Yumi, my sister, and I manage quite well.
With Elena's simple and quite optimistic statement, we set off towards the commercial district of the city and I begin to describe to Elena everything I see.

It's hard to imagine Yumi going window shopping in stores. She doesn't look like the type that places a lot of value on fashion, nor have I seen her flipping through magazines or anything like that. In fact, I think really all I've seen her do as a hobby is read.
There is a household utensils store ahead. But it seems like they are tableware more than anything.
I don't think she has much need for something like that, and what kind of message would that send her?
Um… “cook more food”? That's not such a bad idea, maybe...
Sometimes it's better to leave things alone, Hisao.
Once again, I get the feeling that Yumi's exploits in the kitchen aren't always successful. Elena must have had to help her with that sometimes.
Let's see, the next one is a bookstore... that seems like a good option, she is always reading.
Yes, but there are some problems with the books. I'm not really sure what you have and haven't read.
How about a gift card then?
There's nothing as impersonal as giving someone a gift card. It's like saying “I don't know enough about you to imagine what you would like to receive.”
I always thought of it as making sure they would get what they wanted.
Giving people gifts should show the level of affection you have for them. If you can't decide on a simple gift for them, then how much could you think about them?
True, true, no gift cards.
Elena seems overly passionate about this, but I can see her point. If you are going to find something for someone, then you should put at least a little bit of brain into it.
If I want to find something for Yumi to remind her of us every day, then how good is a gift card?
In that case, what did you give Yumi last year?
A porcelain doll. I thought that if I had someone to talk to, I could help ease the pain.
A doll is never going to criticize her, after all.
So should I look for a gift shop?
If you could be so kind as to keep an eye out for one, I would be very grateful.
Sounds good to me, although I wish you had mentioned it sooner.
But if I had, then you wouldn't have started thinking for yourself, would you?
Once again Elena has a point. My brain is currently scanning every store we pass for gift options. If Elena had mentioned a doll store from the beginning, I wouldn't have thought of anything else.
We wander the streets of the city, but we seem unable to find anything resembling a doll store, or anything we would consider a worthy gift.
The simple act of searching is starting to clear my head. The events of last week are starting to fade, and I can't wait to give Yumi her gift...
…if I can find any.
This is useless. I thought it was certain we could find something in the city. And I'm sure we've walked through this street at least once before.
That sounds like you're almost giving up, Hisao.
yumi_a3_seq_10: I'm not, but it's a lot harder than I thought.
Try not to be so rigid with your ideas. Maybe we should actually go into some stores and look around?
That could work. I've never been very good at window shopping.
Elena and I walk through the streets of the city once again, but this time entering the stores that catch our attention. In the end, however, nothing comes across as particularly appropriate.
Yumi's tastes are often difficult to identify when it suits us best, thanks to her intensely secretive nature, and those tastes we do know are difficult to accommodate.
Could we take a break for a minute? I'm a little exhausted.
I agree with Elena and let her rest against a railing while I go get a couple of drinks from a nearby vending machine.

After walking to the vending machine and grabbing some lemonade for myself, I find myself a little lost. Not really knowing Elena's tastes, I decide to guess and grab something that looks a little girly, but not too strange.
Strawberry flavored milk.
I returned.
I walk over to her and place the cardboard into her outstretched hands, making sure she has grabbed it before letting it go.
She feels its contours before opening it and taking a very hesitant sip, her immediate approving smile telling me I made the right choice. We both rest and drink quietly for a few minutes.
A familiar light chime begins to sound from Elena's side. She quickly apologizes as her hand goes to her bag, pulling out her cell phone.
Do you mind if I take this call?
It's ok don't worry.
She thanks him by bowing her head before turning around and opening the phone, bringing it to the side of her face as she answers the call.

From the tone of Elena's voice, the person on the other end of the phone is undoubtedly a friend or similar. I tune out their conversation quickly, as the fragments Elena says make it sound like little more than gossip.

With nothing else to do, I find myself looking at Elena. She really is a pretty girl, which would hardly affect her popularity at school. It's interesting how much Yumi and Elena contrast with each other, both in personality and appearance.

For a few minutes I just lean back and drink, looking at her. Not long after, Elena says goodbye to the person she's talking to and hangs up, leaving her phone back in her bag and leaning against the railing like before.
Sorry, just a friend from class.
I take one last swig from my can before tossing it in the trash. Shortly after Elena gives me her container to throw away, finishing it relatively quickly.
You seem to have a lot of friends.
Oh?
Elena waits for him to finish, catching his interest.
I was just thinking that you and Yumi really contrast a lot. It's hard to imagine Yumi doing many of the things you do, or meeting the people you know.
You seem to think about Yumi quite a bit.
Don't know. It's just... it's mysterious, I guess. I kind of want to know more about her, which isn't easy to say.
It almost sounds like you're doubting your relationship with her.
I don't think that's it. I just want to do more for her, being her friend and all. I don't even really know how she sees me.
This statement seems to interest Elena somewhat. I wonder if Yumi has said something about me to Elena during their conversations.
I'm about to ask her what's on her mind when she pulls away from the railing.
Should we leave then?
His voice and expression show me that he is playing with me. Elena knows damn well that she's leaving me flying.
With a sigh, I also move away from the railing and take a quick look around. We have things to do, so I'll just try to get her back to this later.
Sandwiched between a newsstand and a convenience store is a small store. The sign above the door says “Othello Antiques” in English decorative script.
It would be easy to miss if we were walking down the street, but since we're standing still and I'm looking around deliberately, it's just noticeable.
Tell me, Elena... that doll you gave to Yumi; Was it new?
Well, yes, but I'm not really sure what you mean.
I think I found our store. He's crossing the street.
Oh? What is it? Some kind of toy store?
It's an antique store. I think that will probably be our best bet.
Actually? I didn't even know we had one of those near here.
Me neither, I missed it the first time we were here. It's pretty well hidden.
Well then, it can't hurt to review.
Inspired by this new find, we quickly dusted ourselves off and headed to the store, Elena's hand reaching for my elbow to guide her.
elena_seq_1: I wake up to the annoying blare of my alarm clock, its bright red numbers lighting up my face.
It's the same alarm clock I had at home, one of the few artifacts left from my days before coming to Yamaku. I was hoping that using it would help ease my transition into this new life.
However, I have no such luck.
Crawling sleepily out of bed, I wipe the sleep from my eyes, and then extend my arm toward the desk. I open a couple of medicine bottles scattered around it, and swallow a few pills dry.
Already the process is starting to become automatic, something I should be happy about, given its purpose.
Feeling much more awake than before, I head to the bathroom.
As the shower heats up, my mind begins to wander as I begin my new daily routine once again.
The bright colors of the fireworks fill my mind, as do the two girls I spent time with watching them. It feels strange to be so moved by such unknown people.
Then again, I guess these aren't normal circumstances either. At least I have someone to talk to now, besides my fellow neighbor.
With the time left before today's classes dwindling, I begin to prepare to leave.
Walking through the door to enter the living room, I notice that I have arrived a little early. I see about five or six students milling around, most of them looking like they'd rather stay in bed.
In times like these, I'm grateful that I'm a morning person. That said, two students in particular look as lively as ever.
Hi Shizune, hi Shiina.
I suddenly realize that my greeting won't be received by the first person, so I quickly follow it up with a hand sign. She doesn't seem too bothered.
Nor interested.
Hello, Hicchan~! Do you feel good?
I can only assume that his greeting comes from Shizune. Sometimes it's hard to tell if she's speaking as herself or as Shizune.
Better than most others, I think. You two seem happy and lively.
Shiina plays Shizune as I speak, getting a slightly gruff response, if the quick, sharp movements of her arms are any indication.
Considering that the two of them placed so much importance on the festival preparations, I probably should have chosen my words more carefully.
Since you're a new student, we've been giving you a break. Please don't expect this type of homework evasion to be allowed in the future.
Shiina appears to be about to add her own comment, but quickly reverts to Shizune as she continues, not stopping.
Although your contribution to the 3-2 group position is appreciated—
Huh. That news did spread quite quickly. That, or these two are on top of everything at school.
—We would prefer that your efforts be focused on the task at hand. Specifically, your own group.
Although I hate to admit it, they are right. However, before he could answer, Shizune adds something else, which makes Shiina smile.
So did you enjoy the festival~?
The sermon is over, I think.
Yes, it was good. Did you two enjoy it?
Shizune nods briefly while Shiina smiles and makes her head pop. The comparison, side by side, is funny.
Out of the corner of my eye, I notice that more students begin to slip into the classroom. A quick glance at my watch confirms that they are a few minutes late.
I look over at Yumi's seat and notice that she's already there, and she's quietly reading a book. It makes me wonder how long it's been there without me noticing.
With heavy footsteps coming from the hallway signaling Mutou's arrival, our talk ends and I sit next to Shiina.
When the door opens, he walks in with a lethargic gait. His posture is even worse than usual, and his eyes are barely open. I guess the joke I told Elena and Yumi about the staff was out of line.
Everyone opens their books as he reaches his desk, and the first class of the new week begins.
I rub my eyes as the lunch bell rings, content with the temporary break from work.
I'm not surprised at all when I look at the door and see Elena standing there, cane in hand, patiently waiting for Yumi.
Considering their approval of my request to join them yesterday, I decide to spend my lunch hour with them instead of eating alone.
Yumi moves surprisingly quickly to greet her companion, and the two enter the hallway before she can catch up to them.
Elena turns her head slightly, registering the sound of footsteps behind her. When Yumi notices him and follows his movement, she almost jumps in surprise.
Hi… Hisao?
I mean… um… hello, Hisao…
Hello. Sorry if I scared you.
Elena turns to greet me, her orientation aided by Yumi.
Good afternoon, Hisao. Will you join us?
elena_seq_2: If it's not a bother. There really isn't much else to do.
Elena nods slightly, as if to silently push away any thoughts that she might cause trouble in the slightest.
We descend a set of stairs and walk down the hallway toward the usual room, our pace a bit quicker thanks to Elena using Yumi to orient herself, instead of her cane and the railings.
As we expected, it is empty. The sounds of the other clubs can barely be heard as light enters the room from outside.
Searching the room, I notice a pair of empty easels leaning against a wall that I don't think were there before. The art club should use this room as an additional storage room.
Shall I take out the chess game?
Yumi's voice seems less strained when she's speaking directly to Elena.
Yes. I'll make tea while you put the pieces together.
Oh, I can do that for you, if you want.
I consider the offer for a moment before smiling, confirming that I've made the right decision. His face is surprisingly easy to read.
Very good. Thank you.
She slides her folded cane through the handle of her bag and rests it against one of the table legs, before taking a seat opposite Yumi.
As I make tea for the three of us, I can hear the small pieces of wood being placed on the board. I wonder how good Elena is at chess, considering her circumstances.
When I finally put the steaming cups of tea on the table, Elena and Yumi have already moved their first pieces while nibbling on sandwiches and rice balls from their respective bags.
I notice that the chess board they are using has gaps in the middle of each square and pegs under the pieces, and that each dark square is raised a little.

Watching Elena's fingers slide over the board, tracing the positions of the pieces, makes me marvel a little at the simple ingenuity of the design. It must have been made specifically for blind players.
Here you go.
Yumi nods slightly when I place a cup on her side of the board. Elena's hand extends slightly, so I place her cup so it touches her fingertips; a gesture that seems appreciated.
I finally take a seat and sip my tea in silence while the two play. It's interesting to watch the contrast in their appearances as they concentrate.
Yumi looks closely at the board, her face showing focused concentration. Elena, on the other hand, keeps her face calm and preserves her serene neutrality.
Elena's soft voice drifts towards the two of us as she continues to play.
How did your classes go, since the festival is over?
I look at Yumi to see if she will answer first, but I see that she is doing the same.
Not very well. Half the group seemed to be dozing, even the teacher. Not to mention that there was also an exam.
Yumi agrees with this quietly.
I can imagine that being somewhat difficult for you, being a transfer student.
Well, I think I did well. Aside from the shock of having a test so early, science is probably my best subject.
How did it go for you, Yumi?
Me? Ah… well… I guess…
Yumi is too sincere to be able to lie very well. At least that's obvious.
Elena's smile falls ever so slightly. From her reaction, Yumi must not be academically skilled enough to do well without preparation.
How did your group handle it, Elena?
In fact, we did surprisingly well. Only one student was missing, so it was better than the teacher expected.
With the topic practically exhausted, the two concentrate once again on their chess game.
I can't say I've ever liked the idea of ​​chess as a spectacle sport, but given its unique nature, this time I'm enthralled watching the game unfold.
As time goes on, they both demonstrate decent gaming ability. Having captured two more pawns than Yumi, Elena has the lead, but only by a little.
…Until Yumi makes a strange move with her queen. Taking advantage of this lapse in judgment, Elena captures the piece with her horse.
Without hesitation, Yumi moves a pawn to capture Elena's rook on the opposite side of the board, promoting her to queen.

Elena's face falls as her fingers move over the pieces and she realizes that she has just fallen into Yumi's trap. It is somewhat distracting to have to draw the board after each move, even if it is out of necessity.
Judging by Yumi's lack of reaction, she must be used to this. She and Elena must have played at least a few games with each other, after all.
Check.
That's not bad at all. Okay, Yumi.
The compliment makes her face bloom with a surprised blush.
G-thank you. I didn't... think it was going to work.
She looked at Elena, her fingers just finishing tracing the position of her remaining pieces in an attempt to get her king out of this bind.
elena_seq_3: I think it's checkmate...
Hmm?
I take another look at the dashboard to confirm it.
Indeed, his king has nowhere to escape without being threatened by another piece. My question from before about which of the two is better at this has just been answered.
That's how it is.
Elena lets out a light sigh as Yumi smiles. From your reactions, this seems like a pretty usual outcome.
How long have they been playing?
Since... I was little.
Elena nods at Yumi's brief response.
Yumi taught me how to play shortly after I met her. I can defeat her from time to time... but that's a rarity. It seems like I don't have the right mindset for it.
If Elena came to Yamaku at the beginning of high school, and met Yumi when she moved into the dorms, that means she has only played for a year.
After seeing Yumi's level of play, I'm not really surprised that Elena has trouble defeating her.
But… she is better with languages than me, so…
Elena lets out an appreciative, if somewhat amused, smile at Yumi's quick reversal of her compliment.
Well, that's right.
To everyone's surprise, the bell suddenly rings, announcing the end of lunch time.
Hmm, that match lasted longer than I thought.
Yes. I think we better go back to class.
Yumi is already putting everything away, so I take Elena's bag and offer it to her. To my surprise, she receives it and nods, but then places it back on the table.
Hisao, can I order something?
Sure, go ahead.
Would you mind if I briefly touched your face?
Oh, uh... no, go ahead. It doesn't bother me.
The question takes me seriously by surprise, but as I regain my composure, it seems reasonable enough. So far Elena has no idea what I look like, and this would be her only way to find out.
Elena raises her right hand, which I take in mine and guide it to my face before releasing it.
The room falls completely silent as Elena's hand moves and runs over my features, from my chin, to my cheeks, to everything else.
I expected this to feel a lot more disturbing than it does. I suppose it's because the action is entirely a matter of practicality, being functionally the same as looking at someone's face.

His hand is soft, but what takes me by surprise is the length of his fingers, not to mention how confident even the slightest of his movements are. I have no doubt that your level of tactile sensation is much better than mine.

His hand briefly runs through my hair once before pulling away. I imagine that every inch of my face has been saved in his memory. And it's also now that I realize that Yumi has been silently watching the entire time.
Thanks for letting me do that, Hisao.
And if I must add, I think you are quite handsome.
I blush a little at his comment, before raising an eyebrow in question.
But if you can't see, how...?
Just because I can't see, doesn't mean I don't have my preferences.
Ahh, we should go now...
True, you are right. So I guess we'll see you later, Elena.
Walking through the hallways back to our own classrooms, I notice that Yumi seems quieter than before, but also more comfortable.
Elena, with her hand on Yumi's shoulder, also seems to notice her confident step, smiling as they walk.
If I could spend the rest of my time in Yamaku this way, I don't think it would be so bad. All it takes to be joyful are small exchanges of happiness, after all.
When I get to my bench and place my bag next to it, I realize something. Or rather, my stomach does.
I was so busy with the two of them that I forgot to buy lunch...
Saturday. My second favorite day of the week.
This is almost entirely due to the fact that it is the second day with fewer classes, since they end at the beginning of lunch.
I open my door with confidence, myself being more than confident that I will be able to enjoy the good weather and the shorter class period.
I walk confidently down the hallway and down the stairs to the hallway of the boys' dormitories.
elena_seq_4: I confidently look behind me to see who the approaching footsteps belong to.
And… I lose my confidence that this day will be pleasant.
Hey man. What's going on?
Not much I guess, just waiting for the afternoon to arrive. You?
He wraps his arm around my slumped shoulders a little too comfortably. Something happens.
Let's go outside, shall we?
That's what I was doing before you stopped me.
He doesn't take kindly to my reaction to his theatrics. Ignoring him, I walk outside and start down the steps.
It doesn't take him long to catch up to me again. I wonder if he wants money, or ranting about another conspiracy. Maybe both.
I have some unfinished business with you.
Aha.
It's about that blonde. You know who I'm talking about.
A conspiracy, then. For a moment I consider feigning ignorance, but I realize this will be over faster if I just let him let it all out.
Elena? The one in your group?
Are you already calling her by her name?!
He seems truly shocked by this development. I didn't expect you to be able to respond?
He regains his composure and coughs into his fist. Dramatically, like everything he does.
Well, never mind that. I'm here to warn you. You know. From man to man.
Warn me about what? Elena?
Clear. You don't know her, man.
That's more or less true. I've only known her and Yumi for less than two weeks, and even then we've only chatted superficially about school over lunch.
I'm pretty sure you don't either.
That's not the point. You are the one spending excessive amounts of time with her.
It distresses me that someone like Kenji, who is probably as uninformed as one can be, knows about a fact as trivial as who I choose to be friends with.
On the other hand… I am a transfer student, and she is not only the representative of her class, but also a tall blonde.
Perhaps I should appreciate this sermon as a warning that the rumor mill also exists in this school, and that I am firmly embedded within it.
It's just lunch. Nothing special.
Look, man, under the bridge. Do you see this bridge? You are under it. A man has to do what a man has to do to get information.
I just want to make sure you don't end up too far under the bridge.
You're losing me, Kenji.
It's okay, a lot of people get lost. That's why I'm here to help.
Just be careful with her, okay? She seems harmless on the outside, but I've heard shit. Serious shit.
You know the student council, right?
He seems to shudder involuntarily as he says those words. Having him and Shizune together in a room is an entertaining mental exercise. I wonder if they know each other.
Sure, Shizune and Shiina are in my group. Although I think I evaded being drafted.
Good man. Good man.
But what about this blonde? She was there. In the student council. Fair. In. It.
I see. AND?
And now she's not there.
Seriously, think about it. Something must have happened.
I stop walking for a moment, thinking more carefully than I should about the idea.
That would explain the fight they had, at least in part. Wait, no, not really. Even leaving the student council would require a catalyst.
Anyway, it doesn't explain much at all. Apart from the fact that their feud has been going on for a while now.
I guess you're right. I don't see how that really affects me though.
Well, now answer this one. Elena is a foreigner, obviously.
elena_seq_5: Obviously.
Now, what nationality do you have?
I open my mouth to give an answer, but realize I don't have one. In fact, I haven't thought much about the topic.
Since she doesn't have an accent and acts perfectly Japanese, I guess it's never really seemed important to me. Although now that you mention it, I'm a little curious.
To be honest with you, I don't know. Maybe English? They like tea.
I probably shouldn't resort to stereotypes, but that's the only clue I have.
You're not thinking. Luckily, you have me here to think for you.
Geez, thanks.
He ignores grace without problems.
Now answer me this: Who has a ton of social power, is filthy rich—you know blondes are all rich, right?—has a long history of feuds, and used to belong to a larger organization?
The Holy Roman Catholic Church?
… Well, yes, there is that one.
But there is also the Mafia. Come on. Rich, foreign, there's no way I don't have connections with them.
I have reason to doubt the logic of his deductions, but he doesn't seem ready to stop.
So do you know where I think it's from?
Italy?
Mainland Italy is small time, man. She has to be from Sicily. All those gangsters come from there.
Wait, no, Russia. Damn, this could be bad. The Mafia there is something serious, man; Ex-KGB everywhere, paramilitaries, serious smuggling, and—
Wait, wait, stop, just calm down for a second. What are you trying to get at with this?
You don't know what he's going to do, man. I won't stand in your way—we agents don't operate like that—but I just want you to be careful.
When the time comes, we will need all the help there is. I don't want to lose you, comrade.
Well, at least he cares about me. Something like that.
I say goodbye to him as we walk to our respective classes, but I'm not sure he sees the gesture.
Piling my books into my bag, I briefly glance at the library books I borrowed last week. Maybe I'll return them, since it only took me two days to finish them.
For a moment, I consider inviting Yumi to the library, but she's already gone. It's probably better for my studies if I'm alone anyway.
Stretching briefly and waving goodbye to a couple of colleagues who respond in kind, I make my way out of the room.

As I open my backpack and toss the books through the returns box at the front counter, I notice a strange person behind the desk. Old and gray-haired, she must be Yuuko's replacement when it's her turn to work at the cafe.
I start looking for an available table, a bit of a difficult task given that, despite there not being many students around, everyone is sitting at their own tables.
I notice a familiar mop of hair, and walk toward one near the braille section.
It's hard to tell whether Elena is concentrating hard or not, her relaxed expression staying perfectly still as her fingers trace the book's dotted pages.
Hello. Do you mind if I sit here?
Hmm? Oh, I don't care at all...
Her words trail off, evidently still focused on her business.
Ah, Hisao.
She greets with a nod as I sit opposite her at the table, grab a chemistry book from my backpack and quickly jump to the chapter we're looking at in class.
For a while, we sat there and read, each in our own way.
However, seeing it reminds me of what Kenji said this morning. That and the fact that I'd never seen anyone read braille before made me keep casting glances her way.
I feel a little guilty about it, since she has no way of realizing what I'm doing, so I decide to just ask her about it.
His lineage isn't exactly a state secret, after all, and there's another thing I just noticed about his movements.
Hey, Elena, do you mind if I ask you a question?
Not at all. Is something wrong?
Just wondering… you're at least part foreign, right?
She giggles before putting down her book.
It's always amused me how squeamish people are about that. Akira mentioned before how different she and I are from the rest.
The details are a bit complicated, but I'm half Japanese, half Scottish.
