elena_seq_6: …Scottish? That wasn't exactly my first assumption. It's a little hard for me not to say it out loud.
I try to conjure images of the place in my mind. I think as far as the UK goes, Scotland isn't a bad place to live... but I'm actually not sure.
My first guess of England was surprisingly close, at least geographically. Although that leaves another question.
But you don't have an accent...
That's where the details begin. I was born and raised in Japan, even though my mother was a foreigner.
Oh, I understand.
Wait, she only moved into the dorms because Akira started working longer hours…
So you don't live near the school?
She lets out a light sigh, as if she didn't expect him to go any further. Was his previous candor nothing more than a facade?
Not quite. It's been a long time since we saw each other.
I feel like I don't know the full story, but I really don't want to intrude too much on your situation. Her change of attitude shows that she feels a little uncomfortable about it.
So… do you speak a lot of English? To be honest I don't know much about Scotland, but at least I know that's the main language there.
It takes him a moment to regain his composure, appreciating the change of topic.
That's how it is. My family mainly used Japanese at home when I was young, but they made sure Akira and I got to know our Scottish side too.
I am fluent in the language, but I am also studying it at school. To maintain my skills and to have the requirements on paper, mainly.
So you are bilingual? That's pretty impressive.
I wouldn't say that much. Having parents who can speak the language is a big advantage, and English braille books are not that difficult to buy or import. With Yuuko's help, at least.
Anyway, there is a relatively high demand for local English teachers here, which also serves as my motivation to learn.
Demand for English teachers? For a moment, I wonder why he mentioned this.
Do you plan to be an English teacher?
She nods enthusiastically.
It must be good, to have such a defined future in mind. I've never given mine much thought, so I'm a little envious.
Hmm…
What happened?
It's just... I can easily see you as a teacher. It suits you well.
For a moment, she is speechless. She lowers her face slightly and gives a nervous giggle, something I've never seen her do before.
With Elena's role as a class representative and her trustworthy nature, teaching seems to be the appropriate field of work for her personality.
Sorry, maybe I said something too much. Anyway, it's the truth.
Waving his hand in front of his face as if it didn't matter, he quickly recovers.
It's not that, it's just... only one person has ever said that to me before.
A brief, awkward silence follows the discussion. Without realizing it, I ended up reaching a problematic topic again.
I should try to cheer her up a little. I was the one who made her melancholy, after all.
Do you want to go to the cafeteria for lunch after this?
It might cheer her up a bit, or at least take her mind off her seemingly complicated family situation.
Judging by his smile, it seems to have had the desired effect.
I appreciate the gesture, but the food there…
What a change in the direction of the conversation. Although you're right, the food there isn't the best.
Maybe Shanghai? We could ask Yumi if she wants to come too.
What happened?
I almost forgot, until you reminded me. Yumi's birthday is coming soon, and tomorrow I was planning to go shopping in the city to find her a gift.
If that's an invitation, I'd love to join you.
The opportunity to get more used to the layout of the city will probably be useful. I've barely set foot in that place, so on my own I would be hopelessly lost.
She nods, signaling that she happily accepts this plan for Sunday.
Eventually we continue with our books, although before starting to read again I take one last look at her.
Maybe I've been thinking too much about my own situation. After all, everyone here must have their own unique circumstances.
elena_seq_7: The chance to get out and clear my head will probably do me some good.
Bored of standing in one place and watching television in a store window, I turn away from the vulgar screen without much effort.
After living in Yamaku, the city seems like a completely different world.
Nobody runs through the hallways. One must behave in a calm and orderly manner at all times in the classrooms. Students must leave the rooms after checking in both directions for anyone approaching.
Elevators are reserved for students with movement difficulties. Single file on the stairs.
Compared to such strict, almost regimental standards, the city's shopping arcade could well be a strange country.
Although the school may have its share of hubbub during the festival, the world outside is very different.
It's strange. Having lived in a metropolitan city before my accident, this should feel more natural than Yamaku and the surrounding town could.
Yet it feels strange, somehow. The elevated walkways and buildings, each adorned with billboards taller than three people, do little to distract me from the reactions of the surrounding crowd.
Elena keeps one hand on my shoulder, the other holding her cane that taps the floor with the regularity of a metronome. When I look at her, I see that neutral smile of hers still remains.

Having only seen her in her school uniform, I wouldn't have recognized her when she was sitting on a bench waiting for me, if it weren't for her cane leaning against the bench and her distinctive hair.
I can't tell if they're looking at her askance because of her height, her foreign appearance, her obvious blindness, or all three. None of those would make the situation any less awkward than it is.
Do you have any idea where to look first, Hisao?
His soft voice makes me lose track of what I was thinking.
I can't imagine she fails to notice the attention she's getting, but she seems to remain unfazed. I have a feeling she's the type who enjoys walking outside, so she may be used to it by now.
Not really. It's my first time in this city, so I have no idea where to go.
She frowns thoughtfully, planning a route we can take. And, now that I think about it, a way to communicate it.
Something I've noticed in my time with her is how, when she's deep in thought, she lacks almost any form of body language to show it.
His expression changes, but there is no trace of movement. Although she generally doesn't seem to have much in the way of dramatic physical gestures, so I've assumed it's part of her reserved nature.
Is there a big box electronics store near here?
I quickly look around, finding mainly clothing stores. After a few seconds I notice a store with a bright blue sign somewhat far away that meets its description.
Yup, it's a little further ahead. Are we going there?
Luckily, it's just the information she needed. At her nod, we began walking and headed towards Elena's unknown destination, guided by landmarks.
Here you go. One vanilla, one chocolate.
I hand the money on the counter and carry the cones to the railing where Elena is sitting.
I can't believe I let her fool me like that. She not only led me to an ice cream stand, but also made me buy one for her. At least he gave me the money for his.
As I assumed, she is there waiting patiently where I left her. I guess I was planning to make the day an event rather than just a shopping trip.
I call to her and slowly place the vanilla cone in her outstretched hands, taking care to make sure she has taken it firmly before releasing it.
At least his tastes are quite normal. I was worried that he would ask for some strange flavor when he asked me.
Here is the change.
Okay, keep it.
I'm about to complain, but I realize the futility of doing that for such a small amount. I keep the coin in my pocket, supplementing my meager allowance even if just barely.
Elena doesn't seem to want to get up, so I sit next to her and start eating my own ice cream.
The summer weather is pleasant. With any luck it will continue like this for a while.
You too? I'm starting to think I'm the only person who prefers winter.
I contemplate his statement for a long time.
Yes, maybe so.
I achieve the desired reaction. She's cute when she pouts.
Still, I can't really imagine what's so good about winter. You can't go out without dressing warm, and you freeze anyway.
I used to live further north where there was a lot of snow to play in, so it's a bit nostalgic. I don't like the heat very much either.
At least you can wear a skirt, so don't complain about it.
She giggles amusedly as we both continue finishing our already melted ice cream cones.
I sit idly and watch the crowd pass by while we eat, listening to snatches of conversation.
Looking at Elena, I can see her diligently licking her ice cream from the tip down, blissfully unaware of the fact that it has started to melt.
It's melting.
elena_seq_8: Where?
Um… a little lower?
She lowers her mouth from the top of the cone, but has no idea where exactly the ice cream is dripping. What follows is a game of guiding her left and right until she finally finds it.
To any onlooker, it must seem totally strange, a girl with her eyes closed spinning her cone over and over while the boy next to her gives instructions.
Perhaps a strange variant of blindfolded children's games.
Finally we finished our ice creams, and let the time pass by chatting casually.
In the middle of a sentence, Elena raises her head in her typical manner. It is an unmistakable sign that something has caught your attention.
What happened?
Is Akira there? I think I heard her.
I raise an eyebrow as I look in the direction she's pointing, somewhat doubtful of her ability to pick out Akira's lone voice among the din.
But sure enough, a blonde girl dressed in a suit can be seen through the small gaps between people walking in any direction.
I raise a hand and wave, trying to get his attention.
Satou! Hey Satou!
She stops completely and looks up at me, evidently noticing my calls. At the same time, I notice someone walking next to her.
I can't see who the unknown person is, but they have both started walking towards us.
As they approach, Elena and I stop and dust ourselves off.
Akira?
Hello, you two.

She nods at me, a gesture I quickly respond to. My gaze turns to the young girl next to her, and our eyes meet. At the same instant, Akira drops his hand on her head, a movement that doesn't seem to faze her.
I don't think we know each other. I'm Hideaki. Nice to meet you, Hisao.
Man's name, huh? I think I just avoided screwing up. He bows, somewhat restrained by Akira's hand on his head.
Oh, is Hideaki here too? All good?
Akira has been taking good care of me, thank you.
Akira smiles as if to assert the point and rubs the boy's head hard, dragging it in a circular motion. His grim face during this is kind of funny.
The guy went out on business again, so I just brought him to the city for today.
I would have preferred to spend the day on a date with my boyfriend, but…
Hideaki coughs to try and redirect Akira's thoughts.
But when it does, I find mine ramble. Are they related? And even more so, cousins? I guess that explains why he's taking care of him, anyway.
Come to think of it, Hideaki, how did you know my name?
Akira told me. As a Yamaku student, I assume you have a disability?
Not everyone in Yamaku is disabled…
Which I only learned a few days ago. I silently thank Shizune and Shiina for their torrent of information on how the school works.
Thanks to them, I discovered that since the school accepts practically anyone with non-mental disabilities, it does not discriminate against healthy people either.
However, it seems unlikely that many healthy people will enroll there. Although the standard of education is quite high, it is extremely isolated and very focused on helping disabled students.
You are evading the question.
Damn, it's sharp.
Anyway, before I can say another word, he decides to try and guess for himself.
If I were to guess... your heart?
Akira looks at me moderately curious, her interest also piqued. That was certainly a lucky guess.
How did you manage…?
You don't have missing limbs or deformities, so I rule out external disabilities.
Considering the absence of strange gestures, it is unlikely that you have any mental disabilities.
But Yamaku does not accept students with mental disabilities.
I know.
Leaving that aside, the only possibility left is that it is an internal disability.
elena_seq_9: I didn't know what it could be, so I guessed. Correctly, it turned out. And your reaction confirmed my assumption.
More than a little perplexed, I look at Akira. She smiles and shrugs, obviously enjoying her partner's deduction.
He is sharp, yes, but also uncompassionate. Logical, but lacking in tact. Her attitude reminds me of Shizune, in a way, and also her appearance.
Can I ask you why you are staring at me like that? I don't think it's that unusual a specimen.
Doesn't he realize how unusual he looks? I could overlook the leggings and clothing as just a coincidence, but the ribbon in her hair is really too much.
Although this is totally irrelevant.
I'm sorry. It's just that you remind me of someone.
Akira elbows him hard.
I told you you weren't that different from her.
He coughs, covering his mouth with his hand, trying to maintain a straight and serious posture.
So I see you already know my sister. Maybe my full name can help you.
I'm Hideaki Hakamichi. You probably think of my sister, Shizune Hakamichi.
Oh, so he's Shizune's brother.
Wait, if Hideaki is Akira's uncle's son, and Shizune is his sister, then that means Elena and Shizune's parents are siblings. Therefore…
Are Elena and Shizune cousins?
Elena grumbles in an unusually uncontrolled manner. The reaction earns an amused smile from his sister.

The feud between the two of them has just taken on a new meaning. I had thought it was simply a matter of the difficulty of communication between the two, but a family dispute complicates things much more.
You can choose your friends, but you can't choose your family.
She shrugs her shoulders without much encouragement. She doesn't seem to give as much importance to the conflict between the two of them as I do.
Well, that's how it is. Anyway, what are you two up to on this pleasant day?
We are looking for a birthday gift for Yumi. The day is coming soon, so this is the last chance we'll have before school starts again during the week.
Akira makes a strange face, as if Elena had just said that the sky is not blue and the clouds are not white.
Isn't your birthday on the tenth of next month?
Yes… Why? Something wrong?
Akira's face seems to collapse. It is a completely inappropriate expression for someone so loud and stubborn.
Haven't the old people called you yet?
As Elena shakes her head cluelessly, I look at Hideaki to see if he knows any of this. A simple shrug is his only response.
For a moment, Akira seems to think about what to do before smiling again. The fact that he can hide his emotions so quickly and effectively is disturbing.
Hey Little One, I'm sorry, but could you stay with Hisao for a little while?
He nods and takes his leave, Akira placing an arm over Elena's shoulder as he guides her away from our earshot.
And so, I am alone with the “Little One”.
So… nice weather, don't you think?
So it seems.
I think they abandoned us.
Indeed.
What an absurd attempt at chitchat. I have no idea how to talk to this guy, and his robotic responses aren't helping. It comes to mind that it's like talking to a wall.
Without saying another word, he begins to rock on his feet in an obvious gesture of boredom with this conversation. He really is like a little child, despite his serious attitude.
Suspecting the conversation is over, I decide to do what I came to do in the first place.
I'm going to go get a birthday present. You come?
There's not much else to do.
In a while, we arrived at a small shop next to a warehouse.
For once the display cases are not filled with electronic goods and computer games, but with dolls, teddy bears and all kinds of wooden curiosities.
Antiques… Othello?
An antique store? Well, if there's anything in this city that would suit Yumi, I guess it would be here.
I extend my hand toward the antique doorknob, but withdraw it at the last second when I realize that my companion has separated.
elena_seq_10: Aren't you coming?
I'll stay at the newsstand for a while. Don't worry.
His voice makes it emphatically clear that he has no interest in what's in the store, and that he doesn't feel obligated to follow me.
When he leaves without another word, I push open the thick wooden door and enter the store, a bell ringing above me.
The musty smell of old books and wooden shelves is distinctively anachronistic.
I look at the counter next to the door. The gray-haired man behind him sits there silently, reading a worn book. It certainly fits the look of the place.
Slowly passing through the aisles, the person who comes to mind every time I inspect an imported craft or curiosity is not Yumi.
Crouching down, I examine an antique oak desk inside the store's display case.
At least thirty dolls, all of different sizes and manufacture. The only similarity between them is the long Victorian dresses they wear.
I turn the label of one of the ones that seems to reach up to my waist.
…It's not in my price range. Not at all.
I do the same with each one of them, getting more and more depressed as they get smaller and smaller.
That is, until I get to the smallest of them all. I can afford her, barely, but she's good quality and she has long copper hair and a little blue dress.
I decide it's the kind of gift Yumi would appreciate. Pretty, and not at all garish.
After carefully taking it, I decide to continue looking around the store. I'm not sure if it's because I like the atmosphere or out of mere curiosity.
Glancing around the corner before moving to the next aisle, I see that the shelves in this one are filled with wooden toys; from toy cars to intricate automata.
Hidden behind a line of nutcrackers, I notice a small, simple wooden box. It feels surprisingly light when I pick it up with my free hand.
The lid only requires a small movement to open, and the small metal cylinder inside begins to rotate immediately.
For a long time, I simply stand there listening to the melody that fits in the palm of one hand.
As he plays, I take the small label between my fingers and lift it to my face, struggling to read the tiny cursive writing.
It's affordable...sort of.
With a small grimace, I close the lid and head to the counter with the doll and music box in hand.
When I place the two items on the counter, the man behind him sits up straight and examines them. He doesn't hide his surprise very well that someone my age would buy them.
It's painful, but I hand over money to pay for both and leave the store with a small opaque bag in hand.
Hideaki being there takes me by surprise.
Oh…hello. I thought you'd be at the newsstand.
Akira called me. He is waiting for us at the fountain along with Elena.
At least that solves the problem of trying to find them again.
We headed back to the source. Hideaki's posture and presentation, despite his appearance, make for a strange contrast as we walk.
Elena and Akira are standing there waiting for us, their expressions hard to read.
Hey. Ready to go, Peque?
Hideaki's mood seems to improve when he reunites with her.
See you Elena, Hisao. Tell Yumi I wish her a happy birthday.
We will tell you. Bye bye.
See you later, Akira.
And with that, the two disappear into the tumult of the evening crowd.

Turning to Elena, I notice that she is carrying a small bag. Now I understand why his disposition feels different than before; Although Elena is one of those who shows her emotions on the surface, now her expression and tone are confusing and difficult to read.
It's more than a little discouraging, but given the effort she's putting into hiding her emotions, I doubt she wants to be cornered with why she feels this way.
Have you bought Yumi a gift yet?
Yes. Have you done it?
Clear.
So shall we return to the bus stop?
OK. There should be a bus back to Yamaku soon.
And with that, we started walking.
It feels strange compared to before. Elena's hand on my forearm feels unusually tense, and the overall atmosphere feels extraordinarily uncomfortable.
elena_a3_seq_1: I rest my chin on my hand as I absentmindedly look out the window, another of Mutou's classes dragging on and on as if it were going on forever.
The summer sky is almost hypnotizing with its celestial splendor. Only the occasional passing cloud interrupts the blue expanse.
This feeling of longing is probably my street side wanting to escape.
Nakai, could you answer this?
Although now that side of me has been lost in the past.
In that case... I suppose one would use the suffix -ano?
Correct. Following, the suffix for…
As my attention on Mutou fades again, I spot Shiina giving me an enthusiastic thumbs-up, and I nod reassuringly.
It's been a handful of days since Elena left for Scotland, days that have passed relatively calmly.
Life went on mostly as usual, unlike what I expected. While thoughts of her have hovered on the periphery of my mind since she left, current events manage to suppress them. At least for the moment.
So I find myself chatting idly with Yumi, as always, when lunchtime arrives.
Are those that follow in the series also good?
Not really. It would be better if you stayed with the original. His subsequent books did not do him justice, apart from perhaps “God Emperor.”
Thanks, I really wasn't sure if...
As Yumi steps to the side, I see Shizune step forward with her typical seriousness, accompanied by her ever-present shade of colorful hair.
No matter how hard I try, I can't see any hint of their intention on their faces. Shizune's impassive face and Shiina's seemingly boundless joy are a demonic combination.
Hello Shizune, Shiina.
Oh… hello.
I emphasize the greeting by nodding to Shizune so she understands the idea. She immediately and bluntly returns the gesture to both of us.

It's been a while since I've really talked to either of them. For a while I thought they might have been avoiding me, but eventually I came to the conclusion that Shizune really isn't the type of person to do that.
Hello~! Shicchan says Mutou wants to see you sometime.
Because of this statement, my face twists as if I had just eaten something rotten, which amuses Shiina to no end.
Wahahaha~! You'd think you were in trouble, Hicchan!
You may not realize it, but out of everyone in the group you have the least to worry about.
What a most unexpected vote of confidence. Even Yumi nods hesitantly to reinforce the point.
Thanks, I'll keep that in mind. Although there is something I have wanted to ask you.
And what would that be, Hicchan?
I have a feeling this won't go well, but here goes...
Is there any reason why you and Elena don't get along? It seems that even a little civility would help them both in their duties.
Shizune's cold look when Shiina happily translates the words stops me completely. In retrospect, I really could have phrased it better.
Out of the corner of my eye, I'm sure I see Yumi move away. Just a little.

Fortunately, Shizune notices this and calms his spirits while forcefully running her hand through his hair to release tension. Perfectly on time, Shiina begins to interpret the moment Shizune's arms begin to move.
I would say that those things are not relevant to you, but since it seems that you have become friends with Elena...
She stops to adjust her glasses, evidently trying to articulate her idea as best as possible.
While I assume it's the same for her, I can't say my opinion on the matter is unbiased. Suffice it to say that we were closer before than now.
Shizune quickly gestures for Shiina to stop playing her, and then has a brief meeting with her before continuing.
The fact that the two can communicate so easily and yet secretly in front of us is somewhat disconcerting.

Yumi seems to share my curiosity about the meeting, watching with barely concealed interest. As they finish their covert conversation, Shiina seems somewhat discouraged. I guess your opinion on the matter was not taken into account.
Shicchan says you should ask Elena about it, since she doesn't want to be the one to involve you.

Oh ok. I'll have to ask him when he gets back. At least I got some information out of Shizune; That the two have had a close relationship means that they were not always at odds, or at least not to this extreme.
I understand. Thanks anyway.
With a nod and a farewell the two part and walk out the door, no doubt headed straight for the student council room.
…It could have been worse, I guess.
Yumi exhales deeply, relieved by the outcome of the confrontation. I can't say I blame her.
Will I see you later, then?
elena_a3_seq_2: Yes, I'll see you in the tea room. See you.
With that, she says goodbye and joins the stream of students leaving the room.
Nakai, could I talk to you for a moment?
Said in its typical monotony. Apparently he decided he needed to remind me to go see him.
Eventually I finish putting my things away. By the time I get to his desk the room is practically empty.
Ah... Yes sir?
He looks up, judging my face before letting out a strange, and obviously staged laugh.
You don't have to feel guilty, you're not in trouble. I just want to ask you something that I've already asked a few other students.
That's something, at least. For a moment I thought that my maxim of keeping my head down and pen up had failed me.
So what do you want to talk about?
To start, what do you think of your progress in this group, so far? Well? Bad?
I hate those kinds of questions. For a long time I try to think of an answer that is neither pathetically humble nor arrogant.

…Damn, Elena not being there makes my thoughts wander. I'm noticeably more bored and sullen without her company, and the same goes for Yumi. All we do during lunch is eat and play chess.

I'm fine.
OK.

More than a little discouraged, I wander back to my room and hope that she feels better tomorrow, despite not knowing exactly what's wrong with her.
Once again, I find myself in front of Yumi's door after another of her unexplained absences from class.
Nothing. Considering this is the second day in a row she's been like this, I'm starting to worry about her.

Yumi, if you don't say something I'll go get the nurse for you.

W…What? It's hard to tell whether his tone is disappointment, anger, or both. What the hell can I do to help her, if she doesn't even want help?
The message is quite clear. However, I just can't leave her like this; just sitting in her room for days on end.
Rubbing my temple thoughtfully, I return to my own room to think about how to proceed. What is needed here is rationality, and overreacting could make things worse.
I dig through drawer by drawer in my desk, looking for where I left that damn piece of paper.

It's only been a month and a half since I arrived here, and yet this school has become like a second home. I have made new friends and contacts, I have managed to get into the rhythm of the lifestyle and culture of the school, and I have become accustomed to the tricks of my classmates.

Getting used to a school where disabilities are the norm, rather than the exception, still takes me by surprise sometimes when I think about it. The same school populated by burn victims, amputees, the blind, the deaf, and the entire range of disabilities in between.

If someone had described this school to me before I came, I would have thought it was something out of an overactive imagination. Even when I first arrived I felt like the Dutch, arriving in this strange new land for the first time.
It's amazing how quickly you can get used to the environment you're forced to live in, really. And now I've even found someone I'm completely in love with. What a strange life.
Before my mind can wander any further, I find a lined page of paper slid under my distracted face. The strident and bright pink ink must undoubtedly have been written by Shiina.
Oh, right, we have Saturday and Monday off. Can't complain about having less classes, I guess.

I uncap my pen and write quickly on the page before sneaking it back to her, moving my eyes to the front of the class from time to time. Mutou continues to scribble mysterious equations and formulas on the blackboard.

Shiina receives the paper back and slouches over it comically, even to herself, with her tongue sticking out the side of her mouth. Has he misinterpreted my expression as depressed, and is trying to cheer me up?
When he receives the note and begins to write, I look up to see an unpleasant image.
elena_a3_seq_10: As I desperately try to get Shiina's attention in silence, Mutou confidently walks through the spaces between the desks at the front of the class, his determined gaze focused directly on her.
She suddenly stops writing when the towering figure casts an impossibly long shadow across the page.
Ah… I…
He silently takes the piece of paper and begins to read.
Sweating profusely, I quickly look around at the class, noticing its complete silence. Of course, it had to be the only thing that really gets his attention during class.
After a few seconds examining the page, he rolls up the paper into a small tube and gently slaps Shiina on the head with it.
Half an hour until you can leave for the student council. I think you can hold out until then.
Shiina's face falls as the entire class bursts into laughter. He may be strange, but he knows how to deal with her excellently.
I'd probably feel sorry for her if I wasn't busy muffling my own laughter.
Hisao, is that it?
No, I think that's a foreign airline.
And so, the third aircraft that they are not on lands.

For the last half hour we've been passing the time with little snippets of meaningless talk. Elena and Akira's flight has been delayed, and at this rate it will probably be night before their flight arrives.
Is that another one?
No, they are not the company colors.
Yumi's eyes move from left to right, following the flow of people entering and exiting the huge glass door in front of us.
Fortunately, no one pays much attention to it, apparently more attentive in more important matters.
Maybe that one is?
No, I think that… wait a minute, I think that might be it after all.
It takes a little longer for the screen to change the status of your flight to “disembarking.”

A loud yawn escapes me, not giving me enough time to contain it. My sleep schedules, once again, have gotten out of whack; possibly due to a mix of worry for Yumi and the side effects of my medications.
Hisao, over there...
I look at Yumi, and then follow her gaze towards the airport gate.
Hmm? Oh, Elena, there they are!
Really?
We all called each other greeting each other, moving quickly to the side to avoid blocking each other's path.
Elena!
Yumi jumps forward to hug Elena, with nothing more than the smile on her face being enough to see her happiness at Elena's return. Elena simply smiles in response, her voice soft.
It's wonderful to meet again, Yumi.
While the two of them give each other a hug, well deserved after everything that has happened while she was gone, I turn to Akira.
Hello.
They arrive quite late.
True, there was a pretty bad storm over the airport. We were soaked just going from the car to the door.
Then I guess you appreciate the climate here more. Welcome too, Elena.
Yumi separates herself from Elena when I speak. For a long time, neither of them says a word.
Contrary to how I thought his return home would be, the atmosphere feels uncomfortable, almost overwhelming. We both try to guess each other's feelings, not entirely sure what we should say.
Curse. This is exactly what I feared when I thought about trying to move things forward between us.
Elena runs her hand through her blonde hair and twists one of her bangs uncomfortably, clearly trying to think of how best to react.
Luckily, eventually, Elena lets out a light sigh and breaks the silence.
Thank you, Hisao. It's good to be back.
Are you OK? You look tired.
Evidently not having recovered completely well, she quickly waves her hand in front of her face to stave off any worries Yumi might have for her.
I'm fine, really. It's just that the time change has affected me a little.
Weak.
You don't have one?
aiko_seq_1: It's already half past eight, but this morning class hasn't started yet. We're supposed to have had Physics, but the teacher is nowhere to be seen.
If I had known beforehand, I would have fallen asleep too.
Suddenly the door to the living room slams open and Mutou growls his morning greeting at us from the entrance.
Hello, everyone!
It seems that Mutou hasn't slept at all.
His stubble, his unkempt hair, and his stained dress shirt create an unfavorable impression.
I guess you had fun at the festival last night, too.
Sorry for the delay, I ran into unexpected problems. I'm not usually one for festivals like this, but I hope everyone had a good time.
After all, these types of events are important to all of you as they give you a short respite from school work.
The group responds with varying levels of enthusiasm, and Mutou proceeds to take roll and begin class.
Well then. Today's topic is Photon Physics.
In a short time I have descended into a comfortable coma-like state along with the rest of the group, letting Mutou's rambling speeches enter one ear and leave the other without a trace.
Well, who could tell us the solution to this problem?
Mutou has written a fairly simple equation on the blackboard. He desperately tries to get the group to participate.
Nobody? Come on, guys. Nakai, what about you?
Unfairly singled out and cornered, I give you an answer. This causes his scruffy features to twist into a jovial smile that would horrify small children.
Precisely! Good job, Nakai!
I am both disturbed and honored that you can remember my name just a week after being transferred.
From what I've seen, Mutou has serious problems remembering the names of anyone else in the group, and almost all of them have been here since first year.
The room settles into a gloomy mood, with the students and teacher trying to get back on track after the festival.
I imagine last week must have been very hectic for everyone.
Not a minute before time, the lunch bell rings.
MAKE PATH! IMPORTANT ISSUE!
I turn my head just in time to see other people scatter out of the way, as someone darts from the far end of the hallway toward the stairs.
It's too late to realize that I'm standing in the middle of the hallway, directly within the path of the oncoming human projectile.
I try to back away towards the door. Unfortunately, the person running towards me dodges in the same direction.
In the next split second, several things come to mind in succession, albeit almost simultaneously.
First, I recognize that the girl on a collision course with me is Sora.
Second, I notice that somehow it feels very natural to be attacked by Sora once again. I could almost feel comfortable, if it weren't for the reflexive panic and terror.
Third, Sora appears to be carrying a 12-inch-high stack of papers as he runs down the hallway.
She crashes into me, but at least this time the impact was a graze with my arm.
Aayyy… Why does this always happen to me?
Geez, I wonder why. Could it have something to do with you running down the hall like you're on fire?
She whimpers regretfully, looking like a hurt puppy. The spectacle makes me regret the abrupt response the moment it emerges from my lips.
But… I was in a hurry.
I can see it.
I'm sorry.
Don't worry about that.
Sora laments weakly one last time and rubs his forehead as if to expel the pain as his gaze passes over the hallway floor.
The moment you realize that your neat stack of papers has been scattered all over the floor in a huge mess, you let out a scream of horror.
Aah! The impressions! Oh no oh no, what am I going to do? The teacher will crucify me if they get dirty.
They're probably fine. Let's put them together, it won't be a problem.
We quickly finish gathering the papers, and Sora tries to organize the scattered pile back into the neat pile it was with his hands.
Where are you going?
Nowhere in particular, I guess. I didn't want to be left alone with Mutou in the living room. I think he's hungover.
aiko_seq_2: Have you already had lunch?
Not yet, but I'm not very hungry anyway.
She looks at me in disbelief, as if she doubts my sanity for letting such a thing come out of my mouth.
You should go to the roof! I promised Aiko that I would have lunch with her. I bet you'd like the company.
Uh-oh. My lunches with Aiko have been remarkably unsuccessful.
I know where this conversation is going and it's hard not to get carried away, so I have no choice but to cooperate.
Okay, I'll go buy some bread or something first.
Sora smiles brightly before I say anything else.
No no, I'll go deliver these super quick and then I'll go buy lunch for us. And for Aiko too, of course. What type of bread do you like?
That's okay, you don't really have to...
Don't worry, it's okay. Consider it an apology. I'll be back before you know it!
That's what worries me. Don't get into another accident.
Sora starts walking down the hallway, but since he's still talking to me, he's not watching where he's going.
I won't do it!
Famous last words. He is already trotting down the stairs while shouting that not very reassuring promise at me.
Sighing silently, I begin to walk with heavy steps after his path. But instead of taking the stairs down, I go up.
The staircase to the roof is unlit and just as daunting as before.
The door creaks weakly in protest as I push it open.
Aiko is there too, as Sora said, for some reason lying on her back on the other side of the gravel-covered rooftop.
Predicting something unnecessarily strange again, I walk towards her as slowly as possible.
Hoooolaa.
She sounds very sleepy when she says that, stretching out the word in a slurred voice. Despite that, his eyes are wide open.
I look down at her, my shadow covering her face.
What are you doing?
Aiko raises an eyebrow.
I thought you had a heart problem, not a vision problem.
She responds, challenging the reason for my perfectly valid question without even tilting her head to look at me.
Aiko's know-it-all comments are infuriating. The worst part is that I don't know if he's doing it on purpose or not.
Very good. So let me rephrase it:
Why are you lying on the roof?
He shrugs lazily and sniffs disdainfully.
I'm trying to experiment. People probably don't do it enough.
What exactly are you trying to experience? I can't really notice it, but there's probably a reason why people don't do... whatever.
He's playing with me again, answering my attempt at chat with riddles I don't want to solve.
But I don't want to ignore it, either.
Yes, but the reason for that is that everyone is too busy with their lives to pay attention to the really important things.
How to see the sky?
He looks away from the sky and finally sees me directly. The piercing depth of his eyes once he focuses them on something is surprising.
You know, if you were a girl I could see your panties.
If I were a girl, I wouldn't be so close to someone trying to peek at my panties. I have that minimum of common sense.
I wouldn't do it either, but there are times when it can't be helped. Like now, for example.
Although, to tell the truth, I don't even want to see your panties.
Underwear is the soul of a girl. You shouldn't pry into someone's soul. Even if you're not a girl.
As a guy, I guess I can understand that. To us, they are some kind of semi-mythical object that we cannot fully understand.
Yes, that's exactly how I think too. What a coincidence.
aiko_seq_3: It really is.
So, did you have World History in the morning classes?
I missed classes.
To do this?
Well, I'm not really doing what I seem to be doing, or at least I think what I'm doing doesn't seem like what I seem to be doing, but from your perspective...
probably…
Yes, I skipped class to do this.
I guess whatever your reason is, it's as good as any other.
Giving in to the tired feeling in my legs, I sit on the roof, next to Aiko.
Rocks aren't the most comfortable bed in the world, but if she can handle it, then I should be able to, too.
What are you waiting for?
Hmm?
Try it.
I tilt my head back to take a look at where she's looking.
The silver-blue sky, dotted with flocks of sheep clouds, completely fills my field of vision.
Although beautiful, the view is not at all special, even if the weather is good.
I shrug, doing my best to mimic the nonchalant manner that Aiko seems to have developed to perfection, and lie down on my back.
The stones dig into my back through the thin shirt every time I try to move even a little, forcing me to stay as still as possible.
I try to ignore the discomfort and myself, instead focusing on the vastness above us.
High above, summer clouds drift across the dome of the sky.
Neither of them has anything else to say, and so silence covers the roof.
The muffled noises of students at lunchtime, cicadas in the trees, and the hum of traffic beyond the school echo pleasantly somewhere in the background.
Listen, I had a great time yesterday.
Oh really?
Well, to be honest, no. But it was good. It was probably the longest I've ever sat in one place doing nothing, which is kind of impressive.
I try to make it sound as convincing as possible.
Is that impressive?
I think it is. I'm usually too restless to do something like that.
I also think I had a good time.
A cloud passes over us, casting its shadow over the school.
A chill runs through me at the sudden change from light to shadow.
I realize that summer is not in full swing yet.
The only measure of elapsed time is the slow passage of the clouds moving towards the town.
A few golden rays of sunlight filter through the gaps, blinding me for a moment each time they reach my eyes directly.
The blue of the sky seems so unattainable.
This reminds me of the time I spent in the hospital, where I was bored to death every day.
Somehow, it wasn't a problem after a while. I learned to appreciate things other than watching TV and gossiping with people I don't even like.
A general feeling of tranquility spreads from my vision to my other senses, finally reaching my brain.
A plane flies by, leaving two thin contrails behind like a pair of chalk lines drawn across the sky from one end to the other.
I wonder where it's going.
The muffled roar of their engines reaches here, to my ears, although it can barely be heard over the noise of the patio.
It's nice.
It's nice, but I can't understand why this is more important than going to class.
Isn't it good to do something you like?
From time to time?
aiko_seq_4: Of course, but—
What are they doing?
Sora has slipped away from us without either of us noticing and is just a step away from me, holding several plastic-wrapped packages in his arms.
She leans forward and looms over me, casting her shadow across my face in almost exactly the same way I did with Aiko earlier.
I wonder how weird this looks, both of us lying on our backs on the rooftop.
That's what I also asked.
I would be more concerned about what you are doing. If I were you, I wouldn't get so close to people that they could see my panties.
Aiko!
Sora's voice is scandalized, but he soon steps back, pressing his hands against the front of her skirt so abruptly that the packages of bread he was carrying fall off.
I quickly look away, and glare at Aiko. She pretends not to see me.
Hisao isn't like that, right?
That's how it is.
Sora frowns at Aiko and bends down to pick up the packages.
She dusts them off and jumps nimbly around me to Aiko's other side, where she sits.
Anyway, here's your bread. Sorry for being late.
Alright. Thanks for inviting me.
I rise to a sitting position and gratefully accept the bread Sora is offering.
The three of us voraciously attacked the simple food. The bread is surprisingly passable and easily fills my stomach.
From the corner of my eye I follow the skill with which Aiko handles the bread between her feet.
I haven't seen you on the track in a few days.
Oh. True, I… I thought starting that routine was too heavy for me.
So you've been doing something else?
I've been considering my options.
She frowns but doesn't press the matter any further, for which I'm grateful.
Sora seems to be very stubborn and I really wouldn't want him to bother me about this on a daily basis. I already have enough responsibilities to bear with Shizune and Shiina.
We barely finish lunch before the bells ring, calling us back to our classrooms.
Hicchan!
Shiina waves at me as soon as I enter, and starts talking before I've even crossed the room.
How was your festival? Did you have fun?
Ehhh… still a little undecided about it. I would say “probably.”
Because?
Wow~, I was just asking, just asking!
Her eyes shine in a way that tells me she wasn't just asking. However, I can't even imagine his motives.
Since the English teacher's timely entrance prevents us from talking about it any further, Shiina switches to plan B.
I don't answer that, and he leaves me alone after Shizune demands his attention.
My own attention, on the other hand, is directed out the window.
Now that I look at it from here, through the window and the foliage just outside, the sky seems smaller.
I make out only small glimpses of blue; everything else is a bunch of noise right in the middle of my field of vision.
What “experience” did Aiko want to get from looking at the sky? He's certainly done it before. Everyone has done it.
There's no use trying to guess what she was thinking, but if I don't, then I have no excuse not to focus on the teacher's words.
I look at the scribbles on the blackboard, trying to figure out their meaning with little success.
English is definitely not my favorite subject. We have a strong mutual dislike.
The strong, hot afternoon light invades the corridor, making the air feel heavy and peaceful.
My body feels weighed down by it as I drag it two doors down the hallway toward the art room.
Maybe this is part of the reason I didn't join any clubs before: afternoons just aren't suitable for activities.
aiko_seq_5: I knock on the art room door and open it. A girl who was possibly doing something important with that sheet of paper she's carrying turns to appraise me and smiles sweetly, if a little confusedly.
Hello…?
This is the art club, right?
Yes. Interested in joining?
Yes. In fact, it may have already been done, but we'll see.
I give him a weak smile, and his widens, making me feel less nervous.
Brilliant! Take a seat, then. We will start as soon as the teacher arrives.
Without even scanning the room for a good spot, I quickly walk to the back of the room and sit in a free spot, away from everyone else.
Some other members are resting in their seats, waiting for the teacher. Aiko sits alone in a spot near the window, looking outside.
She's the only person I know, although a guy from my classroom I've never gotten along with is here too.
No one comes to greet me—perhaps introductions are left for later?—so I also settle for silent observation.
A boy has sunglasses; An unusual image in the interiors, if we were not in Yamaku. I bet this is the blind student Aiko was talking about.
The wait proves to be extremely short.
Nomiya walks three long strides to stand behind his desk, then gives a smile and an extravagant wave.
Good afternoon everyone!
First things first: Hisao is a new member, so everyone get along with him.
He winks at me disturbingly.
The eight members of the club, including me, responded to his greeting with considerably less enthusiasm. Still, people finally straighten up in their seats and we start to pay attention.
I think some of you still have projects to work on, so please continue with them if you wish.
And for the rest, I was thinking that this day we could sketch out some studies.
What do you think?
No one responds, except for some unintelligible murmurs that Nomiya apparently interprets as unanimous approval.
Well very good! Everyone who isn't working on other projects, pick a partner and draw a sketch of each other.
You should be able to complete it this day, but if not, we can continue next time, or even do it again if you find it interesting.
Remember to pay attention to lighting and shadows, and do your best!
Couples? I feel quite uncomfortable about it, since I hardly know anyone here. I wish someone would ask me to be their partner.
The students stand up and move their chairs to be closer together, but no one comes towards me.
Soon everyone else has a partner. Friends gather together, but I am alone.
Well, there's Aiko.
She is sitting in the far corner of the room, still looking out the window and seemingly uninterested in taking part in the exercise.
Since she is the only other person without a partner, I walk to her seat.
I can't see his face because his hair mostly covers it, and he's not looking at me.
Aiko?
I call her out loud. There is no answer.
Hello, do you want to be my partner? You're the only one I know here.
It seems that he finally recognizes my presence, turning his head like a robot as he looks to see who is speaking to him.
Aiko doesn't answer, and I don't want to repeat the question either. I'm sure he heard it the first time.
Why don't you say anything? It can't be such a terrible fate to have me as a companion, can it?
He doesn't look at my face, and instead stares directly at my chest and stomach.
Oh, okay. Why not?
Alright. Very good. Brilliant. I'll go get things for us.
Looking at the equipment that Nomiya has prepared for today's meeting confuses me. Instead of graphite or pencils, we are supposed to sketch with ink.
I've never done anything like this before.
The teacher, however, seems confident in my abilities to adapt to this medium.
Simple!
aiko_seq_6: First you make the outline in ink. You let it dry, and then you shade it with diluted ink. This is known as India ink, it works like watercolors.
If you're uncomfortable with that, use a pen instead of a brush for contouring.
Understood.
I grab paper, two glasses of water, a pen for me, a brush for Aiko, and ink for both of us, then I return to Aiko.
Reaching for an unoccupied chair nearby, I sit directly opposite her.
Do you want me to do it with my foot or with my mouth?
What did you say?
She tilts her head to the side and her eyebrows form two questioning arcs, as if she didn't understand that I didn't understand the question.
I don't mind drawing anyway. Although you'll look better if I do it with my foot.
With the foot, then, it makes no difference to you.
Nodding in response, Aiko stands up from her seat and takes off her sandals.
In two fluid movements, she picks up the sheet of paper and drops it on the floor, then takes the paintbrush between her fingers before sitting on the floor in an awkward cross-legged position.
Although I have already seen her do everything with her feet, from eating to painting, this demonstration of skill is so prodigious that I simply stare at her, stunned.
Aiko looks at her blank paper intently. The sharp tip of his brush hovers over the sheet in anticipation.
When he lifts his head to see if I'm ready, I quickly turn my face away.
I'll go first. Strike a pose.
What kind of pose?
It doesn't matter. That's the point. You have to sketch the impression you have, not decide beforehand.
I end up sitting in my chair with my hands hanging limply between my knees.
I look at her, and she looks at me for a moment before starting.
Aiko's gaze is piercing but unflappable, as if she were trying to absorb a part of me into herself. I feel like I'm physically shrinking under the pressure of his gaze.
I have the feeling that, for the first time since we met, Aiko is actually looking at me, instead of the direction I'm facing.
She draws with confidence, bold strokes with the delicate brush, unmindful of the potentially destructive consequences of a misplaced brushstroke.
Since she is happy with the contour, she stands up to pose for me, stretching her back and legs.
This time he doesn't look at me. Instead, Aiko lets her gaze wander around the room. I feel relieved, it's easier to watch someone when they're not watching you.
Even so, it is difficult for me to draw.
I don't have any special artistic talent, so I fear that my portrait will end up being somewhat deformed, especially when compared to my partner's skill.
I don't want to embarrass myself too much on the first try.
Aiko isn't helping the process either.

She doesn't stay still for even ten seconds, tilting her head from side to side to judge her drawing, biting her lower lip, looking dissatisfied, and moving constantly as if she were standing on hot coals.
I finally make progress on my drawing, and with my outline done, we both begin to ink the light and shadow.
Nomiya walks by and makes comments about the beginnings of our drawings.
Very good! The standing figure is easier for a beginner to understand.
But I didn't choose the pose...
In confusion, I look at him and then at Aiko, but the teacher has already moved on to the next pair, and Aiko seems indifferent.
Just like when she was painting the mural, Aiko is so absorbed in her work that she seems to have locked me, the room, and the entire world out of her own little existential bubble.
Every once in a while he leans back, apparently to get some perspective. Sometimes he leans forward, getting closer until his nose is almost touching the paper.
This rocking back and forth looks ridiculous.
Suddenly, Aiko shows that she has not completely immersed herself in a world of her own, and speaks.
Are you already having fun?
He doesn't look up from the drawing, which is a good thing. The breaking of the silence sends a jolt of surprise through me, as if I've been electrocuted.
I…I don't know, yet. It's hard to say.
I can't hear him reply to my response, because it seems like he's suddenly having a private conversation in a low voice with his drawing.
I don't understand how he can draw so well when he has the attention span of a butterfly.
Since it seems like he lost his interest, I'm also going back to work on my drawing.
aiko_seq_7: I try to add texture to Aiko's hair to somehow capture the way the golden afternoon light lights her tousled hair on fire and transfer it to my paper in shades of black and gray.
For some reason, this pen and ink bottle come across as such lousy tools and inadequate for the task.
Minutes pass, but the drawing magically doesn't look any more like Aiko than it did before. His voice wakes me up from my misfortune.
How about now?
Sorry?
Are you already having fun?
Why do you keep asking that?
Because it's a club, isn't it? Clubs are supposed to be fun. You joined to have fun. Are you having fun?
Is it important that I'm having fun?
…Yes.
…Okay, I'm having fun.
Good.
I wonder if I said that just to please her, or if I really meant it. I really can't decide which one it was.
However, I don't hate it. I can honestly say that. It's good enough for now.
As the time allotted to finish school passes quickly, I desperately try to improve my horrible drawing, but it doesn't seem to do so.
I want to start over from scratch, but what would be the point? There's no time for that either.
Okay guys, that's all for today! Please leave your drawings on my desk, and I'll see you all next Monday!
I take a look at my portrait. He doesn't look exactly like Aiko. I guess you could say it portrays her, but that would perhaps be a bit generous.
The nose and jaw look horrendous, and the shading is terrible. Sure, it's my first attempt at drawing with ink, but it's still really bad.
That's not bad.
He snuck up behind me while I was lost in thought.
Curse. I was hoping I could give it to the teacher secretly without you seeing it.
Because?
I'm not really happy with this. I wish I could draw better.
You just need a little practice. Could you take my drawing to the teacher, too?
Curious to know how the drawing turned out, I take a look at it. From the way Aiko was drawing, it seemed like she was really concentrating.
It's excellent. Somehow the seemingly arbitrary strokes come together to form an image of my face, from the shape of my chin, to the messy hair, to the somewhat pessimistic expression.
Wow, you are impressive.
It's not that impressive.
But thanks.
Wow, I wish I was that good. I'm a little ashamed of myself.
Wouldn't you have to be me to be as good as me? I don't think you wanted to be me.
No, I guess not. Maybe just some kind of approximation.
I take a closer look at his work. It still gleams with the ink slowly drying.
You know, I look kind of grumpy.
You look a little moody. I mean, I agree; but it is also true the other way. Like this you, not the you I made.
Oh really?
I think so, at least.
His simple statement suddenly gives me an extremely embarrassing feeling. I feel like I need a mirror right now, to confirm or deny what Aiko says. It's an unpleasant feeling.
Maybe it's just her. I hope it's just her and that she doesn't look like that drawing to everyone.
It's a good drawing, but somehow I get a very oppressive feeling from this one.
I see. Either way, it looks great. You really are impressive.
Thank you. I'm glad I could have drawn you. You are an interesting person.
You're an interesting person too, but that didn't help me much.
My self-hatred today has no limits, but Aiko ignores it all. I knew I could never compare, but seeing the difference with my own eyes is pretty humbling.
aiko_seq_8: You know, I tried to make you look like you thought a lot, since you thought a lot.
And yes, I may have exaggerated the expression “I'm sick of life,” but that's how cynics are, right?
I want to reply with something sharp, but Nomiya doesn't give me time to think as he leads us to the door.
Hurry up, you two!
While we were chatting, the rest of the club has left.
I quickly grab my drawings and take them to the teacher's desk before hurrying after Aiko, who has already left the classroom.
It's not in the hallway, to my surprise. I wonder where he managed to run to in just a few seconds. It would have been nice to talk more.
Well, it's not like I had much to say, except maybe get back at you for calling me a cynic.
It's surprisingly late. I'm already used to school finishing at the same time every day, so I can feel the extra hours in my head. And in my stomach.
The growling of my stomach reminds me that I am absolutely starving. I'm so hungry that I would dare try to eat anything that the cafeteria staff considers edible.
Even at the sight of today's delicacies, fried mysterious pieces, my steely determination does not fade. I swallow my dinner without tasting it in the slightest, which is probably for the best.
I don't have much homework to do, but what little I have won't do itself, so I walk towards the dorms.
Preparing for the calm after homework, I knock on Kenji's door.
He answers from the other side, although I can't understand what he said. I try to open the door, but it is locked.
A few seconds later, the sound of locks is heard and the door opens.
Hello. Hey, could you lend me a book? The library was already closed when I left the club meeting.
He squints more than usual, and his eyebrows twitch nervously.
Club? Man, that's dangerous. Indoctrination, groupthink, brainwashing, it's all.
School clubs sow the seeds of conspiracy. Do you know how many secret societies have grown from school clubs?
Be careful and don't get too involved in it. You might not come back.
It's okay, Kenji. So what about the book?
Hey, sure, but you return them and don't ruin any of my books. No drinks, no food stains, no bodily fluids, capisce?
Sure. Thank you.
Instead of letting me in, he walks away from the door, closing it again.
A few seconds later, he returns with a stack of three thick books and hands them to me.
Opening the top one, I'm greeted by a familiar emblem stamped on the copyright page.
Hey, your books? These are from the school library.
They are mine now.
Did you steal them?
Man, what are you talking about? I have been freeing them from the oppressive feminist movement that controls the library.
Please say that the “oppressive feminist movement” does not refer to that poor librarian, Yuuko. She couldn't even hold down a wet towel.
Kenji turns around, mumbling something I can't understand, and closes the door behind him.
Before going to my room, I go into the bathroom. As I wash my hands, the reflection of the mirror on the sink catches my attention.
I try to look for the bad mood Aiko saw in me, but it's the usual Hisao staring back at me inside the mirror.
I try to tell myself that this is how I've always looked, but I realize that I don't remember what I looked like half a year ago.
I wake up drenched in sweat, as if I had run a half marathon in my sleep.
How strange, I don't remember sleeping badly. A feeling of restlessness passes through me, I wouldn't want something to happen to my heart without being able to realize it.
Still, other than this strange exhaustion just before I wake up, I feel pretty good.
My mouth feels like sandpaper and I have nothing to drink, so I have to go to the bathroom to take my medicine. On impulse, I decide to shower while I'm at it.
While I'm in the shower, I decide that this counts as morning exercise, if I appropriately offset it with a nice half-hour walk after class.
I wouldn't want to risk potential complications by going running now, obviously. Besides, Sora will never know, and I think he's losing faith in me, anyway.
Walking would be nice, anyway, just to get to know the place.
There's a big forest in the hills behind the school, or I could go to the convenience store.
As I dry the moisture off my skin, I decide to go get my uniform.
I quickly button my shirt and pull up my pants before leaving.
aiko_seq_9: Normally, this time of year, I would be eagerly awaiting summer vacation. Since I've been here just over a week, I don't really have those kinds of feelings.
I'm still savoring school life and, considering the abrupt and complicated turn my life has taken, I haven't had the time to worry about extricating myself from it.
Plus, once the holidays come, they will be a pleasant surprise if I'm not expecting them. Especially with final exams looming.
At least I don't have to catch up on studying. My hard work has finally paid off.
I push my way through the kids gathered at the door and slump into my seat.
From the corner of my eye I can see Shizune and Shiina suspend their inevitably animated conversation, and turn almost simultaneously in my direction.
They clearly want something from me, I can tell by the way Shizune smiles. It is too broad to be sincere and too calculated to be spontaneous.
Good morning~!
His greeting is made of one hundred percent joy and overflowing energy.
Hello good.
I fail to try to put any of these in my answer.
You don't look like you have much energy.
It's no surprise, I don't feel very energetic either. I don't think I slept well, but I'm not sure.
He pats me on the back and smiles.
Cheer up a little! It's a great day~!
I meet Shizune's gaze. He has a strange, focused expression on his face, but he frowns a little under direct eye contact and looks away.
For a moment I think Shizune sees my concerns, somehow, and is thinking about how to respond. But then he quickly straightens his glasses, and with that, his expression.
Anyway, we were wondering if you're still interested in that student council position, because we'll make you an offer you can't refuse~.
Wait, what? I wasn't really interested in the first place. You're putting words in my mouth.
It's not like that. But wouldn't it be nice to hang out with us every day while also being useful to your school?
Well, to tell you the truth, I... I kind of already joined a club. So, in fact, it would be a bit heavy for me to join the student council as well.
Even if I wanted to. Which is not the case, as I said.
Oh really? Which club is it, Hicchan~?
The art club.
Shizune's eyes flash in a sinister manner as she frowns at me.
With the way he looks at me, I'll be waiting for the art club to lose its funding before lunchtime is over, or for the art teacher to mysteriously disappear off the face of the Earth.
Before she can comment, the teacher finally enters the room, taking Shizune and Shiina off of me and sending everyone to rummage through their backpacks for their books and pens.
I did join the art club, but the first meeting didn't really boost my confidence. I'm actually not sure what I'm doing it for.
I wish I could draw like Aiko, but I don't know what I would do if I could. For what purposes would you use such an ability? I really don't know.
Ignoring the teacher's sleep-inducing voice, I open my notebook to a blank page and press the needle-sharp tip of the pencil onto it.
What will I draw?
I really can't think of anything good to draw.
As I hesitate and raise my hand, a timid black mark left on the previously blank paper looks unpleasant.
I can't seem to even get the opening line, much less get started. It's almost a physical sensation of being held. Annoyingly, it reminds me of my failed attempt at jogging with Sora.
I look out the window in despair. Just then, a little bird takes flight from one of the cherry trees that grow everywhere on the school campus.
I couldn't really see it clearly, and it's not like I could tell one tiny bird from another. But I choose it as my subject of study, anyway.
Conjuring up an image of a bird in my mind's eye, I look back at my notebook and deliberately draw a thick line across the page to begin.
He seems to be mocking me, as I can't continue right away. Either way, it's a start. Starting is good.
Little by little I draw the image on the notebook paper, the image in my mind becomes clearer as the drawing takes shape.
It's really nothing, just that random, nameless bird on paper, but that's not important.

My hesitation fades into the background along with the teacher's voice as I continue my fight. The feathers form a simple pattern in my mind, but on paper it's a mess of too many rough lines despite my best efforts.

I realize that I don't really know what a bird's wing should look like, even if I try to think about it. I even put down the pencil and close my eyes for a moment, trying to trace his figure in my mind.
For me to take it so seriously so suddenly makes me feel a little frustrated.
Art class in high school was the “easy” class between grueling subjects like math or Japanese. But there's this other side of art, the one you see when you're not just being silly.
It's something almost completely different.
aiko_seq_10: Hicchan?
I look up to see two girls looking at me.
Shiina and Shizune have brought their chairs to my bench and are now standing on my sides, looking at my drawing.
How long have they been there?
I think you need more practice.
Shizune draws some signs gravely in the air between her and Shiina.
Shicchan agrees.
Aiko said the exact same thing yesterday, but why did it sound less condescending?
They shouldn't judge before it's over.
Plus, don't they know that it's bad luck to see an unfinished piece of work?
Shiina breaks into exuberant laughter.
That? Don't be silly~! That can't be true.
One way or the other.
Shizune's brow furrows dangerously, and her hand movements become abrupt, like the cutting of a knife.
You should learn to take constructive criticism better.
I would do it if you did offer some.
I know I'm being too defensive and that Shizune is taking advantage of it, but I can't help it.
What are you two doing here, anyway?
Shiina wags her finger reprimandingly in front of my nose.
Tch, tch, Hicchan. Weren't you listening to the teacher?
We have group work now.
I nod discouraged, and let them take the reins.
So what do you think of today's lesson?
No big deal… I didn't hear a single word from her.
Shiina slaps her forehead and shakes her head theatrically.
How are we going to deal with you, Hicchan?
Fortunately, Shizune and Shiina together are more effective than three or four normal people, so I can slack off for most of the exercise.
I try my best to offer at least a little help, but end up being practically useless.
The teacher keeps us in the room for five minutes after the lunch bell rang, but eventually lets us out.
I quickly stuff my books into my backpack while Shizune and Shiina carry their chairs back to their places.
The failed attempt at drawing a bird ends up crumpled and stuffed in my pocket as I rush out the door.
After that morning class, and throughout the week, I keep running into Aiko.
Hello.
This is somewhat natural, since our rooms are adjacent. But instead of just crossing paths in the hallway, like people normally do, we seem to pause when we see each other.
Invariably we end up chatting a little, or just hanging out together, in silence.
I think I'm getting used to being silent in Aiko's company, since it doesn't feel as awkward as before. I am, by nature, a bit of an introvert like her, so we fit well.
I think it's actually an anomaly for someone at this school to be so quiet. Most people here seem to love to socialize.
It's something I've already noticed, even though I haven't been here for long: People here talk a lot, and they do it all the time.

It's a rare case when I see someone sitting alone, just staring into space or something similar. Obviously there are people like that here too; that girl Yumi and I, just to name two of my own group. But in general, they are the minority.
In any case, I wouldn't exactly call what Aiko and I do “socializing,” but it's something, at least.
These occurrences in and of themselves don't bother me, but the fact that they happen at all does.
I would hesitate to claim that anything unites us, but we certainly act as if it does.
However, this feeling of a budding friendship is completely shattered every time Aiko opens her mouth.
Can I hear your heart beating?
She says this, or something else just as outrageous, and I have to rid myself of whatever nonsense her mind has concocted during the previous class in some subject she's not interested in.
aiko_a3_seq_1: I asked you a question, Nakai.
I shake my head to fight off the daze. The teacher is looking at me, as is everyone else in the room.
Oh, sorry. I wasn't paying attention.
What's the difference between... doesn't matter, different question:
Why are you here, in this class?
To, ehh… learn about Physics.
Yeah! Well, no, but that's the answer I wanted to hear.
Acquiring knowledge is the secondary reason for you being in school.
The primary reason is to learn the rules of society, norms and ethics that govern your daily life.
You don't come to school for the classes, you come to interact with the other people here, your classmates as your equals and the teachers who are your superiors.
You learn how to form social contacts and maintain them; in other words, how to be part of society. The school itself is a microcosm of the entire universe.
Locke was the one who realized that, you know? School is not just a place of learning, and of all the kids your age, you should know that better than anyone.
He pauses for a moment and lets his eyes move around the room to see if the message has been captured.
At the very least he silenced everyone and made them focus on him, captivated either by his voice or by the sudden change of subject from Physics to the philosophy of education.
However, my classes—as you so rightly say—are a place for learning Physics.
He points the piece of chalk he is holding at me.
So, no falling asleep in class, got it, Nakai?
Yes sir.
From the corner of my eye I notice Shizune's frown and Shiina's barely contained laughter. I sink deeper into my seat.
After classes end, I am the last one to leave the room. I close the door behind me and quietly make my way to the art room.
Time passes with relative peace and tranquility. I sit in my usual spot next to Aiko, but she doesn't seem to be in a very conversational mood.
She is even more distant than usual.
Today we are going to draw a still life, and we can choose between a vase full of fake flowers or an arrangement of rocks, sticks, and canvas.
The teacher encourages us to approach the preferred topic, emphasizing perspective, texture and lighting as the key points of this exercise.
I look at Aiko to see if she prefers one of the topics over the other, but she just cocks her head, which means nothing.
Club members quickly move their chairs around the room to get closer to either the vase or the jumble. Aiko and I choose the vase with flowers, but only one of us seems to do any work.
She's ignoring Nomiya's homework just like she suddenly started ignoring me, and has begun to idly scribble something with her foot, without really seeing what she's drawing.
I try to see her eyes, but she looks out the window. It's making me uncomfortable.
Aiko almost looks like she's asleep, with the way she's leaning against the back of the chair with her legs resting peacefully on the desk. He has already completely abandoned drawing.
As much as I try to relax, ignore her, and just be myself, the more it feels like I should ask if something is wrong.
After the activities are over and the others have left, Aiko gets up from her seat and marches straight towards Nomiya with unusual determination.
I will do that.
Nomiya, who was humming to himself while tidying up a box of pencils out of harshness, turns around with an expression that is a mix between kindness and incomprehension on his face.
Hmm? What will you do, my girl?
That person from the gallery. I can talk to that person. At least yesterday I thought I could.
And today too.
Believe. I want to try it. I'm going to go to the end.
The bravest smile I have ever seen on someone's face lights up the teacher's features. He almost literally shines.
Oh, wonderful! I had almost given up hope!
What a stubborn girl you are! But I knew that sooner or later you would understand, you too!
I'll call my friend Saionji and arrange a meeting.
You will have to show her your work so she can value it. I've told him about you, but obviously you two should talk face to face.
This is so exciting, isn't it?
Nomiya talks more to himself than to us and walks in circles around his desk, waving his hands frantically the entire time.
He takes the cell phone in his jacket pocket and opens it with an elegant movement, looking to find the number to call.
aiko_a3_seq_2: As he searches, he notices that I'm looking at him and gives me a cheerful approval. I shrug in response, trying my best not to sound smug.
Nomiya finds the number and makes the call, walking away from us and lowering her voice once they answer. Still, I can hear the excited tone in his voice.
The call doesn't last long.
Fabulous! Sae is in the gallery right now, and said we could stop by right now if that's okay. This is really excellent!
Do you have some kind of portfolio to show, Aiko?
She simply shakes her head at the question.
No need to fear, I have taken some photos of your paintings. We can take those and maybe a couple of originals with us. That will be more than enough for now.
There must be some recent ones here in the back, right?

Nomiya pulls a folder full of photos from a desk drawer, then darts to the back where there is a small storage room and extra shelves for all the materials and tools that the art classes and the club use.
He soon finds what he was looking for and crudely wraps two of Aiko's paintings in some brown packing paper.
Nakai, could you take these to my car?
I pick up the two oil paintings. They are not heavy, but they do make the journey a bit difficult when following Nomiya and Aiko to the parking lot.
Nomiya has a very nice car, not something you would expect a high school teacher to drive. I wonder what kind of salaries they earn in Yamaku.
The paintings are stuffed in the trunk, where they barely fit. Because of the teacher's overzealous insistence, I get into the car with them.
Aiko responds to my questioning look with a reassuring nod and a nonchalant shrug.
I guess I've become some kind of assistant to her, now.
Nomiya steps on the accelerator to the floor. The comfortable ride takes about 10 minutes to bring us to the city center, where we pull into a tiny parking lot and get out of the car.

I pick up the paintings again, looking around. It's just like any other city in Japan, to tell the truth. Same style of buildings, people hurrying here and there, office workers sweating inside their suits in the summer heat.
Wide tree-lined streets aren't something you see everywhere, however. Maybe they are the specialty of this city.
It definitely has that city feel, which I thought I had forgotten about. I feel immediately comfortable walking in it.
I had never come here before.
No? In that case, it was time.
It's a great city! Tons of wonderful people around here. And most important of all, a vibrant cultural life.
Oh, Sae's gallery is right around the corner.
After turning three more corners, Nomiya stops in front of a door. There is a plaque with big red letters on it: “22nd Corner.”
Is this really the twenty-second corner?
About what?
That's bothering me too. I mean, where do you start counting from? And in what direction are you going to count?
Aiko gets upset over the strangest things. Unlike me, Nomiya completely ignores her and opens the door.
The gallery is very clean looking, and the air conditioning makes it cool and very comfortable.
The white walls and large windows facing the busy street make the whole place feel airy and bright. However, there is no one he can see.
Most of the space on the floor is empty, with just a few large tables and a counter for furniture.
There are paintings too, of course. A poster advertises an exhibition for an artist I've never heard of.
Most of her work appears to be portraits or landscapes done in a more traditional style than Aiko's abstractions.

Summoned by the bell on the door, a lady who appears to be around Nomiya's age comes from around the corner. She wears an elegant suit, and wears her straight, dark hair in a ponytail behind her head.
A pair of eye-catching, expensive-looking glasses frame his eyes.
But looking again, I'm not so sure of his age anymore. She looks older and yet...not really older.
Sae, hello!
She clearly recognizes the teacher, greeting him warmly.
Oh there you are, Shinichi, and so fast. I take it these two are your students?
Indeed, let me introduce you. This is Aiko Tezuka, who I told you about, and the healthy-looking boy over there is Hisao Nakai.
She takes a long, serious look at both of us, especially Aiko. It feels like we are being evaluated, that a value of some abstract kind is being calculated for us.
His eyes remain for a long time on Aiko, in her eyes, her empty sleeves tied with a knot, her posture.
Sae takes her first impression of Aiko with an intensity I haven't seen used by anyone else before. Once finished, she smiles kindly.
Nice to meet you. My name is Sae Saionji, and I am the owner of this gallery.
aiko_a3_seq_3: Could you perhaps offer them some tea?
Oh no thanks, we're fine. Let's get straight to the point.
I leave the paintings on the table so the gallery owner can take a better look and Nomiya takes out her photo folder.
The older woman studies Aiko's works carefully, mindlessly rubbing her cheek with her fingers as she lets her gaze pass over the paintings.
His eyes remind me of a bird of prey of some kind. They are so sharp and somehow very calculating.
She takes her time, slowly going through the paintings in order without saying a word.
Even the teacher looks very nervous. He tries to point out certain details and other things in Aiko's work, but it seems like she isn't listening.
