While Nomiya and I continue looking at Sae, trying to look for any trace of reaction on the gallerist's face, Aiko lets her gaze wander around the gallery space. Suddenly, he says something.
Is this really the twenty-second corner?
Sae looks up from the paintings to see Aiko, but she doesn't respond.
It's probably for the best.
She studies Aiko's hunched posture and her dreamy eyes that are once again moving restlessly around.
The way Aiko seems disconnected from a situation that is supposed to be very important to her bothers me just a little. I'm practically holding my breath.
After Sae has gone through all of Nomiya's photos and inspected the two oil paintings I carried here, he goes through all the material again, this time at a faster speed.
Finally, he gives his verdict.
I like it.
Although, if you don't mind me saying so, you're still a little immature. Looking for your own direction, perhaps?
She takes one of the photos.
Still, just look at this. I just can't take my eyes off this. Like a little kitten playing. That's how your art makes me feel, young lady.
Thank you. Believe. No one had ever told me that before. Believe.
That's all Aiko has to say. Some of what the gallerist says and how she says it makes it sound condescending, to me, but I keep it to myself.
Ahem, anyway…
What a wonderful imagination, though, isn't it?
I have always said that Tezuka has a great eye for color composition and harmony. And technique! Remember, these were all made with their feet!
Sure, we'd need to put some of the simpler ones on display too, for the common people, right, Sae?
The teacher snorts derisively.
You know what those Philistines are like. What do you understand about true art? They would just be lost with the abstractions and themes here!
But that will generate more publicity, and that's a good thing, isn't it?
Sae smiles gently at Nomiya's comments and turns back to the paintings.
I wonder...
To tell the truth, I don't know if all this makes an art exhibition. Even if I like it, I don't have the feeling of a theme, of cohesion.
There is no complete work, and to tell the truth, who would expect such a thing from a young artist like the kitten?
Oh no no no! It's certainly doable, especially if we get some new parts and touch up some of the old ones.
I don't mind painting more. I'll do anything.
It's a bit exaggerated.
Believe me. I wouldn't have come to you if I didn't think Tezuka was ready. You can see it too, can't you?
I know exactly what your kind are capable of. And you know it too.
Those words make the gallerist lady pause. A hollow, bottomless look takes over his eyes for a moment, as if he were seeing through or perhaps beyond Nomiya.
She doesn't say anything, but her mouth becomes a tight line, as if she's been stretched. Finally, the moment passes.
Is that what you're saying?
That's what I'm saying.

Sae sighs and takes a few steps, walking in a circle as if to help organize her thoughts. She takes another look at the photo of the painting she especially liked, the one that made her call Aiko kitten.
She places her hand over her mouth, speechless.
I don't know what to say.
After seeing you, my dear, and these paintings of yours... could you excuse us for a moment? I want to talk to your teacher privately for a bit.
aiko_a3_seq_4: Sae takes the art teacher aside, and they talk quietly for a while.
I can't hear what they're saying, but over her shoulder, I can see the lines at the corners of her mouth tighten as she moves her hands in coordination with her words.
The expression on his face is… what kind of expression is that? I couldn't say it.
Once they're done discussing whatever they had to discuss, they give each other a serious look. I feel something beyond just words happening here.
They walk back to us. Sae looks seriously at Aiko, her left hand instinctively reaching for her pack of cigarettes on the table.
She takes the pack and takes one out, looks at it absentmindedly as if only now realizing she's just done it, and puts it back.
Finally, he fixes his gaze on Aiko, assessing her once more.
It's okay, little kitten. I'm going to believe in you.
I will show your paintings in this place, but as far as I can see, this is not enough. You don't really have a consistent theme, and you don't have enough of the good stuff.
You're going to have to work hard to actually have something we can put on display here.
I know.
It's a good thing my gallery is so small, right?
Aiko already spends practically every waking moment painting. How is it possible to work harder?
She would have to miss classes to do more than she already does. And how can someone work so hard?
Silence falls inside the gallery after my words. Sae looks at the art teacher, who looks contemplatively at his star student. I see the three of them, confused.
It's feasible.
What do you mean?
I mean, school is special. The council places great value on things like this. I'm sure I could arrange some kind of leave for her. It's not unprecedented by any means.
I will discuss it with his parents as well, although they have already been very supportive.
However...it might be a bit of a stretch to get work space for her at school if she's not actually going to attend classes.
I was actually thinking about this before. Do you use that upstairs spot for anything?
No, I don't use it… I haven't since. It's more like a garbage dump than a workshop now.
Above?
I have a small workshop-apartment on the floor above this building, but it hasn't been in use for… jeez, it's been that long, hasn't it?
His eyes jump to Nomiya, who has a strange, muted expression on his face.
Certainly. Do you think...
Even Nomiya, in all her brashness, has trouble asking the question directly. Sae, of course, sees through it and raises her hands, sighing deeply.
I guess I can't say no, can I? Very good. I will also lend you the use of that place, if necessary. It's not like I actually use it.
Excellent! I knew I could count on you!
Don't celebrate yet. It really is a mess, so don't be surprised when you see it for the first time.
But, you can use it however you see fit. Since it's a workshop, it already has easels and things like that. You'll need your own tools and materials, and somehow clean it up a bit.
It's not habitable though, so I can't let you live there. I doubt your school or parents would allow that, in any case.
Alright.
However, it is convenient to stay overnight if necessary. It won't bother me.
Hahaha, this is actually excellent, isn't it, Tezuka?
He enthusiastically pats Aiko on the shoulder, laughing in relief and happiness as if all this good fortune has fallen solely on him.
Sae smiles too, perhaps more entertained by the old master's glee than anything else.
Oh wow, Shinichi, this is really like back then. Are you sure we're not trying to take on more than we can handle?
She looks at Aiko, who looks strangely subdued despite all this.
I hope it's worth it, kitten.
She extends her hand as if to shake it with Aiko's, but realizes the impossibility and quickly switches to patting Aiko's shoulder.
Aiko looks back at her silently, her eyes serious and impenetrable like the darkness of the night.

Aiko sends in the application, and—thanks to Nomiya who pressured the principal, surely—she is granted permission not to attend for the rest of the term due to “exceptional extracurricular activities.” She has to make up for it during summer vacation, but it doesn't seem to bother her.
Aiko will be allowed to eat and sleep at school, of course; She just doesn't have to go to class. I'm not entirely sure if I envy her or not.
All of that makes me feel anxious, somehow.
aiko_a3_seq_5: It's the last day of school for Aiko. I feel like I should send her off with a word of encouragement, or at least say something. It was somewhat due to my influence that she decided to dive headfirst into this, after all.

My class ends about twenty minutes early, so I walk to the lobby and buy a can of juice, then sit on a bench and wait for Aiko. I take a novel out of my backpack and look for the part where I left off.
Time stretches comfortably over the warm afternoon as I lazily sip my juice and read a few chapters of the book. The plot doesn't seem to move forward at all, but I don't care.
The bell rings to end the school day and students go to club meetings or outside. Nobody notices me, sitting on the bench with my nose in the novel.
I keep an eye out for Aiko, but I don't see her familiar face or red hair passing by.

I look at my watch 20 minutes after the end of class, when the hallway has emptied of people again. Even Aiko should have managed to get out of class, but either I didn't see her pass, or she never came down the stairs.
Maybe she went to the art club for something last minute instead, or was held back by her strict home teacher.
I haven't waited that long, but having grown tired of waiting, I decide to go look for her on my own.
I put my book back in my backpack and throw the now empty can in the trash can, then head up the stairs.
The hallway is eerily quiet, as there are no club rooms other than the art room nearby. I check there first, but not even the teacher is inside.
Returning to the stairs, I discreetly knock on the door of 3-4 and open it to peek inside.
Yellow rays of sunlight cross the classroom, falling on the floor. The dust and chalk floating slowly in the air make the light almost palpable.
The entire room is bathed in the gentle light that shines through the windows, washing away the shadows.
There is only one person inside the room.
Aiko is sitting in what I assume is her spot, by the window in the third row. His head rests on the bench.
I wonder if he slept through the entire class. Apparently not even Sora had the heart—or perhaps the ability—to wake her up.
I close the door without making a sound. Leaving behind the orderly and uniform rows, I go to where she sits.
Aiko?
My mouth is suddenly so dry that the word comes out as a tiny whisper.
She doesn't respond, so I leave my backpack on the floor; right next to hers, and I lean over her to see her face.
Aiko's eyes are quietly closed, her long eyelashes casting thin shadows across her cheeks. His mouth slightly open, letting me hear the quiet sound of his breathing.
His usually messy hair is even more so today, being completely disheveled over half of his face and forehead.
Aiko's backpack lies at her feet like a forgotten rag doll. A few books and pens have fallen outside, near his place. The scene makes me smile a little.
She lightly touched Aiko's head, brushing a few strands from her ear. Her hair feels warm against my palm.
Aiko moves and I reflexively withdraw my hand, feeling embarrassed for touching her so casually.
He looks so vulnerable, like any sleeping person. It's impossible not to feel affection for her.
I sit on the bench of whoever is sitting in front of Aiko, then I open the window slightly to let in some fresh air, this will wake her up and I won't have to resort to more rough methods.
She doesn't wake up, but I really didn't expect her to.
Seeing her makes me feel tired too. To be honest, I wouldn't mind a quick nap either, but I'll settle for leaning against the big window.
The glass feels warm against my ear and cheek, as these windows face west toward the evening sunset.
That afternoon light slowly melts into Aiko's copper hair, softening her contour so that she appears to be fading into her surroundings.
The tiny movements of her muscles, her hair swaying in the air current, the regular rhythm of her breathing, all this gives the strong impression of a dreamy girl.
Like all sleeping people, Aiko seems to be out of this world, in some distant dreamland.
With her, it doesn't feel so obvious that she will one day return. She seems so detached from her surroundings even when she's awake, in fact she has this same kind of air next to her when…
Understanding hits me without warning.
Aiko sometimes looks like this when she's painting.
His expression of concentration gives the same feeling of being on the other side of some imaginary gap as looking at his face while he sleeps.
I feel a pain in my chest.
There's no way I can close that gap to be on the same level as her. It hurts, even though I know it's impossible for any two people to truly understand each other.
But Aiko… she is almost literally in another world when she talks about art, thinks about art, or creates art.
It's not a world that I—or anyone else, for that matter—can share with her. Just like the world of dreams.
Aiko still shows no sign of waking up, so I'm faced with the decision of either waking her up myself, or waiting for her to wake up on her own.
I choose the last one.
Waiting is something I'm good at. I realized this during my hospitalization. But even the hospital ward is livelier than school after classes are over.
The only sounds in this place are the loud ticking of the clock above the door, and the distant voices of the students in the courtyard.
aiko_a3_seq_6: A genuine summer breeze blows inside through the window I opened, full of warmth and bringing the aroma of light.
I look outside to see where it came from, but I'm dazzled almost instantly. The window glass seems to trap all the sunlight inside, making it painful to look there.
All I can glimpse through the window are the dark silhouettes of the trees and the wall surrounding the campus against the glow of the setting sun.
As I turn to look at Aiko, she moves again.
A single tear slides from the corner of her eye, slowly making its way down her face before falling onto the bench.
It's tiny, just a droplet, but it captivates me.
Another tear follows the first, and then a third. A feeling of anxiety overcomes me, instantly petrifying me.
It's so strange, seeing Aiko's calm face while she sleeps at the same time that tears fall down her cheeks, wetting the wooden bench on which she rests her head.
I don't know what to do, so I do nothing, and just watch the tears run down her face one by one.
I wonder what he is dreaming about.
Aiko wakes up after shuddering one last time, or perhaps because of tears.
She sits up straight and yawns so excessively it looks like her jaw might dislocate.
She notices my presence, but her reaction is more like a lack of any kind of response. It is just a recognition; not a cry of surprise or anything.
Hello.
Good morning.
She's so sleepy she can't even return my smile that somehow I can't exaggerate to be completely honest.
Aiko notices her wet cheeks and quickly wipes them on the shoulders of her blouse. It seems like she's not at all surprised or nervous about them.
You cried in your sleep. A bad dream?
No. It's nothing of the sort. It's something I've learned to do. From other people.
It's a funny story, I'll tell you later.
Come to think of it, she's actually not that funny. I think I won't tell you. Did you want something or did you just come to watch me sleep?
Hey... I wanted to see you after class.
Oh. Well, it's after school now and I'm looking at you right here.
Yeah. I just wanted to say good luck, or something. I imagine the next few weeks are going to be a lot of work for you.
Thank you.
Aiko yawns and blinks a few times.
I feel strange. I actually didn't sleep much last night.
Butterflies in the stomach?
That? No. I mean yes. I know what that means. Butterflies. I don't feel very well now.
It will be fine.
You are very trusting. Someday that will bite your ear.
I will look forward to it.
I think I have to go. I promised Mrs. Saionji that I would go straight there after school, and now it's after school.
Is it okay if I stop by? I'm assuming you're planning to work long hours, so if you'd prefer to avoid distractions...
It's okay. It's not a distraction. Not like Sora. But don't bring it with you. I wouldn't like that this time.
I told her to stay away.
I see. Very good.
Aiko stands up and silently walks towards the door with me, following behind her.
The empty hallways of the school, devoid of the usual crowd, feel very lonely.
It's only a few hours since classes ended, but the building seems to be completely deserted. Our footsteps are all that intrude on the stillness of the hallways.
The change is sudden, but it shows how the building is just an empty shell, dead without its students and teachers to give it life.
It's as if the school has become a private world just for the two of us, a desolate place full of silence and chalk dust.
I'm going to change.
Out of nowhere, she says this as we walk down the stairs from the third floor, and it makes me wonder how she sees this challenge ahead of her.
That's something people have to do, sometimes.
aiko_a3_seq_7: That's the last thing we said to each other that day, even though there was so much we could talk about.
And even those words drown in the all-encompassing silence, disappearing into the stagnant air as if they had never been spoken.
The following Monday is notable for a strange emptiness that takes over me, caused by knowing that I will no longer be able to see Aiko whenever I want.
This feeling of emptiness is a little disconcerting, but I make it through the afternoon anyway. My last class is, in a word, terrible.
It's not that the lesson is so bad. However, it's boring, and it's so hot inside the classroom that I feel like I'm melting.
The air conditioning is either broken or turned off, so the windows are open. It makes no difference, since the air outside is completely still. Only the song of the cicadas reaches inside.
The suffocating heat permeates the room. Both students and teachers are in a state of almost delirium.
I just want to get up and walk out of here without caring what the teacher or anyone else says. I can also see that I'm not the only one with these thoughts.
Next to me, Shiina shamelessly lifts her skirt a little and fans herself with her notebook.
Only Shizune seems as fresh as ever, sitting with her back perfectly straight, her arms across her chest, and her eyes fixed on the equations scribbled on the blackboard.
I keep casting longing glances at my watch, but this doesn't make the time go by any faster.
It's funny. I remember how much I wanted to get out of the hospital and go back to school.
Now all I can think about is the upcoming summer vacation, and freedom from classes and homework. Maybe it's human nature to just think about the current situation.
Finally the bell rings.
Relieved, my classmates and I escaped to the hallway already crowded with students from our neighboring classrooms.
I notice Sora's tiny figure nearby and walk towards her.
How are you.
She smiles tenderly, clearly happy to see me.
Hisao! How's it going? Is your living room super hot too?
Yes, it is. I thought I was going to melt in there.
Although nothing else has happened, really. Feeling a little weird now that Aiko's gone on her big adventure or whatever you want to call it.
Sora's face breaks into an even wider smile and he jumps up and down excitedly.
Isn't that cool? I'm sooo happy for her, I bet everyone is going to like her paintings and sell a ton of them and make tons of money.
Yes, I'm sure everything will turn out great.
Although I am very angry with her.

She huffs in disgust and places her hands firmly on her hips, even letting a bit of anger creep into her voice. It doesn't really have the impact you're probably hoping for, but I'm not saying anything.
Why is that?
She said she doesn't want me to go see her.
Oh yeah, she mentioned that. I guess she prefers not to be distracted. I can understand that.
I don't think I'm that distracting! Plus, I'm sure you'll forget to sleep and eat properly if someone isn't there telling you to do it.
Sometimes she's like that, she concentrates completely on whatever it is and leaves everything else.
It really makes me worry, you know. Is it going to be okay?
What a friendship.
Speaking of which... I don't know if I should even say this, but it's been bothering me.
How can I say it…? Aiko said that she doesn't really see you as a friend... or anything like that. And I really can't understand why he would say something like that.
You two seem so close.

I feel very uncomfortable saying this, but I have finally managed to get those words out. Sora doesn't seem too shocked, but it makes him pause for a moment. Even his perpetual smile transforms into an expression that is harder to read.
Ahaha, really? I guess maybe I'm more like an older sister, or something, to her.
Sorry? Big sister? You?
I put my hand on my head and then on his, as if measuring and reconfirming our heights. Sora playfully smacks my wrist and sticks her tongue out at me, looking angry.
Hey, that's a hit below the belt. I thought you were more gentlemanly.
Sorry, I couldn't resist. Too easy.
Although I actually wanted to make the joke more to lighten the mood than to make fun of Sora.
But I'm serious. Plus, I'm a year older than Aiko, or even you, for that matter. So, that's how it is.
Oh really?
aiko_a3_seq_8: Yes, I lost a year of school when I learned to walk and run again with these legs.
Oh, right. That makes sense.
I should have figured it out on my own. In my defense, her diminutive figure is truly deceptive.
Sora smiles wryly and something deep and hidden comes to the surface in his eyes, like a whirlpool suddenly appearing in an otherwise calm river.
I watch her struggle with this for a brief moment, until she blinks it away and her smile grows wider.
Anyway, it's true. She is just so cute that I want to cuddle her. I had always wanted to have a little sister but, well... I guess I never got to have one.
It's kind of hard to be serious with Aiko, so I guess I never really tried.
I like her a lot though, so hearing that she said that doesn't make me happy. It's not like I can really argue with it, so maybe that's just how things are.
We're very close, but maybe just not that way, you know?
She sighs heavily.
I wonder...
I wonder if she thinks I'm annoying.
I am very sure that is not the case at all.
Sora shakes his head with a happy expression. I'm not sure if he's joking or not.
She has these weird ideas about a lot of things. Things make sense to her in a completely different way than they do to me. I can't even remember all the weird things he's talked about all this time.
I don't think Aiko remembers either, to tell the truth. She's the kind of person who would forget her own head if it weren't attached to her shoulders. That's why I just can't leave her alone.
Is that weird?
She leans against the wall, looking distressed and at the same time happy as always. I have a strange feeling about it, like I'm talking to two people at the same time.
How could I know? Everyone is weird in some way, but if that's yours, it's a really cute way. At least I can understand what you're talking about, unlike Aiko.
Most of the time, I also have no idea what's going on in his head.
Sora laughs, nodding his head.
I think it's okay, even if you don't understand it. That's how she is, usually.
Sora stands straighter, dusting the hem of her skirt and fixing her waist. He laughs in a strange way.
Ahaha, wow, we ended up being pretty serious. What's wrong, Hisao? Why are you talking about this?
Oh, excuse me. I didn't really intend to get into this kind of discussion either. It's just... I don't know. I've been having this weird feeling about Aiko lately.
I don't know why.
I feel a little guilty, talking about something like this for no reason except my own anxiety.
It will be fine. Don't worry about that.
Suddenly Sora grabs my wrist and twists it so he can see the time on my watch.
Oh damn, is it already that late? I really should go, there's a meeting with the rest of the track team on the field.
It's not going to be fun in this heat. We're going to sweat like pigs, but I promised I'd be there.
See you later!
Sora bounds down the stairs, making me wonder if what I said—or what Aiko said, rather—hurt her or not. Maybe what she said herself was what hurt her the most, now that I think about it.
So at the end of the day, even the person closest to Aiko is as far away from her as everyone else.
I wonder if Aiko herself feels that distance.

I have also felt as if I were separating myself from the world, during my hospitalization. I was feeling anxious and depressed, and even now, I still feel that way sometimes. But I fight against it with all my strength.
If Aiko has been on that side of the divide her entire life, I can't imagine how she wouldn't feel alone, but maybe she really is different.
I refuse to belong to that other side, but she may have found solace there.
As I walk down the hall this afternoon, I glance at my watch. It's almost half past four.
Normally I would go to the art club meeting, but I don't feel like going at all, so I start walking in the opposite direction.
It feels like a bad decision. I just know that if I miss once, I'm going to miss again and again. This is probably the end for me and the art club.
Although it's been simmering beneath the surface for a while now. I guess I'll formally resign later.
I keep staring at the boring linoleum floor as I walk aimlessly. This takes me—maybe subconsciously?—to the library.
It is almost empty and completely silent. Some studious first-year students are sitting at the tables, joining forces to finish homework before dinner time.

Yuuko is also working hard today. She is methodically processing a huge pile of books on her desk, going through them one by one and then placing them in a cart next to her. I greet her upon entering.
aiko_a3_seq_9: Good afternoon.
I haven't seen you around here for a while. Have you read all the books yet?
She seems to be in a good mood.
Haha, I don't think so. I joined the art club, so I've been spending time there instead of making an effort to read your collection.
I think I'm going to quit though, so I guess you'll be seeing me more often from now on.
You didn't like the club?
Honestly? Don't know. I'm not very talented at art, but I didn't hate doing it either.
I guess he just felt a little useless. I can't really see any purpose in going.
The art teacher scares me a little.
Oh really? He seems to be a very good guy. Maybe a little over the top sometimes.
Yuuko makes a face I can't read, but doesn't say anything else.
How are you doing?
Something good happened to me today. I didn't fail my course in college.
Well, that's great, isn't it?
Yeah! Without the credit they could have fired me and then I would have a lot of things to explain to my family. I'm really lucky.
I think I'm going to buy pudding today to celebrate.
Being a college student sounds difficult. I'm surprised you have two jobs while still attending classes.
My part-time jobs really make it difficult for me to keep up with my studies, and my student advisor yells at me.
And then if I stay up late studying, I get sleepy at work and my boss yells at me.
But if I quit my jobs I will starve to death.
It's like I just can't win, hehe. I wonder why that is.
I really don't know what to say. Yuuko isn't really complaining to seek empathy from a guy much younger than her. He's just talking about the facts of his daily life, basically.
It makes me feel even more sorry for her, somehow.
Wow, that must be hard for you.
I don't know. It's been like this for so long that I've forgotten what it's like to have a normal life. Or maybe this is a normal life for my age.
Is this normal? Yes it is, right? It must be. Why is being normal so depressing?
I couldn't say it. Although it's not like being abnormal is much different.
Oh, I didn't mean to say it that way! Sorry, sorry, sorry! I just got carried away.
Alright. It was a joke, more or less. Either way, it seems like you're doing well now.

Yes, when I feel really sad, I take a step back and make a cup of tea! And when I've had my tea, I kick my spirits in the butt, like BAM! and then I say to myself “now you're going to do this, Yuuko!”, and then I go and do it!
That's why I'm working so hard now.
She clenches her fists dramatically at the height of her fiery explanation. It's not very clear what she really means, but it's good that she feels so motivated.

Leaving Yuuko alone with her work, I head to the back of the library, where the novels are. I briefly consider reading something non-fiction for a change, maybe a biography? But in the end, I decide otherwise.
My fingers trace the spines through the rows and rows of novels. Occasionally they'll pull out a book at random so I can read the back and maybe try the first two or three pages.
Nothing really captures my interest, so I end up picking up a book I had already read back in March, in the hospital. I remember liking it.

I sit down on one of the beanbags and quickly dive into the book, turning pages quickly. I'm probably not the fastest reader around here, but I'm pretty fast. Reading quickly makes me feel strangely satisfied.
Focusing on reading is something I'm also very good at. Studying intensively is something that I can still do very well, as long as I stay motivated.
It is the secret of my good grades, although at the same time I am quite a worker in class.
That's what Aiko and I have in common. She can seriously concentrate on painting if she wants.
I wonder what he's doing now. Probably working hard, painting.
This distance that suddenly grew between us irritates me. I thought we were getting closer, but now that feeling is lost.
I'm a little worried about her, too.
I share Sora's sentiment of being worried about Aiko. She's the kind of person who could get so wrapped up in her own strange world, and get lost in there before she realizes it.
It's not that I feel like I'm some kind of white knight who could save Aiko from herself. She doesn't need saving. But I just can't leave her alone either.
Without Aiko, I actually don't have anyone else at school that I really talk to. It's not like we talk much, anyway, but at least we hang out together.
aiko_a3_seq_10: I really don't want to lose that.
If I want to keep what I have with Aiko, I have to be involved with making this exhibition happen, right next to her.
I realize I've been on the same page for a while now.
I turn my gaze back to the book I'm reading. The jungle of glyphs has somehow become almost incomprehensible code. I look at it carefully, waiting for the text to start to make sense to me.
No pattern emerges, nothing that can take me further than I already am.
Dazed, I close the book, put it back on the shelf, then sit down again and think honestly and deeply about what it is that I really want.
Like Sora, I have a club meeting, so I head straight to the art room at the end of the hall.
Only a few members are present today, so the mood is even more relaxed than usual.
Aiko is away working on her exhibition project, but I wonder if the others are just zoning out, defeated by the heat.

I half-heartedly make a sketch with a piece of graphite, but the result is poor. My fingertips are turning tarry black from holding the graphite and smearing it on the paper, by accident and on purpose.
I've improved a little, but Aiko's level is still beyond my reach.
Eventually Nomiya enters and makes her way around the room, reviewing what we are doing and making comments on the work in progress.
He stops behind me and leans closer to look at my poor drawing.
You tried to take some advice from Tezuka, right?
Oh, well, I've seen how she draws but I haven't asked for advice, exactly.
Let's see here.
He nonchalantly takes the piece of graphite from my hand and lightly draws some faint, barely visible lines over my drawing to illustrate places that need improvement.
I'm already frustrated by not seeing the obvious flaws sooner, but with a couple of quick and seemingly careless flicks of the wrist, Nomiya has made them as clear as day.
Straightening up, he casts a sidelong glance at the spot where Aiko usually sits.
What a nostalgic feeling, almost like a bird flying from its nest. I'll miss Tezuka when he graduates. Start from here, you know.
It almost makes my eyes water.
Do you really think she has a chance to have great success with her exhibition?
Nomiya turns and looks over my drawing, adjusting her glasses. He rubs his chin, looking contemplative.
Why not? It's not like it's going to be an overnight success or anything like that, but getting the word out is very important.
Connections are pure gold, perhaps the most important thing to achieve if she is going to become an artist. Word of mouth is very powerful in these circles.
She has some advantages, such as her young age and her technique. You know, the feet. People will naturally be curious about those kinds of extraordinary things.
His words have an unpleasant tone.
Isn't that just taking advantage of her disability to make her more popular? It sounds dirty.
Oh, now, now. It's not that way at all. Think about it from another point of view, like an artist.
Would you rather have Tezuka hide completely from public view, as if his condition were something shameful?
Some people will say it's taking advantage if we promote that aspect, or discrimination if we hide it. At the end of the day, we're just being honest about it.
There is nothing wrong with that, is there, my son?
I guess.
Bright!
It is true that disability always has all kinds of implications on society, often unpleasant, but sweeping things under the rug will not help at all.
I'm sure Sae will handle her side of the matter delicately. I have known her since art school and she is most reliable.
Why is she doing so much for Aiko's sake? Because you are the one who asked for it?
Oh, she has her own reasons too. Trust this old man, she is kinder than she seems.
Oh, but don't let him know I said that.
He gives me a big wink and covers his mouth with his hand, as if he wants to save the comment.
I remember the curious way Miss Saionji looked at Aiko almost all the time during our visit to the gallery. It was as if this woman was trying to record everything about her into her memory.
Or maybe it was that Aiko reminded him of something else.
More than anything, Sae adores young people with a passion for art. His gallery specializes in that very thing, bringing promising talent to the public.
It suits someone like Tezuka perfectly.
However I don't even know if she really wants to become a professional artist. But I guess that would be the next logical step.
shizu_seq_1: The next morning, I remember what a perfect night yesterday was. So much so that I can't stop thinking about it.
It's probably not the best time to reminisce, since I have a test in the first class.

Ah, it's so unfair. How can they do this? They hold a festival that is the culmination of what has to be the effort of at least a few weeks of work on a Sunday, and then follow up with exams starting the next morning?
It has to be some kind of bad joke.
I'm not too worried about it, but I wonder if they really couldn't have postponed this for at least another week.
Well, at least the weather this morning is so nice that I can study outside before class.
It's much more refreshing out here than it would be in the classroom. Not to mention how quiet it is, I'm starting to think everyone else will be sleeping in pretty late today.
I put down the notes I'm reviewing for a second and stare at the school campus, still packed with festival booths.
Looking at them now in the daytime, without paper lanterns or crowds of people to divert my attention from them, I notice something curious.
Many of the stalls that Shizune, Shiina, and I visited last night also happen to be the same ones we built.
How adorable. Did Shizune come up with this? It had to be intentional, especially knowing her. Did she expect me to notice and see the fruit of our labors?
I hear footsteps crunching the grass behind me and I turn around. I feel a little paranoid, but all I find is Shizune standing there with an innocuous look on her face.
Good morning.
Why do I keep forgetting that she can't hear me?

It's probably because I've gotten so used to Shiina translating for both of us that I haven't encountered many situations where I was forced to acknowledge Shizune's deafness and the problems that might arise from it.
I think yesterday was the first.
I wave at her anyway. At least I can do this, but I'm not even going to pretend for a moment that I could hold a conversation with her, considering my ignorance of sign language.
Would it be rude if I just went back to my notes? I really don't know what else I could do.
Where is Shiina?
It's not just because I can't understand you. You two are always together anyway, so I'm not used to seeing you alone.
I know it's silly but for some reason talking to her makes me feel less awkward.
Surprisingly, he doesn't get angry at all. She begins to sign; but it is different from normal. Shizune's hands move more slowly, and the gestures are simpler.
I quickly realize that this isn't sign language at all, but that she is still trying to communicate with me.
So this is the equivalent of sign language reduced to simple terms?
I'm terrified that if I try to gesture back, I'll just look like a complete idiot.
The look on Shizune's face tells me that she's starting to think that trying to have any kind of exchange like this isn't exactly the best way to go about things.
There has to be a better way.
Write in a notebook? Well, yes I have paper and pencil. But what else?
Cell phones? I don't really get much use out of mine here, so I barely carry it, and I don't even know if Shizune has one.
She takes the lead, raising a finger to ask for a pause before pulling a notebook and pen from her backpack and writing a single word on it:
I stare at her blankly and receive a similar, but somehow more intimidating look in response. She pushes the notebook toward me forcefully, clearly wanting me to respond.
Shizune smiles with a disproportionate amount of happiness. She begins to twirl her pen triumphantly as she thinks about where to go from here.
Oh, come on, it's not like we've just invented fire.
Shizune pushes her glasses up sharply, as if she heard me, and then begins to write at a breakneck pace.
I'm confused; Now I'm supposed to take it and write “good”?
This is about as far from a smooth, flowing conversation as I could imagine. It makes me envy the ease with which Shiina is able to communicate with Shizune.
I'm pretty sure I can get away with answering simple yes or no questions like this with nods.
…Oh, yeah?
But before I deliver that answer to her, I remember what I had noticed before, and add:
She shakes her head from side to side indignantly.
I'm a little moved. Still, I have to wonder why she would do something so unusual for her, and I ask in my response.

I mean I was depressed for days, but enough. Admittedly, I was pretty bummed, and I wasn't being very subtle about it half the time either, so it's possible she knew. So everything he did was to cheer me up?
Thank you.
I mutter it before I can realize it, but Shizune doesn't seem to care. Instead I write it, and she nods once, like she's not used to it.
The silence between us grows enormously with each passing second, and there is nothing I can do to break it. Having to write everything down on paper kind of destroys any hope of being casual.
shizu_seq_2: Shizune shoves the notebook right in front of my eyes, breaking my concentration. Taking the initiative again, as always.
As she walks towards the school building, I can't help but feel a little sad.

Those felt like the longest twenty minutes of my life, all because it's so strange for me to have a face-to-face conversation with someone passing notes to each other, that I can't help but go blank most of the time.
It makes me want to learn sign language.
That's easier said than done. Although at a school like Yamaku, they could very well have sign language classes. In that case, there would be very little reason not to do so.
The only person I can think of to ask, right now, is Shiina.
How badly do I want to know this? There are two options: wait until after class, or go find her now.

I guess I'll go now, but I'm not sure where she is. However, my best bet would be to start looking for her in the girls' dormitory. After all, if he wasn't with Shizune, that's probably the only place she would be.
A guy casually hanging around the girls' dormitory early in the morning is unacceptable, but asking Shiina about sign language classes in front of Shizune would be unthinkable.
She has to come to school sometime. After all, we are in the same class, so she has to take the exam too.
If I wait here, I'll be sure to see her sooner or later.
I just hope it doesn't walk in front of me while I'm flipping through my notes.
It turns out to be quite a long wait. As the students enter the school, I wonder if Shiina is going to be late.
I finally see her. As she bounces around campus, I realize I'd have to be blind to miss seeing her with her incredibly distinctive hair.
Hello, Hicchan~! Good morning~!
Good morning.
I don't have much time before class starts, so I'll get straight to the point.
Hey, can I ask you a question?
A question? Hm~…Very good, Hicchan~! Sure~ sure~! I have time, but only because I'm going to be late!
What does that mean?
Haha~. I should have woken up earlier, but I was so tired~…if I had, I would have to study, but since I didn't, it won't hurt~! What's wrong, Hicchan?
Well, there are sign language classes here, right?
Yep~! They are optional! Why do you want to know, Hicchan?
For some reason that question briefly makes me panic.
For no reason. Sounds interesting, but I guess it's too late to sign up now, right?
I'm not exactly being very subtle here, but Shiina never seems to pick up on things like that anyway, so I'm probably being more careful than necessary.
Hm~? Ah well, Hicchan, I've heard that there are fewer and fewer students taking sign language each year. So! If you want that, I'm sure they'll let you in~!
Are you thinking about learning sign language, Hicchan?
…Yes.
If you learned sign language, Hicchan, that would make Shicchan very happy~. If you want, we can go to the teachers office after school. They'll probably let you in.
That would be great.
But don't tell Shizune I want to learn it.
Why not?
So it can be a surprise. Plus, it'll look bad if you tell him this morning, and then I find out in the afternoon that I can't take classes.
Oh~. You're right, Hicchan. Still, this will be difficult~… This is such good news…

I'm on the student council, so I might as well try to learn it. Even if it's just the basics, it would be progress over nothing. Besides, Shizune and I can't keep passing everything through you like you're a phone or something, right?
Wow~!
You're right, Hicchan~!
The bell rings to signal the start of the first class, interrupting our conversation. I guess I'll just ask a teacher after school is over.
His reaction was a little strange, but I forget about it as the day progresses.
The bell rings and the teacher at the front of the room gestures that classes are over for the day.
Although getting into this class was surprisingly easy, it's only been a few days and I'm still not used to the experience.
The signs themselves are easier to learn than I expected, but most of my classmates are hearing impaired.
On top of that, the teacher encourages immersion. I haven't heard her speak since I asked her if I could take the class. It's a strange concept, and really disturbing.
The moment I leave the classroom, I hear familiar laughter explode into the air a short distance to my left.
shizu_seq_3: Hello, Hicchan~!
Shiina is not in my sign language class, so this is the first time I have seen her in this context. I still don't know if her not being in my class is good or bad.
It would be more interesting with her in it, but the potential for awkward situations would increase dramatically.
Hello.
It's a surprise to see you here, Hicchan! …Ah, that's right! You're taking sign language, aren't you~? True~!
How do you like the class so far, Hicchan?
It's not easy to learn a new language, but I think I'm getting used to it. Despite how different it is from other languages, it is still easier than English.
Haha~! Seriously, Hicchan?
Hm~…I agree~!
She was just joking, but apparently she's totally serious.
I wonder how Shiina can easily translate things for me and at the same time have a conversation with Shizune in a different language, just like she does.
Until now, I had taken for granted how amazing it is.
Someone bumps into my shoulder and apologizes. It's getting a little crowded here, what with it being the end of the day and all.
I think we should talk somewhere better than the hallway. Let's go to the roof or something.
Okay~!
I decide to continue talking on the way. It's amazing and calm enough to have a conversation while we go.

It's still taking me some time to get used to always having to look at the teacher. I guess I took for granted all those years of just listening to the lessons while doodling. It also makes taking notes much more difficult.
The introductory class is small, and I'm already falling behind. I guess I have a lot of things to do.
Yes, this is much better.
I turn around to look at Shiina and see her staring at me with her hands on her hips and her cheeks puffed out.
Hicchan, are you falling behind? That's not good at all!
I started class a week after everyone else. It's not that bad.
Alright, Hicchan, then let's go over what you learned~! I'll be your tutor, okay~?
This is the first time I've heard “I'll be your guardian” used outside of pornographic movies; I'm not nearly as excited as I would have hoped.
I don't know if I need a tutor yet.
She looks more disappointed than usual. It makes me uncomfortable to see her make that face.
I want to be a sign language teacher, Hicchan! But~, it would be really cool if I could try tutoring someone first. Even if it is for a little while, the experience would be valuable.
Oh well, yes, that's true.
I didn't know you wanted to be a sign language teacher.
It's hard to believe she's not intentionally trying to make me feel guilty, because she's so good at it.

Still, it makes sense. She's already very good at sign language from what I've seen, and certainly has the voice to deal with deaf people. Although I never saw her as the kind of person who would be a teacher.
Hahaha~! That's the reason I wanted to come to this school, Hicchan!
It's also very expensive to attend here, you know? Since I want to be a sign language teacher, I have reduced tuition fees. If it weren't for that, I don't know if I could continue here.
I see. It's not that I think you'd be bad at tutoring, I just don't know if I need it right now.
You're right, Hicchan, you're smart.
Well, no, that just makes me sound arrogant.
Very well, please be my tutor.
Ahahaha~! Oh really? Very good~! Good good good~! Hurray~! Thanks, Hicchan~! I will do my best!
Let's start right now~!
Too soon.
I miss Shicchan~…
Didn't you see her this morning?
But she's hard to talk to in class, Hicchan! And today there is no student council either~.
Well, there have been exams all week. I'd be kind of mad if there was a student council; I'll be glad when they're done.
When we get back, you're not going to run away, are you, Hicchan?
shizu_seq_4: Of course not. I'm already involved in this, after all.
Don't worry, I won't suddenly stop showing up. A promise is a promise.
Shiina stops for a second, not looking very convinced.
Shicchan takes the student council very seriously, Hicchan. Now that you've joined, she works harder than before, as she wants to make a good impression.
Some people joined at first, but stopped coming soon after. Shicchan tried to get more people interested in the student council but was unsuccessful.
Even when someone joined, they eventually stopped coming. They made excuses and only put it off more and more until they stopped coming altogether.
However… I think you're really serious, Hicchan.
My eyes stay focused on her hands, bending and moving almost of their own volition, gently gesturing everything she says to herself as she speaks.
When you said you would join, she was very happy.
Shicchan thinks you're interesting, Hicchan. An uninteresting person will not have the drive to join. Even if you do, an uninteresting person will leave soon after.
That's what Shicchan said.
So~! It's my duty to make sure you continue~!
Is that why you want to be my tutor? You are somewhat malicious.
Seriously, Hicchan? It's the first time someone has said that about me~! Wahahaha~!
There's no chance I would avoid student council work now.
Thinking back over the past few days, I've started to realize that the only reason I joined in the first place was because of Shizune; His competitiveness and willpower are attractive.
But I can't say that to Shiina.
Alright, Hicchan, let's go over what you learned in class today~!
You don't even know what I learned in class today.
Hm~, you're right, Hicchan~! Alright, then let's start with the basics~! I'm going to teach you everything from the beginning~!
You're kidding, right?
Huh~?
Are you serious? That's like, days of lessons, and we're not even learning at the same level...
It's like riding a bike, Hicchan~! You never forget the basics! Wow~!
Although I don't know how to ride a bike~…
Oh no.
True, true~. I want to be a teacher one day, so of course I know what I'm doing... Very good~! Good good good~! Let's get started~!
…Mmm~…
Ahahaha~…
It seems like he's trying too hard, so this could be bad. Well, learning a language is very different from teaching it, and the first step is usually the hardest. Honestly, I couldn't do it better.
Still...

Um... Sign language was formally introduced in the 18th century by a Frenchman named... ah... whose name I can't pronounce, and he founded the first public school for the deaf in 1755, but the unwritten history of sign language says that...
I really don't know where to start. Sorry~…Well~, what better place to start than the history of sign language? Right~? True~!
No, wait, maybe the alphabet. Very well~, let it be the alphabet, then!
Very good, Hicchan~! This is very basic, although some people think that this is all sign language, and forget that there are all kinds of specific words and gestures.
Although you really can't get anywhere without the basics! This is A. Do you see it? Now, try it!
But I already know this.
I please her anyway.
Ha ha ha! Yes, that's it!
Now, this is B, and this is C.
Shiina makes a symbol with each hand, without specifying which is which.
And now D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, Ñ, O, P, Q, R, S, T, U, VWXY and Z~!
Yes, this is bad.
Do you think Shizune wants to do some student council work today anyway? We could go.
Of course not, Hicchan~!! Come on, I'll do it again! A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K... Your turn~!
shizu_seq_5: So there's really no student council work that needs to be done, or anything like that?
What are you talking about, Hicchan? Come on, sign, sign~!
So?
No, like this!
So...
Like this~!
A…ha…
I wish Shicchan was here, this would be so much easier with her. Hahaha, anyway, that's how sign language is taught most of the time, with two instructors~! Did you know that, Hicchan?
I let my brain think about what this would be like if Shizune was here.
Hicchan~! Are you paying attention?

Shicchan says sign language is different from any other because you have to think about everything before you say it. That means every word has more weight, Hicchan. Each one of them is more important than normal.
So~, pay attention please.
She continues her basic overview of the fundamentals of sign language. Finally she starts talking about things I'm starting to recognize.
In the end, I'm impressed. It took her a few stumbles to get there, but as a teacher, she's very good when she gets serious.
After a while I start to notice that it's getting late, so I thank Shiina, say goodbye to her, and return to my room.
I learned a lot today.
I wake up startled by a thunderous knocking sound coming from my door.
My first thought is, it could be Shizune. After all, only a deaf person or an idiot would hit that hard at this hour.
Who is it?
Of course, if it's Shizune, he wouldn't be able to hear that or answer it.
There's no response, so I'm kind of happy. I haven't seen Shizune in a while.
Opening the door, I find Kenji standing out in the hallway, his eyes shifting nervously from side to side.
Oh, it's you.
Yes, it's me. What kind of reaction is that?
Well, I could give you a more personalized answer if you had responded when I asked who it was.
Kenji frowns and pushes his glasses up exactly like Shizune.
Why are you making that funny face?

I wonder how he's able to see me making a face now, but he wasn't able to the other million times I've reacted to something weird he's said or done. I kind of want to find out, but I'm too tired to do it.
Shizune pushes her glasses up exactly like that. You know, the student council president. It's a little strange.
What the devil? What do you mean there is a girl who does the same thing? You mean he touches his glasses? I do that, that's my thing.
Who is that bitch? Why are those bitches involved in my business, stealing what I make?
His character jumps from anger to fear in the blink of an eye.
Is she trying to replace me? Body usurpers? No, wait, that's an exact copy. Usurping women?
It's like a combination of my two biggest fears.
It is!
I can't believe he's right...
Hey, are you going to town today?
Eh, maybe later.
Very good. Brilliant. I have some… things I want you to pick up for me at the post office. Some delicate and secret things.
He speaks quietly, as if talking about his mail, even in a normal tone of voice, puts him in danger.
You can have your mail sent directly here, you know?
No, you can't. You can have your mail sent to the school, and then the student council picks it up, and then they give it to you. It is not the same as mail reaching your hands.
I don't trust the student council. A lot of guys don't get their mail here, you know?
They probably steal everything! Do they think that just because it is sent to them, they have a license to steal?
I can see them now, up to their necks in the mail, quickly grabbing all the free loot they can get their hands on. Disgusting.
shizu_seq_6: Where can I find the postman who can appear mail out of nowhere in your hands?
I don't know, I bet the student council killed him to preserve their monopoly on all student shit.
It doesn't work that way.
That's what you wanted, right? Well, I can collect your mail for you, but in the end I'm going to collect all these favors. You already owe me some money.
Thanks for reminding me. I will pay you after I receive my package.
Yeah, sorry, I can't actually pay you until then. I'm still broke.
So basically I'm doing it for money, like a job. Why do you need the package in the first place? Is there money in the package?
I am seriously flabbergasted.
Why can't you go get him?
Because today I'm going to remodel my room like a war room.
As the days go by, I realize more and more how dangerous feminism is. It really is everywhere, even in places like Iran. You can't know how far it goes.
When the war begins, if we have not transcended the concept of nations to fight for our genders, it will be chaos.
No one will know who will take which side, and a war against feminism would not only mean World War III, but the end of all life on Earth as we know it.
If we lose, all of our lithe Japanese women will be raped and enslaved by a bunch of sociopathic lesbian supremacists.
Meanwhile, the handful of men who did not die in the war will be castrated and forced to repair toilets and build huge monuments commemorating the feminist victory.
That's crazy. You're crazy. I think you're overthinking this.
As the days go by, I realize more and more that you're not cool.
We've only talked like four times.
Oh. I'm sorry.
Yeah, whatever, I'll bring your package.
Brilliant.
I close the door and throw myself back into bed.

The second my head hits the pillow, a painfully loud sound assaults my ears, and I realize it's my watch. The alarm going off means that right now is the time I'm supposed to wake up in the first place.
At least during the week.
I take it and throw it without looking up. He gets trapped between the bed and the wall, and the noise doesn't stop. In fact, it seems to sound louder.
By the time I can get him out of there I know I won't be able to sleep again. The only thing I can think of to do now is go to town and just bring Kenji's stupid package, but it's too early for that.
After the shower, I take my medication. I'm actually really hungry today since I went without dinner yesterday, and before that I only had a very light lunch.
I eat the pills, chewing them like a leg of lamb. They are incredibly bitter and disgusting.
Well, good medicine tastes bad, or something like that. I'm still hungry, and there's still plenty of time to burn, so I decide to head into town and find somewhere to have breakfast.
I can't remember the last time I ate out. Plus, the weather is nice, so why not?
The walk to town is longer than I remember, possibly because it's been a while, and probably because I rarely come here alone.
There are hardly any cars on the road because it is so early in the morning, making it unusually quiet.
The first thing I do is start looking for a place to eat. I immediately think of Shanghai, but I want something heartier than sandwiches or a cake.
But since it's so early, I decide to pick up Kenji's package first.
Picking it up at the post office doesn't take long, but the moment I see it, I'm infuriated at how annoying it will be to carry this thing all the way back to school.
The box is huge, you need two hands to hold it. Insultingly, it's not even very heavy.
I was thinking about wandering around for a bit, but with this thing in tow, that's going to be a real problem. I guess Shanghai is my only option now.
Everything else is closed, and those that aren't all have almost the same menu. That fact also makes me bring a little more clientele to Yuuko.
Before I can open the door and walk in, someone taps me on the shoulder from behind. I turn around and see Shizune there. Instinctively, I look for Shiina, but she doesn't seem to be here.
Good morning.
It seems those sign language classes are already starting to bear fruit. I'm tempted to wave to her to answer her, but then she might think I know more than I really do.
For now, I just wave at her and open the door. She's probably here for her morning tea and didn't come here just to greet me. Turns out I'm right, as Shizune follows me into the teahouse.
It's a complete ghost town here. It's not exactly rush hour, but every other cafe I passed had at least a few customers.
Actually, Shanghai has been pretty lonely every time I've passed through here. How is this place still running?
Hello! Thank you for choosing to be customers of our establishment!
shizu_seq_7: Yuuko leans down with the force of a falling ax and her head collides with the box in my hands, sending it crashing to the ground.
Oh no, I'm sorry, I'm very, very sorry, please forgive me!
That's okay, and you don't have to do that “Hey, thanks for choosing our business!” since we know you.
But it's part of my job.
You're here early, how can I help you?
I just want some coffee for now.
I wonder what Shizune wants. Without Shiina, there's no real way to tell, nor any way to ask. I haven't learned about that yet. She's here, so I'm pretty sure that means she wants something too.
Eh, I don't really know what Shizune wants. Does she ask for something customary?
Wait, she might want something else though. Maybe you should bring us a menu just in case.
I look around for one, but can't find anything that remotely resembles a menu.
Menus… I'll look for one right now.
Hey?
Um… there are menus. They're just… weird.
It's just a restaurant menu, not a collector's edition.
How odd.
Is that what Shizune is saying?
No, she can't hear you. It's just weird for a cafe to make you have to complicate your life to look up a menu.
Queer…?

Yes you're right. It's so illogical. There are so many things… Like, why is it called Shanghai? This is a Western-style tea house… but, the name is Chinese… and the architecture is old-fashioned, but my uniform is so modern and sophisticated…
She looks like she's about to faint. If that happens, she will probably fall forward and make a complete mess.
I can't work here anymore.
What a bad place for your thread of circular logic to end.
No, let's go. That kind of thing is what sets this place apart; There are a lot of cafes around here, you know? I think it's lovely, actually. Please don't give up. Business is good, isn't it?
Not really…
You see, I think this is a good job for you. You're doing well, you shouldn't give up.
I've never had to diffuse this type of crisis before.
In the end, I manage to calm her down, and convince her that I'm sure Shizune only wants what she always orders here.
Yuuko leaves to get our drinks, and by then, Shizune has already chosen a table.
There are no other customers, and Yuuko isn't the most talkative person, so it's very quiet.
It doesn't really bother me, but I wish there was some way we could communicate. There are so few moments when we are alone.
Shizune and Shiina are almost always together, to the point where sometimes it seems as if they are one.
Now, it's just me and her, and I'm unable to understand her or make her understand me. It's terrible.
Don't you have your little notebook today? I know it's the weekend and all, but it's not like you to be caught off guard.
OK that's fine. I don't really like using it anyway. However, it would be useful now.
Shizune begins signing in short bursts interrupted by pausing to take a sip of tea. It's strange how she doesn't make the slightest attempt to change the way she normally acts.
I'm talking to you largely because I'm not used to long silences. I briefly wonder if it's the same for her, in a way; however, it seems unlikely.
I think more that she is the type of person who doesn't change her ways for anyone.
Hey, it looks like Shiina joined the student council thanks to you. That makes two of us, you know? I'm only there because you forced me to join.
Well, you didn't really force me, I guess. If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have joined.
That sounds slightly romantic, and I'm blushing a little. I feel like an idiot.
Although, I still don't know why you joined. It should have been the first thing I asked, looking back, but I'm really curious. I'll have to remember that to ask Shiina sometime.
It's nice to talk to you, even if you can't understand me. I wonder if it's the same for you.
That would be really… cool.
I don't think sign language will be as natural to me as Shiina makes it seem, but it has to be a step up from using pen and paper, right?
We're both done with our drinks for a while, and Shizune's eyes fall on the box sitting in her own chair next to me.
shizu_seq_8: I'm just collecting it for someone, it's not mine.
Shizune pulls it towards her, intending to open it, and my heart almost leaps into my throat. I quickly try to bring her back by wrapping my leg around the leg of the chair.
But what the hell, don't open it. You can't open other people's mail, that's not legal.
No!

Once she gets going, there is almost no way to stop her. Eyes full of excitement, she looks ready to fight me over this stupid package and I realize how quickly this could turn into a game of tug of war.
Now I'm almost out of my seat and waving my hands like an air traffic controller, before she finally calms down.
Shizune pouts, not happy with having her curiosity curbed, and gets up to leave.
It's almost time, I guess. We've been here a while. I protectively pick up the box before standing.
Suddenly, she puts her fingers together excitedly and pulls a marker out of her pocket, and begins to write on Kenji's box.
Hey, what are you doing? I said it's not mine!
Hey!
I can't even see her with the box blocking my vision.
Well, at least let me put it on the ground first.
I have to do it to read whatever I'm writing, anyway.
However it doesn't seem like it's over, and Shizune then draws a fierce line to indicate that there is a trap.
That's stupid, there's a fifty percent chance I'll end up carrying it myself anyway.
Actually, I feel pretty stupid myself right now. I forgot she can't hear me. I stop talking and shake my head.
I can't understand her at all, but she gives a very energetic impression. It's clear he thinks it's a great idea.
Well, if he drops the box or something, she'll have to carry it. That would make things a lot easier for me, obviously.
The chances are 50-50, so… they're probably higher than they would be for any other plan of yours. Very well, I will accept.

Thinking about it, I'm not sure how we should do this. Then Shizune grabs one end of the box and lifts it, and I grab the side she's not holding. Is it okay like this? It is very uncomfortable to walk this way.
We leave the café, and I find myself wishing the streets were still empty. Yuuko seemed confused as to what we were doing, and I imagine it will only get worse as more people see us.
Shizune doesn't seem bothered at all as she walks with her arm at this unnatural angle; He just smiles confidently and occasionally makes some kind of strange gesture.
There are people watching us as time passes, and the usual morning crowd begins to fill the streets.
I feel foolish, but I'm sure that if I give up, Shizune will take it as a sign of surrender. I can't allow it, because I think I'm doing well so far.
At first, I simply dismiss Shizune's small hand signals as her gloating in anticipation, but I quickly catch on that she's actually indicating where she wants to go.

I realize this is not a competition. It's not much of a challenge, first of all, and second, it's really more of a team-building exercise. It's just that Shizune has made it a punishment for failing instead of a reward for doing well.
Our fingers touch under the box, and Shizune pulls her hand away, almost dropping her side of the box in the process.
Well, it's game over for her.
She doesn't look very happy. Do you think I did it on purpose to make her lose? If so, you are not giving it much importance. All is fair in love and war.
I feel like I should pick her up and carry her myself, but she pushes me away when I try.
She looks at me fiercely as if she wants to scold me, but she can't. With that box in her hands, she's basically gagged.
A sad expression flickers on his face for a second, perhaps realizing that and having to acknowledge that there are some limitations he has to deal with after all.
However, she remains as proud as ever, even when it is to her detriment. She would not agree to let me allow her to evade the consequences of her bet.
Anything goes during the game, but the results have to be honored to the letter, eh?
Shizune is an interesting type of person.
The walk back to the dorms is calm. Shizune spends the trip occasionally moving the box around like a giant Rubik's Cube. It seems like another game he invented for fun.
It can't be good for whatever's inside, but I don't care enough to stop her.
Maybe that's how she deals with things, turning everything into a game; However, it is difficult to know for sure.
It seems pointless to try to psychoanalyze Shizune. In the short time we have known each other, I have surprised myself on quite a few occasions.
I notice Shizune shiver. The wind is increasing, and the school is quite high. It makes sense that she is cold. However, if I gave you my jacket, would you reject it?
I take off my jacket and drape it over his shoulders before he has a chance to protest. Her shoulders are thin and delicate, so much so that I want to leave my hands on them for a moment.
Shizune shudders when my fingers brush against her, understandably surprised.
I'm sorry.

Her fingers dance softly over the surface of the box, and I think about taking it, but I doubt she'll let me. Shizune makes a quick gesture with her hands as best she can, pausing a little after as if she wants to say more.
shizu_seq_9: I'm sure what she wants to say is “thank you.” I'm glad I was able to understand it.
The sign language teacher says I'm very good.

I try not to think about it too much, but the truth is that I've been studying it so thoroughly lately that it's hard not to keep coming back to it at least a couple of times a day. I guess I'm learning it faster than expected, but it's still not enough.
I understand it very well; Understanding it is simple. Well, I have to concentrate on it to read it, but it's pretty easy when I do.
The signs themselves can be done, I just need a little more practice. However, trying to do both at the same time, even at half the speed Shiina does it? It's impossible.
Where I am now is good for my level, but in order to get to the point where I can actually converse with Shizune, I will need more work.
I'm doing my best to get there step by step, studying as much as I can during lunch.
I look up from the “Introduction to Japanese Sign Language” to check if Shizune or Shiina are nearby.
Of course, since this is taking up my lunch hour, I've had to avoid them for a few days. What's more, I'll have to continue doing it if I want to prevent Shizune from finding out.
With my back to the corner, scanning the area every ten minutes, I feel like some kind of criminal trying to evade capture.
Every chance she gets, Shiina asks me why I want to hide the fact that I'm learning sign language from Shizune.
Looking back, there wasn't really any reason, but now I think I know.
If I want Shizune to be able to treat me as a true equal, sign language is an important step toward that goal.
If I want to be able to treat Shizune as an equal, then sign language is an important step towards that goal.
Another important step is to make sure she doesn't know, so that when we can finally talk on equal terms, I will be completely ready, able to do it well, not like some dilettante.
Anything less, I think, would be insulting. She would see it the same way.
So for me, this is the only option. Especially now that I've decided to be so firm about it.

Shizune has a huge aura. It is very easy to see it coming, or even feel it coming. Mostly because Shiina's hair lights up any crowd she's in like a beacon, and you can hear her laughing from a mile away.
Although, even if Shiina wasn't with her, it would be the same. Her directness and efficiency are essential parts of her, so it's no surprise that these shine through in the way she walks too.
Because of all of those factors, I'm able to put my stuff away and put on my best casual face long before they see me and come my way.
Hello.
Student council.
Student Council~!
“Student council” was the first thing I asked to learn; It seemed like it would be useful to me.
Yeah, I've been avoiding it for a while now, huh?
Yep~!
Shizune sits in front of me, on my right, and Shiina on my left. It was a mistake to place myself in the corner; Now I'm, well, backed into a corner.
In the end, I am dragged to the student council room, but I don't care. I was starting to miss them a little, anyway.
In some ways this makes it easier: satisfied with having caught me, Shizune doesn't ask me where I've been this whole time.
Once I'm in front of the door, I wonder what could be so important to make them so eager to push me inside.
Games.

There are more games than books. This finally explains why whenever I come here there are piles of books stacked on all the tables and occasionally on parts of the floor: they need the space to put all these games somewhere.
Hahaha~!
It's boring to play with each other too much, Hicchan. So, it's your turn, okay? Good~! Then it's decided~!
I didn't even say anything!
Hicchan, this is one of the last days we can relax like this for a while. So~, it's especially important that we make the most of it, don't you think?
The Tanabata festival is coming soon, and we'll have to put in a lot of work for that, too.
So for now, play with us~!
Now that I think about it, it's true. I hadn't even noticed it because I've been so caught up in wanting to learn sign language. Shortly after one festival, another larger one appears.
I wonder if Shizune will try to nab a couple of new members to help with this as well.
You're right.
Hahaha~! Hurray~! Hicchan agrees~! Let's celebrate!
I know, we should play a game.
Let's play a game to celebrate, Hicchan~!
I don't know, that kind of thing usually ends badly for me.
shizu_seq_10: Hicchan is worried about the risks~.
Shiina makes a very disappointed face. It's hard to tell if she's making fun of me, since her expressions are so exaggerated by default. She is the kind of girl who “goes with everything”.
I turn my head towards Shizune. Now, this person is definitely making fun of me.
Hey, stop that. But, yes, I will play with you if you tell me first what is at stake.
How Japanese, putting consequences above all else.
Hicchan, have you ever heard the expression “You can't see the forest for the trees”?
That's a lie. But I have my pride, which right now feels hurt.
Okay, I'll play, but I want to choose the game.
Shiina nods.
Furthermore, I choose the punishment if you lose.
Shizune makes an X with her arms. That either means "denied" or that he's about to use his special attack.
Aha, now who's afraid of the consequences?
How vindictive, still thinking so resentfully for a nice little joke.
If a... bit you, you would surely bite back.
Shizune gestures for a word that I don't understand very well.
Hicchan is so vengeful~, although it was just a nice little joke. If an armadillo bit you, you would surely bite back!
Armadillo?
It's silly to bite back an armadillo, Hicchan!
But Hicchan would do it anyway! See~? Ha ha ha!
I see.
Shizune adjusts her glasses with a small ostentatious wave of her hand.
Hicchan, we didn't have anything planned at all if you were going to win or lose, you just assumed there would be something like that~.
I wonder why.
Hm~, me too~! But oh well~! There isn't. Does that change your mind, Hicchan?
Well… yes.
Shiina moves her arm like a windmill at high speed to show her joy. A strange habit. This is the kind of thing you could only see in the student council room, occupied by only three people.
Anywhere else she would end up punching someone in the face.
Long live~! Let's start right now!
Not yet.
It's okay, it's okay.
However, we all have to be able to play. That is my condition.

I don't like games where one person is clearly the star player right off the bat, or games where only two people can play and so one of us has to sit. It has to be something that the three of us can play equally.
Ladies?
The moment he says it, Shiina takes out a bag of checkers and puts them on the table.
Only two people can play that. I told them that—
Good good~! Hicchan, how about... Monopoly?
A Monopoly box slowly approaches me, and I take it out of Shiina's hands and put it under my chair.
I don't like games that revolve around a question of luck; They are too much about chance and not about skill. Also, stop rushing into these games!
Luck is like a skill, you know?
No, it's not!
It can be if you're constantly lucky~! Right~?
Once at that point it is something completely different.
Hm~, hm~ hm~ hm~~. Baccarat? Marbles? Life? Snakes and ladders? Roulette? Blackjack? Table soccer? Trivial Pursuit?
Shiina starts excitedly naming a bunch of games as if she were reading them off a list. With each hint, a new box, board, and pieces appear around you.
A rare catalog of games ranging from those aimed at children to polished looking serious gambling instruments that look very out of place in this humble room.
shizu_a3_seq_1: The following days pass without incident and with surprising speed. I find renewed motivation in learning sign language. I seem to have a gift for learning signs, so it would be a waste not to, and falling behind would be even more unacceptable.

Summer holidays are approaching. Although I imagined that student council work would see a decrease proportional to how lethargic my classes are becoming, that is not the case. Every day, I am overwhelmed with increasingly meaningless work.

Despite how much I want to, I don't even have a free second to talk to Shizune currently. Every time I look at her, her face is buried in some record book or some stack of papers that need to be reviewed in triplicate.

Today, I woke up early to come to school before everyone else, hoping to catch up with Shizune. She has the habit of coming first thing in the morning, to be more punctual than all the other students. Unfortunately, I think I'm earlier than her.
Hearing the door to the student council room click shut to my right tells me that's not the case. I guess I got here right after her.
I enter the room and tap Shizune on her shoulder to get her attention.
Maybe she's expecting a conversation, which is why she lowers the carton of orange juice in her hand.
Good morning.
Where is your better half?
We are separate individuals.
Thinking about it, they must be told that a lot. I can't think of any other way to explain how prepared I was with that answer.
You're here early. That's good, you can help me review some brochures. They will leave later today.
I came here early specifically so I could see you without having to do work.
According to Shiina, arriving early is not new to you.
It's not new to you either.
Are you saying you want to compete?
Shizune nonchalantly adjusts her glasses, a gesture that belies how giddy she is inside about the idea of ​​having something very insignificant to take on competitively and seriously.
I think the smaller the issue, the more excited he is.
It's not a competition. Do you want to turn it into a contest? I don't.
I almost forgot to add the last part, the most important part.
… OK that's fine. There are so many days left in the school year, I'd get tired of it anyway.

With that, Shizune drinks her juice and finishes it. I wonder if she's going to try to throw the empty container in the trash, but she doesn't. In fact, she seems perplexed as to why I seem so disappointed. I better get to the point.
I just wanted to talk. Our vacation is practically here, you know?
And we should spend more time together, anyway. I was thinking we could do that over the summer.

Shizune's face turns as red as mine should be, and she begins to adjust her glasses nervously. What a multipurpose gesture. She drums her fingers together thoughtfully, considering her next words carefully.
Do you mean a date?
Just because we're going out somewhere, does that immediately make it a date?
Isn't it?
I want it to be a date.
So it's one.
Shizune claps her hands in approval once, before adding to my statement:
But not today.
I'm leaving for a week to visit my family.
That's an oddly formal way of putting it, and for that reason, my interest is piqued.
Maybe your family is the formal, proper type, living in a giant old mansion with a stream and a koi pond, where everyone wears kimonos all the time.
It's a wild guess, but it's fun to speculate sometimes. I wonder if Shizune fakes the appearance of being a good, calm and mature daughter like Elena when she is with her family.
I can't imagine it, but if there's even a chance it's true, then I have to see it.
Just one week? The trip shouldn't be that far, then.
Of course not, they're still in Japan after all.
Seriously…
It's not like you can come with me. Is that what you're trying to say?
Why can't I?
It's not like you'd enjoy it.
You don't know that. It could be fun.
Oh, I almost forgot: you didn't answer my question. Are you going alone, or is Shiina going with you? Does your family know signs?
shizu_a3_seq_2: Shiina is going too.
