The part of the question that remains unanswered is the most revealing.
If Shizune's family can't contact her, I have to wonder what her childhood was like. He probably wrote everything in that notebook he carries with him and still pulls out of nowhere sometimes.
It's usually when neither Shiina nor I are around. I can see her from afar when he takes her out as a last resort, grimacing the entire time.
If Shiina goes, then I'll go, too.
Do you like Shiina?
It's a matter of principles.
I entertain the idea that Shizune might actually be jealous, but I doubt it. She usually wears her emotions very clearly on her face, and I don't see anything to support my theory right now.
I think you're just bored.
But it's okay. Okay, we'll all go together. It's what I wanted from the beginning.
Today you can't escape from the student council to pack your bags, just because you're coming with us on such short notice, that's no excuse!
It's okay, I barely have anything to pack anyway.
Shizune pauses, clasping her fingers together thoughtfully.
You should have come to this school on very short notice.

It could be that she is remembering the time when Shiina and her unexpectedly barged into my room and caught a glimpse of all my medications. That was an awkward moment that I would like to forget, and I don't like to remember it.
The way she tiptoes around the topic even now only makes me more uncomfortable.
That's how it was. It was like a decision on the spot. However, it turned out better than I expected.
I hope Shizune doesn't continue with that matter, and to my relief, she doesn't.
My house is in a particularly beautiful area of ​​Saitama.
We will be leaving early in the morning, so be prepared. Let's talk about that later, okay? For now, those pamphlets won't review themselves, and you're going to help me.
As Shizune throws herself into her work, dragging me along with her, I think she seems almost, but not quite, excited to go.
When Shizune and Shiina arrive early the next morning to pick me up, they are dressed in something other than the school uniform I had become accustomed to seeing.
It makes sense, since we're on vacation, but it's still shocking. Shizune's dress is elegant and fashionable, almost too fashionable for a quiet place like Yamaku.
Remembering what she wore at the Tanabata festival, I'm starting to notice a trend in her.
All their clothes are mature and of very good taste; very well made. So, then, I wonder why she herself is so immature.
Well, at least Shiina's clothes reflect her inner self on the outside.
You are bringing very little.
I said I would do it. I said there wasn't much to pack.

Shizune pouts and kicks her own rather large collection of luggage with her foot as if embarrassed. Shiina only brings a suitcase with her, but it's almost bigger than her. She looks self-conscious about it too.

God, that suitcase is as big as a compact car. The pea green color is also disturbing. It looks like something used to transport corpses. The way they look right now makes me want to tease them a little.
Oh, that's bad luck for you and Shiina, isn't it? Having to carry those huge suitcases. They have to pack light next time, like me. Everything fits in a small suitcase.
Like James Bond~!
Yes, exactly like James Bond.
Shizune gently tugs at her glasses in concentration.
We should divide the amount we carry equally.
Wow~! That's a great idea, Shicchan~!
That? No.
It would benefit all of us.
Yep~! Wow~!
I'm going to have to say no.
You are a minority!
She almost lunges forward when she signs it. Scary.
Oh ok. I was just joking. I don't mind carrying a little extra. I just thought it would be fun to play with you two.
But, if they were going to try to make me carry everything, I was going to ride that giant green suitcase down the mountain like a sleigh.

That seems to make Shizune laugh, and she raises a hand to her mouth to restrain it. It's like he's hiding it. I wonder if she can laugh. If not, that may be why she does that. It kind of makes me feel sad.
shizu_a3_seq_3: Having taken care of that, we head to the train station, and a very peaceful walk ensues.
Shizune and Shiina manage to fall asleep almost instantly, but I find myself unable to do so. That's never happened to me before. Maybe it's my medicine.
When we get to Shizune's house, it's much bigger than I imagined it would be. I don't think huge is an exaggeration.
Do you live in a mansion?

Shizune stands on the tip of her feet, indignant, so that we are at eye level, and frowns deeply, after my comment is translated by Shiina. It's like he's saying, “How can you say something like that?”
This is just a normal house. Nothing as ostentatious as a mansion.
I think our definitions of those terms are quite different, then.
Wow~. Hicchan, are you surprised? Do you want me to show you where you're staying?
I think we have one guest room, but I'm not sure if we have two. I'll go check.
Hm~, but it's no problem, Hicchan~! Shicchan and I can share a room if necessary. Well~, unless yours is being used for something else.

"I'm not sure"? I'm starting to think that Shizune doesn't spend much time at home. Before I can make a joke about it at her expense, Shizune vanishes into the house, and Shiina goes with her, leaving me alone in the garden.
I don't want to follow them in yet. I leave my suitcase by the front door, and take the opportunity to look at the gardens, just taking a quick lap around the house.

Although it only takes a few minutes, when I return the first thing I notice is that my suitcase is gone, and a little girl is in its place. She looks a lot like Shizune, although Shizune wouldn't wear red shorts or socks with stars and moons on them.
Hello! Are you Shizune's little sister or something?
No. I'm his younger brother. My name is Hideaki.
Nice to meet you.

The voice that answers is direct, monotonous, and also undoubtedly masculine. I feel embarrassed to the point where I could almost turn around and leave right now, if I could remember the way back to the train.
Are you the second person my sister brought with her?
“Did she bring it with her?” I am not luggage.
Anyway, I'm Hisao. Did you take my suitcase?
Yes, it is my right to keep anything I find on my property.
No, it's not. That's not how it works at all.

I suppose even young, particularly well-spoken children believe in the law of “find it, keep it.” Although I call him small, he doesn't seem that young, now that I think about it. Maybe two or three years younger, tops.
I gave it to Shizune. It's inside. Are you on the student council?
Yeah, how did you know? Does she bring it up often?
I almost said “does she talk about that often?” That could have been bad.
Yes, all the time. Do you get along with her?
Get along? That's a strange question. I wouldn't be on the student council if I couldn't get along with her. What about you, do you two get along?

Although he has a monotone voice, his face is as expressive as Shizune's, and contradicts what he really feels. It must be a family thing. It seems like he's not happy with my question, for whatever reason.
I'm sorry. I was just asking because you two act very similar.
I don't know why, but it feels like he's pulling my leg. Unfortunately, it works. I don't like being compared to Shizune.
You're more like Shizune, but that's to be expected. I even confused you with his younger sister. If you don't want people to make that mistake, you should dress more appropriately.
I don't understand, my clothes match the season.
What about tights?
They are fashionable.
You act like my sister. Eventually people will start to confuse you with her.
I guess my comment hit him harder than I thought. That would explain this attempt to turn it around.
I hate being compared to other people.
Shizune also doesn't like it when she is compared to other people.

I had thought that Hideaki was a little more mature than Shizune, but they have the same competitive streak and the same penchant for provoking people. I wonder if he is like this because of Shizune, or if it's the other way around.
And neither do you, right? Okay, I understand. I shouldn't be so petty.
Especially with small children. Hideaki seems to accept this as an admission of defeat, which is something I feel like I can't let go of. However, I'll just have to let it go while I have the chance.
I can hear Shiina's laughter bouncing through the hallways the moment I enter the door of the house, and I follow her into what I assume to be the living room. It has more people than I expected.
Among them I see a distinctive and familiar blonde ponytail. I'm more confused than surprised as to why Elena is here. Elena doesn't seem euphoric about this chance encounter either.
Sitting next to Elena is a tall, androgynous-looking woman in an elegant suit. I'd like to assume it's his older sister, but I don't want to take the risk.
shizu_a3_seq_4: I didn't expect you to arrive so soon.

At first I think she's talking to me, but it turns out she's referring to Shizune. I don't think Elena even notices my presence. I clearly caught them in the middle of the conversation, and it seems that with their focus on Shizune, she wouldn't be able to hear me.
I should have rearranged my entire schedule for you.
Shicchan says: I should have rearranged my schedule just for you~!
That would have been nice, but I wouldn't expect you to do something like that.
Oh, hello, Hicchan~! You are finally here.
Yes. Hello, Elena.
Oh, Hisao? This is a big surprise. Akira, this is Hisao, a classmate. Hisao, this is Akira, my sister.
What's up.
She raises her hand in a brief and rather casual gesture of greeting. So she is the older sister after all.
I hope we're not going to ruin any of your plans. Since we're only going to be here for one more day, Elena and I thought she might as well come with me.
Akira turns to me, as if she feels obligated to explain. I'm grateful for that.
I guess my position here would be better described as a babysitter.
Akira ruffles Hideaki's hair as he continues his hobby of looking displeased.
That's humiliating.
Oh really? I'll change my title once you're a few years old. Or at least a few centimeters.
They make an interesting couple, although Akira looks more like a lawyer than a babysitter. However, I'm still not quite sure why she and Elena are here.
Taking a look around the room, there are tennis rackets, golf clubs, and even a stack of fishing rods and tackle boxes hidden here and there.
Behind every chair, in every corner, and under every table is some piece of amateur outdoor equipment. I pick up one of the fishing rods and play with it.
This is a nice house.
Shizune, it seems like your dad has a lot of hobbies.
For a moment I forget to sign what I say, but Shiina is already in the process of interpreting what I said for her. I'm still a little impressed at how automatic the acting is for Shiina.
Do you fish?
No, I don't know how. I kind of want to learn, since I heard it's relaxing.
There is a river just a short drive away, my whole family knows how to fish. If you want, we could go there someday.
Can you and Hideaki fish? He didn't expect people his age to know about it, considering it always seemed like an old man's hobby.
You know, Elena is great in the kitchen. If we had some fresh fish…
It's not difficult to follow Akira's line of thinking.
If you want to eat fish, we could go to the store.
Elena's voice sounds slightly more authoritative than normal. She doesn't really seem to share her sister's enthusiasm for the idea.
It's more fun to go fishing; We could even make it a game and try to see who catches the biggest one~! That would be exciting, right? Yes~! Hicchan, what do you think? Sounds fun, doesn't it?
Yes, it certainly could be.
It seems like a good idea to me. I don't know how to fish either, so now is as good a time as any to learn.
His eyes move to Elena, who remains impassive. This sours Akira's smile a little, and makes me wonder why Elena is being so stubborn about it.
I don't think we have enough fishing equipment for everyone.
We can take turns. It will be a team battle.
What is she saying?
We can take turns. She also wants it to be a contest.
Come on Elena, we might as well make the most of this.
So this is going to be a competition to see who can catch the biggest fish, or the most?
It seems that the older sister understands better, as always.

Shicchan says he guesses Elena would rather go to the store, right~? It's a lot less work, so it's only natural that she preferred it! But going fishing would be more fun, and we'd save money. Akira, you have the right idea~!
Akira gives a polite, if a little forced, smile. Shizune's praise wasn't his goal, after all.
Isn't the river far away?
I don't think it's that far, and I can drive if we have to. That's fine with me, as long as they catch something.
shizu_a3_seq_5: Can your car fit that many people, plus all the fishing equipment?
She purses her lips as her fingers move subtly, counting the number of passengers and cargo required. If Shizune, Shiina, Elena, Akira, Hideaki and I are going...
Six people. Damn, my car can only carry five.
In fact, if Hideaki sat on my lap, we could—
I'm not going to sit on your lap.
Shicchan says his father's car would be big enough.
What, the Escape? If he doesn't mind us using it, then I guess we have no choice. It feels a little bad to abandon my car, considering I won't have it for long.

Despite Elena's stubbornness, and Hideaki's questions about whether we'd rather eat first than gamble on a fish dinner that might not materialize, there's no dissuading Akira and Shizune as they argue over the transportation plan.
My expectations for a somewhat relaxing drive through the countryside are met. Akira's driving is as calm and relaxed as the surroundings, to the point that Shiina falls asleep during the ride.

I thought this trip would have been too slow for Shizune's liking, but she seems to genuinely enjoy it. Even with Hideaki squeezed uncomfortably between her and the door, she just keeps staring out the window and smiling.
The area around the river is very beautiful. Akira and Shizune go to the river so quickly that we have no choice but to chase them. Otherwise, we would have been left eating dust.

I can see that Hideaki and Elena are just pleasing their sisters, with Elena being the less enthusiastic of the two. However, Shiina seems as happy as ever. It seems like he's managed to hold on to a bit of Shizune and Akira's excitement.
As for me, I would prefer to eat now, but the idea of ​​fresh fish prepared by Elena is appealing.

The river is larger than I imagined, although very picturesque and peaceful. Aside from a small pier apparently built just for fishing, this place seems untouched by civilization, and I realize how much greenery I've seen lately.
Shizune pulls Shiina aside so they can explain to Akira how to fish. Hideaki and Elena are talking to each other, so I decide to join the enthusiastic trio.
Hmm…so which of these lures should I use, then? Can I use this cute little one?
Wait, wait~! This is a contest, we need to choose the teams first! Shicchan and I will be on a team, of course. Hicchan, you're going to be on our team, right? We can be the student council team~!
Very good.
Very well, then. With that it's Hideaki, Elena and I on the other team. Elena, what should we call each other?
It's the No Enthusiasm team...
Once again, Akira's best efforts are rejected. Shizune and Shiina, on the other hand, don't lack enthusiasm at all.
Hisao! You can be our point man, please strive to catch as many fish as possible, or the biggest one.
Why me? No one has taught me how to fish yet.
We can do it now~.
After a quick tutorial, Shizune immediately tries to get us into a discussion about strategy in a team fishing competition.
Somehow, competition doesn't seem particularly applicable to a sport where you spend hours sitting and waiting for a fish to bite into a worm.
It seems that Hideaki had the spare rod left. You know it's just a rope tied to a bamboo stick, right? That means that when deciding the order, you should compete against him.
What, why me?
You're the one with the least experience here, Hicchan~.
Yeah? So who's the best here? Shizune? Hideaki is your brother, he's probably just as good. He probably fishes all the time, since he lives near a lake. It could even be better.
Looking at you three makes my head hurt. You know I'm only hearing two-thirds of the conversation, right? What is it about?
Choose our lineup.
Akira makes a worried face. She's getting impatient, which probably isn't too unreasonable.
If you're impatient, that only excites me more. Now I want to up the ante.
What is she saying?
He wants to up the ante.
I wouldn't be in such a hurry; We have two-time beginner's luck on our side, after all. The only way you can top that is by capturing an entire ocean.
This is a body of fresh water, marine biologist~.
A strange insult, delivered with unabashed, innocent glee. Akira doesn't seem bothered. He laughs it off, and Shizune looks like her usual mischievous self again. I'm glad you guys get along.
So are we going to choose teams, or what? I'm a little hungry...
Hisao, Shiina, and I are on one team, and Elena, Hideaki, and you are on the other, right?
I guess that's the most obvious fix. But wouldn't it be more fun to mix them up a little? Hey?
Hmm~, don't you want to fish with your own sister?
Well, neither of us knows how to fish, so putting us both on the same team is something…
Well, it sounds like you heard something a little dangerous. I try to change the subject before Shizune can turn that incredulous look on her face into something else.
shizu_a3_seq_6: So I guess you and Shizune know each other?
Of course. We've known each other for a long time.
Akira flashes a knowing smile at Shizune. It's not until Shiina has finished translating what she said that Shizune looks worried.

Akira is certainly different from Elena. Aside from her appearance, she is much more casual and relaxed. I expected Elena's entire family to be proper and formal like her, so this is a surprise. But, I feel like she's easy to talk to.
As much as I like to talk about catching fish, we should surely do it at some point.
Would you suggest there should be a lineup, like in baseball? Or should it be all at once, or tag battle style?
Can everyone sit wherever they want, or do teams have to be together? Do we announce where we fish? What sizes of fish will we be counting?
Seeing Akira groan after Shiina obediently translates for her, Shizune rubs her glasses, laughing silently.
It doesn't matter. Let's go fishing, then.
It can be an individual contest.

I sit down, ready to fish, although I don't feel very confident. Everyone else is already seated, except Akira, who takes a seat next to me and casts his line after taking off his jacket and rolling up his sleeves.

Hideaki and Shiina end up sitting on the shore and fishing together, since there isn't enough room on the dock for everyone. Truth be told, I'd rather be sitting next to Shizune, but Akira seems pretty approachable.
Be careful, you're a little close. Don't tangle our lines, okay?
So you've never fished before?
No, but I've seen how they do it on television. I always wanted to catch one of those big fish with a sword instead of a face. A marlin, I think.
If I remember correctly, those are from the ocean; They are saltwater fish.
I know that. Why does everyone act like I don't know the difference between freshwater fish and saltwater fish?
If you're not careful, you'll scare away fish, whether they're saltwater or not.

Akira's voice is a little loud between her efforts to goad Shizune and entertain Elena, so she may be right. My fishing line doesn't seem to be grabbing anything, but I don't know how much of that is due to Akira.

Shizune tries her best to relax in the sun, and manages to fake it very well, but I can tell that she would be a little bummed not to know what she's talking about. Not having Shiina around can be a real problem.
Hisao, what is the result so far? Are we winning? I hope so, since I entrusted the team's success to you.
I manage to make some awkward signs by creatively positioning my rod. This is probably close to babbling in speech terms.
You're like, right there. Can't you know?
Disappointing; you let yourself get distracted. You have to concentrate.
I should have known. Well, it's 0-0 in any case.
Akira chuckles, although it's clear that it really put him off.
Are they just numbers now, or are we also keeping track of size?
Both; qualification matters.
Who is going to rate them? Are you a certified fish judge?
Shizune shakes her head to indicate that she is not.
…But it doesn't seem like it's very difficult. Tell Shiina to stop shaking her hands like that, she's scaring away all the fish. And ask Hideaki why he hasn't even bothered to cast yet.
I take a look at the two and shout out what Shizune said to them.
Shicchan, I think he's upset that he kept the spare rod~!
Since Shiina is largely unable to sign coherently right now, she only receives a bewildered look from Shizune in response. Shizune simply sighs after I translate it for her.
Hey, even if you're depressed about it, you have to try it! You could hit the jackpot, for all you know. But you won't catch anything unless you do!

I feel like at least half of her support is because if Hideaki catches “the jackpot,” she wants to be there to eat it, and having six people fishing only leads to better chances of catching something than having five.
The constant and awkward rush I have to make to communicate with Shizune, not to mention her growing restless, makes me think that it might be okay for her to have a chance to fish.
Hey, can we change now?
Clear. Elena?
No, no, please. I have no idea how to fish.
I sign to her what they say, since I seem to have taken Shiina's place as Shizune's interpreter at the moment.
How magnanimous of you, Elena.
Oh dear, here we go. I don't bother translating what she says for fear of provoking another fight.
Shizune says you should at least try. It might even be fun.
Very good. Akira, how do you use this?
shizu_a3_seq_7: It's pretty simple...
I wonder how ethical it is to intentionally and completely change what Shizune said like that. At least it was worth it.
…I think I understand. What bait do you think would be the best to use? I would prefer something that wouldn't hurt the fish too much.
If you're going to put a hook in his mouth, I don't think the bait is going to hurt him much more.
And let him go...? No, no, don't do that.
But if it's not big, there's little point in killing it...
With my hands free, it's much easier for me to translate what everyone is saying. Now Shizune is the one who has to deal with her hands full, but she seems to take it in stride.
That's very arrogant. Alright, I'll only blow the big ones out of the water too, from now on.
What is he saying?
Akira just sighs after I translate it for her.
No, I don't like that “only”. You know, a fish is a fish, and you take what you can get.
Unfortunately, Shizune can't hear her and Elena doesn't seem to be paying much attention right now.

Elena is taking to fishing easily; It is a very relaxing activity, after all. It's not long before they both catch a fish, and surprisingly, Elena is just as interested as Shizune in knowing which is the bigger of the two.
As the hours go by, it seems like they are even starting to have fun.

At the end of the day, we have several good-sized fish between us. Even Hideaki and Shiina managed to catch one. No one brings up that we were competing to see who could catch the most. I don't think anyone cares anymore.
Shizune and Shiina are talking to each other from a distance, while Hideaki and Elena are doing the same. I decide to take advantage of the tranquility of the moment to talk to Akira.
Elena and Shizune got along well today. I actually didn't expect it, after seeing how they treat each other at school.
She gives an amused snort. It seems like you don't take your disputes as seriously as I do.
They have their reasons. Elena and I are leaving tomorrow for a while, so we were thinking about giving them a visit.
In the end, I'm glad we did it.
After a brief silence, she stretches loudly and then claps her hands to get everyone's attention.
Well, that seems like enough to feed everyone. We should go back, now.

Elena nods, but then hesitates. Even with her face slightly clouded, she seems to be in a better mood than this morning. Akira really seems to know how to treat her, and diffused his antipathy towards Shizune very well.
Today's catch looks delicious, I kind of wish I had some soy sauce so I could eat it now.
I thought you wanted me to cook it...
Don't you think eating it raw is okay?
Despite Akira's protests, or jokes since I can't tell which one it is, we decide to wait to at least cook the fish before eating it.
It's already gotten pretty late while we've been away, and by the time we get back to Shizune's house, it's a good time for dinner.

Some of my pills scattered all over the bottom of my suitcase, which I didn't notice until minutes before I was ready to go to bed last night. I spent quite a bit of time getting them out of my luggage.
By the time I wake up, I'm already starting the day with a migraine, thanks to a combination of problems falling asleep and waking up late.

When I enter the living room, Hideaki is there finishing his breakfast. With his fork raised halfway to his mouth, he seems unsure whether he should continue eating or greet me. Maybe I should leave the room.
Good morning.
Good morning.
What do you think we should have for breakfast?
“Should we”? Aren't you having breakfast already?
Yes. Everyone else already ate.
Despite that, he repeats his question again. He's just trying to be nice. It's a strange way to put it, but I appreciate it nonetheless, and I'm feeling very hungry.
I try to make some conversation with him while I prepare my breakfast, to fill the silence.
That fishing trip yesterday was fun. Do the Hakamichi and Satou often get together like this?
Not really.
I see.
Not really. There's a brief pause before Hideaki deigns to fill me in a bit more.
Family matters. Our parents are brothers-in-law, and they don't like each other.
Hearing that gives me a lot to think about. It puts into context the way Shizune and Elena deal with each other, and even makes me not want to get involved anymore.
Oh. Family matters can be problematic.
shizu_a3_seq_8: Hideaki simply nods as I sit at the table with my breakfast. I wish it were a little easier to talk to him.

While I'm eating, I notice that the house seems strangely quiet for a place where Shiina is. If Shizune and Shiina already had breakfast, it can't be because they are asleep. I ask Hideaki where they are.
Shizune and Shiina left to run some errands for our dad. The local merchants like to deal with Shiina, so he insisted.
Well, she has a kind and cheerful personality. I can see why they like it. Maybe you should start taking lessons from her, you could increase your business relationships.
Are you serious?
He seems to be serious. I don't know what kind of business relationships a little boy would need. Maybe you want to have the best bake sale fundraiser ever.
It's a shame that eventually I'll have to leave here and won't be around to see whatever he's planning.

I wonder again what kind of person Shizune's dad is, other than being relatively passionate about the outdoors. What I know so far is that he asks his partners and his daughter's friends to do him favors.
I'm assuming he is extremely shy or extremely lazy. Maybe it's too early to make a crude prediction, but it would certainly explain a lot of Shizune's personality.
Do you want to go somewhere?
Not really. Why, do you?
I thought there might be somewhere you wanted to go. Don't you want to go sightseeing, or eat at a specific restaurant?
Don't know. I've never been here before.
I see.

I was about to ask him about what Shizune was like when she was younger, but he managed to throw me off with just one question. This seems to be as uncomfortable a conversation for him as it is for me.
Wow, you are eager to please me today. Why are you being so nice? Are you showing your secret soft side now that your sister isn't around?
You are somewhat right. Shizune wanted me to keep you company today.
I don't want to upset him, and I try to make him see that, but Hideaki is just as stubborn as his sister and feels like it's his duty. He also seems to be seriously trying to be nice.
Quickly, I begin to realize that Hideaki's idea of ​​fun is fishing, collecting cameras, and making esoteric puns.
Fishing is fun, but it's something I'd rather do than talk. The same goes for cameras; I would rather handle them than collect them.
This is something Hideaki notices on his own.
Are you bored?
I'm not bored at all.
I almost yawned at the words, so Hideaki ignored them completely.
You are bored. Shizune said to have fun, and I guess I don't know how to do that.
I'm having fun.
You don't seem to have fun.
I am!
Why are you screaming? I hope you don't shout so much around Shizune.
It's hard to tell if he's joking. Either way, I'm a little surprised. I try to ignore that and change the subject.
Do you only collect cameras, or do you also like photography?
Not really. If that were the case, there would be more photos in this house than there are now. What is there to take photos of?

Don't know. Birds? Architecture? One of those restaurants you were talking about? I thought this city had lots of interesting things. How can you live in a place with so many things to do and do nothing?

I thought you didn't know what there was to do here. Suddenly you have so many ideas and you're an authority on how interesting it is. You're like our tourism board. Do you want to go see birds or buildings?
Okay, okay, there's no need to get so angry.
…I'm not angry. I just think that if you're that interested, then we should go to an amusement park.
Because?
So you can have fun. It will be fun.

Will he have this same monotone, serious expression on his face while we're riding roller coasters and drop towers? That would certainly lower the fun levels. The idea does not convince me that it is worth the trip.
I don't know, I always felt like going to an amusement park meant spending more time waiting in lines than actually doing things. You would have to go earlier just to skip the lines.
Have you ever been to one?
No, but it seems that's how it is.
… Good. How about a normal park? There's one nearby where Shizune likes to go. Maybe she's there, and I can leave you with her.
What do you mean “leave me”? I am not luggage.
You don't want to go to an amusement park. I don't know what to do.
shizu_a3_seq_9: It seems like I hurt his feelings by refusing to go with him. I'm already rationalizing my decision. I don't like waiting in lines. It would be very similar to a date. I would rather go with Shizune. It would be very exhausting.
It's nothing personal, it's just that I'd rather Shizune show me around the city.
And I don't think going to an amusement park with my condition is a good idea.
The park is so close that your property could almost be considered an extension of it. Both this place and Shizune's backyard look almost the same, except that the park has benches and more people.
That said, it is very nice. There are even people walking their dogs, and children flying kites that can be seen in the distance letting themselves drift lazily back and forth over the trees.
I could sit here, in a relaxing, scenic place like this, forever.
Hideaki, on the other hand, seems to be extremely bored. I want to poke him with my finger to see if he's still alive. But would he react anyway?
Are you bored?
No. Do you go jogging or play Frisbee with the dogs like everyone else? Is that what people do in parks?
Well, you go to parks to get back to nature and enjoy the atmosphere. That's why you jog in the park, instead of on the sidewalk or something. You can jog anywhere.
I can't believe I'm having this conversation. How can you not know this? You shouldn't have brought that up, it's very strange. Have you never heard that “children should be seen and not heard”?
I lied. I'm bored. Would you like to play a game?
I complain, so that it can be heard, hoping that he understands that I don't want to. He doesn't care. In fact, you are already playing with a deck of cards.
Why are you upset? That's why we are here.
I thought we were here to look for Shizune.
Exact. That's why we should play a game. It's a trap for Shizune. You can catch anything, including people.

If we compete among ourselves in a spirit of competition and in a sporting manner, she will come here to challenge the winner, like a shark. Then I will defeat her like a safari hunter. And then we will take a photo of the award ceremony.
Sharks don't go around challenging people to games of chance like they're dojo challengers.
When did you bring that camera? Anyway, no. I have enough games hanging out with your sister.
No, let's go. It will be fun. We can play chess.
Please don't. Plus, playing chess in the park is something old people do, like fishing. You're going to age very quickly if you keep doing all these old things.

Hideaki freezes as if I suddenly start speaking a foreign language. Maybe I offended him again. Maybe he's secretly 50 years old and has aged incredibly well. Him being Shizune's brother could be a cover.
How about ladies, or go? Or even backgammon is fine, although I don't like it. If board games aren't your thing, we can play card games. Anything that isn't seven card, because that's for weaklings.
Are you afraid that you are going to lose? If you can beat me I will give you candy.
Hideaki, you are just like Shizune. I'm starting to think this is all an excuse to play games.
No. That's not true.
You are! I bet that competitive streak is genetic. I'll sell you to science.
No one can possess a human being.
How about I teach you sign language instead?

When Shizune asked me if I wanted to come here, we talked for a bit, and it seemed like you and your dad didn't use sign language. I'm just guessing, but if you don't use it, I might be able to teach you a little. Although I'm not an expert.
Anyway, I think it might be good for you to move your arms more.
He barely moves his arms. Most of the time they just hang limply at their sides. How disturbing.

It's been bothering me that Shizune's entire family apparently doesn't know how to sign. I wonder what he did before he met Shiina. Did they hire translators for her? Did he write everything in that notebook he carries with him?

The latter is most likely, or you could type it on a phone. That would explain why he dislikes using the notebook so much. As sad as it is, I can kind of see why Hideaki or his father wouldn't have bothered to learn sign language.
It was probably too much trouble at the time. It's very easy to think that. However, from what I've seen so far, neither of them resent each other or are too affected by it.
It could be that I'm overthinking the situation.

Come on. Well, to be honest, I'm still learning sign language myself. I brought all my books with me so I could keep up. Still, at least I can teach you the alphabet. It's very simple. This is “comet”.
I feel very cheesy right now, and even more so when Hideaki stares back at me blankly, as if the whole concept of learning is foreign to him.
Shizune also liked to fly kites here.
This is your attempt to save the conversation, and I'm happy to help.
Fishing, and now kites, too? Does Shizune really like all these relaxing hobbies?
Combat kites. In fact, about Shizune—
Hideaki freezes when Shiina appears behind him and puts her hands over his eyes.
Hello hello~! Guess who~!
He also seemed to finally be relaxing.
shizu_a3_seq_10: Hello, Shiina. Is Shizune with you?
Hicchan, don't ruin it! Don't spoil it, don't ruin the surprise, okay~?
Shiina.
Bingo~! It's right! But~, it was too easy, for some reason.
I don't know what she means by “for some reason.”
Too many people can know it was me! I want to surprise someone! She was sure she would manage to fool Hideaki~. Why didn't you fall, hm~?
You're the only person who does that. You, and the kidnappers.
Oh really? Wow~!
Why are you laughing?
Are you giving Hisao trouble? I thought you'd take him somewhere more exciting than the park. It's not even that far from home. You are very lazy.
Hideaki, are you giving Hicchan trouble? You should have taken it somewhere more exciting! The park is very close to home, Shicchan says you're lazy~.
He wanted to come here. Why are you so argumentative?
I have to keep my little brother in line.
What is he saying?
That you must be kept in line.
Seriously…

They are ready to fight so soon. On the one hand, I've heard that siblings who fight a lot are not uncommon, and the fact that they fight at all shows that there must be some level of communication going on. So, it's good that they get along.

They argue all the way back home. Shiina translates for Shizune, and I translate for Hideaki. So it seems more like we're the ones arguing, except not really. No one could listen to Shiina and believe that.
The day was fun in the end, at least.
Despite having been here for only two days, it feels like it has been so much longer. I wake up feeling more tired than refreshed. Maybe because I've been moving almost constantly since I got here.
Whatever the reason, it's making me wake up unusually late every day. I like sleeping in, but it could be inconvenient if it ends up becoming a habit.

I can hear a deep, male voice shouting loudly in the background. It must be Shizune's dad. Or maybe, with the size of this place, its creditors. The former is more likely, since the screams don't seem angry, just loud.

Shizune, Hideaki, and Shiina are sitting in the living room, having a one-sided conversation with a giant werebear who alternates between choking on food from a plate balanced on his leg and twirling a sword.

From the way Hideaki and Shizune look, I expected their dad to be a very reserved, neat, and possibly androgynous person, so I'm very surprised. I'm surprised for a moment, until he starts talking to me.
Hello! You must be Shizune's other friend. Did you rest well last night? The guest rooms are a little sparse, if there is anything you need feel free to let me know.
Thank you. He must be Shizune's father. It's a pleasure to meet you. I am Shizune's classmate, Hisao Nakai.

The pleasure is mine. I have wanted to meet you, after hearing that I would have a second guest in my house. Unexpected. You hear something like that, and obviously you want to see what that person is like. Would you like my business card?

He holds up a box full of them for a second and I can see that his name is Jigoro and his office hours are eight to six. They also say he is a “consultant.” What a prepared guy, carrying his box of cards in his own home.
We just sat down for a rather late lunch, you're just in time to join us. Good. Pick a place to sit and I'll bring you a plate. I hope you don't mind eating bear liver.

I thought bear liver was toxic. Anyway, the idea of ​​eating a bear liver doesn't appeal to me, except for the ability to tell people that I ate bear liver. I guess it wouldn't hurt to try it. But Shizune's dad just laughs.
I'm just kidding. Although, maybe it wouldn't be such a bad idea to cook up some bear livers for you guys. They will make them strong.
Actually we're going to eat omelets. I'll make you one right now. Is it unusual for you to have an omelette for lunch?
Very unusual.
No not at all.
Jigoro fades away to where the kitchen should be. I'm surprised that despite living in this place, he has to cook my lunch. Maybe he just cooks because he likes to do it.
My steaming plate of food is ready in no time. It smells very good.
Are you on the student council, like Shizune? Is the student council so busy, Shizune has to drag her friends everywhere she goes?
Sometimes vacations are just vacations.
You're right about the student council part. Although I think we're just here for fun.
I see. That's true? When I was young, our student councils were so busy that I don't think we could have afforded to go on vacation.
It must be nice, having so much free time. It should give you plenty of time to think about your future.
I don't like the direction this discussion is going, and I'm starting to think about how to avoid it.
Have you thought about that? About what you want to do?
No, I haven't thought about it much lately. What do you do, if you don't mind me asking? It must be a very good thing, if you can give him a house like this.
Why do you want to know that? Children are not interested in business. What interest do you have in my businesses? Suspicious. Are you some kind of tax collector, boy?
sora_paranoia_confrontation: Sora took out a thermal bottle from his sports bag and offered it to me with a shaky smile.
Drink some warm tea, Hisao. Your hands are cold.
Kenji's voice echoed in my mind: 'Never take anything they give you! The syndrome starts with a sleeping pill in the drink!'
My chest started to burn. The irregular beat of my heart echoed like a war drum in my ears.
Hisao? Why are you looking at me like that? Are you... afraid of me?
sora_trust_breakthrough: I took the thermal bottle and took a sip. It was barley tea with a touch of honey. Hot, sweet and comforting.
Forgive me, Sora... I've been hearing stupid rumors and I let fear cloud my head.
(His eyes water and he wraps his arms around me in a tight, warm hug.)
Silly... I'm never going to hurt you. We're two broken people trying to stay together, remember?
The wind blew with increasing fury. The first drops of the typhoon hit the runway.
paranoia_collapse_track: I pushed the bottle away from me. The thermos clinked onto the plaid.
Get away from me! I know what they plan on this hill!
Hisao! What's the matter?! Why do you say that?!
The pain was a withering stab in the sternum. I fell to my knees, gasping for oxygen that wasn't reaching my lungs.
My vision clouded in red static. The world turned off between Sora's desperate screams...
yumi_sanctuary_promise: I took Yumi's trembling hands in mine. I could feel the rough marks of his scars against my skin.
I'm not going to let anything happen to you, Yumi. Neither fire, nor wind, nor any ghost from the past will harm you while I am here.
(She looks up and for the first time does not remove her bangs to hide herself. A shy smile illuminates her face.)
Thank you, Hisao... With you I feel like I can be brave.
elena_scotland_dilemma: Hisao... my family awaits my arrival in Scotland. Blindness never prevented me from feeling affection, but I fear that the ocean will cool what has been born between us.
Elena, I will cross that ocean as many times as necessary. No distance will erase the sound of your laughter.
(A sweet smile blooms on her lips as she tilts her head excitedly.)
aiko_lighthouse_sanctuary: We enter the lantern room of the lighthouse. The thick stone walls protected us from the outside gale.
Your hands are warm, Hisao. It's a strange feeling. Like touching the sun when you thought it had gone out.
I'm not going to let anyone erase you, Aiko. You are real, and your art matters.
(He rests his head against my chest and listens to the rhythmic beat of my heart).
It sounds like a tired metronome... but it's the most beautiful rhythm in the world.
shizu_council_truth: (Checks the school evacuation maps with a determined gesture, giving quick instructions to Shiina.)
Shizune says that the Council will not let any students suffer during this typhoon! Everyone to designated shelters!
I admire your strength, Shizune. You are a true beacon to all of us.
mystery_dossier_analysis: At midnight in my room, I examined the photocopies that Kenji had given me with a magnifying glass.
'Year 2012: Disappearance of Keiko Fujiwara, a patient with severe kidney failure. Last seen on the beach of La Cala'.
'Year 2016: Death of Daiki Satou, cardiac arrest on the roof during the festival blackout'.
Satou... Satou as Elena? Did Elena have a brother here before I arrived?
A shadow was cast against the curtain of my window. When I drew the curtain... there was no one on the balcony.
Just a small withered flower placed on the windowsill.
typhoon_warning: Saturday, 9:00 p.m. The typhoon hit Yamaku Hill with the force of an enraged titan.
Lightning tore through the night sky and all of the academy's transformers exploded in a shower of green sparks.
The darkness was total and instantaneous.
The emergency system's speakers began to emit a terrifying static screech.
'Attention... save file corrupted... The remaining heartbeats are not enough to maintain the timeline...'
ddlc_reality_crack: I felt my way back to my room. My computer screen was on, emitting a blood red glow.
In the center of the screen floated the translucent image of a girl in a white bow who did not belong to Yamaku.
Hello, Hisao. Or rather... hello to whoever is behind the screen.
You have been trying to save them all, ignoring that their destinies are predetermined by fear and illness.
But if your heart refuses to give up... the code will be rewritten as many times as necessary.
What is happening?! My heart... can't take it anymore!
The monitor exploded in a blinding flash. A wave of pain took my last breath away.
timeloop_train_awakening: The clatter of the train against the rails brought me back to consciousness with a sudden jolt.
I blinked in bewilderment. I was wearing my school uniform and my suitcase at my feet.
'Next stop: Yamaku Hill Station. Please prepare your luggage.'
What...what does this mean?! The train? Was everything I experienced... the typhoon, the lighthouse, my collapse... a hallucination?
I put my hand in my pants pocket. My fingers brushed against a folded sheet of paper.
It was Kenji's file with cuts from the last 15 years. It wasn't a dream! Time has gone backwards!
This time I know the dangers. I know the typhoon and the weight of loneliness that torments the girls. This time I will save them all!
timeloop_knowledge_choices: I walked through the doors of Yamaku with a completely different look.
He was no longer a fearful boy awaiting his medical death sentence; He was a protector who understood the sacred value of every second of life.
To what path should I direct my determination to break the loop of tragedy?
ending_sora_true: Weeks after the typhoon, the athletics track shone again in the summer sun.
Come on, Hisao! Today we will complete the fifteen hundred meters together!
I'm no longer afraid of my heart stopping, because I know that as long as you run next to me, it will beat strong.
(He takes my hand, intertwining his fingers with mine with a radiant smile).
Until the end of the world, Hisao! Together!
ending_yumi_true: Yumi walked barefoot along the edge of the cove. The sea breeze fluttered her white dress.
For the first time, her hair was pulled back into a high ponytail, leaving her face bare in the bright sun.
The sun is warm, Hisao... It doesn't burn anymore. It feels wonderful.
(He blushes tenderly and comes closer to give me a soft kiss on the cheek.)
You taught me that scars are not something to be ashamed of, but proof that we survived.
ending_elena_true: In front of Yamaku's door, the taxi was waiting for Elena's luggage to the airport.
My family is waiting for me in Inverness... but I left half of my heart in this garden in Yamaku.
I held his hand in mine and handed him a plane ticket to Edinburgh.
Then I'll come look for you as soon as this semester ends, Elena. I will not allow an ocean to separate us.
(A tear of happiness rolls down her cheek as she smiles with infinite tenderness).
I will be waiting on the dock listening to the bells, my dear Hisao.
ending_aiko_true: The large mural in the art workshop was finally completed.
In the center of the immense canvas, two silhouettes contemplated a sky composed of millions of shades of green, blue and pure light.
It doesn't taste like factory smoke anymore, Hisao. Now it tastes like dawn after the storm.
It is the most beautiful work I have ever seen, Aiko.
(He leans gently against my shoulder, closing his eyes in serene peace).
Thank you for not letting me jump... Now I know what color love is.
ending_kenji_bunker: Kenji and I barricaded ourselves in room 204 with three boxes of instant noodles and binoculars.
We survived the festival, brother! The feminists couldn't with our strategic alliance!
Kenji... I think the girls just wanted to sell us raffle tickets.
That's what they want you to believe! Cheers to survival!
ending_ddlc_epiphany: Reality began to disintegrate into lines of code and fragments of text.
Thank you for playing our story to the end, Hisao... or should I say, dear reader.
No matter if their bodies were flawed or their hearts were fragile, you gave them life with every minute of your reading.
The screen slowly darkened leaving only a bright message: 'Never forget the value of those around you.'
ending_true_miracle: The cove beach was full of life. Sora was splashing water laughing out loud with Shiina and Shizune.
Aiko painted the golden sparkles in the sand, while Elena and Yumi prepared the picnic under an umbrella.
Even Kenji was there, complaining about the heat while drinking cold lemonade with the others.
I looked towards the infinite horizon where the sky and the sea merged in an embrace of perfect light.
When I arrived in Yamaku I thought my life had ended in that frozen park.
Now I understand that my heart didn't stop that winter to die... it stopped so I had to find my way up this hill.
Hey Hisao! Stop philosophizing and come swim with us!
We save you the best place under the sun!
I ran towards them across the warm sand. My heart beat strong, full, alive... and in perfect harmony with the world.

ending_sora_true.title: Sora Ending: Wind and Ash
ending_sora_true.summary: They overcame the pain of their broken bodies to run together towards a future without limits.
epilogue: Months after that scorching summer, you and Sora learned that physical and heart wounds do not define the speed at which you can move forward. On the Yamaku athletic fields, the echo of each stride became a shared compass.

Sora found in you not a look of pity or condescension, but a companion who ran to his side even when his legs gave out and his chest burned. Morning training became a sacred ritual of complicity and laughter.

The cardiologist's medical report revealed a surprising stability: prudent exercise and the warmth of mutual affection strengthened a heartbeat that once teetered on the brink. Together they crossed the finish line towards a new life where pain is just an overcome memory.
mysteries: ✦ Who was the lone figure who left an offering of white flowers and an antique stopwatch on the track's bleachers on the eve of graduation?

✦ In the confidential diaries of the infirmary there is still a cryptic note from the former school doctor: "The patient maintains her speed, but the echo of the wind on the hill always demands its price." Will their hearts truly be safe when the harsh winter falls?

ending_yumi_true.title: Yumi Ending: The Flower Among Ashes
ending_yumi_true.summary: She healed her past traumas and learned to walk proudly in the light of the world.
epilogue: The Yamaku library fell silent, but it was no longer that oppressive silence of loneliness and fear, but a haven of peace and shared tenderness. Yumi slowly began to brush aside her dark bangs, allowing the light to caress the marks on her skin without shame.

At your side, his timid voice regained his lost confidence. His hands, which had previously trembled as he turned the pages, learned to intertwine with yours with unwavering warmth. Those afternoons of barley tea and shared readings germinated in a serene and protective love.
Yumi discovered that the beauty of a flower lies not in the absence of scars, but in the miraculous strength with which it is reborn from the ashes.
mysteries: ✦ What was the real cause of the devastating fire that consumed Yumi's childhood home? An old newspaper clipping filed in the basement suggests that the fire was not started by a chance short circuit, and that a hooded figure was seen fleeing through the pouring rain.
✦ Who continues to send letters without a return address or postmark to the library every anniversary of the tragedy, sealed with crimson wax?

ending_elena_true.title: Final Elena: The Melody of the Ocean
ending_elena_true.summary: Geographic distance could not break the promise sealed between tea and violin melodies.
epilogue: The farewell at the international terminal was not a definitive goodbye, but rather the prelude to a promise that crossed oceans and continents. Elena returned to Scotland carrying in her memory every aroma, every breeze and every musical note shared in Yamaku.

The letters written in Braille and the tapes with sound recordings that they exchanged week after week kept alive the fire of an indestructible bond. In their world where the eye cannot see, love became a tangible certainty guided by touch and music.
As the end of autumn arrived, the unmistakable clatter of her white cane echoed again on the station platform: Elena had returned to walk by your side forever.
mysteries: ✦ Why was Elena's influential family so vehemently opposed to her stays in Japan? Ancient notarial documents link Elena's blindness to a mysterious inheritance dispute and an abandoned estate in the hills.
✦ What unpublished violin score, without title or signature but dated one hundred years ago, did Elena find hidden in the lining of her case the night before her departure?

ending_aiko_true.title: Final Aiko: The Colors of the Soul
ending_aiko_true.summary: His art found meaning beyond words in shared warmth.
epilogue: In the old painting workshop bathed in the twilight sun, Aiko displayed colossal canvases that breathed an unknown force. His inability to articulate with words the labyrinth of his thoughts dissolved the moment you learned to decipher the secret language of his strokes.

There was no need for speeches or solemn promises: each brushstroke loaded with oil was a caress, and each combination of nuances revealed the purest truth of his heart. Together they inaugurated the academy's most acclaimed exhibition.
Aiko smiled like never before, knowing that her loneliness had become an eternal bridge to your soul.
mysteries: ✦ What meaning do the blurry faces and cryptic dates that Aiko obsessively paints on the back of her frames hold?

✦ No one in Yamaku has been able to explain why, on full moon nights, Aiko secretly climbs to the roof to look at the ruined tower in the surrounding forest. What secret did you witness in that forgotten place during your first days at the academy?

ending_kenji_bunker.title: Comic Ending: Camaraderie in the Trenches
ending_kenji_bunker.summary: You chose Kenji's paranoid prudence. The world keeps spinning outside.
epilogue: You decided to ignore the risks of romance and barricaded yourself in Kenji Seto's conspiratorial sanctuary. Among mountains of bean cans, maps covered in red threads and dismantled radio sets, you fortified your room against the supposed "global feminist conspiracy."

The weeks passed between delirious conspiracy theories, night watch shifts and heated debates about survival in the face of the end of the world. Although love was left out of your horizon, you forged a brotherhood as extravagant as it was unbreakable.
Kenji appointed you his Trusted Lieutenant and supreme commander of the emergency pantry.
mysteries: ✦ Although Kenji's ideas seemed like a product of his feverish imagination, one night the shortwave radio tuned to a classified military frequency that transmitted exactly the coordinates Kenji had scribbled in his notebook.
✦ Who is the enigmatic woman in the dark trench coat who stops at 3:33 AM every Tuesday in front of Kenji's window before vanishing into the fog?

ending_ddlc_epiphany.title: Final Goal: The Window to the Soul
ending_ddlc_epiphany.summary: You broke the barrier of fiction. Your empathy transcended the screen.
epilogue: The lines of dialogue faded and the digital curtain fell into an eerie silence. In that abyss beyond the sprites and drawn backgrounds, the Yamaku girls became aware of your gaze on the other side of the screen.

They understood that you were not a simple entity programmed to follow a predefined route, but a real person with your own heartbeat who decided to dedicate hours of your life to listening to them, understanding their fears and relieving their pain.
A silent, infinite gratitude hung in the air before the world dissolved into an embrace of light.
mysteries: ✦ Why has an invisible file that stores the heartbeats of your elections been registered in the operating system's memory?
✦ Does a story really restart when you read again, or do the souls within the code wait patiently remembering every caress and tear of your previous journey?

ending_true_miracle.title: TRUE ENDING: The Great Miracle of Yamaku
ending_true_miracle.summary: You broke the curse of isolation and suspicion. They all found healing, love and a future on the flowering hill.
epilogue: Against all odds, you broke down one after another the walls of silence, mistrust and pain that kept the souls of Yamaku isolated in their own fortresses. Sora, Yumi, Elena, Aiko, Shizune, Shiina, and even Kenji gathered at the top of the hill under a snowfall of cherry petals.
The heart that once threatened to go out on a frigid winter day now beat with indomitable strength, nourished by the collective miracle of empathy, forgiveness and love.
Scars stopped being symbols of tragedy and became medals of victory. The entire academy celebrated the rebirth of a spring that will never die out.
mysteries: ✦ What is the origin of the ancient legend that the village elders tell about the old shrine on Yamaku Hill, according to which a heart that gives itself unreservedly to healing others is blessed with renewed life?

✦ Among the historical archives of Yamaku, a photograph from eighty years ago was found showing seven students identical to the current ones, smiling under the same century-old cherry tree. Has this miracle been repeated through generations?
